Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

People aged 15 years and older and adults take 1 capsule as 1 dose, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported, and if a skin rash or another sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or a history of it, people who have had asthma when taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics, or cold remedies, and infants under 3 months of age must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, children under 2 years of age, infants and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, people with an allergic constitution, women who are pregnant or may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, people who have had allergic symptoms caused by medicines such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, or itching, elderly people, people who are physically weak or have a high fever, and patients with hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5 or Sunset Yellow FCF or a history of it should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • If symptoms do not improve after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • Drowsiness may occur while taking it.
  • Avoid driving a car or operating machinery.
  • Follow the specified dosage and administration carefully.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, difficulty urinating, (persistent or severe) thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, or insomnia occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If, rarely, shock (anaphylaxis) occurs — in which urticaria, edema, and chest tightness appear right after taking it, together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing — or if Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, general lethargy, liver function disorders such as jaundice, or interstitial pneumonia occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take antitussives and expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives or oral medicines containing an antihistamine.
  • People who are taking an MAO inhibitor used for the treatment of depression, Parkinson's disease and the like, or who are within 2 weeks of stopping one, should not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who are being given a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid or the like should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Eye drops

How it works

This medicine is used for dryness of the eye and eye fatigue accompanied by discomfort, stabbing pain, or irritation cau

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202202835. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use the eye drops

When needed, instill 1 drop at a time into each eye, several times a day. To do this, gently pull the lower eyelid down and, while looking upward, put one drop into the lower conjunctival sac.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, people with severe eye pain, patients with glaucoma, and people who have experienced allergic symptoms from eye drops such as redness of the eye, itching, swelling, or rash should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use this medicine only as eye drops, that is, a medicine put into the eye.
  • After opening, use it only once; after instilling it into the eye, discard the remaining solution and the container.
  • If symptoms worsen or last 3 days or longer, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Wash your hands thoroughly before use.
  • When using it for the first time, discard 1 to 2 drops without putting them into the eye, in order to remove any container fragments that may be produced when opening it.
  • Do not let the tip of the container touch the eyelid or eyelashes.
  • If it does, the solution may become contaminated or cloudy from eye mucus, mold, or the like.
  • Also, do not use the medicine if it has become cloudy.
  • To prevent contamination, do not share it with others.
  • This medicine can be used even while wearing contact lenses.
  • Follow the specified dosage and administration carefully.

Possible side effects

  • If eye irritation rarely appears, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • If using this medicine at the same time as other eye drops, use the other eye drops first and use this medicine about 10 minutes later.

payloads.content:

Oral medicine (MFDS 202400148)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202400148. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used to prevent and relieve dizziness, vomiting, and headache caused by motion sickness.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to prevent and relieve dizziness, vomiting, and headache caused by motion sickness.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202400148. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and over take 12 mL (2 sachets) at a time, those aged 11 years and over but under 15 years take 8 mL (1⅓ sachets) at a time, those aged 7 years and over but under 11 years take 6 mL (1 sachet) at a time, and those aged 3 years and over but under 7 years take 4 mL (⅔ of a sachet) at a time. To prevent motion sickness, take a single dose 30 minutes before boarding. If an additional dose is needed, take a single dose after allowing an interval of at least 4 hours, and limit the number of doses a day to 3 times.

Precautions for use

  • Breastfeeding women and infants and young children under 3 years of age must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who have experienced allergic symptoms (rash, reddening of the skin, itching, etc.), women who are pregnant or may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, patients with glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), patients with urination disorders, and patients suffering from respiratory diseases such as emphysema or chronic bronchitis should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.
  • If you divide 1 sachet and use the remainder later, seal the opening well for storage and use it within 2 days.
  • Follow the specified dosage and administration carefully.
  • When it is given to children, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Possible side effects

  • If rash, congested and reddened skin, itching, palpitations, or thirst occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with other antiemetics, cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, antihistamines, sedatives, or antitussives and expectorants.
  • Do not drink alcoholic beverages.

This medicine is used to relieve various symptoms of a cold, such as runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to relieve various symptoms of a cold, such as runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202302925. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and over take 1 sachet (20 ml) at a time, those aged 11 years to under 15 years take 2/3 of a sachet at a time, those aged 7 years to under 11 years take 1/2 of a sachet at a time, those aged 3 years to under 7 years take 1/3 of a sachet at a time, and those aged 2 years to under 3 years take 1/4 of a sachet at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious and potentially fatal skin reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of hypersensitivity appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen.
  • If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking this medicine and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine or have experienced such hypersensitivity, people who have experienced asthma when taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics or cold medicines, infants under 3 months of age and children under 2 years of age, and patients with severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, children under 2 years of age when it is absolutely necessary, infants and children under 15 years of age who have or are suspected of having a chickenpox or influenza infection, people with an allergic constitution, women who are pregnant or may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, people in whom symptoms of ischemic colitis such as sudden abdominal pain or rectal bleeding appear in connection with the pseudoephedrine component, people who have experienced allergic symptoms caused by a medicine such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching, the elderly, and people with a weak body or a high fever should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Before taking this medicine, people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma or difficulty urinating, people with persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or with ulcer or bleeding problems, and people with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts more than 1 week or recurs, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever and rash or a persistent headache should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If symptoms do not improve after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Children should take it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Do not take it continuously over a long period.
  • Drowsiness may come on while you are taking it.
  • Avoid driving a car or operating machinery.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty urinating, (persistent or severe) thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, or insomnia occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If, rarely, shock (anaphylaxis) occurs, which may appear immediately after taking it as hives, swelling, and chest tightness together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing, or if skin-mucosa-eye syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, liver dysfunction such as general lethargy and jaundice, interstitial pneumonia, or symptoms of reversible posterior encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome such as sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, or visual disturbance occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take antitussives and expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives or oral medicines containing an antihistamine.
  • People who are taking an MAO inhibitor used for the treatment of depression, Parkinson's disease and the like, or who are within 2 weeks of stopping one, should not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who are being given a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid or the like should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Patients who are being given a barbiturate, a tricyclic antidepressant or alcohol should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

This medicine is used for the treatment of male-pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia).

At a glance

Category

How it works

This medicine is used for the treatment of male-pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia).

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201904260. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

After the hair and scalp are completely dry, apply 0.5–1 mL of this medicine only to the affected area, twice a day (morning and evening), for at least 4 months.Do not exceed a total daily dose of 2 mL.

Precautions for use

  • Patients hypersensitive to this medicine, women, patients under 18 years of age, patients with cardiovascular disease (coronary artery disease, arrhythmia, congestive heart failure, heart valve disease, treated or untreated high blood pressure, low blood pressure), hair loss without a hereditary cause, sudden patchy hair loss, abnormalities of the scalp (erythema, inflammation, infection, irritation or pain, psoriasis, sunburn), or hair loss of unknown cause, patients who have shaved the scalp, and patients with poor tolerance to the 2% strength must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, elderly people, patients with edema or thyroid dysfunction (hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism), and patients hypersensitive to propylene glycol or with such a history should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Even if you forget to use this medicine, do not make up the missed dose; simply apply the next dose as usual.
  • This medicine is for external use only; do not use it on areas other than the scalp.
  • Do not use occlusive dressing.
  • Use of this medicine may cause burning and irritation of the eyes, so be careful that it does not get into the eyes, and if it comes into contact with sensitive areas such as the eyes, broken skin, or mucous membranes, rinse them immediately with clean water.
  • Wash your hands thoroughly after using this medicine.
  • Use hair styling products after this medicine has dried, and when using it in the evening, apply it 2 to 4 hours before bedtime so that it can dry.
  • Because circulation of air over the scalp may reduce the effect of this medicine, do not use a hair dryer to speed up its drying.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after 4 months or more of use, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If itching, scaling, erythema, redness, dermatitis, dry skin, hypertrichosis in areas other than where this medicine was applied (facial hair growth in women), folliculitis, local irritation including burning sensation and skin eruption, peeling, hair loss, skin abscess, acne, nail disorder, seborrhea, eczema, hair abnormalities, occasionally diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, chest pain, changes in blood pressure, changes in pulse, palpitations, increased heart rate, pericardial effusion, pericarditis, embolism, tachycardia, worsening of pre-existing angina or induction of angina in patients with undiagnosed coronary artery disease, bronchitis, upper respiratory tract infection, sinusitis, difficulty breathing, shortness of breath, fracture, back pain, tendinitis, pain, neuritis (such as polyneuritis), weakness, dizziness, headache, feeling dazed, fainting, hepatitis, edema, kidney stones, inflammation and fluid retention, fever, urticaria, allergic rhinitis, generalized erythema and facial swelling, chills, eye irritation, bitter taste, otitis (especially otitis externa), taste changes, visual impairment, erectile dysfunction, stabbing pain, or sudden unexplained weight gain occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not use it together with other scalp medicines, topical corticoids, retinoids, petrolatum, dithranol, medicines known to promote percutaneous absorption, or vasodilators such as guanethidine.

Oral medicine (MFDS 201005606)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201005606. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used to bring down fever caused by an acute upper respiratory tract infection.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to bring down fever caused by an acute upper respiratory tract infection.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201005606. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Children aged 6 months and older take a dose of 0.4–0.6 mL/kg (5 – 7 mg/kg) at a time at intervals of 4 to 6 hours as needed, not exceeding a maximum of 4 times a day (28 mg/kg).For children weighing 30 kg or less, do not exceed a maximum of 25 mL (300 mg) a day.For the recommended dose by age group, refer to the approved product information.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and potentially fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction, and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration, and perforation may occur.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine, patients with peptic ulcer, severe blood abnormalities, liver disorder, kidney disorder, cardiac insufficiency, high blood pressure or bronchial asthma or who have experienced these, patients who have asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics or have experienced these, and patients being treated for pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG) must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with hypersensitivity, peptic ulcer, blood abnormalities, liver disorder or kidney disorder or who have experienced these, patients with a tendency to bleed, patients with cardiac insufficiency, high blood pressure, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, the elderly and children, patients with stomach cancer, people taking low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke, women who are pregnant or may be pregnant, and breastfeeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, a drop in blood pressure, etc.), aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, granulocytopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), eosinophilia, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome) or toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency, acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, induction of asthma attacks, urticaria, eczema, purpura, occasionally rash, itching, visual disturbances such as loss of vision (not being able to see) or dark spots in the field of vision, aseptic meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or impaired consciousness, etc.), acute renal failure, oliguria (reduced urine), blood in the urine, protein in the urine, elevated BUN and blood creatinine, or hyperkalemia rarely occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, or periorbital edema; rarely jaundice, elevated GOT, GPT, or AL-P, hearing loss, tinnitus, abnormal taste, a drop in blood pressure, a rise in blood pressure, palpitations, decreased urine volume, generalized edema and the accompanying shortness of breath, or listlessness; and very rarely thirst, stomatitis, abdominal bloating, constipation, malaise, fever, or nosebleeds may occur.

Interactions

  • Do not use this medicine together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, aspirin, or high-dose methotrexate.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when using it together with glucocorticoids, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, sulfonylureas, the combined use of diuretics and antihypertensives, ACE inhibitors, furosemide, lithium, low-dose methotrexate, or coumarin anticoagulants (warfarin, etc.).

payloads.title: Topical medicine (MFDS 201802564)
payloads.summary: This medicine is used for the treatment of male-pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia).
payloads.content:
Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicineThis medicine is used for the treatment of male-pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia).

Topical medicine (MFDS 201802564)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201802564. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for the treatment of male-pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the treatment of male-pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia).

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201802564. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

After the hair and the scalp are completely dry, apply 0.5 to 1 mL of this medicine to the affected area only, twice a day (morning and evening), for at least 4 months, and do not let the total daily amount exceed 2 mL.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be used by women, people under 18 years of age, patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with a cardiovascular disease (coronary artery disease, arrhythmia, congestive heart failure, valvular heart disease, treated or untreated high blood pressure, low blood pressure), patients who have no hereditary factor for hair loss, patients with sudden patchy hair loss, patients with a scalp abnormality such as erythema, inflammation, infection, irritation or pain of the scalp, psoriasis or sunburn, patients with hair loss of unknown cause, patients who are using another medicine for the scalp, patients who have shaved the scalp, or patients who tolerate the 2 % strength poorly.
  • Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is elderly, has edema, has thyroid dysfunction (hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism), has local exfoliation, dermatitis, psoriasis of the scalp or a severe burn, or has a history of heart disease.
  • Use this medicine externally only and do not use it on any area other than the scalp.
  • Do not use an occlusive dressing.
  • Because this medicine may cause burning and irritation of the eyes, be careful to keep it out of the eyes, and if it touches a sensitive area such as the eyes, broken skin or a mucous membrane, rinse it off immediately with clean water.
  • Use hair styling products after this medicine has dried, and when using it in the evening, use it 2 to 4 hours before bedtime so that it can dry.
  • Because circulation of air over the scalp may reduce the effect of this medicine, do not use a hair dryer to speed up its drying.

Possible side effects

  • If any of the following appears, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: itching, scaling, erythema, redness, dermatitis, dry skin, excessive hair growth at sites other than the area where this medicine was applied (facial hair growth in women), folliculitis, local irritation including a burning sensation and skin eruption, exfoliation, hair loss, skin abscess, acne, nail disorder, seborrhea, eczema, hair abnormality, bronchitis, upper respiratory tract infection, sinusitis, difficulty breathing, occasional diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, chest pain, change in blood pressure, change in pulse, palpitations, increased heart rate, pericardial effusion, pericarditis, embolism, tachycardia, worsening of pre-existing angina or induction of angina in a person with undiagnosed coronary artery disease, shortness of breath, fracture, back pain, tendinitis, pain, neuritis (including polyneuritis), weakness, dizziness, headache, feeling dazed, fainting, hepatitis, edema, kidney stones, inflammation and fluid retention, fever, urticaria, allergic rhinitis, systemic erythema and facial swelling, chills, eye irritation, bitter taste, otitis (especially otitis externa), change in taste, visual disturbance, erectile dysfunction, stabbing pain, or sudden unexplained weight gain.

Interactions

  • Do not use it together with other medicines for the scalp, medicines that promote absorption through the skin (for example topical corticosteroids, retinoids, petrolatum, dithranol), or vasodilators (for example guanethidine, etc.).

payloads.title: Oral medicine (MFDS 201405340)
payloads.summary: This medicine is used to relieve various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, chills
payloads.content:
Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicineThis medicine is used to relieve various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, chills

Oral medicine (MFDS 201405340)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201405340. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used to relieve various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, chills, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to relieve various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, chills

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201405340. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults aged 15 years and over take 1 sachet (90 mL) per dose 3 times a day; children aged 11 years to under 15 years take 2/3 sachet (about 60 mL) per dose 3 times a day; children aged 7 years to under 11 years take 1/2 sachet (about 45 mL) per dose 3 times a day; children aged 3 years to under 7 years take 1/3 sachet (about 30 mL) per dose 3 times a day; children aged 2 years to under 3 years take 1/4 sachet (about 22.5 mL) per dose 3 times a day, in each case 30 minutes after a meal. If necessary it may be taken at bedtime, and as a rule the interval between doses is 4 hours.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported, and if a skin rash or another sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be taken by patients who have or have had hypersensitivity to this medicine, by people who have had an asthma attack after taking this medicine or its components, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold remedy, or by infants under 3 months of age and children under 2 years of age.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has or is suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, is a child under 2 years of age for whom it is strictly necessary, has a constitution prone to urticaria, contact dermatitis, bronchial asthma, allergic rhinitis, migraine or food allergy, is a patient who has had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine, has a liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, edema, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma or difficulty urinating, is elderly, is physically weak or has a high fever, has persistent or recurrent stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or a bleeding problem, is a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant or a breast-feeding woman, smokes, has asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, or has a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts for 1 week or more or recurs, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache.
  • Follow the prescribed directions and amounts.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Because drowsiness may appear after taking it, take care when driving or operating machinery.
  • If the symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, difficulty urinating, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor or insomnia appears, if urticaria, swelling and a feeling of tightness in the chest appear right after taking it together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing, or if mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms such as high fever together with rash, redness and blisters like a burn), asthma, hepatic impairment, interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing and fever), reduced urine volume, swelling of the face, hands and feet, heavy eyelids, stiffening of the hands, a rise in blood pressure, headache or myopathy (languor, cramp of the limbs, paralysis) appears, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilizers, antiparkinson drugs, etc.), antitussives and expectorants, other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, allergy medicines).
  • People who stopped MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilizers, antiparkinson drugs, etc.) within the past 2 weeks must not take this medicine.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with medicines for diabetes, medicines for gout, medicines for arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, potassium-containing preparations, licorice-containing preparations, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, etacrynic acid) or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide).
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

Oral medicine (MFDS 199803133)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 199803133. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis, chronic idiopathic urticaria, and pruritus, and for eczema and dermatitis when used together with a topical hydrocortisone preparation.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis, chronic idiopathic urticari

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 199803133. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults and children aged 6 years and over take 1 tablet (10 mg) once a day before bedtime, and patients who are sensitive to adverse reactions take 1/2 tablet (5 mg) in divided doses in the morning and in the evening. Increase or decrease the dose as appropriate according to age and symptoms. In patients with moderate to severe (severe symptoms) renal impairment the dosing interval must be adjusted according to the patient's renal function, and in child patients with renal impairment the dose must be adjusted individually taking into account the patient's renal clearance and body weight, so refer to the approved product information for details.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or to hydroxyzine or piperazine derivatives, patients with renal failure, children under 6 years of age, and patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, pregnant women, breastfeeding women, patients with renal impairment (kidney disorder) or hepatic impairment, elderly people, patients with epilepsy and patients at risk of seizures, and patients with predisposing factors for urinary retention (spinal cord lesions, benign prostatic hyperplasia, etc.) should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If drowsiness or headache; occasionally malaise, a sensation of numbness, asthenia, restlessness, or paresthesia; rarely mild and transient lassitude, fatigue, dizziness, a heavy feeling in the head, excitement, convulsions, dyskinesia, dystonia, fainting, tremor, aggression, confusion, depression, hallucinations, insomnia, tic disorder, amnesia, memory impairment, suicidal ideation, or nightmares; occasionally thirst, dryness of the lips, nausea, loss of appetite, gastric discomfort, indigestion, abdominal pain, stomach pain, abdominal discomfort, or diarrhea; rarely vomiting, gastrointestinal disorders, cheilitis, taste disturbance, or increased appetite; rarely tachycardia, arrhythmia, or a rise in blood pressure; occasionally palpitations or vasculitis; occasionally leukopenia, neutropenia, lymphocytosis, or eosinophilia; rarely monocytosis, an increase or decrease in platelets, or photosensitivity; rarely hypersensitivity and anaphylactic shock, urticaria, angioneurotic edema, fixed drug eruption, or acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis; rarely blurred vision, conjunctival congestion, disturbance of ocular accommodation, oculogyric crisis, vertigo, or hepatitis; occasionally elevated BUN, glycosuria, or blood-stained urine; rarely difficulty urinating, nocturnal enuresis, urinary retention, joint pain, muscle pain, pharyngitis, cough, nosebleed, bronchospasm, hearing abnormalities, or visual abnormalities; occasionally chest pain; or rarely menstrual irregularity, ringing in the ears, rhinitis, or weight gain occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.Itching, urticaria, and the like may occur after stopping this medicine.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with theophylline, ritonavir, or excessive alcohol while taking it.

This medicine is used for the sterilization and disinfection of torn wounds, burns and wounds, the sterilization and disinfection of ulcers and abscesses, the disinfection of infected skin surfaces, the sterilization and disinfection of surgical sites, and the disinfection of injection and catheter sites.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the sterilization and disinfection of torn wounds, burns and wounds, the sterilization and dis

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202302242. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area several times a day.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with thyroid dysfunction (especially nodular goiter, endemic goiter, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, etc.), patients with renal failure, newborns and infants under 6 months of age, patients with dermatitis herpetiformis, and patients before or after radioactive iodine treatment must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, seriously ill patients (such as burn patients), those with a history of thyroid disease, and those with a history of renal failure should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If it is used just before delivery, wash the newborn's eyes and bathe the baby as soon as possible after delivery, taking care that the medicine does not remain on the baby.
  • Do not use this medicine in the eyes or take it by mouth.
  • If the undiluted solution gets into the eyes, rinse it out.
  • Do not mix it with other preparations.
  • Soap weakens the germicidal action of this medicine, so wash it off thoroughly before use.
  • For details, please refer to the approved labeling.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms occur rarely (itching, swelling, heartburn, pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, flushing, urticaria, etc.), or iodine rash, or occasionally pain, itching, a stinging sensation, rash, redness, or dermatitis, or rarely a burning sensation, skin ulcer, contact dermatitis, or skin discoloration, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not use this medicine together with chlorhexidine, sulfadiazine and silver compounds, alkalis, preparations containing mercury, enzyme-based wound treatments, hydrogen peroxide, or lithium therapy.

How it works

This medicine is used to supply vitamins B1, B2 and B6 in cases of physical fatigue, pregnancy and lactation, and reduce

How to take it

Children aged 8 years and older or adults take 2 sachets at a time, and those aged 24 months and older but under 8 years take 1 sachet at a time, twice a day.Those aged 12 months and older but under 24 months take 1 sachet at a time, once a day.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and over and adults take 2 capsules at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. Those aged 8 years and over but under 15 years take 1 capsule at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

  • Patients hypersensitive to this medicine and those who have experienced it, those who have experienced asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold medicines, infants under 3 months of age, and people who are taking MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinson drugs, etc.) or are within 2 weeks of stopping them must not take this medicine.

Apply to the affected area (diseased site) 5 times a day at intervals of about 4 hours. Treatment should be continued for 5 days, and if the condition has not healed after 5 days of use, it may be used for a further 5 days.

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine, breastfeeding women, and children must not use this medicine.

  • Do not use this medicine for the purpose of preventing transmission to others or preventing recurrent herpes simplex (blister) infection.
  • Do not use this medicine as a base for diluting it or mixing it with other medicines.
  • Use this medicine for external use only.
  • Do not use it for the eyes on the cornea or mucous membranes.

  • Discomfort such as tenderness, a temporary burning sensation, mild pain including stinging pain, contact dermatitis, erythematous rash, eczema, allergic reactions, and occasionally irritation at the application site, itching, vulvitis, facial swelling, skin discoloration, urticaria, rash, vesicular rash, and peeling of the skin may occur.

At a glance

How it works

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202003405. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Children aged 6 months and over take 0.4 to 0.6 mL per kg of body weight per dose, at intervals of 4 to 6 hours when needed, and must not exceed 4 doses a day (28 mg/kg). For children weighing 30 kg or less, do not exceed 25 mL a day. When the body weight is known it is more appropriate to use the amount based on body weight, so refer to the approved product information for details.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic reactions, myocardial infarction and stroke, which may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcer and perforation may appear.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be taken by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, peptic ulcer, severe blood abnormality, liver impairment, renal impairment, cardiac insufficiency, high blood pressure or bronchial asthma or by those who have had them, by people who have had asthma, urticaria or an allergy in response to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, by patients being treated for pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass surgery, or by a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant or a breast-feeding woman.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user has or has had peptic ulcer, blood abnormality, a bleeding tendency, liver impairment, renal impairment, cardiac insufficiency, high blood pressure or hypersensitivity, is a patient with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, is elderly or a child, has stomach cancer, or is taking low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke, especially a patient with an autoimmune disease (SLE, MCTD).

Possible side effects

  • If any of the following appears, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: rarely shock (chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, fall in blood pressure, etc.); blood disorders such as aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, granulocytopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) and eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, or very rarely dry mouth, stomatitis, abdominal distension and constipation; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) or toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency; acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis; jaundice and increases in GOT, GPT and AL-P; induction of an asthma attack; urticaria, eczema, purpura, occasionally rash and itching; rarely visual disturbance such as blurred or dim vision, hearing loss, tinnitus and abnormal taste; aseptic meningitis, severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness; fall in blood pressure, rise in blood pressure and palpitations; acute renal failure, oliguria and hematuria together with proteinuria and increases in BUN and blood creatinine; hyperkalemia, reduced urine volume, generalized edema and the accompanying shortness of breath and languor; acute pulmonary edema; occasionally periorbital edema; and very rarely malaise, fever and nosebleed.

Interactions

  • Do not use it together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when using it together with glucocorticoids, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, sulfonylureas, diuretics, antihypertensive medicines, ACE inhibitors, furosemide, aspirin, lithium, methotrexate, or coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin).

This medicine is used to inhibit thrombus formation in myocardial infarction, cerebral infarction, and unstable angina, to inhibit thrombus formation after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG) or percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA), and to reduce cardiovascular risk in high-risk patients (patients with multiple risk factors such as a family history of ischemic heart disease, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, obesity, and diabetes).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to inhibit thrombus formation in myocardial infarction, cerebral infarction, and unstable angina,

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 199001012. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults take 1 capsule per dose, 1 time a day. Since this medicine is an enteric-coated capsule, it may be taken before meals with plenty of water.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or other salicylate preparations, patients with peptic ulcer, patients with aspirin-induced asthma (induction of asthma attacks by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, etc.) or those who have experienced it, patients with hemophilia, severe hepatic impairment, severe renal impairment, cardiac insufficiency, or a bleeding tendency, patients receiving concomitant methotrexate at a dose of 15 milligrams or more per week (15 mg/week), and pregnant women in the third trimester of pregnancy should not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with renal impairment, cardiovascular circulatory dysfunction, hepatic impairment, cardiac dysfunction, blood abnormalities, or bronchial asthma, patients about to undergo surgery, infants aged 3 years or younger, patients who have experienced hypersensitivity to analgesics, anti-inflammatory drugs, or antirheumatic drugs or other allergic diseases, elderly people, patients with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency, and patients with hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5 should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Take care not to damage the enteric coating of this medicine.
  • If you are to undergo surgery (including dental surgery), you must tell the doctor in charge that you are taking an aspirin preparation and receive advice.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (for example, difficulty breathing, generalized flushing, angioedema, urticaria), asthma attacks, erythema, itching, nasal congestion, cardiac and respiratory disorders, occasionally rash, swelling, urticaria, rhinitis symptoms, conjunctivitis, rarely toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), exfoliative dermatitis, rarely aplastic anemia, anemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), ringing in the ears, hearing loss, dizziness, headache, agitation, rarely liver disorder, very rarely temporary liver damage with elevated liver transaminases, kidney disorder, acute renal failure, hyperventilation, metabolic acidosis, excessive drop in body temperature, collapse, or coldness of the limbs occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Loss of appetite, heartburn, stomach pain, nausea, and vomiting may occur.

Interactions

  • Do not use it together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, salicylate preparations, or high-dose methotrexate.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with anticoagulants, thrombolytics or other platelet aggregation inhibitors, hemostatics, antidiabetic medicines (insulin preparations, tolbutamide, etc.), uricosuric agents (benzbromarone, probenecid), lithium preparations, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, digoxin, systemically acting adrenocortical hormone preparations (except hydrocortisone used as replacement therapy for Addison's disease), angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, valproic acid, or alkaline preparations (e.g. sodium bicarbonate, magnesium carbonate).
  • When taken together with alcohol, damage to the gastrointestinal mucosa may increase and bleeding time may be prolonged.

How it works

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201801818. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the applicator from its packaging and hold it with the sponge facing downwards. Do not touch the sponge part of the applicator. Squeeze the applicator firmly only once so that the ampoule breaks and the solution comes out, and leave the broken ampoule inside the applicator. For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

Precautions for use

  • People with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine, isopropanol, or Yellow No. 5 and infants aged 2 months or younger should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use this medicine for disinfecting surgical instruments, or on nervous tissue (e.g., brain or spinal cord tissue), the eyes, ears, mouth, mucous membranes, genital mucous membranes, open wounds, or torn or damaged skin, or for general washing of the skin.
  • Before using this medicine, people with hypersensitivity to other medicines, people who have experienced allergic diseases such as asthma or who have a family history of them, people with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, and people with a drug-hypersensitive constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only on intact skin.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get in, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty breathing, redness, a sudden drop in blood pressure, urticaria, angioedema, etc.), occasionally rash, photosensitization, irritation, sensitization, erythema or inflammation, itching, dry and thinly peeling skin, local pain at the application site, or local skin reactions, or very rarely rash (e.g., erythematous, papular, or maculopapular), blisters, small blisters at the application site, a burning sensation of the skin, dermatitis, eczema, chemical burns in newborns, eye irritation, congestion, impaired vision, or eye damage occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, peptic ulcer, severe blood disorders, severe liver disorder, severe kidney disorder, severe heart failure, severe high blood pressure, or bronchial asthma or a history of it, patients with or a history of asthma, urticaria, or allergy caused by aspirin or other anti-inflammatory analgesics, patients being treated for pain before or after coronary artery bypass surgery, and pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and nursing mothers must not take this medicine.

This medicine is used for diarrhea, for the adsorption of gas produced by abnormal fermentation in the digestive tract, and as an adsorbent for emergency detoxification in poisoning by drugs and chemicals. (However, medicinal charcoal does not adsorb cyanide, and it is relatively ineffective at adsorbing alcohol, aliphatic hydrocarbons, lithium salts, corrosive sodium chloride, heavy metals such as iron, lead, and lead cyanide, boric acid, other inorganic acids, and petroleum distillates.)

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for diarrhea, for the adsorption of gas produced by abnormal fermentation in the digestive tract,

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202302822. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Take 2 to 20 g of medicinal charcoal a day, divided into several doses. In acute poisoning, medicinal charcoal is administered within 30 minutes after ingestion of the poisonous substance. (When the amount of the ingested poisonous substance is known, the recommended dose of medicinal charcoal is usually 5-10 times the amount of the ingested poisonous substance.)
Increase or decrease the dose appropriately according to age and symptoms, following the instructions of a doctor.

Warning

  • Because it degrades the imaging of esophageal erosion, do not use it when a corrosive substance has been ingested.
  • Do not use it in patients with diabetes without a doctor's diagnosis and prescription.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine should be administered after gastric aspiration or gastric lavage has been completed with the involvement of a doctor.
  • Within 2 hours of administering medicinal charcoal, the charcoal adsorbs other medicines and so reduces their effect.
  • This medicine may turn the stools black.

Possible side effects

  • Be careful, as indigestion may occur and as the adsorption of vitamins, minerals and the like may cause nutritional disturbance.

Interactions

  • Ice cream and sherbet lower the adsorptive power of medicinal charcoal, so do not take them together with it.
  • When it is used as an antidote for oral poisoning, do not take it together with ipecac syrup.
  • The ipecac syrup may be adsorbed by the medicinal charcoal and so prevent vomiting.
  • If ipecac syrup and medicinal charcoal are used at the same time, it is recommended that the medicinal charcoal be given after vomiting has been induced and has finished.

How it works

This medicine is used for the relief of the various symptoms of the common cold (sore throat (pain in the throat), chill

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201900992. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and over and adults take 1 packet (a single dose) at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. The interval between doses should be 4 hours.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of a hypersensitivity reaction appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine, people who have experienced asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold medicines, infants (babies) under 3 months of age, and people who are taking MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.) or are within 2 weeks of having stopped them must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, infants and children under 15 years of age who have or are suspected of having a chickenpox or influenza infection, people with an allergic constitution, people who have experienced allergic symptoms (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.), people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, edema (swelling), gastroduodenal ulcer and the like, the elderly, people with a weak body or a high fever, people with persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach (upper abdominal) discomfort or stomach pain, or with ulcer or bleeding problems, women who are pregnant or may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, and children under 2 years of age should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If the following occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling (puffiness), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia; rarely shock symptoms (urticaria, swelling (puffiness), and chest tightness right after taking it, together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing); Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) (severe symptoms accompanied by high fever, with rash and redness (reddening of the skin) and blistering like burns appearing on the skin all over the body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes); asthma; liver function disorder (general lethargy, jaundice (the skin or the whites of the eyes turn yellow)); interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever); pseudoaldosteronism; or myopathy (muscle disease).

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with antitussives (which stop coughing) and expectorants (phlegm medicines), other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis (nasal inflammation), motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).
  • If it is taken together with diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, potassium-containing preparations, licorice-containing preparations, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, etacrynic acid), or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide), consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202302990. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and over and adults take 2 capsules at a time, and those over 7 years but under 15 years take 1 capsule at a time, three times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious and potentially fatal skin reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of hypersensitivity appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen.
  • If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking this medicine and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine or have experienced such hypersensitivity, people who have experienced asthma when taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics or cold medicines, infants under 3 months of age and children under 2 years of age, and patients with severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, children under 2 years of age when it is absolutely necessary, infants and children under 15 years of age who have or are suspected of having a chickenpox or influenza infection, people with an allergic constitution, women who are pregnant or may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, people in whom symptoms of ischemic colitis such as sudden abdominal pain or rectal bleeding appear in connection with the pseudoephedrine component, people who have experienced allergic symptoms caused by a medicine such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching, the elderly, and people with a weak body or a high fever should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Before taking this medicine, people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma or difficulty urinating, people with persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or with ulcer or bleeding problems, and people with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts more than 1 week or recurs, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever and rash or a persistent headache should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If symptoms do not improve after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Children should take it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Do not take it continuously over a long period.
  • Drowsiness may come on while you are taking it.
  • Avoid driving a car or operating machinery.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty urinating, (persistent or severe) thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, or insomnia occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If, rarely, shock (anaphylaxis) occurs, which may appear immediately after taking it as hives, swelling, and chest tightness together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing, or if skin-mucosa-eye syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, liver dysfunction such as general lethargy and jaundice, interstitial pneumonia, or symptoms of reversible posterior encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome such as sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, or visual disturbance occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take antitussives and expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives or oral medicines containing an antihistamine.
  • People who are taking an MAO inhibitor used for the treatment of depression, Parkinson's disease and the like, or who are within 2 weeks of stopping one, should not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who are being given a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid or the like should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Patients who are being given a barbiturate, a tricyclic antidepressant or alcohol should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

Oral medicine (MFDS 202302823)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202302823. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for diarrhea, for the adsorption of gas produced by abnormal fermentation in the digestive tract, and as an adsorbent for emergency detoxification in cases of poisoning by medicines and chemicals.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for diarrhea, for the adsorption of gas produced by abnormal fermentation in the digestive tract,

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202302823. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Take 2 to 20 g of medicinal charcoal in 1 day, divided into several doses. In acute poisoning, administer medicinal charcoal within 30 minutes after ingestion of the poisonous substance. When the amount of poisonous substance ingested is known, the recommended dose of medicinal charcoal is usually 5-10 times the amount of the ingested poisonous substance. Increase or decrease the amount appropriately according to age and symptoms as directed by a doctor.

Warning

  • Since this medicine impairs the imaging of esophageal erosion, do not take it if a corrosive substance has been ingested.
  • Do not use this medicine in patients with diabetes without a doctor's diagnosis and prescription.

Precautions for use

  • When this medicine is used as an antidote for oral poisoning, giving medicinal charcoal together with ipecac syrup is not recommended, because the ipecac syrup is adsorbed by the medicinal charcoal and vomiting is thereby prevented.
  • If ipecac syrup and medicinal charcoal are used together, it is recommended that the medicinal charcoal be given after vomiting has been induced and completed.
  • This medicine should be given after gastric aspiration or gastric lavage has been completed with the involvement of a doctor.
  • Within 2 hours of giving medicinal charcoal, the charcoal adsorbs other medicines and therefore reduces their effect.
  • This medicine may colour the stool black.

Possible side effects

  • Indigestion may occur.

Interactions

  • Ice cream and sherbet lower the adsorptive power of medicinal charcoal, so do not take them together with this medicine.

Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area (the diseased site) 1 to 2 times a day (in the morning, or in the morning and evening).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This drug is used for reducing fever when fever occurs due to acute upper respiratory tract infection.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201309080. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Children aged 6 months and over take 0.4 to 0.6 mL/kg (5 to 7 mg/kg) at a time at intervals of 4 to 6 hours as needed, and do not exceed a maximum of 4 doses a day (28 mg/kg). Children weighing 30 kg or less must not exceed a maximum of 25 mL (300 mg) a day. Refer to the approved labeling for the recommended single dose by age group.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious, potentially fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction, and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration, and perforation may occur.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with peptic ulcer, severe blood abnormalities, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency, or severe hypertension, those with bronchial asthma or who have experienced it, those who have experienced asthma, urticaria, or allergic reactions to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, patients being treated for pain before or after coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, newborns and infants under 6 months of age, and elderly people must not take this medicine.Before taking this medicine, those who have experienced peptic ulcer, those with blood abnormalities or who have experienced them, patients with a bleeding tendency, those with liver impairment or who have experienced it, those with kidney impairment or who have experienced it, patients with cardiac insufficiency or high blood pressure, those who have experienced hypersensitivity, patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), ulcerative colitis, or Crohn's disease, elderly people, children, and patients with gastric cancer should consult a doctor or pharmacist.Considering the importance of the drug treatment, either stop breastfeeding or stop the drug treatment.Dizziness or fatigue may occur after taking this medicine, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.When taking it long term for an acute condition, as a rule limit it to within 5 days.

Possible side effects

  • If the following occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: rarely, shock symptoms (chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, drop in blood pressure, etc.); blood disorders such as aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, granulocytopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), and eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) or toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); triggering of asthma attacks, urticaria, eczema, purpura; occasionally rash, itching, and visual disturbances such as blurred vision and scotoma; aseptic meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, stiff neck, fever, or impaired consciousness, etc.); acute renal failure, oliguria (decreased urination), hematuria, proteinuria, elevated BUN and blood creatinine, and hyperkalemia.
  • Occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, and stomach discomfort; very rarely thirst, stomatitis, abdominal bloating, and constipation; rarely jaundice, elevated GOT, GPT, and AL-P, hearing loss, tinnitus, taste disturbance, decreased blood pressure, increased blood pressure, palpitations, decreased urine volume, generalized edema with accompanying shortness of breath and lethargy; occasionally periorbital edema; and also very rarely malaise, fever, and nosebleed may occur.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics or high-dose methotrexate.
  • If you take it together with glucocorticoids, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, sulfonylureas, diuretics, antihypertensives, ACE inhibitors, furosemide, aspirin, lithium, low-dose methotrexate, or coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin), consult a doctor or pharmacist.

This medicine is used for the relief of the various symptoms of the common cold (headache, sore throat, chills, fever, j

Why this one

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults aged 15 years and older take 1 bottle 3 times a day; those aged 11 years and older but under 15 years take 2/3 bottle 3 times a day; those aged 7 years and older but under 11 years take 1/2 bottle 3 times a day; those aged 3 years and older but under 7 years take 1/3 bottle 3 times a day; and those aged 1 year and older but under 3 years take 1/4 bottle 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.If necessary, take it at bedtime, and as a rule leave an interval of 4 hours between doses.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.It may cause liver damage.Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of hypersensitivity appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).It may cause liver damage.Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolized to phenylalanine in the body, so patients with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their phenylalanine intake must not take it.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or a history of it, people who have had asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, and infants under 3 months of age must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist in the following cases: infants and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza; people with an allergic constitution; people who have had allergic reactions (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.); people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, edema, or gastroduodenal ulcer; elderly people; people who are physically weak or have a high fever; people with persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain, or with ulcers or bleeding problems; women who are pregnant or may be pregnant; breastfeeding women; and children under 2 years of age.
  • Follow the specified dosage and administration carefully.
  • When it is given to children, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, light-headedness, or, rarely, shock (urticaria, swelling, chest tightness, etc. together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweats, and difficulty breathing), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, listlessness of the whole body, jaundice (the skin or the whites of the eyes turning yellow), interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by coughing, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, and fever), pseudoaldosteronism (decreased urine volume, swelling of the face, hands and feet, heaviness of the eyelids, stiffening of the hands, a rise in blood pressure or headache, etc.), or myopathy (weakness, cramps in the limbs, paralysis, etc.) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take it together with antitussives and expectorants, other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines), or MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.).People receiving other medicines such as barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants and alcohol, potassium-containing preparations, licorice-containing preparations, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, etacrynic acid) or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide), antidiabetic medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, or steroids should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine.Do not drink alcohol while taking it.
