  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients under 18 years of age, patients with cardiovascular disease (coronary artery disease, arrhythmia, congestive heart failure, heart valve disease, treated or untreated high blood pressure, low blood pressure), hair loss without a genetic cause, sudden patchy hair loss, abnormalities of the scalp (erythema, inflammation, infection, irritation or pain, psoriasis, sunburn), hair loss of unknown cause, patients who have shaved the scalp, and patients with myocardial infarction or a history of it must not use this medicine.

  • Even if you forget to use this medicine, do not make up for the missed dose; simply apply the next dose as usual.
  • Use this medicine for external use only and do not use it on areas other than the scalp.
  • Do not use occlusive dressings.

How it works

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201801818. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the applicator from its packaging and hold it with the sponge facing downwards. Do not touch the sponge part of the applicator. Squeeze the applicator firmly only once so that the ampoule breaks and the solution comes out, and leave the broken ampoule inside the applicator. For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

Precautions for use

  • People with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine, isopropanol, or Yellow No. 5 and infants aged 2 months or younger should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use this medicine for disinfecting surgical instruments, or on nervous tissue (e.g., brain or spinal cord tissue), the eyes, ears, mouth, mucous membranes, genital mucous membranes, open wounds, or torn or damaged skin, or for general washing of the skin.
  • Before using this medicine, people with hypersensitivity to other medicines, people who have experienced allergic diseases such as asthma or who have a family history of them, people with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, and people with a drug-hypersensitive constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only on intact skin.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get in, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty breathing, redness, a sudden drop in blood pressure, urticaria, angioedema, etc.), occasionally rash, photosensitization, irritation, sensitization, erythema or inflammation, itching, dry and thinly peeling skin, local pain at the application site, or local skin reactions, or very rarely rash (e.g., erythematous, papular, or maculopapular), blisters, small blisters at the application site, a burning sensation of the skin, dermatitis, eczema, chemical burns in newborns, eye irritation, congestion, impaired vision, or eye damage occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

How it works

This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint diseas

Who should ask first

How to take it

For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout, and psoriatic arthritis, adults take 200-600 mg per dose, 3 to 4 times a day. Up to a maximum of 3,200 mg a day may be taken. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, take 30 to 40 mg per kg of body weight per dose, in 3 to 4 divided doses a day. For mild to moderate pain and for colds, adults take 200 to 400 mg per dose, 3 to 4 times a day. The dose may be increased or decreased as appropriate according to age and symptoms. For children, those aged 11 to 14 years take 200 to 250 mg (10 to 12.5 mL) per dose, those aged 7 to 10 years take 150 to 200 mg (7.5 to 10 mL) per dose, those aged 3 to 6 years take 100 to 150 mg (5 to 7.5 mL) per dose, and those aged 1 to 2 years take 50 to 100 mg (2.5 to 5 mL) per dose, 3 to 4 times a day, and it is advisable to avoid taking it on an empty stomach. For children, those aged 11 to 14 years may take up to 1,000 mg (50 mL) a day, those aged 7 to 10 years up to 800 mg (40 mL), those aged 3 to 6 years up to 600 mg (30 mL), and those aged 1 to 2 years up to 400 mg (20 mL).

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic reactions, myocardial infarction and stroke, which may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcer and perforation may appear.
  • Patients with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease must avoid taking high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day), and patients who have cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, smoking, etc.) and need to take high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, severe blood abnormalities, severe hepatic impairment, severe renal impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency, severe high blood pressure, or bronchial asthma, patients who have experienced asthma, urticaria, or allergic reactions caused by aspirin or other anti-inflammatory analgesics, patients with pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass surgery, pregnant women in the last 3 months of pregnancy, breastfeeding women, patients receiving high-dose methotrexate as cancer chemotherapy, and patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.
  • Do not take more than the recommended dose.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with blood abnormalities or a bleeding tendency, patients with liver cirrhosis, hepatic impairment, renal impairment, cardiac insufficiency, heart disease, high blood pressure, systemic lupus erythematosus, mixed connective tissue disease, ulcerative colitis, or Crohn's disease, elderly people, children under 2 years of age, pregnant women, and patients with chickenpox should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • When taking it for a cold, take it for no more than 5 days as a rule, and without the direction of a doctor or pharmacist do not take it for pain for 10 days or more (adults) or 5 days or more (children), and do not take it for fever for 3 days or more.

Possible side effects

  • If shock (difficulty breathing, fall in blood pressure, etc.), blood disorders such as decreased hematocrit, decreased hemoglobin, anemia, aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function or eosinophilia, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, vomiting of blood, Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, dry mouth, stomatitis, abdominal distension, oral ulcers, constipation, black stools, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms of unknown frequency, angioneurotic edema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash, exfoliative dermatitis, acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, hepatitis, jaundice, abnormal liver function, liver disorder, hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reaction, asthma attack, urticaria, eczema, purple spots, visual disturbance, deafness, ringing in the ears, taste abnormality, vertigo, drowsiness, dizziness, depression, headache, cerebrovascular accident or nervousness, aseptic meningitis or meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or impaired consciousness), acute renal failure, decreased urination, hematuria, proteinuria, elevated BUN or blood creatinine, hyperkalemia, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, decreased urine volume, generalized edema and the accompanying shortness of breath or listlessness, Kounis syndrome of unknown frequency, swelling around the eyes, facial swelling, malaise, fever, nosebleed, swelling or peripheral edema appear, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Patients receiving high-dose methotrexate as cancer chemotherapy should not take this medicine, and do not take this medicine together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics.
  • Before taking this medicine, people taking low-dose aspirin or ACE inhibitors and patients taking lithium, furosemide and thiazide diuretics, low-dose methotrexate, coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin), or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Those 15 years and older take 1 sachet (5 g) at a time, those 11 years and older but under 15 years take 2/3 sachet at a time, and those 7 years and older but under 11 years take 1/2 sachet at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals, dissolved in water.   • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.

  • It may cause liver damage.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine and those who have experienced it, people who have had asthma when taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics, or cold remedies, and infants under 3 months of age must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist in the following cases: infants and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza; people with an allergic constitution; people who have had allergic reactions (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.); patients with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), or difficulty urinating; people who are physically weak or have a high fever; people with stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain, or with ulcers or bleeding problems; patients with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough lasting 1 week or longer or recurring, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever and rash or a persistent headache; patients with hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4 or tartrazine or people who have experienced allergic reactions to them; and children under 2 years of age.

  • If rash, redness, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, difficulty urinating, thirst (persistent or severe), light-headedness, high anion gap metabolic acidosis, or, rarely, shock symptoms (urticaria, swelling, chest tightness, etc. immediately after taking it, together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweats, and difficulty breathing), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms accompanied by high fever, in which rash and redness and blisters like burns appear on the skin of the whole body or on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), asthma, listlessness of the whole body, jaundice, or interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by coughing, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, and fever) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.), antitussive expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).

Oral medicine (MFDS 202300723)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202300723. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used as supportive therapy for symptoms of mental and physical asthenia and as supportive therapy during the recovery period (a state of amino acid deficiency).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used as supportive therapy for symptoms of mental and physical asthenia and as supportive therapy durin

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202300723. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adolescents aged 12 years and over and adults take 5 g once a day as L-aspartic acid-L-arginine.
It is better to take it in the morning, but it can also be taken before bedtime. It can be taken with a small amount of water.

Warning

  • Because this medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolized to phenylalanine in the body, patients with phenylketonuria who need to restrict phenylalanine intake should not take it.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be taken by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, by patients with severe renal dysfunction or hepatic dysfunction, or by patients who have had myocardial infarction.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user has a problem with urinary retention (urine collecting in the bladder), is a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant or a breast-feeding woman, is taking it continuously for 15 days or more, or has had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to caramel.
  • Follow the prescribed directions and amounts.

Possible side effects

  • If an allergic reaction appears, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take it together with an antipsychotic and a sleeping pill.
  • They may increase the hypnotic effect.

payloads.content:

Oral medicine (MFDS 202400148)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202400148. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used to prevent and relieve dizziness, vomiting, and headache caused by motion sickness.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to prevent and relieve dizziness, vomiting, and headache caused by motion sickness.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202400148. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and over take 12 mL (2 sachets) at a time, those aged 11 years and over but under 15 years take 8 mL (1⅓ sachets) at a time, those aged 7 years and over but under 11 years take 6 mL (1 sachet) at a time, and those aged 3 years and over but under 7 years take 4 mL (⅔ of a sachet) at a time. To prevent motion sickness, take a single dose 30 minutes before boarding. If an additional dose is needed, take a single dose after allowing an interval of at least 4 hours, and limit the number of doses a day to 3 times.

Precautions for use

  • Breastfeeding women and infants and young children under 3 years of age must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who have experienced allergic symptoms (rash, reddening of the skin, itching, etc.), women who are pregnant or may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, patients with glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), patients with urination disorders, and patients suffering from respiratory diseases such as emphysema or chronic bronchitis should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.
  • If you divide 1 sachet and use the remainder later, seal the opening well for storage and use it within 2 days.
  • Follow the specified dosage and administration carefully.
  • When it is given to children, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Possible side effects

  • If rash, congested and reddened skin, itching, palpitations, or thirst occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with other antiemetics, cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, antihistamines, sedatives, or antitussives and expectorants.
  • Do not drink alcoholic beverages.

At a glance

How it works

This medicine is used for the eczema and dermatitis group, itching of the skin, and insect bites.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200707403. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Shake well to mix before use, then apply an appropriate amount to the affected area (the diseased site) 1 to 3 times a day, increasing or decreasing the amount appropriately according to symptoms.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine, patients with skin infections (tuberculosis, syphilis, candidiasis, tinea, herpes zoster, herpes simplex, chickenpox, vaccinia, scabies, pubic lice), eczematous otitis externa with a perforated eardrum, ulcers (excluding Behcet's disease), deep second-degree or worse burns and frostbite, perioral dermatitis, acne vulgaris or rosacea, and infants under 2 years of age must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, women who are pregnant or may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, infants, children and the elderly should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not use it in the eyes.
  • Do not use it for purposes other than treatment, such as after applying makeup or shaving.
  • Do not use an occlusive dressing without a doctor's supervision.
  • Limit the treatment period with this medicine to 7 days or less.

Possible side effects

  • If impetigo contagiosa, folliculitis, candidiasis, tinea, folliculitis, boils, skin irritation, stabbing pain (a pricking pain), fever, a burning sensation, rash, redness (turning red from congestion), flushing, itching, dry skin, pustular (pus-blister) dermatitis, allergic contact dermatitis, heat rash, worsening of wounds, bedsores, pustulosis (pus blisters), or, when used on the skin of the eyelids, increased intraocular pressure or glaucoma (blurred vision, visual impairment) occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Because of systemic absorption, reversible suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, Cushing's syndrome, hyperglycemia, diabetes and visual impairment, and blurred vision of unknown frequency may occur.

This medicine is used for the analgesic and anti-inflammatory treatment of stiff shoulders, low back pain, neuralgia, rheumatism, bruises, sprains, muscle pain and joint pain.

At a glance

Category

How it works

This medicine is used for the analgesic and anti-inflammatory treatment of stiff shoulders, low back pain, neuralgia, rh

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200501321. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Attach it to the affected area 1 to 2 times a day.

Precautions for use

  • Do not use it on infants aged 30 months or under, around the eyes, on eczema, on dermatitis caused by lacquer, on wounded areas, or on mucous membranes.
  • Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have experienced allergic symptoms caused by a medicine or cosmetic (for example rash, redness, itching, dermatitis caused by lacquer), if you have an allergic constitution, if you have severe skin maceration or moisture retention, or if the user is a child, a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant, or a breast-feeding woman.
  • When using it for a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Clean the affected area, wipe off sweat well, and then attach it.
  • Do not warm the attached area with a heater or an electric blanket.
  • Bathing while it is attached causes strong irritation, so remove it 30 minutes to 1 hour before bathing.
  • Also, do not attach it immediately after bathing.
  • If the symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 days of use, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use this medicine externally only.
  • Follow the prescribed directions and amounts.
  • Because symptoms of poisoning may appear if a large amount is absorbed through the skin, avoid long-term use over a wide surface.

Possible side effects

  • If rash, redness with congestion, itching or pain appears, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202106502. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use the eye drops

Instill 1 to 2 drops at a time, 4 to 5 times a day. After instillation, discard the remaining solution and the container.

Precautions for use

  • Before using this medicine, patients with severe eye pain, people who have previously had allergic symptoms from eye drops (redness of the eye, itching, swelling, rash, congested and reddened skin), and patients with glaucoma should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration exactly.
  • When using it in a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Use this medicine for instillation into the eye only.
  • After opening, use it immediately and only once, and be sure to discard the remaining solution and the container.
  • Do not use it if it has become cloudy (turbid).
  • To prevent contamination, avoid sharing it with others as far as possible.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 2 weeks of use, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If redness of the eye, itching, or swelling (puffiness) occurs, if a person wearing hard contact lenses has a large amount of discharge such as eye mucus with rare clouding of the lens, or if blurred vision does not improve, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

This medicine is used for cough, phlegm, and hoarseness of the throat, pain and swelling of the throat, and throat discomfort caused by inflammation of the throat.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for cough, phlegm, and hoarseness of the throat, pain and swelling of the throat, and throat disco

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200101057. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults and adolescents aged 15 years and older take 1 sachet as 1 dose, those aged 11 years or older and under 15 years take 2/3 of a sachet as 1 dose, those aged 7 years or older and under 11 years take 1/2 of a sachet as 1 dose, and those aged 3 years or older and under 7 years take 1/3 of a sachet as 1 dose, 3 to 6 times a day without water. The interval between doses should be 2 hours or more.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, people who are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian drugs, etc.) or who stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks, children under 3 years of age, and patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine (applies to the mint flavor).
  • Before taking this medicine, people with an allergic constitution, people who have experienced allergic symptoms from medicines (e.g., fever, rash, joint pain, itching, etc.), patients with diseases such as liver disease, kidney disease, thyroid disease, or diabetes, patients with a high fever, frail people, patients with heart disease and high blood pressure, elderly people, breastfeeding women, patients with edema (swelling), patients with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, or emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts 1 week or more or recurs, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash, or persistent headache, and people who have experienced hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 5 (applies to the mint flavor and the mint coffee flavor) should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration exactly.
  • When giving it to a child, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Possible side effects

  • If rash, redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, decreased urine volume, swelling of the face and limbs, heaviness of the eyelids, stiffening of the hands, increased blood pressure, headache, weakness, cramps in the limbs, or paralysis occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take together with other antitussives and expectorants, cold remedies, antihistamines, sedatives, or alcohol.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you use it together with potassium-containing preparations, licorice-containing preparations, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, etacrynic acid), or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide).
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

This medicine is used for dryness of the eye and eye fatigue accompanied by discomfort, stabbing pain, or irritation caused by wind, smoke, pollution, dust, dry heat, air conditioning, air travel, prolonged computer use, and the like.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Eye drops

How it works

This medicine is used for dryness of the eye and eye fatigue accompanied by discomfort, stabbing pain, or irritation cau

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202202835. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use the eye drops

When needed, instill 1 drop at a time into each eye, several times a day. To do this, gently pull the lower eyelid down and, while looking upward, put one drop into the lower conjunctival sac.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, people with severe eye pain, patients with glaucoma, and people who have experienced allergic symptoms from eye drops such as redness of the eye, itching, swelling, or rash should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use this medicine only as eye drops, that is, a medicine put into the eye.
  • After opening, use it only once; after instilling it into the eye, discard the remaining solution and the container.
  • If symptoms worsen or last 3 days or longer, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Wash your hands thoroughly before use.
  • When using it for the first time, discard 1 to 2 drops without putting them into the eye, in order to remove any container fragments that may be produced when opening it.
  • Do not let the tip of the container touch the eyelid or eyelashes.
  • If it does, the solution may become contaminated or cloudy from eye mucus, mold, or the like.
  • Also, do not use the medicine if it has become cloudy.
  • To prevent contamination, do not share it with others.
  • This medicine can be used even while wearing contact lenses.
  • Follow the specified dosage and administration carefully.

Possible side effects

  • If eye irritation rarely appears, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • If using this medicine at the same time as other eye drops, use the other eye drops first and use this medicine about 10 minutes later.

Oral medicine (MFDS 202005623)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202005623. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for fever and pain caused by colds, headache, neuralgia, muscle pain, menstrual pain, sprain pain, toothache, joint pain, and rheumatic pain.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for fever and pain caused by colds, headache, neuralgia, muscle pain, menstrual pain, sprain pain,

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202005623. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Children aged 7 to 12 years take the recommended single dose directly on the tongue without water, every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Take this medicine at the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible period, and do not take it more than 5 times a day (75 mg/kg). If the body weight is known, it is more appropriate to take a dose based on body weight (10 to 15 mg/kg). For the doses by age group, refer to the approved product information.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of a hypersensitivity reaction appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, peptic ulcer, severe blood abnormalities, severe liver disorder, severe kidney disorder, or severe cardiac dysfunction, and patients with aspirin-induced asthma (asthma attacks triggered by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory agents) or a history of it must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with liver disorder or a history of it, patients with kidney disorder or a history of it, people who have had peptic ulcer, patients with blood abnormalities or a history of them, patients with a bleeding tendency, cardiac dysfunction, or a history of hypersensitivity, patients with bronchial asthma, elderly people (the aged), children under 2 years of age, pregnant or breastfeeding women, and patients with low glutathione reserves should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Without the direction of a doctor or pharmacist, do not take it for pain for more than 10 days (adults) or more than 5 days (children), and do not take it for fever for more than 3 days.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (difficulty breathing, reddening of the whole body, angioedema, urticaria, etc.), asthma attacks, thrombocytopenia, granulocytopenia, hemolytic (red blood cell-destroying) anemia, methemoglobinemia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), cyanosis, hypersensitivity symptoms (facial swelling, difficulty breathing, sweating, low blood pressure, shock), nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, gastrointestinal problems with long-term use such as gastrointestinal bleeding, peptic ulcer, and perforation (a hole), rash, allergic reactions, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), elevated AST, elevated ALT, or fixed drug eruption occurs, or if pain or fever persists or worsens, or if new symptoms appear, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol or other anti-inflammatory analgesics.
  • If you take it together with warfarin or flucloxacillin, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

How to take it

People aged 15 years and over and adults take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times a day, within 30 minutes after a meal.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported, and if a skin rash or another sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

  • Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.
  • If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis appears, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be taken by patients who have or have had hypersensitivity to this medicine, by people who have had an asthma attack after taking this medicine, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold remedy, by children under 2 years of age and infants under 3 months of age, or by patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

  • If the symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed directions and amounts.
  • When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Because drowsiness may appear after taking it, take care when driving or operating machinery.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, difficulty urinating, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia or high anion gap metabolic acidosis appears, if symptoms of shock rarely appear (urticaria, swelling and a feeling of tightness in the chest right after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), or if asthma, generalized languor, jaundice, interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever, etc.), pseudoaldosteronism (reduced urine volume, swelling of the face, hands and feet, heavy eyelids, stiffening of the hands, a rise in blood pressure or headache, etc.) or myopathy (languor, cramp of the limbs, paralysis) appears, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Do not take it together with antitussives (medicines that stop coughing) and expectorants (phlegm medicines), other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, oral medicines containing an antihistamine (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, allergy medicines), or flucloxacillin.
  • People who are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinson drugs, etc.) or who are within 2 weeks of stopping one should not take this medicine.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with a barbiturate, a tricyclic antidepressant, alcohol, a potassium-containing preparation, a licorice-containing preparation, a preparation containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, a loop diuretic (furosemide, ethacrynic acid) or a thiazide diuretic (trichlormethiazide).
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

Children aged 12 years and under take the recommended single dose for their age group and body weight every 4 to 6 hours as needed.   • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.

Precautions for use

  • Patients hypersensitive to this medicine, patients with peptic ulcer, severe blood abnormalities, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, or severe cardiac dysfunction, and patients with or with a history of aspirin-induced asthma (asthma attacks induced by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs) must not take this medicine.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with other anti-inflammatory analgesics, other products containing acetaminophen, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, or alcohol.

At a glance

Category

How it works

This medicine is used for disinfection of the patient's skin before surgery or before insertion of a syringe needle or a

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201801818. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the applicator from its packaging and hold it with the sponge facing downwards. Do not touch the sponge part of the applicator. Squeeze the applicator firmly only once so that the ampoule breaks and the solution comes out, and leave the broken ampoule inside the applicator. For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

Precautions for use

  • People with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine, isopropanol, or Yellow No. 5 and infants aged 2 months or younger should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use this medicine for disinfecting surgical instruments, or on nervous tissue (e.g., brain or spinal cord tissue), the eyes, ears, mouth, mucous membranes, genital mucous membranes, open wounds, or torn or damaged skin, or for general washing of the skin.
  • Before using this medicine, people with hypersensitivity to other medicines, people who have experienced allergic diseases such as asthma or who have a family history of them, people with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, and people with a drug-hypersensitive constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only on intact skin.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get in, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty breathing, redness, a sudden drop in blood pressure, urticaria, angioedema, etc.), occasionally rash, photosensitization, irritation, sensitization, erythema or inflammation, itching, dry and thinly peeling skin, local pain at the application site, or local skin reactions, or very rarely rash (e.g., erythematous, papular, or maculopapular), blisters, small blisters at the application site, a burning sensation of the skin, dermatitis, eczema, chemical burns in newborns, eye irritation, congestion, impaired vision, or eye damage occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

How it works

Why this one

Who should ask first

How to take it

Children aged 6 months and over take 0.4 to 0.6 mL/kg (5 to 7 mg/kg) at a time at intervals of 4 to 6 hours as needed, and do not exceed a maximum of 4 doses a day (28 mg/kg). Children weighing 30 kg or less must not exceed a maximum of 25 mL (300 mg) a day. Refer to the approved labeling for the recommended single dose by age group.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious, potentially fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction, and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration, and perforation may occur.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with peptic ulcer, severe blood abnormalities, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency, or severe hypertension, those with bronchial asthma or who have experienced it, those who have experienced asthma, urticaria, or allergic reactions to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, patients being treated for pain before or after coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, newborns and infants under 6 months of age, and elderly people must not take this medicine.Before taking this medicine, those who have experienced peptic ulcer, those with blood abnormalities or who have experienced them, patients with a bleeding tendency, those with liver impairment or who have experienced it, those with kidney impairment or who have experienced it, patients with cardiac insufficiency or high blood pressure, those who have experienced hypersensitivity, patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), ulcerative colitis, or Crohn's disease, elderly people, children, and patients with gastric cancer should consult a doctor or pharmacist.Considering the importance of the drug treatment, either stop breastfeeding or stop the drug treatment.Dizziness or fatigue may occur after taking this medicine, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.When taking it long term for an acute condition, as a rule limit it to within 5 days.

Possible side effects

  • If the following occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: rarely, shock symptoms (chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, drop in blood pressure, etc.); blood disorders such as aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, granulocytopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), and eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) or toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); triggering of asthma attacks, urticaria, eczema, purpura; occasionally rash, itching, and visual disturbances such as blurred vision and scotoma; aseptic meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, stiff neck, fever, or impaired consciousness, etc.); acute renal failure, oliguria (decreased urination), hematuria, proteinuria, elevated BUN and blood creatinine, and hyperkalemia.
  • Occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, and stomach discomfort; very rarely thirst, stomatitis, abdominal bloating, and constipation; rarely jaundice, elevated GOT, GPT, and AL-P, hearing loss, tinnitus, taste disturbance, decreased blood pressure, increased blood pressure, palpitations, decreased urine volume, generalized edema with accompanying shortness of breath and lethargy; occasionally periorbital edema; and also very rarely malaise, fever, and nosebleed may occur.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics or high-dose methotrexate.
  • If you take it together with glucocorticoids, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, sulfonylureas, diuretics, antihypertensives, ACE inhibitors, furosemide, aspirin, lithium, low-dose methotrexate, or coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin), consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • This medicine is for external use only; do not use it on areas other than the scalp.
  • Do not use occlusive dressing.
  • Use of this medicine may cause burning and irritation of the eyes, so be careful that it does not get into the eyes, and if it comes into contact with sensitive areas such as the eyes, broken skin, or mucous membranes, rinse them immediately with clean water.
  • Wash your hands thoroughly after using this medicine.
  • Use hair styling products after this medicine has dried, and when using it in the evening, apply it 2 to 4 hours before bedtime so that it can dry.
  • Because circulation of air over the scalp may reduce the effect of this medicine, do not use a hair dryer to speed up its drying.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after 4 months or more of use, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • If itching, scaling, erythema, redness, dermatitis, dry skin, hypertrichosis in areas other than where this medicine was applied (facial hair growth in women), folliculitis, local irritation including burning sensation and skin eruption, peeling, hair loss, skin abscess, acne, nail disorder, seborrhea, eczema, hair abnormalities, occasionally diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, chest pain, changes in blood pressure, changes in pulse, palpitations, increased heart rate, pericardial effusion, pericarditis, embolism, tachycardia, worsening of pre-existing angina or induction of angina in patients with undiagnosed coronary artery disease, bronchitis, upper respiratory tract infection, sinusitis, difficulty breathing, shortness of breath, fracture, back pain, tendinitis, pain, neuritis (such as polyneuritis), weakness, dizziness, headache, feeling dazed, fainting, hepatitis, edema, kidney stones, inflammation and fluid retention, fever, urticaria, allergic rhinitis, generalized erythema and facial swelling, chills, eye irritation, bitter taste, otitis (especially otitis externa), taste changes, visual impairment, erectile dysfunction, stabbing pain, or sudden unexplained weight gain occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not use it together with other scalp medicines, topical corticoids, retinoids, petrolatum, dithranol, medicines known to promote percutaneous absorption, or vasodilators such as guanethidine.

This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis (occurring at a young age), osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), fever and pain caused by colds, back pain, dysmenorrhea, pain after surgery, ankylosing spondylitis, headache, toothache, muscle pain, neuralgia, acute gout, psoriatic arthritis, soft tissue injury (sprains, contusions), and non-articular rheumatic disease (tendinitis, tenosynovitis, bursitis).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis (occurring at a young age), osteoarthritis

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201904193. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout, and psoriatic arthritis, adults take 200 to 600 mg at a time, 3 to 4 times a day, up to a maximum of 3200 mg per day. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, take 30 to 40 mg per kg of body weight per day, divided into 3 to 4 doses. For mild to moderate pain and colds, adults take 200 to 400 mg at a time, children aged 11 to 14 years take 200 to 250 mg (10 to 13 mL) at a time, children aged 7 to 10 years take 150 to 200 mg (8 to 10 mL) at a time, children aged 3 to 6 years take 100 to 150 mg (5 to 8 mL) at a time, and children aged 1 to 2 years take 50 to 100 mg (3 to 5 mL) at a time, 3 to 4 times a day. For children weighing less than 30 kg, the daily dose must not exceed 500 mg (25 mL), and it is preferable to avoid taking it on an empty stomach.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic reactions, myocardial infarction and stroke, which may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcer and perforation may appear.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with gastrointestinal ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding or a history of it, patients with severe blood disorders, severe liver disorder, severe kidney disorder, severe cardiac insufficiency, severe high blood pressure or bronchial asthma or a history of it, patients with hypersensitivity such as asthma, urticaria or allergic reactions to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics (including COX-2 inhibitors) or a history of it, patients with pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG), pregnant women in the last 3 months of pregnancy, and patients receiving high-dose methotrexate as anticancer therapy must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with blood disorders or a history of them, patients with a tendency to bleed, patients with liver cirrhosis, liver disorder or a history of it, patients with kidney disorder or a history of it, patients with cardiac insufficiency or heart disease, high blood pressure, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, elderly people and children, pregnant women, and breastfeeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.

Possible side effects

  • If any of the following occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: shock symptoms (chest distress (heartburn), chills, difficulty breathing, a drop in blood pressure, etc.); blood disorders such as decreased hematocrit, decreased hemoglobin, anemia, aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), and eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, hematemesis (vomiting of blood), Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, thirst, stomatitis, abdominal bloating, mouth ulcers, constipation, black stools; skin-mucosa-eye syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), photosensitivity reactions, drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome), angioneurotic edema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash; hepatitis, jaundice, abnormal liver function such as elevated GOT, GPT and ALP, liver disorder; hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reactions, asthma attacks, hives, eczema, purpura (purple spots), rash, itching, asthma, bronchoconstriction, difficulty breathing or wheezing; visual disturbances such as scotoma (an area of vision loss), hearing loss (deafness), ringing in the ears, taste disturbance, vertigo, drowsiness, dizziness, depression, headache, cerebrovascular accident or nervousness, aseptic meningitis or meningitis (symptoms such as severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, stiff neck, fever, or disturbance of consciousness); a drop in blood pressure, a rise in blood pressure, palpitations (pounding heart), heart failure, myocardial infarction or angina; acute renal failure, oliguria (decreased urination), blood in the urine, protein in the urine, elevated BUN and blood creatinine, hyperkalemia, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, decreased urine volume, generalized edema and the accompanying shortness of breath, lethargy, periorbital edema (swelling around the eyes), facial edema (swelling of the face), malaise, fever, nosebleed, swelling, and peripheral edema.

Interactions

  • Do not take it together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics or with high-dose methotrexate used in cancer chemotherapy.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with low-dose aspirin, ACE inhibitors, lithium, furosemide and thiazide diuretics, low-dose methotrexate, coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin), or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors.

How to take it

Adults usually take 4 tablets at a time, 3 times a day, before meals or between meals.

Precautions for use

  • People who have hypersensitivity to the soybean oil in this medicine or who have experienced allergic reactions to it, patients with hypersensitivity to soybeans or peanuts, women who are pregnant or may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, and patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption must not take this medicine.

  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it for about 1 month (1 week when taking it for constipation), stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the specified dosage and administration carefully.

Possible side effects

  • If pseudoaldosteronism (a decrease in urine volume, swelling of the face, hands and feet, heaviness of the eyelids, stiffening of the hands, a rise in blood pressure, headache, etc.), myopathy (weakness, cramps in the limbs, paralysis), loss of appetite, stomach discomfort, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea, rash and redness, itching, insomnia, excessive sweating, a rapid pulse, frequent urination, palpitations, generalized weakness, mental excitement, urinary difficulty, or liver function disorder accompanied by elevated AST, ALT, ALP or -GTP (generalized listlessness, jaundice (the skin or the whites of the eyes turning yellow)) occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Do not take this medicine together with other laxatives.
  • When taking it in combination with other herbal (crude drug) preparations, take care not to duplicate the crude drugs they contain.

Instill 1 drop per dose into each eye several times a day as needed. Instill it into the lower conjunctival sac while gently pulling the lower eyelid down and looking upward.

How it works

This medicine is used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, co

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202203513. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and older take 15 mL per dose, those aged 11 years to under 15 years take 10 mL, those aged 7 years to under 11 years take 7.5 mL, those aged 3 years to under 7 years take 5 mL, and those aged 2 years to under 3 years take 3.75 mL, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals and, if necessary, at bedtime. As a rule, keep the interval between doses at 4 hours.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of a hypersensitivity reaction appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.
  • If severe skin adverse reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis occur, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Precautions for use

  • Those with hypersensitivity to this medicine or a history of it, people who have had asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold medicines, infants (newborns) under 3 months of age, and people who are taking MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian drugs, etc.) or are within 2 weeks of stopping them must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have an allergic constitution, have experienced drug allergy (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.), are an infant or young child aged 3 months or older and under 2 years, are an infant or a child under 15 years of age who is infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, have liver, kidney, heart, or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), or difficulty urinating (passing urine), are elderly, are physically weak or have a high fever, have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain, or have ulcer or bleeding problems, are pregnant or may be pregnant, are a nursing mother, or have symptoms such as smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or longer, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash, or persistent headache.
  • If symptoms do not improve after taking it 5 to 6 times, consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • When giving it to children, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

Possible side effects

  • If symptoms of ischemic colitis related to the pseudoephedrine component (acute abdominal pain, intestinal bleeding, etc.), rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty urinating (passing urine), persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, rarely shock symptoms (urticaria, swelling, and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweats, and difficulty breathing), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome: severe symptoms with high fever, rash and redness, and burn-like blisters), asthma, general listlessness, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes), or interstitial pneumonia (with cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever, etc.) occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian drugs, etc.), antitussives and expectorants (cough and phlegm medicines), other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis [nasal inflammation], motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).
  • People who are receiving other drugs such as barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants and alcohol, diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, or steroids should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

payloads.summary: This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, fever and pain due to a c

Oral medicine (MFDS 198601920)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 198601920. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, fever and pain due to a cold, low back pain, dysmenorrhea, postoperative pain and ankylosing spondylitis, headache, toothache, muscle pain, neuralgia, acute gout, psoriatic arthritis, soft tissue injuries (sprains, contusions), and non-articular rheumatic diseases (tendinitis, tenosynovitis, bursitis).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, fever and pain due to a c

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 198601920. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout and psoriatic arthritis, adults take 200-600 mg at a time, 3-4 times a day. Up to a maximum of 3,200 mg a day may be administered. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, take 30-40 mg per kg of body weight at a time, 3 to 4 times a day. For mild to moderate pain and colds, adults take 200-400 mg at a time, 3 to 4 times a day. The dose may be increased or decreased as appropriate according to age and symptoms. In children, those aged 11 to 14 years take 200-250 mg (10 to 12.5 ml), those aged 7 to 10 years take 150 to 200 mg (7.5 to 10 ml), those aged 3 to 6 years take 100 to 150 mg (5 to 7.5 ml), and those aged 1 to 2 years take 50 to 100 mg (2.5 to 5 ml) at a time, 3 to 4 times a day.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic reactions, myocardial infarction and stroke, which may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcer and perforation may appear.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, gastrointestinal ulcers, gastrointestinal bleeding or a history of it, severe blood abnormalities, liver disorder, kidney disorder, cardiac insufficiency, high blood pressure, or bronchial asthma or a history of it, people who have experienced asthma, urticaria, or allergic reactions to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics (including COX-2 inhibitors), patients with pain occurring before or after coronary artery (heart artery) bypass surgery (CABG), pregnant women in the last 3 months of pregnancy, patients receiving high-dose methotrexate as chemotherapy, and patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with blood abnormalities or a history of them, a bleeding tendency, cirrhosis, liver disorder or a history of it, kidney disorder or a history of it, cardiac insufficiency or heart disease, high blood pressure, or a history of hypersensitivity, patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and patients with mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), patients with ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease, or chickenpox, elderly people, children under 2 years of age, pregnant women, and breastfeeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the specified dosage and administration carefully.
  • Take care when driving or operating machinery after taking it.
  • Without the direction of a doctor or pharmacist, do not take it for pain for more than 10 days (adults) or more than 5 days (children), and do not take it for fever for more than 3 days.

Possible side effects

  • If the following occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: shock symptoms (difficulty breathing, drop in blood pressure, etc.); blood disorders such as decreased hematocrit and hemoglobin, anemia, aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, agranulocytosis, decreased granulocytes, white blood cells, and platelets, reduced platelet function, and increased eosinophils; How it works

This medicine is used for disinfection of the patient's skin before surgery or before insertion of a syringe needle or a

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201801818. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the applicator from its packaging and hold it with the sponge facing downwards. Do not touch the sponge part of the applicator. Squeeze the applicator firmly only once so that the ampoule breaks and the solution comes out, and leave the broken ampoule inside the applicator. For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

Precautions for use

  • People with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine, isopropanol, or Yellow No. 5 and infants aged 2 months or younger should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use this medicine for disinfecting surgical instruments, or on nervous tissue (e.g., brain or spinal cord tissue), the eyes, ears, mouth, mucous membranes, genital mucous membranes, open wounds, or torn or damaged skin, or for general washing of the skin.
  • Before using this medicine, people with hypersensitivity to other medicines, people who have experienced allergic diseases such as asthma or who have a family history of them, people with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, and people with a drug-hypersensitive constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only on intact skin.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get in, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty breathing, redness, a sudden drop in blood pressure, urticaria, angioedema, etc.), occasionally rash, photosensitization, irritation, sensitization, erythema or inflammation, itching, dry and thinly peeling skin, local pain at the application site, or local skin reactions, or very rarely rash (e.g., erythematous, papular, or maculopapular), blisters, small blisters at the application site, a burning sensation of the skin, dermatitis, eczema, chemical burns in newborns, eye irritation, congestion, impaired vision, or eye damage occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age for whom it is strictly necessary, is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has or is suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, develops symptoms of ischemic colitis related to the pseudoephedrine component (for example sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, etc.), has an allergic constitution, has experienced allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.), has a liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, edema, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain, dim vision, etc.) or difficulty urinating, is elderly, is physically weak or has a high fever, has persistent or recurrent stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or has an ulcer or a bleeding problem, is a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant or a breast-feeding woman, smokes, has asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, has a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts for 1 week or more or recurs, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache, or has or has had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 5 (Sunset Yellow FCF) or Yellow No. 4 (tartrazine).
  • If the symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed directions and amounts.
  • When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Because drowsiness may appear after taking it, take care when driving or operating machinery.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, difficulty urinating, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia or high anion gap metabolic acidosis appears, if symptoms of shock rarely appear (urticaria, swelling and a feeling of tightness in the chest right after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), or if asthma, generalized languor, jaundice, interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever, etc.), pseudoaldosteronism (reduced urine volume, swelling of the face, hands and feet, heavy eyelids, stiffening of the hands, a rise in blood pressure or headache, etc.) or myopathy (languor, cramp of the limbs, paralysis) appears, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take it together with antitussives (medicines that stop coughing) and expectorants (phlegm medicines), other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, oral medicines containing an antihistamine (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, allergy medicines), or flucloxacillin.
  • People who are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinson drugs, etc.) or who are within 2 weeks of stopping one should not take this medicine.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with a barbiturate, a tricyclic antidepressant, alcohol, a potassium-containing preparation, a licorice-containing preparation, a preparation containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, a loop diuretic (furosemide, ethacrynic acid) or a thiazide diuretic (trichlormethiazide).
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

Those aged 15 years and over and adults take 2 capsules at a time, three times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

For an acute disease, adults take 1 sachet (200 mg) per dose 3 times a day, children aged 6 to 14 years take 1 sachet (200 mg) per dose twice a day, and children aged 2 to 5 years take 1/2 sachet (100 mg) per dose 3 times a day, in each case with a small amount of water. This drug is used for reducing fever when fever occurs due to acute upper respiratory tract infection.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This drug is used for reducing fever when fever occurs due to acute upper respiratory tract infection.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201309080. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Children aged 6 months and over take 0.4 to 0.6 mL/kg (5 to 7 mg/kg) at a time at intervals of 4 to 6 hours as needed, and do not exceed a maximum of 4 doses a day (28 mg/kg). Children weighing 30 kg or less must not exceed a maximum of 25 mL (300 mg) a day. Refer to the approved labeling for the recommended single dose by age group.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious, potentially fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction, and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration, and perforation may occur.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with peptic ulcer, severe blood abnormalities, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency, or severe hypertension, those with bronchial asthma or who have experienced it, those who have experienced asthma, urticaria, or allergic reactions to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, patients being treated for pain before or after coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, newborns and infants under 6 months of age, and elderly people must not take this medicine.Before taking this medicine, those who have experienced peptic ulcer, those with blood abnormalities or who have experienced them, patients with a bleeding tendency, those with liver impairment or who have experienced it, those with kidney impairment or who have experienced it, patients with cardiac insufficiency or high blood pressure, those who have experienced hypersensitivity, patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), ulcerative colitis, or Crohn's disease, elderly people, children, and patients with gastric cancer should consult a doctor or pharmacist.Considering the importance of the drug treatment, either stop breastfeeding or stop the drug treatment.Dizziness or fatigue may occur after taking this medicine, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.When taking it long term for an acute condition, as a rule limit it to within 5 days.

Possible side effects

  • If the following occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: rarely, shock symptoms (chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, drop in blood pressure, etc.); blood disorders such as aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, granulocytopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), and eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) or toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); triggering of asthma attacks, urticaria, eczema, purpura; occasionally rash, itching, and visual disturbances such as blurred vision and scotoma; aseptic meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, stiff neck, fever, or impaired consciousness, etc.); acute renal failure, oliguria (decreased urination), hematuria, proteinuria, elevated BUN and blood creatinine, and hyperkalemia.
  • Occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, and stomach discomfort; very rarely thirst, stomatitis, abdominal bloating, and constipation; rarely jaundice, elevated GOT, GPT, and AL-P, hearing loss, tinnitus, taste disturbance, decreased blood pressure, increased blood pressure, palpitations, decreased urine volume, generalized edema with accompanying shortness of breath and lethargy; occasionally periorbital edema; and also very rarely malaise, fever, and nosebleed may occur.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics or high-dose methotrexate.
  • If you take it together with glucocorticoids, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, sulfonylureas, diuretics, antihypertensives, ACE inhibitors, furosemide, aspirin, lithium, low-dose methotrexate, or coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin), consult a doctor or pharmacist.

How it works
