Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202201816. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and over and adults take 1 sachet (one dose) at a time, three times a day, 30 minutes after meals. If necessary it may be taken at bedtime, and the interval between doses should be 4 hours.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported; if a skin rash or another sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, people who have experienced asthma after taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold medicines, infants (nurslings, newborns) under 3 months of age and children under 2 years of age, and women from week 30 of pregnancy onward must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the following apply: an infant (nursling, newborn) or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; a child under 2 years of age for whom it is absolutely necessary; a person with an allergic constitution; a person who has experienced allergic reactions (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.); a person with liver disease, kidney (renal) disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, edema (swelling), or gastroduodenal ulcer; an elderly person (senior); a person in poor physical condition or a person with a high fever; a person whose gastrointestinal problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain persist or recur, or who has ulcers or bleeding problems; or a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant or a breastfeeding woman.
  • If symptoms do not improve after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema (swelling), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, rarely shock symptoms (urticaria, edema (swelling), or chest tightness immediately after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) (accompanied by high fever, with severe symptoms such as rash and redness and burn-like blistering appearing on the skin over the whole body, the mouth, or the mucous membranes of the eyes), asthma, liver function disorder (generalized lassitude, jaundice, etc.), interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever, etc.), pseudoaldosteronism (decreased urine volume, swelling of the face, hands and feet, heaviness of the eyelids, stiffening of the hands, raised blood pressure, headache, etc.), or myopathy (weakness, cramps in the limbs, paralysis, etc.) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with antitussives (which stop coughing) and expectorants (phlegm medicines), other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis (nasal inflammation), motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).
  • People who are taking MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinson drugs, etc.) or are within 2 weeks of stopping them must not take this medicine.
  • Patients who have taken diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol, and those taking it together with potassium-containing preparations, licorice-containing preparations, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, ethacrynic acid) or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide), should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, infants under 12 months of age, and patients with hypercalcemia (a state in which calcium is present in excess in the blood), sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause), kidney disease, hyperkalemia, hemochromatosis (a disease in which iron is deposited in the liver and pancreas due to abnormal iron metabolism), hemosiderosis, non-iron-deficiency anemia (for iron-containing preparations), kidney stones, or hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption must not take this medicine.Before taking this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, premature infants, young children, and patients with hyperoxaluria (a state in which excessive oxalate is excreted in the urine), gastrointestinal diseases such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis, or regional (occurring in a specific part) colitis, cardiac and circulatory system dysfunction, kidney impairment, hypoproteinemia, gallbladder-related disease, liver disease, or alkalosis, those who have experienced peptic ulcer, gout, or kidney stones, patients with a predisposition to thrombosis (blockage of blood vessels), and patients with folic acid deficiency should consult a doctor or pharmacist.Strictly observe the specified dosage and administration.It may interfere with the detection of glucose in various urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, affecting clinical test values.

  • If nausea, vomiting, itching, dry and rough skin, painful joint swelling (edema), diarrhea, stomach discomfort, constipation, rash, redness (congested and reddened skin), loose stools, urticaria, photosensitivity reactions, abdominal and stomach pain, convulsions, fever, coma, hyperkalemia, a build-up of gas, gastrointestinal pain, dermatitis, a bad odor in sweat and breath, hair loss, restlessness, gastrointestinal disorders, digestive disorders, low blood pressure or pulmonary edema occur, or if menstruation starts earlier than expected, the amount gradually increases and bleeding continues for a long time, stop taking the medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids, or levodopa.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with oral contraceptives containing estrogen, antialdosterone agents, or triamterene.
  • Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before or after taking it.

How to take it

Adults and adolescents (aged 12 years and older, weighing 35 kg or more) take 10 mg at a time (5 mg when levodopa is being administered), 3 times a day before meals. The maximum daily dose is 30 mg, and it should generally not be used for more than 1 week.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients for whom stimulation of gastric motility is dangerous (gastrointestinal bleeding, mechanical obstruction, perforation), patients with prolactin-secreting tumors, patients receiving potent CYP3A4 inhibitors, patients with moderate or severe liver disorder, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, patients receiving medicines that prolong the QTc interval, patients with electrolyte imbalance (hypokalemia, hyperkalemia, hypomagnesemia), patients with underlying heart disease such as heart failure, and patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, children, patients with kidney disorder or mild liver disorder, elderly people, patients with heart disease or a history of it, breastfeeding women, those who have had breast cancer, and patients with hypersensitivity to caramel should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Drowsiness and dizziness may occur after taking this medicine, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

Possible side effects

  • Dry mouth, loss of libido, anxiety, drowsiness, headache, diarrhea, rash, itching, excessive milk secretion, breast pain, breast tenderness on pressure, asthenia, anaphylactic reaction, agitation, nervousness, dizziness, extrapyramidal disorder, convulsions, oculogyric crisis, ventricular arrhythmia, sudden cardiac death, torsades de pointes (attacks of atypical ventricular tachycardia), QTc prolongation, angioedema, urticaria, urinary retention, gynecomastia, amenorrhea, abnormal liver function tests, and increased blood prolactin may occur.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (fluconazole, itraconazole, ketoconazole, voriconazole, clarithromycin, erythromycin, telithromycin, amprenavir, atazanavir, fosamprenavir, indinavir, nelfinavir, ritonavir, saquinavir) or medicines that prolong cardiac conduction intervals such as the QTc interval (disopyramide, quinidine, amiodarone, dronedarone, sotalol, dofetilide, ibutilide, haloperidol, pimozide, sertindole, citalopram, escitalopram, levofloxacin, moxifloxacin, erythromycin, spiramycin, pentamidine, halofantrine, lumefantrine, dolasetron, cisapride, prucalopride, mequitazine, mizolastine, toremifene, vandetanib, vincamine, bepridil, diphemanil, methadone, etc.).
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with phenothiazine preparations (prochlorperazine, chlorpromazine, thiethylperazine, etc.), butyrophenone preparations (haloperidol, etc.), rauwolfia alkaloid preparations (reserpine, etc.), digitalis preparations, anticholinergic agents (scopolamine butylbromide, tiquizium bromide, timepidium bromide, etc.), dopamine agonists (bromocriptine, levodopa), antacids, gastric acid secretion inhibitors, antimuscarinic medicines, or opioid analgesics.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This drug is used for reducing fever when fever occurs due to acute upper respiratory tract infection.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201309080. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Children aged 6 months and over take 0.4 to 0.6 mL/kg (5 to 7 mg/kg) at a time at intervals of 4 to 6 hours as needed, and do not exceed a maximum of 4 doses a day (28 mg/kg). Children weighing 30 kg or less must not exceed a maximum of 25 mL (300 mg) a day. Refer to the approved labeling for the recommended single dose by age group.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious, potentially fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction, and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration, and perforation may occur.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with peptic ulcer, severe blood abnormalities, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency, or severe hypertension, those with bronchial asthma or who have experienced it, those who have experienced asthma, urticaria, or allergic reactions to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, patients being treated for pain before or after coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, newborns and infants under 6 months of age, and elderly people must not take this medicine.Before taking this medicine, those who have experienced peptic ulcer, those with blood abnormalities or who have experienced them, patients with a bleeding tendency, those with liver impairment or who have experienced it, those with kidney impairment or who have experienced it, patients with cardiac insufficiency or high blood pressure, those who have experienced hypersensitivity, patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), ulcerative colitis, or Crohn's disease, elderly people, children, and patients with gastric cancer should consult a doctor or pharmacist.Considering the importance of the drug treatment, either stop breastfeeding or stop the drug treatment.Dizziness or fatigue may occur after taking this medicine, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.When taking it long term for an acute condition, as a rule limit it to within 5 days.

Possible side effects

  • If the following occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: rarely, shock symptoms (chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, drop in blood pressure, etc.); blood disorders such as aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, granulocytopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), and eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) or toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); triggering of asthma attacks, urticaria, eczema, purpura; occasionally rash, itching, and visual disturbances such as blurred vision and scotoma; aseptic meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, stiff neck, fever, or impaired consciousness, etc.); acute renal failure, oliguria (decreased urination), hematuria, proteinuria, elevated BUN and blood creatinine, and hyperkalemia.
  • Occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, and stomach discomfort; very rarely thirst, stomatitis, abdominal bloating, and constipation; rarely jaundice, elevated GOT, GPT, and AL-P, hearing loss, tinnitus, taste disturbance, decreased blood pressure, increased blood pressure, palpitations, decreased urine volume, generalized edema with accompanying shortness of breath and lethargy; occasionally periorbital edema; and also very rarely malaise, fever, and nosebleed may occur.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics or high-dose methotrexate.
  • If you take it together with glucocorticoids, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, sulfonylureas, diuretics, antihypertensives, ACE inhibitors, furosemide, aspirin, lithium, low-dose methotrexate, or coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin), consult a doctor or pharmacist.

This medicine is used for cough, phlegm and asthma.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202302506. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and over take 1 sachet (15 ml) at a time, those aged 11 years and over but under 15 years take 2/3 sachet (10 ml) at a time, those aged 8 years and over but under 11 years take 1/2 sachet (7.5 ml) at a time, those aged 5 years and over but under 8 years take 1/3 sachet (5 ml) at a time, those aged 3 years and over but under 5 years take 1/4 sachet (3.75 ml) at a time, and those aged 2 years and over but under 3 years take 1/5 sachet (3 ml) at a time, three times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Warning

  • Patients with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their phenylalanine intake must not take this medicine.
  • This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolized to phenylalanine in the body.
  • The permitted daily amount, as recommended by the WHO, is 40 mg/kg per day or less as aspartame.
  • It should be used at the smallest possible amount.
  • For an adult weighing 60 kg, the maximum daily dose is 2.4 g.

Precautions for use

  • Patients hypersensitive to this medicine or with such a history, infants under 3 months of age, and children under 2 years of age must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, children under 2 years of age when it is absolutely necessary, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, elderly people, and people who are physically weak or who have a high fever should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Before taking this medicine, people with an allergic constitution, people who have experienced allergic symptoms caused by medicines such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, or itching, people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, or high blood pressure, and people with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that persists or recurs for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash, or a persistent headache should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Children should take it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness in which the skin becomes congested and red, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, or insomnia occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take other antitussive-expectorants, cold medicines or oral medicines containing antihistamines.
  • People who are taking MAO inhibitors used in the treatment of depression or Parkinson's disease, or who are within 2 weeks of stopping them, must not take this medicine.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis (occurring at a young age), osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), fever and pain caused by colds, back pain, dysmenorrhea, pain after surgery, ankylosing spondylitis, headache, toothache, muscle pain, neuralgia, acute gout, psoriatic arthritis, soft tissue injury (sprains, contusions), and non-articular rheumatic disease (tendinitis, tenosynovitis, bursitis).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis (occurring at a young age), osteoarthritis

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201904193. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout, and psoriatic arthritis, adults take 200 to 600 mg at a time, 3 to 4 times a day, up to a maximum of 3200 mg per day. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, take 30 to 40 mg per kg of body weight per day, divided into 3 to 4 doses. For mild to moderate pain and colds, adults take 200 to 400 mg at a time, children aged 11 to 14 years take 200 to 250 mg (10 to 13 mL) at a time, children aged 7 to 10 years take 150 to 200 mg (8 to 10 mL) at a time, children aged 3 to 6 years take 100 to 150 mg (5 to 8 mL) at a time, and children aged 1 to 2 years take 50 to 100 mg (3 to 5 mL) at a time, 3 to 4 times a day. For children weighing less than 30 kg, the daily dose must not exceed 500 mg (25 mL), and it is preferable to avoid taking it on an empty stomach.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic reactions, myocardial infarction and stroke, which may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcer and perforation may appear.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with gastrointestinal ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding or a history of it, patients with severe blood disorders, severe liver disorder, severe kidney disorder, severe cardiac insufficiency, severe high blood pressure or bronchial asthma or a history of it, patients with hypersensitivity such as asthma, urticaria or allergic reactions to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics (including COX-2 inhibitors) or a history of it, patients with pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG), pregnant women in the last 3 months of pregnancy, and patients receiving high-dose methotrexate as anticancer therapy must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with blood disorders or a history of them, patients with a tendency to bleed, patients with liver cirrhosis, liver disorder or a history of it, patients with kidney disorder or a history of it, patients with cardiac insufficiency or heart disease, high blood pressure, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, elderly people and children, pregnant women, and breastfeeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.

Possible side effects

  • If any of the following occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: shock symptoms (chest distress (heartburn), chills, difficulty breathing, a drop in blood pressure, etc.); blood disorders such as decreased hematocrit, decreased hemoglobin, anemia, aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), and eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, hematemesis (vomiting of blood), Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, thirst, stomatitis, abdominal bloating, mouth ulcers, constipation, black stools; skin-mucosa-eye syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), photosensitivity reactions, drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome), angioneurotic edema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash; hepatitis, jaundice, abnormal liver function such as elevated GOT, GPT and ALP, liver disorder; hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reactions, asthma attacks, hives, eczema, purpura (purple spots), rash, itching, asthma, bronchoconstriction, difficulty breathing or wheezing; visual disturbances such as scotoma (an area of vision loss), hearing loss (deafness), ringing in the ears, taste disturbance, vertigo, drowsiness, dizziness, depression, headache, cerebrovascular accident or nervousness, aseptic meningitis or meningitis (symptoms such as severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, stiff neck, fever, or disturbance of consciousness); a drop in blood pressure, a rise in blood pressure, palpitations (pounding heart), heart failure, myocardial infarction or angina; acute renal failure, oliguria (decreased urination), blood in the urine, protein in the urine, elevated BUN and blood creatinine, hyperkalemia, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, decreased urine volume, generalized edema and the accompanying shortness of breath, lethargy, periorbital edema (swelling around the eyes), facial edema (swelling of the face), malaise, fever, nosebleed, swelling, and peripheral edema.

Interactions

  • Do not take it together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics or with high-dose methotrexate used in cancer chemotherapy.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with low-dose aspirin, ACE inhibitors, lithium, furosemide and thiazide diuretics, low-dose methotrexate, coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin), or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors.

  • In patients who have taken barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, or alcohol, the ability to metabolize large amounts of acetaminophen is reduced, which may increase the plasma half-life of acetaminophen.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

This medicine is used to inhibit thrombus formation in myocardial infarction, cerebral infarction, and unstable angina, to inhibit thrombus formation after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG) or percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA), and to reduce cardiovascular risk in high-risk patients (patients with multiple risk factors such as a family history of ischemic heart disease, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, obesity, and diabetes).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to inhibit thrombus formation in myocardial infarction, cerebral infarction, and unstable angina,

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201603416. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults take 1 tablet as 1 dose, 1 time a day. Since this medicine is an enteric-coated tablet, it may be taken before meals with plenty of water.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or to other salicylate preparations, analgesics, anti-inflammatory agents or antirheumatic agents, patients with peptic ulcer or aspirin-induced asthma or a history of it, patients with hemophilia, severe liver disorder, severe kidney disorder, severe cardiac insufficiency or a tendency to bleed, patients receiving concomitant methotrexate at doses of 15 mg or more per week (15 mg/week), and pregnant women in the third trimester must not take this medicine.
  • Do not take this medicine during the first and second trimesters of pregnancy unless it is absolutely necessary.
  • Before using this medicine, patients with kidney disorder, cardiovascular circulatory dysfunction (renal vascular disease, congestive heart failure, fluid depletion, major surgery, sepsis or major bleeding events, etc.), liver disorder, impaired cardiac function or bronchial asthma, patients before surgery, young children aged 3 years or under, elderly people, patients with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency, patients with Reye's syndrome, patients aged 14 years or under with chickenpox or influenza infection, and patients with gout should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Because there is a risk of bleeding, tell your doctor that you are taking this medicine if you are going to have surgery (including dental surgery).
  • Take care not to damage the enteric coating of this medicine.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (e.g. difficulty breathing, generalized flushing, angioedema, hives), asthma attacks, hypersensitivity (erythema, itching, nasal congestion, cardiac and respiratory disorders, and sometimes rash, swelling, hives, rhinitis-like symptoms, conjunctivitis), rarely toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), skin-mucosa-eye syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), exfoliative dermatitis, rarely aplastic anemia, anemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), ringing in the ears, deafness, dizziness, headache, agitation, rarely liver disorder, or very rarely temporary liver damage, renal impairment, acute renal failure, hyperventilation, metabolic acidosis, an excessive drop in body temperature, collapse, or coldness of the limbs occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Loss of appetite, heartburn, stomach pain, nausea, and vomiting may occur.

Interactions

  • Other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics and salicylate preparations, and methotrexate at doses of 15 mg or more per week (15 mg/week), must not be used together with this medicine, because concomitant use may increase bleeding or reduce kidney function.
  • People taking anticoagulants, some non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics such as ibuprofen and naproxen, thrombolytics, other platelet aggregation inhibitors, hemostatics, antidiabetic agents (insulin preparations, tolbutamide, etc.), uricosuric agents (benzbromarone, probenecid), thiazide diuretics, lithium preparations, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, digoxin, systemically acting adrenocortical hormone preparations (excluding hydrocortisone used as replacement therapy for Addison's disease), angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors, or valproic acid preparations should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not mix this medicine with alkaline preparations (for example, sodium bicarbonate, magnesium carbonate) or with preparations that easily absorb moisture.
  • Concomitant use with alcohol increases damage to the gastrointestinal mucosa, and the synergistic effect of this medicine and alcohol may prolong bleeding time.

Those aged 15 years and over take 12 mL (2 sachets) at a time, those aged 11 years and over but under 15 years take 8 mL (1⅓ sachets) at a time, those aged 7 years and over but under 11 years take 6 mL (1 sachet) at a time, and those aged 3 years and over but under 7 years take 4 mL (⅔ of a sachet) at a time.   • Breastfeeding women and infants and young children under 3 years of age must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who have experienced allergic symptoms (rash, reddening of the skin, itching, etc.), women who are pregnant or may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, patients with glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), patients with urination disorders, and patients suffering from respiratory diseases such as emphysema or chronic bronchitis should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.
  • If you divide 1 sachet and use the remainder later, seal the opening well for storage and use it within 2 days.
  • Follow the specified dosage and administration carefully.
  • When it is given to children, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Possible side effects

  • If rash, congested and reddened skin, itching, palpitations, or thirst occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with other antiemetics, cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, antihistamines, sedatives, or antitussives and expectorants.
  • Do not drink alcoholic beverages.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

For sterilizing and disinfecting the hands and arms of the surgeon, put 5 mL of this medicine on the hands and arms, rub it in well for about 5 minutes to produce plenty of lather, and then rinse it off thoroughly with running water. For sterilizing and disinfecting the surgical site, apply this medicine directly or use an appropriate amount, rub it in well to produce plenty of lather, and then wipe it off with sterile gauze.

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with thyroid dysfunction (especially nodular goiter, endemic goiter, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, etc.), renal failure, or dermatitis herpetiformis, patients before or after radioactive iodine treatment, and newborns and infants under 6 months of age must not use this medicine.

  • Do not use it in the eyes or take it by mouth.
  • Be careful not to let it get into the eyes, and if it does, rinse immediately with clean water.
  • Do not mix it with other preparations.
  • Soap weakens the germicidal action of this medicine, so wash it off thoroughly before use.
  • Wash and disinfect the affected area thoroughly.
  • When it is used on severe wounds, use distilled water for injection or sterile purified water as the diluent; do not use tap water or purified water.

  • If shock symptoms (difficulty breathing, flushing, hives, etc.) or iododerma rarely occur, if pain, itching, an irritated feeling, rash, redness, or dermatitis sometimes occurs, or if a burning sensation, skin ulcer, contact dermatitis, or skin discoloration rarely occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not use this medicine together with hydrogen peroxide.

This medicine is used to relieve nasal congestion, runny nose, sneezing, watery eyes, throat pain and a feeling of heavi

How to take it

People aged 15 years and over and adults take 1 film per dose, 3 times a day, letting it dissolve in the mouth. The interval between doses must be 4 hours or more. Take this medicine (film) in the following order. Open the aluminum sheet, peel it away slowly from the mouth and take out only the medicine (film). (Do not swallow the whole aluminum sheet. This medicine (film) is a film that dissolves easily in water, so do not handle it with wet hands. Also, if there is little saliva and it is difficult to take, put water in the mouth and take it while it dissolves.

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilizers, antiparkinson drugs, etc.), other oral medicines for rhinitis, oral medicines containing antihistamines (cold remedies, antitussives and expectorants, motion sickness medicines, allergy medicines, etc.), or gastrointestinal analgesic and antispasmodic medicines.

This medicine is used for diarrhea, for the adsorption of gas produced by abnormal fermentation in the digestive tract, and as an adsorbent for emergency detoxification in poisoning by drugs and chemicals. (However, medicinal charcoal does not adsorb cyanide, and it is relatively ineffective at adsorbing alcohol, aliphatic hydrocarbons, lithium salts, corrosive sodium chloride, heavy metals such as iron, lead, and lead cyanide, boric acid, other inorganic acids, and petroleum distillates.)

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for diarrhea, for the adsorption of gas produced by abnormal fermentation in the digestive tract,

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202302822. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Take 2 to 20 g of medicinal charcoal a day, divided into several doses. In acute poisoning, medicinal charcoal is administered within 30 minutes after ingestion of the poisonous substance. (When the amount of the ingested poisonous substance is known, the recommended dose of medicinal charcoal is usually 5-10 times the amount of the ingested poisonous substance.)
Increase or decrease the dose appropriately according to age and symptoms, following the instructions of a doctor.

Warning

  • Because it degrades the imaging of esophageal erosion, do not use it when a corrosive substance has been ingested.
  • Do not use it in patients with diabetes without a doctor's diagnosis and prescription.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine should be administered after gastric aspiration or gastric lavage has been completed with the involvement of a doctor.
  • Within 2 hours of administering medicinal charcoal, the charcoal adsorbs other medicines and so reduces their effect.
  • This medicine may turn the stools black.

Possible side effects

  • Be careful, as indigestion may occur and as the adsorption of vitamins, minerals and the like may cause nutritional disturbance.

Interactions

  • Ice cream and sherbet lower the adsorptive power of medicinal charcoal, so do not take them together with it.
  • When it is used as an antidote for oral poisoning, do not take it together with ipecac syrup.
  • The ipecac syrup may be adsorbed by the medicinal charcoal and so prevent vomiting.
  • If ipecac syrup and medicinal charcoal are used at the same time, it is recommended that the medicinal charcoal be given after vomiting has been induced and has finished.

How to take it

Adults (aged 15 years and over) take 2 capsules at a time and children (aged 8 years and over but under 15 years) take 1 capsule at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of hypersensitivity appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients hypersensitive to this medicine or with such a history, people who have experienced asthma when taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics, or cold remedies, and infants under 3 months of age must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, infants and children under 15 years of age who have had or are suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, people with an allergic constitution, people who have experienced allergic reactions (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.), people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, edema, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), or difficulty urinating, elderly people, people who are physically weak or who have a high fever, people with gastrointestinal problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain, or with ulcers or bleeding problems, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, patients with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that persists or recurs for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash, or a persistent headache, and children under 2 years of age should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When administering it to children, do so under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Possible side effects

  • If the following occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: rash, redness, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, difficulty urinating, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, high anion gap metabolic acidosis; rarely shock symptoms (urticaria, edema, and chest tightness right after taking it, together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing); Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms accompanied by high fever, with rash and redness and blistering like burns appearing on the skin all over the body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes); asthma; general lethargy; jaundice; interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, and fever); pseudoaldosteronism (decreased urine volume, swelling of the face, hands, and feet, heaviness of the eyelids, stiffening of the hands, raised blood pressure, or headache); or myopathy (weakness, cramping of the limbs, paralysis).

Interactions

Those aged 15 years and older take 2 capsules at a time, 3 times a day, and those aged 8 years and older but under 15 years take 1 capsule at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of a hypersensitivity reaction appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.
  • If severe skin adverse reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis occur, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine or have experienced such hypersensitivity, people who have experienced asthma when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics or cold medicines, infants under 3 months of age, and patients with severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, infants and children under 15 years of age who have or are suspected of having a chickenpox or influenza infection, people in whom symptoms of ischemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, etc.) appear in connection with the pseudoephedrine component, people with an allergic constitution, people who have experienced an allergic reaction to a medicine (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.), people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.) or difficulty urinating, the elderly, people with a weak body or a high fever, people with persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or with ulcer or bleeding problems, women who are pregnant or may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, and children under 2 years of age should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with a cough (smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts more than 1 week or recurs, a chronic cough, a cough accompanied by fever and rash or a persistent headache) should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If symptoms do not improve after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When using it in a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, difficulty urinating, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, rarely shock symptoms (urticaria, edema and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing, etc.), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) (severe symptoms accompanied by high fever, with rash and redness and blistering like a burn, which may appear on the skin all over the body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), asthma, liver function disorder (generalized listlessness and jaundice (the skin or the whites of the eyes turning yellow) may appear), interstitial pneumonia (coughing, breathlessness, difficulty breathing and fever appear), or posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizure and visual disturbance may appear) occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.), antitussives and expectorants, other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness remedies, antiallergic remedies).

Category

How it works

This medicine is used for disinfection of the patient's skin before surgery or before insertion of a syringe needle or a

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201801818. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the applicator from its packaging and hold it with the sponge facing downwards. Do not touch the sponge part of the applicator. Squeeze the applicator firmly only once so that the ampoule breaks and the solution comes out, and leave the broken ampoule inside the applicator. For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

Precautions for use

  • People with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine, isopropanol, or Yellow No. 5 and infants aged 2 months or younger should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use this medicine for disinfecting surgical instruments, or on nervous tissue (e.g., brain or spinal cord tissue), the eyes, ears, mouth, mucous membranes, genital mucous membranes, open wounds, or torn or damaged skin, or for general washing of the skin.
  • Before using this medicine, people with hypersensitivity to other medicines, people who have experienced allergic diseases such as asthma or who have a family history of them, people with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, and people with a drug-hypersensitive constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only on intact skin.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get in, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty breathing, redness, a sudden drop in blood pressure, urticaria, angioedema, etc.), occasionally rash, photosensitization, irritation, sensitization, erythema or inflammation, itching, dry and thinly peeling skin, local pain at the application site, or local skin reactions, or very rarely rash (e.g., erythematous, papular, or maculopapular), blisters, small blisters at the application site, a burning sensation of the skin, dermatitis, eczema, chemical burns in newborns, eye irritation, congestion, impaired vision, or eye damage occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

How to take it

For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout, and psoriatic arthritis, adults take 200 to 600 mg orally as 1 dose, 3 to 4 times a day. Up to a maximum of 4200 mg may be given in 1 day. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, 30 to 40 mg per kg of body weight is given orally in 1 day, divided into 3 to 4 doses. For the single dose and the maximum daily dose for children, refer to the approved product information.

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Who should ask first

How to take it

Adults and elderly people (the aged), when they feel an urge to smoke, place 1 tablet of this medicine in the mouth and take it by sucking it slowly without chewing or swallowing it. At first, take 1 tablet of this medicine every 1 to 2 hours. Usually 8 to 12 tablets a day are taken, and do not exceed a maximum of 25 tablets a day. Take this medicine in the following order. Place 1 tablet of this medicine in the mouth and suck it until a strong taste is felt. Then place it between the gum and the cheek, and when the taste fades, repeat in the same way, sucking until it dissolves completely. The treatment period is at least 3 months; from 3 months onward the dose should be reduced in stages, and treatment should be stopped when the dose of this medicine has been reduced to 1 to 2 tablets a day. In general, nicotine replacement products such as this medicine are not recommended for use for more than 6 months.

Precautions for use

  • Patients hypersensitive to this medicine, patients with unstable angina or worsening angina, patients who have had a myocardial infarction within the last 3 months, patients in the late acute infarction period, patients with clinically relevant cardiac arrhythmias including severe cardiac arrhythmias, patients with severe cardiovascular disease such as systemic hypertension or peripheral vascular disease, patients with acute stroke or recent cerebrovascular disease, pregnant women, breastfeeding women, children and adolescents under 18 years of age, and non-smokers and occasional smokers must not use this medicine.

  • If insomnia, dizziness, headache, tremor, nausea, vomiting, indigestion, upper abdominal pain, diarrhea, constipation, abdominal distension, hiccups, gastritis, dry mouth, stomatitis, esophagitis, oral discomfort, difficulty swallowing, belching, excessive salivation, pharyngitis, cough, sore throat, difficulty breathing, palpitations, atrial arrhythmia, tachycardia (rapid pulse), hypersensitivity, angioneurotic edema, urticaria, ulcerative stomatitis, anaphylaxis, asthenia, fatigue, malaise, or influenza-like illness occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.Occasionally, mild throat irritation, increased salivation, hiccups, indigestion, or heartburn may occur at the beginning of treatment.

Interactions

  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you use it together with paracetamol, caffeine, imipramine, oxazepam, pentazocine, propranolol, theophylline, warfarin, estrogen, lignocaine, phenacetin, insulin, adrenergic antagonists (prazosin, labetalol, etc.), flecainide, adrenergic agonists (isoprenaline, phenylephrine), propoxyphene, furosemide diuretics, H2 antagonists, beta blockers, theophylline, tacrine, clozapine, or ropinirole.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201801818. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the applicator from its packaging and hold it with the sponge facing downwards. Do not touch the sponge part of the applicator. Squeeze the applicator firmly only once so that the ampoule breaks and the solution comes out, and leave the broken ampoule inside the applicator. For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

  • People with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine, isopropanol, or Yellow No. 5 and infants aged 2 months or younger should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use this medicine for disinfecting surgical instruments, or on nervous tissue (e.g., brain or spinal cord tissue), the eyes, ears, mouth, mucous membranes, genital mucous membranes, open wounds, or torn or damaged skin, or for general washing of the skin.
  • Before using this medicine, people with hypersensitivity to other medicines, people who have experienced allergic diseases such as asthma or who have a family history of them, people with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, and people with a drug-hypersensitive constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only on intact skin.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get in, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.

  • If shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty breathing, redness, a sudden drop in blood pressure, urticaria, angioedema, etc.), occasionally rash, photosensitization, irritation, sensitization, erythema or inflammation, itching, dry and thinly peeling skin, local pain at the application site, or local skin reactions, or very rarely rash (e.g., erythematous, papular, or maculopapular), blisters, small blisters at the application site, a burning sensation of the skin, dermatitis, eczema, chemical burns in newborns, eye irritation, congestion, impaired vision, or eye damage occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202401314. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Take the following single dose 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. Those aged 15 years and over take 1 sachet (20 mL) at a time, those aged 11 years and over but under 15 years take 2/3 of a sachet at a time, those aged 7 years and over but under 11 years take 1/2 of a sachet at a time, those aged 3 years and over but under 7 years take 1/3 of a sachet at a time, and those aged 2 years and over but under 3 years take 1/4 of a sachet at a time.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of hypersensitivity appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine, people who have experienced asthma when taking the ingredients of this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, and infants (newborns) under 3 months of age must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is an infant or young child under 2 years of age; if the user is an infant (nursing infant, newborn) or a child under 15 years of age who has or is suspected of having chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if you have an allergic constitution or have experienced allergic reactions (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), or difficulty urinating; if you are elderly, frail, or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain, or ulcer or bleeding problems; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant, or are breastfeeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or recurs for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever and rash or a persistent headache.
  • If the symptoms do not improve after taking 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When giving it to a child, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness (turning red from congestion), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema (swelling), difficulty urinating (passing urine), thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, rarely shock symptoms (urticaria, swelling, and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, along with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) (accompanied by high fever, with severe symptoms such as rash and redness and blistering like burns appearing on the skin all over the body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), asthma, liver function disorder (general fatigue, jaundice), or interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by coughing, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, and fever) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.), antitussive (cough-stopping) expectorants (phlegm remedies), other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis (nasal inflammation), motion sickness remedies, allergy remedies).
  • People within 2 weeks of stopping MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.) must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who are taking diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, or steroids should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, or alcohol.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), fever and pain due to a cold, low back pain, dysmenorrhea, post-operative pain and ankylosing spondylitis, headache, toothache, muscle pain, neuralgia, acute gout, psoriatic arthritis, soft tissue injury (sprain, contusion), and non-articular rheumatic diseases (tendinitis, tenosynovitis, bursitis).

How it works

This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint diseas

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 199302363. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout, and psoriatic arthritis, adults take 200-600 mg per dose, 3 to 4 times a day. Up to a maximum of 3,200 mg a day may be taken. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, take 30 to 40 mg per kg of body weight per dose, in 3 to 4 divided doses a day. For mild to moderate pain and for colds, adults take 200 to 400 mg per dose, 3 to 4 times a day. The dose may be increased or decreased as appropriate according to age and symptoms. For children, those aged 11 to 14 years take 200 to 250 mg (10 to 12.5 mL) per dose, those aged 7 to 10 years take 150 to 200 mg (7.5 to 10 mL) per dose, those aged 3 to 6 years take 100 to 150 mg (5 to 7.5 mL) per dose, and those aged 1 to 2 years take 50 to 100 mg (2.5 to 5 mL) per dose, 3 to 4 times a day, and it is advisable to avoid taking it on an empty stomach. For children, those aged 11 to 14 years may take up to 1,000 mg (50 mL) a day, those aged 7 to 10 years up to 800 mg (40 mL), those aged 3 to 6 years up to 600 mg (30 mL), and those aged 1 to 2 years up to 400 mg (20 mL).

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic reactions, myocardial infarction and stroke, which may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcer and perforation may appear.
  • Patients with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease must avoid taking high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day), and patients who have cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, smoking, etc.) and need to take high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, severe blood abnormalities, severe hepatic impairment, severe renal impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency, severe high blood pressure, or bronchial asthma, patients who have experienced asthma, urticaria, or allergic reactions caused by aspirin or other anti-inflammatory analgesics, patients with pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass surgery, pregnant women in the last 3 months of pregnancy, breastfeeding women, patients receiving high-dose methotrexate as cancer chemotherapy, and patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.
  • Do not take more than the recommended dose.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with blood abnormalities or a bleeding tendency, patients with liver cirrhosis, hepatic impairment, renal impairment, cardiac insufficiency, heart disease, high blood pressure, systemic lupus erythematosus, mixed connective tissue disease, ulcerative colitis, or Crohn's disease, elderly people, children under 2 years of age, pregnant women, and patients with chickenpox should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • When taking it for a cold, take it for no more than 5 days as a rule, and without the direction of a doctor or pharmacist do not take it for pain for 10 days or more (adults) or 5 days or more (children), and do not take it for fever for 3 days or more.

Possible side effects

  • If shock (difficulty breathing, fall in blood pressure, etc.), blood disorders such as decreased hematocrit, decreased hemoglobin, anemia, aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function or eosinophilia, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, vomiting of blood, Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, dry mouth, stomatitis, abdominal distension, oral ulcers, constipation, black stools, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms of unknown frequency, angioneurotic edema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash, exfoliative dermatitis, acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, hepatitis, jaundice, abnormal liver function, liver disorder, hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reaction, asthma attack, urticaria, eczema, purple spots, visual disturbance, deafness, ringing in the ears, taste abnormality, vertigo, drowsiness, dizziness, depression, headache, cerebrovascular accident or nervousness, aseptic meningitis or meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or impaired consciousness), acute renal failure, decreased urination, hematuria, proteinuria, elevated BUN or blood creatinine, hyperkalemia, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, decreased urine volume, generalized edema and the accompanying shortness of breath or listlessness, Kounis syndrome of unknown frequency, swelling around the eyes, facial swelling, malaise, fever, nosebleed, swelling or peripheral edema appear, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Patients receiving high-dose methotrexate as cancer chemotherapy should not take this medicine, and do not take this medicine together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics.
  • Before taking this medicine, people taking low-dose aspirin or ACE inhibitors and patients taking lithium, furosemide and thiazide diuretics, low-dose methotrexate, coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin), or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area (diseased site) several times a day.

Topical medicine (MFDS 201803219)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201803219. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for secondarily infected allergic or inflammatory skin diseases (eczema, contact dermatitis, seborrheic dermatitis, atopic dermatitis, photodermatitis, lichen simplex chronicus, intertrigo, exfoliative dermatitis, itching, psoriasis) and for first-degree burns.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for secondarily infected allergic or inflammatory skin diseases (eczema, contact dermatitis, sebor

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201803219. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area (diseased site) 1 to 3 times a day.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be used by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, by patients who have or have had hypersensitivity to aminoglycoside antibiotics such as streptomycin, kanamycin, gentamicin and neomycin or to bacitracin, or by patients with a skin infection (tuberculosis, syphilis, candidiasis, tinea, herpes zoster, herpes simplex, chickenpox, vaccinia, scabies, pubic lice), eczematous otitis externa with perforation of the eardrum, ulcer (except Behcet's disease), a burn or frostbite of deep second degree or worse, perioral dermatitis, acne vulgaris or rosacea.
  • Before using this medicine, a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant and a breast-feeding woman, and young children and children, should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed directions and amounts.
  • When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Do not use it for the eyes.
  • Do not use it for any purpose other than treatment, such as after applying makeup or shaving.
  • Do not use an occlusive dressing without the supervision of a doctor.

Possible side effects

  • If contagious impetigo (pus scab disease), folliculitis, viral infection, boils, skin irritation, a stabbing pain (piercing pain), fever, a burning sensation (a hot feeling), itching, rash, redness (reddening from congestion), flushing, swelling, papules, small blisters (vesicles), dry skin, pustular (pus blister) dermatitis, heat rash, worsening of the wound, bedsores, pustulosis (pus blister disease), hypersensitivity, skin discoloration, hypertrichosis (excessive hair), acneiform rash, hypopigmentation, perioral dermatitis, allergic contact dermatitis, maceration of the skin, secondary infection, skin atrophy, striae, or a rise in intraocular pressure or glaucoma (blurred vision) when it is used on the skin of the eyelid occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

payloads.title: Topical medicine (MFDS 202402515)
payloads.summary: This medicine is used for rinsing the inside of the nose in cases of nasal congestion caused by nasal mucous secretions
payloads.content:

Topical medicine (MFDS 202402515)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202402515. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for rinsing the inside of the nose in cases of nasal congestion caused by nasal mucous secretions or suppuration (festering), and to relieve dryness of the nasal mucosa.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for rinsing the inside of the nose in cases of nasal congestion caused by nasal mucous secretions

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202402515. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Spray this medicine into each nostril every 2 to 3 hours as needed. The number of sprays varies according to age. Insert the nozzle into the nostril and point its tip slightly backwards. Press the pump firmly to activate the spray, spray the specified amount into both nostrils, then tilt your head to the right for 10 seconds and then to the left for 10 seconds. After that, hold your nose with your hand to close the nostrils and bend your head forward for 10 seconds. Infants may be given 1 spray, those aged 1 month to 12 months 1 to 2 sprays, those aged 1 to 2 years 1 to 3 sprays, those aged 2 to 5 years 1 to 4 sprays, those aged 5 to 8 years 1 to 5 sprays, those aged 8 to 12 years 1 to 6 sprays, and adults 1 to 8 sprays.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine or to benzalkonium chloride must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, people who have experienced allergic symptoms to nasal drops and people who have recently had nasal surgery or have a nasal lesion should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use this medicine only as a nasal preparation, that is, a medicine applied inside the nose.
  • One product should be used by only one person.
  • To keep the solution from running down into the larynx or pharynx, use it while lying on your side at an angle or while standing with your head tilted.

Possible side effects

  • This medicine contains benzalkonium chloride, so it may cause bronchospasm.

payloads.title: Oral medicine (MFDS 202007065)
payloads.summary: This medicine is used to relieve various symptoms of a cold (sore throat, chills, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pa
payloads.content:

Oral medicine (MFDS 202007065)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202007065. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used to relieve various symptoms of a cold (sore throat, chills, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to relieve various symptoms of a cold (sore throat, chills, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pa

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202007065. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults (15 years and older) take 1 sachet at a time, those 11 years and older but under 15 years take 2/3 sachet at a time, those 7 years and older but under 11 years take 1/2 sachet at a time, those 3 years and older but under 7 years take 1/3 sachet at a time, and those 1 year and older but under 3 years take 1/4 sachet at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of a hypersensitivity reaction appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients hypersensitive to this medicine, those who have experienced asthma when taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics or cold medicines, infants (nursing infants, newborns) under 3 months of age, people who are taking MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinson drugs, etc.) or are within 2 weeks of stopping them, and patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, the following should consult a doctor or pharmacist: infants (nursing infants, newborns) and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza; infants and young children aged 3 months and over but under 2 years; people with an allergic constitution or who have experienced allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (e.g. fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.); people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, edema (swelling) or gastroduodenal ulcer; the elderly; people with a weak body or a high fever; people with persistent or recurrent stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or with ulcers or bleeding problems; and pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When giving it to a child, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Possible side effects

  • If the following occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: rash and redness (reddening of the skin), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling (puffiness), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia; rarely shock (urticaria, swelling (puffiness), and chest tightness right after taking it, together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, difficulty breathing, etc.); Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); asthma; liver function disorder (general lethargy, jaundice, etc.); interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever, etc.); pseudoaldosteronism (decreased urine volume, swelling of the face, hands, and feet, heaviness of the eyelids, stiffening of the hands, raised blood pressure or headache, etc.); or myopathy (muscle disease) (weakness, cramping of the limbs, paralysis, etc.).

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.), antitussives (which stop coughing) and expectorants (phlegm medicines), other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis (nasal inflammation), motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).If taking it together with antidiabetic medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants and alcohol, potassium-containing preparations, licorice-containing preparations, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, etacrynic acid), or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide), consult a doctor or pharmacist.Do not drink alcohol when taking it.
