payloads.title: Oral medicine (MFDS 201702324)
payloads.summary: This medicine is used as an adjunct in the treatment of chronic polyarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, arthropathy, ankylo
payloads.content:
Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicineThis medicine is used as an adjunct in the treatment of chronic polyarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, arthropathy, ankylo

Oral medicine (MFDS 201702324)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201702324. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used as an adjunct in the treatment of chronic polyarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, arthropathy, ankylosing spondylitis, painful swelling or inflammation after trauma and surgery, and infections accompanied by inflammation, pain, and fever.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used as an adjunct in the treatment of chronic polyarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, arthropathy, ankylo

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201702324. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults take 1 capsule (300 mg) at a time, 2 to 4 times a day. However, do not exceed 4 capsules (1,200 mg) a day.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious, potentially fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction, and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration, and perforation may occur.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with or a history of gastrointestinal ulcer, patients with bleeding in the gastrointestinal tract, the cerebral blood vessels, or other sites, severe blood disorders, severe liver disorder, severe kidney disorder, severe cardiac insufficiency, severe high blood pressure, or bronchial asthma or a history of it, those who have experienced asthma, urticaria, or an allergic reaction to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, patients being treated for pain before or after coronary artery (heart artery) bypass graft surgery (CABG), pregnant women at 6 months of pregnancy or later, nursing mothers, patients with inflammatory bowel disease such as Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis, and those who have experienced gastrointestinal bleeding or perforation from previous treatment with non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with or a history of blood disorders, patients with a bleeding tendency, patients with or a history of liver disorder or kidney disorder, patients with fluid retention (accumulation of body fluid) or heart failure, patients with high blood pressure, those who have experienced hypersensitivity, patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), elderly people, children aged 6 years and older, patients with stomach cancer or alcoholism, pregnant women in early or mid pregnancy and women who may be pregnant, patients with ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, cerebrovascular disease, or risk factors for cardiovascular disease (e.g., high blood pressure, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, smoking), patients with hepatic porphyria, patients who have had major surgery that caused blood loss, patients with a blood coagulation disorder or who are receiving anticoagulants, and those who have experienced hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 5 should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Considering the importance of the drug treatment, either stop breastfeeding or stop taking the drug.
  • Dizziness or fatigue may occur after taking this medicine, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.
  • When it is taken for a long period for an acute illness, in principle this should be limited to within 5 days.

Possible side effects

  • If the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: rarely shock (chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, lowered blood pressure, etc.); rarely blood disorders such as aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, agranulocytosis, pancytopenia, thrombocytopenia, decreased platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), and eosinophilia; indigestion, abdominal distension, heartburn, upper abdominal pain, diarrhea or constipation; occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, or stomach discomfort; rarely esophagitis, esophageal stricture, worsening of diverticula, nonspecific hemorrhagic colitis, ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, bloody stools, gastritis, or pancreatitis; very rarely thirst, stomatitis, erythema multiforme, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), or hair loss; occasionally angioedema; rarely Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency; occasionally rash, urticaria, itching, or purpura; rarely induction of an asthma attack, eczema, anaphylactic reactions, or photosensitivity reactions; rarely jaundice, elevated ALT, elevated AST, elevated ALP, abnormal liver function, hepatitis, or jaundice; occasionally rhinitis, bronchospasm, or acute pneumonia; rarely visual disturbances such as impaired vision and dark spots, hearing loss, tinnitus, or taste abnormality; fatigue, drowsiness, headache, or dizziness; occasionally anxiety, restlessness, confusion, or depression; rarely aseptic meningitis, severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, stiff neck, fever, or impaired consciousness; rarely mental abnormality, agitation, excitement, disorientation, or reversible toxic amblyopia; rarely lowered blood pressure, raised blood pressure, palpitations, oliguria, hematuria, proteinuria, elevated BUN and blood creatinine, hyperkalemia, decreased urine volume, generalized edema and the accompanying shortness of breath, or languor; rarely renal papillary necrosis, nephrotic syndrome, interstitial nephritis, peripheral edema, acute pulmonary edema, fluid retention, hypertension, heart failure, or reduced fertility in women; occasionally periorbital edema; very rarely malaise, fever, nosebleed, or worsening of inflammation.

Interactions

  • Do not take together with aspirin, other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, or high-dose methotrexate used in cancer chemotherapy (15 mg/week or more).
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are taking corticosteroids, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, sulfonylureas, ACE inhibitors, angiotensin II receptor antagonists, diuretics, lithium, coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin), baclofen, immunosuppressants (cyclosporine, tacrolimus, sirolimus), thrombolytics, ticlopidine, antithrombotic agents, medicines that increase blood potassium levels (trimethoprim, heparin, etc.), inducers of CYP2C8 or CYP2C9 (e.g., rifampicin, phenobarbital), low-dose methotrexate (less than 15 mg/week), antiplatelet agents, or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, if you take low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke, or if you have experienced hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 5.

payloads.title: Topical medicine (MFDS 202500570)
payloads.summary: This medicine is used for the disinfection of surgical sites.
payloads.content:
Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicineThis medicine is used for the disinfection of surgical sites.

Topical medicine (MFDS 202500570)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202500570. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for the disinfection of surgical sites.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the disinfection of surgical sites.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202500570. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Press the cap at the end of the applicator handle so that the antiseptic solution soaks into the sponge, and apply it to the area to be disinfected. During use, adjust the amount of solution with the sponge attached to the applicator. Do not use it on the head, the neck, or small areas. Do not rub it off. Do not let the solution pool, and if a lot of solution runs, absorb it using the sponge. If the solution runs outside the area of use, wipe it off with gauze. If the solution gets into the navel, wipe it off with a cotton swab. Prepare a towel as needed to keep the solution from running down, and remove it before covering with a surgical drape. When applying it to skin folds such as the fingers and toes, hold the application site open with sterile-gloved hands until the liquid dries. Otherwise the skin surfaces may stick together. Use it as a single-use product only and discard any remaining solution.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine, patients with thyroid function abnormalities (nodular goiter, endemic goiter, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, etc.), patients with renal failure, newborns and infants under 6 months of age, patients with dermatitis herpetiformis, patients before and after radioactive iodine treatment, severely ill patients such as burn patients, and patients receiving lithium treatment must not use this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who have had thyroid disease and patients with it, patients with renal failure, women who are pregnant or may be pregnant, and breastfeeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not apply it to burns or mucous membranes, and do not use it as a substitute for an ordinary skin cleanser.
  • Use it for external use only.
  • Do not mix it with other preparations.

Possible side effects

  • If occasionally pain, itching, an irritating sensation, rash, redness or dermatitis, or rarely shock (anaphylaxis: severe symptoms such as sudden itching, swelling and heartburn together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and shortness of breath), a burning sensation, skin ulcer, contact dermatitis or skin discoloration occur, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not use it together with lithium, chlorhexidine, sulfadiazine-silver compounds, alkalis, preparations containing mercury, enzyme-based wound treatments, or hydrogen peroxide.

At a glance

How it works

This medicine is used for athlete's foot, tinea cruris (ringworm of the groin) and tinea.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201903099. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area (the diseased site) 1 time a day.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine, women who are pregnant, may be pregnant, or are breastfeeding, infants, and children must not use this medicine, and it must not be used on or around the eyes, on mucous membranes (inside the mouth, inside the nose, the vagina), on the scrotum or external genitalia, on eczema, on moist (damp) areas, on erosion, on diseased areas with severe cracking or wounds, on the nails, or on the scalp.

  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • Clean the diseased area and its surroundings before use.
  • Be careful not to let it get into the eyes, and if it does get into the eyes, rinse them immediately with water or warm water.
  • Do not touch your eyes or mucous membranes with hands that have this medicine on them.
  • Use this medicine for external use only; do not use it internally.

Possible side effects

  • If inflammation, scaling (peeling of the skin like dandruff or flakes), wounds, dry skin and a feeling of tightness in the skin, cracking of the skin, pain, pigmentation, irritation, a hot sensation, hangnails, skin breakdown, blisters, rash and redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, swelling, or urticaria occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Category

How it works

This medicine is used for disinfecting the patient's skin before surgery and for disinfecting the patient's skin before

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201402375. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Apply it to the area to be disinfected.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine and infants aged 2 months or younger must not use it.
  • Do not use it to disinfect surgical instruments, or on the brain, spinal cord, eyes, ears (inner ear, middle ear, outer ear), or mucous membranes (especially genital mucous membranes).
  • Before using this medicine, patients with an allergic constitution and those applying it to broken skin (especially burns), mucous membranes, or large areas of immature skin should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only; do not take it by mouth or inject it.
  • Be careful not to let it get into the eyes, and if it does, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.
  • Soap weakens the germicidal action of this medicine, so wash it off thoroughly before use.
  • This medicine is adsorbed by fibers and cloth (cotton, gauze, wool, rayon, etc.), so when it is used soaked into such materials, supply fresh solution if the concentration is no longer above the effective level.
  • It is a flammable liquid, so be careful.
  • Dry it before using electrical devices.

Possible side effects

  • If hypersensitivity symptoms such as local allergy, systemic allergy, contact eczema, photosensitization, shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, tightness in the chest, difficulty breathing, redness), or occasionally rash or urticaria occur, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Category

How it works

This medicine is used for cough and phlegm.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202203444. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and older take 20 ml at a time, those aged 11 years to under 15 years take 13.3 ml, those aged 8 years to under 11 years take 10 ml, those aged 5 years to under 8 years take 6.7 ml, those aged 3 years to under 5 years take 5 ml, and those aged 2 years to under 3 years take 4 ml, 5-6 times a day, at intervals of about 4 hours.

Precautions for use

  • People who are hypersensitive to this medicine or have been in the past, infants (newborns) under 3 months of age, and people who are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian drugs, etc.) or are within 2 weeks of stopping one must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have an allergic constitution or have experienced allergy to medicines (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.); if the user is an infant or young child aged 3 months or older and under 2 years; if you have liver, kidney, heart or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), or difficulty urinating; if you are elderly, frail, or have a high fever; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant, or are breastfeeding; or if symptoms such as smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or recurs for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever and rash or a persistent headache appear.
  • If the symptoms do not improve after taking 5 to 6 doses, consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.
  • When giving it to a child, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, difficulty urinating (passing urine), persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, or insomnia occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian drugs, etc.), other antitussives and expectorants (cough and phlegm medicines), cold medicines, oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis [nasal inflammation], motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines), or sedatives.

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201902565. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Children aged 8 years and older and adults take 2 tablets as 1 dose, 2 times a day, and children aged 36 months or older and under 8 years take 1 tablet as 1 dose, 2 times a day. Let the tablet dissolve in the mouth or chew it before swallowing.

Warning

  • Taking 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A a day may cause congenital malformations.
  • Women within 3 months of pregnancy or who may be pregnant must not take it.
  • An overdose in children aged 6 years or younger may cause death from iron poisoning, so keep it out of the reach of children.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypercalcemia (a condition in which calcium is present in excess in the blood), sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause), kidney disease, or hypersensitivity to this medicine, infants under 12 months of age, patients with hemochromatosis (a disease in which iron is deposited in the liver and pancreas because of abnormal iron metabolism), hemosiderosis, non-iron-deficiency anemia, kidney stones, or severe renal failure, and patients with genetic problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, infants under 1 year of age, children who get plenty of sunlight and eat a normal diet, patients with hyperoxaluria (a condition in which an excessive amount of oxalate is excreted in the urine), pregnant women and women who may be pregnant, nursing mothers, premature infants, infants, patients with gastrointestinal diseases such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis, or localized [appearing in a specific area] colitis, and those with cardiac and circulatory dysfunction, kidney [renal] disorder, hypoproteinemia, gout, or a history of kidney stones should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When giving it to children, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • It may turn the urine yellow and affect clinical laboratory test values.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it for about 1 month, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If nausea, vomiting, itching, dry and rough skin, painful joint swelling, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, constipation, rash, redness (congested and reddened), loose stools, low blood pressure, facial flushing, irregular heartbeat, hives, photosensitivity reactions, abdominal or stomach pain, convulsions, fever, coma, red spots, asystole (cardiac arrest), depression of central nervous system function, gastrointestinal disorders, digestive disorders, upper abdominal pain, pulmonary edema, or symptoms such as menstruation coming earlier than expected, the flow gradually becoming heavier, or bleeding lasting for a long time occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral (taken by mouth) tetracycline preparations, antacids, or levodopa.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with oral (taken by mouth) contraceptives containing estrogen, antialdosterone agents, triamterene, or cardiac glycosides.
  • Avoid teas containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, while taking it and before and after taking it.

How to take it

Children aged 6 months and over take 0.4 to 0.6 mL per kg of body weight per dose, at intervals of 4 to 6 hours when needed, and must not exceed 4 doses a day (28 mg/kg). For children weighing 30 kg or less, do not exceed 25 mL a day. When the body weight is known it is more appropriate to use the amount based on body weight, so refer to the approved product information for details.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic reactions, myocardial infarction and stroke, which may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcer and perforation may appear.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be taken by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, peptic ulcer, severe blood abnormality, liver impairment, renal impairment, cardiac insufficiency, high blood pressure or bronchial asthma or by those who have had them, by people who have had asthma, urticaria or an allergy in response to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, by patients being treated for pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass surgery, or by a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant or a breast-feeding woman.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user has or has had peptic ulcer, blood abnormality, a bleeding tendency, liver impairment, renal impairment, cardiac insufficiency, high blood pressure or hypersensitivity, is a patient with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, is elderly or a child, has stomach cancer, or is taking low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke, especially a patient with an autoimmune disease (SLE, MCTD).

  • Do not use it together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics.

At a glance

Category

How it works

This medicine is used for disinfection of the patient's skin before surgery or before insertion of a syringe needle or a

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201801818. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the applicator from its packaging and hold it with the sponge facing downwards. Do not touch the sponge part of the applicator. Squeeze the applicator firmly only once so that the ampoule breaks and the solution comes out, and leave the broken ampoule inside the applicator. For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

Precautions for use

  • People with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine, isopropanol, or Yellow No. 5 and infants aged 2 months or younger should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use this medicine for disinfecting surgical instruments, or on nervous tissue (e.g., brain or spinal cord tissue), the eyes, ears, mouth, mucous membranes, genital mucous membranes, open wounds, or torn or damaged skin, or for general washing of the skin.
  • Before using this medicine, people with hypersensitivity to other medicines, people who have experienced allergic diseases such as asthma or who have a family history of them, people with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, and people with a drug-hypersensitive constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only on intact skin.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get in, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty breathing, redness, a sudden drop in blood pressure, urticaria, angioedema, etc.), occasionally rash, photosensitization, irritation, sensitization, erythema or inflammation, itching, dry and thinly peeling skin, local pain at the application site, or local skin reactions, or very rarely rash (e.g., erythematous, papular, or maculopapular), blisters, small blisters at the application site, a burning sensation of the skin, dermatitis, eczema, chemical burns in newborns, eye irritation, congestion, impaired vision, or eye damage occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Before taking this medicine, children under 2 years of age when it is absolutely necessary, infants and children under 15 years of age who have or are suspected of having a chickenpox or influenza infection, people with an allergic constitution, women who are pregnant or may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, people in whom symptoms of ischemic colitis such as sudden abdominal pain or rectal bleeding appear in connection with the pseudoephedrine component, people who have experienced allergic symptoms caused by a medicine such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching, the elderly, and people with a weak body or a high fever should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Before taking this medicine, people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma or difficulty urinating, people with persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or with ulcer or bleeding problems, and people with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts more than 1 week or recurs, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever and rash or a persistent headache should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If symptoms do not improve after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Children should take it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Do not take it continuously over a long period.
  • Drowsiness may come on while you are taking it.
  • Avoid driving a car or operating machinery.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty urinating, (persistent or severe) thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, or insomnia occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If, rarely, shock (anaphylaxis) occurs, which may appear immediately after taking it as hives, swelling, and chest tightness together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing, or if skin-mucosa-eye syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, liver dysfunction such as general lethargy and jaundice, interstitial pneumonia, or symptoms of reversible posterior encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome such as sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, or visual disturbance occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take antitussives and expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives or oral medicines containing an antihistamine.
  • People who are taking an MAO inhibitor used for the treatment of depression, Parkinson's disease and the like, or who are within 2 weeks of stopping one, should not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who are being given a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid or the like should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Patients who are being given a barbiturate, a tricyclic antidepressant or alcohol should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

Adults take 1 capsule per dose, 1 time a day. Since this medicine is an enteric-coated capsule, it may be taken before meals with plenty of water.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or other salicylate preparations, patients with peptic ulcer, patients with aspirin-induced asthma (induction of asthma attacks by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, etc.) or those who have experienced it, patients with hemophilia, severe hepatic impairment, severe renal impairment, cardiac insufficiency, or a bleeding tendency, patients receiving concomitant methotrexate at a dose of 15 milligrams or more per week (15 mg/week), and pregnant women in the third trimester of pregnancy should not take this medicine.

  • When taken together with alcohol, damage to the gastrointestinal mucosa may increase and bleeding time may be prolonged.

Those aged 15 years and over take 1 sachet (20 mL), those aged 11 years to under 15 years take 2/3 of a sachet, those aged 7 years to under 11 years take 1/2 of a sachet, those aged 3 years to under 7 years take 1/3 of a sachet, and those aged 2 years to under 3 years take 1/4 of a sachet, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.It may cause liver damage.Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of hypersensitivity appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).It may cause liver damage.Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolized to phenylalanine in the body, so patients with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their phenylalanine intake must not take it.

Precautions for use

  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • When giving it to a child, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.
  • If the symptoms do not improve after taking it 5 to 6 times, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema (swelling), difficulty urinating (passing urine), persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, shock symptoms (urticaria, swelling and tightness in the chest immediately after taking it, together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweats and difficulty breathing), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome: severe symptoms accompanied by high fever, such as rash and redness and blisters like burns), asthma, listlessness of the whole body, jaundice (the skin or the whites of the eyes taking on a yellow color) or interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by coughing, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever, etc.) occurs, stop taking the medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian drugs, etc.), antitussives and expectorants (cough and phlegm medicines), other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis [nasal inflammation], motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).

Category

How it works

This medicine is used for the relief of headache, toothache, pain after tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint pa

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202401379. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Take the following single dose up to 3 times a day, avoiding an empty stomach, and leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.Those aged 15 years and older take 1 sachet (1,100 mg) at a time; those aged 11 years and older but under 15 years take 2/3 sachet (733.33 mg) at a time; those aged 7 years and older but under 11 years take 1/2 sachet (550 mg) at a time; those aged 3 years and older but under 7 years take 1/3 sachet (366.67 mg) at a time; and those aged 2 years and older but under 3 years take 1/4 sachet (275 mg) at a time.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of hypersensitivity appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, people who have experienced asthma after taking the ingredients of this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics or cold medicines, and infants under 3 months of age must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, infants (newborns) and children under 15 years of age who have, or are suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza, children under 2 years of age, people with an allergic constitution, people who have experienced allergic reactions (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.), people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, or high blood pressure, people in poor physical condition or with a high fever, the elderly, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, and people whose gastrointestinal problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain persist or recur or who have ulcers or bleeding problems should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If symptoms do not improve after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When administering it to children, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, dizziness, edema, rarely shock symptoms (urticaria, swelling, or chest tightness immediately after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, difficulty breathing, etc.), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) (accompanied by high fever, with severe symptoms such as rash and redness and burn-like blistering appearing on the skin over the whole body, the mouth, or the mucous membranes of the eyes), asthma, or liver function disorder (generalized lassitude, jaundice) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with other antipyretic analgesics, cold medicines or sedatives If you take this medicine together with antidiabetic drugs, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, or alcohol, consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201900992. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and over and adults take 1 packet (a single dose) at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. The interval between doses should be 4 hours.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of a hypersensitivity reaction appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine, people who have experienced asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold medicines, infants (babies) under 3 months of age, and people who are taking MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.) or are within 2 weeks of having stopped them must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, infants and children under 15 years of age who have or are suspected of having a chickenpox or influenza infection, people with an allergic constitution, people who have experienced allergic symptoms (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.), people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, edema (swelling), gastroduodenal ulcer and the like, the elderly, people with a weak body or a high fever, people with persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach (upper abdominal) discomfort or stomach pain, or with ulcer or bleeding problems, women who are pregnant or may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, and children under 2 years of age should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If the following occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling (puffiness), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia; rarely shock symptoms (urticaria, swelling (puffiness), and chest tightness right after taking it, together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing); Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) (severe symptoms accompanied by high fever, with rash and redness (reddening of the skin) and blistering like burns appearing on the skin all over the body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes); asthma; liver function disorder (general lethargy, jaundice (the skin or the whites of the eyes turn yellow)); interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever); pseudoaldosteronism; or myopathy (muscle disease).

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with antitussives (which stop coughing) and expectorants (phlegm medicines), other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis (nasal inflammation), motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).
  • If it is taken together with diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, potassium-containing preparations, licorice-containing preparations, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, etacrynic acid), or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide), consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

payloads.title: Oral medicine (MFDS 199902599)
payloads.summary: This drug is used for rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), ankylosing spondylitis, tendini
payloads.content:

Oral medicine (MFDS 199902599)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 199902599. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This drug is used for rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), ankylosing spondylitis, tendinitis, acute gout, dysmenorrhea and bursitis, skeletal muscle disorders (sprain, contusion (bruise), trauma (wound), lumbosacral pain (low back pain)), postoperative pain (aches), migraine, and pain after tooth extraction (pulling out a tooth).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This drug is used for rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), ankylosing spondylitis, tendini

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 199902599. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, and ankylosing spondylitis, adults take 1 to 2 tablets (275 to 550 mg) at a time, twice a day (every 12 hours). For acute gout, take 3 tablets (825 mg) as the initial dose (the first dose), then take 1 tablet (275 mg) every 8 hours until the attack subsides. For skeletal muscle disorders, pain after surgery, pain after tooth extraction (having a tooth pulled), dysmenorrhea, tendinitis (inflammation of a tendon), and bursitis (inflammation of the lubricating sac), take 2 tablets (550 mg) as the initial dose (the first dose), then take 1 tablet (275 mg) every 6 to 8 hours, and do not let the total daily dose exceed 5 tablets (1,375 mg). For migraine, take 3 tablets (825 mg) as the initial dose (the first dose); if necessary, 1 to 2 more tablets (275 to 550 mg) may be taken a day, and these are taken 30 minutes after the initial dose (the first dose). Do not let the total daily dose exceed 5 tablets (1,375 mg).

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and potentially fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction, and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration, and perforation may occur.

Precautions for use

  • Patients hypersensitive to this medicine, patients with peptic ulcer, severe blood abnormalities, severe liver disorder, severe cardiac insufficiency, severe renal disorder or severe high blood pressure, patients hypersensitive to non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics such as aspirin, patients who have had asthma, rhinitis (nasal inflammation), nasal polyps, urticaria or an allergic reaction caused by aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics (including COX-2 inhibitors) or those who have experienced them, patients being treated for pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass surgery, patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption, pregnant women, breastfeeding women, and children aged 2 years or under must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, pregnant women and women who may be pregnant, children, the elderly, those who have experienced peptic ulcer, those who have experienced blood abnormalities, patients with a tendency to bleed, patients with liver disorder or those who have experienced it, patients with renal disorder or those who have experienced it, and patients with cardiac dysfunction, high blood pressure, bronchial asthma, systemic lupus erythematosus or mixed connective tissue disease should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If an increased risk of myocardial infarction and stroke, serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions that may be fatal such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcers, and perforation, rarely shock symptoms (difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure, bradycardia (a slow pulse), cold sweat, swelling), PIE syndrome (pulmonary infiltration with eosinophilia: accompanied by fever, wheezing, coughing, and phlegm), urticaria, occasionally hypersensitivity symptoms such as rash or itching, hematemesis (vomiting of blood), gastrointestinal bleeding, peptic ulcer, perforation, aseptic meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever, or impaired consciousness), eczema, sweating, purpura (purple spots), photosensitivity, hair loss, redness (turning red from congestion), necrolysis, erythema multiforme (red spots of various shapes), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), urticaria, epidermolysis bullosa, drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms, fixed drug eruption, exfoliative dermatitis, or rarely blood disorders such as agranulocytosis, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, aplastic anemia, hemolytic (red-blood-cell-destroying) anemia, or reduced platelet function (prolongation of bleeding time) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202008963. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and over take 1 sachet (20 mL), those aged 11 years to under 15 years take 2/3 of a sachet, those aged 7 years to under 11 years take 1/2 of a sachet, those aged 3 years to under 7 years take 1/3 of a sachet, and those aged 2 years to under 3 years take 1/4 of a sachet, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. Do not give it to those under 2 years of age.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when they take this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of a hypersensitivity reaction appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.
  • If severe skin adverse reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis occur, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolized to phenylalanine in the body, so patients with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their phenylalanine intake must not take it.

Precautions for use

  • Patients hypersensitive to this medicine or with such a history, people who have had asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, infants (newborns) under 3 months of age, and patients with severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are a child aged 3 months and over but under 2 years, an infant or a child under 15 years of age who is infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, a person with an allergic constitution or a history of allergy to medicines, a person with liver, kidney, heart, or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), or difficulty urinating (passing urine), an elderly person, a person who is physically weak or who has a high fever, a person with persistent or recurring gastrointestinal problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain or with ulcers or bleeding problems, a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant, a breastfeeding woman, or a person with symptoms such as smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that persists or recurs for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash, or a persistent headache.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • When administering it to children, do so under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.
  • If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness (turning red from congestion), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema (swelling), difficulty urinating (passing urine), persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, shock symptoms (urticaria, swelling, and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, along with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome: accompanied by high fever, with severe symptoms such as rash and redness and blistering like burns), asthma, general fatigue, jaundice (the skin or the whites of the eyes take on a yellow color), interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by coughing, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, and fever), symptoms of ischemic colitis associated with the pseudoephedrine component (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding), or posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance, etc.) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.), antitussives and expectorants (cough and phlegm medicines), other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis [nasal inflammation], motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).
  • People who are within 2 weeks of stopping MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.) must not take this medicine.
  • People who are being given other medicines such as barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants and alcohol, diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, or steroids should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • If edema (swelling), shortness of breath, fatigue, symptoms of dehydration, heart failure or the like occurs, stop taking the medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Do not take this medicine together with orally administered medicines (such as antiepileptics) or with medicines that dissolve well in alcohol but have relatively low solubility in water.

This medicine is used for difficulty in expectorating sputum in bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis, pulmonary tuberculosis, emphysema, upper respiratory tract inflammation (pharyngitis and laryngitis), lung abscess, pneumonia, cystic fibrosis and postoperative pulmonary complications, and for the preparation and aftercare of bronchography, bronchoscopy, lung cancer cytology and tracheostomy.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for difficulty in expectorating sputum in bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis, pu

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 198600267. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

This medicine may be diluted to a lower concentration with sodium chloride solution for injection, sodium chloride solution for inhalation, sterile distilled water for injection or sterile distilled water for inhalation. For nebulization therapy using a face mask, a mouthpiece or a tracheostomy, nebulize 1 to 10 mL every 2 to 6 hours. The recommended amount is 3 to 5 mL nebulized 3 to 4 times a day. Nebulization therapy using a nebulization tent or an inhaler (Croupette) is a method needed in special cases, and it is used individually according to the personal needs of the patient and the convenience of the method of administration. This method of administration requires a large volume of solution, and sometimes as much as about 300 mL may be required for a single treatment. The recommended amount should be an amount that can maintain a very dense mist-like state inside the tent or the inhaler during the treatment period. Intermittent or continuous administration over a long period is preferable. For direct instillation, give 1 to 2 mL every hour. For the regular treatment of a patient who has had a tracheostomy, give 1 to 2 mL through the tracheostomy every 1 to 4 hours. When a small plastic catheter is inserted into the trachea under local anesthesia through a direct incision to give it directly to a specific part of the bronchial tree, give 2 to 5 mL every 1 to 4 hours using a syringe connected to the catheter. When it is given using a percutaneous intrabronchial catheter, give 1 to 2 mL of this medicine every 1 to 4 hours with a syringe connected to the catheter. For diagnostic bronchography, give 1 to 2 mL 2 to 3 times by nebulization or by intrabronchial instillation before the bronchography is performed.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user has bronchial asthma or accompanying respiratory insufficiency, is a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant or a breast-feeding woman, is a child, or is elderly.
  • Do not use it as an injection or as eye drops.
  • After nebulization therapy the face mask may stick to the face, but it comes off easily when washed with water.

Possible side effects

  • If bronchial obstruction, bronchospasm, rash or difficulty breathing occasionally appears, or if anaphylaxis rarely appears, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • A slight odor (smell of sulfur) may appear, nausea, vomiting and loss of appetite may occasionally appear, and bloody sputum, chills, fever, runny nose, stomatitis, drowsiness, a feeling of pressure in the chest and irritation of the trachea and bronchi may rarely appear.

Interactions

  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when it is used together with an antibiotic, tetracycline, erythromycin, bromhexine or the like.

Who should ask first

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the applicator from its packaging and hold it with the sponge facing downwards. Do not touch the sponge part of the applicator. Squeeze the applicator firmly only once so that the ampoule breaks and the solution comes out, and leave the broken ampoule inside the applicator. For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

  • Before using this medicine, people with hypersensitivity to other medicines, people who have experienced allergic diseases such as asthma or who have a family history of them, people with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, and people with a drug-hypersensitive constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only on intact skin.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get in, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.

  • If shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty breathing, redness, a sudden drop in blood pressure, urticaria, angioedema, etc.), occasionally rash, photosensitization, irritation, sensitization, erythema or inflammation, itching, dry and thinly peeling skin, local pain at the application site, or local skin reactions, or very rarely rash (e.g., erythematous, papular, or maculopapular), blisters, small blisters at the application site, a burning sensation of the skin, dermatitis, eczema, chemical burns in newborns, eye irritation, congestion, impaired vision, or eye damage occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Oral medicine (MFDS 201900783)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201900783. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for the relief of nasal congestion, runny nose, sneezing, watery eyes, sore throat, and heaviness of the head due to a head cold (acute rhinitis), allergic rhinitis, or sinusitis.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the relief of nasal congestion, runny nose, sneezing, watery eyes, sore throat, and heaviness

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201900783. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those 15 years and older take 24 mL at a time, those 11 years and older but under 15 years take 16 mL at a time, those 7 years and older but under 11 years take 12 mL at a time, those 3 years and older but under 7 years take 8 mL at a time, and those 2 years and older but under 3 years take 6 mL at a time, 4 times a day, after each meal and, if necessary, before bedtime. If needed, it may be taken about every 4 hours, up to 6 times a day.

Precautions for use

  • Infants under 3 months of age must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist in the case of children under 2 years of age; an allergic constitution; a history of allergic reactions (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.); liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, heart disease, kidney disease, edema, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), difficulty urinating, thyroid disease, or diabetes; being physically weak or having a high fever; being pregnant, possibly pregnant, or breastfeeding; being elderly; or smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough lasting 1 week or longer or recurring, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever and rash or a persistent headache.
  • Follow the specified dosage and administration carefully.
  • When it is given to children, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If hemorrhagic stroke, nausea and vomiting, thirst (persistent or severe), constipation, loss of appetite, rash and redness, itching, difficulty urinating, rarely shock symptoms (urticaria, swelling, and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, along with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing), pseudoaldosteronism (decreased urine volume, swelling of the face, hands and feet, heaviness of the eyelids, stiffening of the hands, a rise in blood pressure, headache, etc.), or myopathy (weakness, cramps in the limbs, paralysis, etc.) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilizers, antiparkinson drugs, etc.), other oral medicines for rhinitis, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (cold remedies, antitussives and expectorants, motion sickness medicines, allergy medicines, etc.).
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

Oral medicine (MFDS 202501161)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202501161. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold, such as runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills (feeling cold and shivering), fever, headache, joint pain, and muscle pain.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold, such as runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore th

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202501161. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults (aged 15 years and over) take 2 capsules at a time and children (aged 8 years and over but under 15 years) take 1 capsule at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of hypersensitivity appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients hypersensitive to this medicine or with such a history, people who have experienced asthma when taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics, or cold remedies, and infants under 3 months of age must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, infants and children under 15 years of age who have had or are suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, people with an allergic constitution, people who have experienced allergic reactions (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.), people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, edema, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), or difficulty urinating, elderly people, people who are physically weak or who have a high fever, people with gastrointestinal problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain, or with ulcers or bleeding problems, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, patients with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that persists or recurs for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash, or a persistent headache, and children under 2 years of age should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When administering it to children, do so under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Possible side effects

  • If the following occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: rash, redness, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, difficulty urinating, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, high anion gap metabolic acidosis; rarely shock symptoms (urticaria, edema, and chest tightness right after taking it, together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing); Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms accompanied by high fever, with rash and redness and blistering like burns appearing on the skin all over the body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes); asthma; general lethargy; jaundice; interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, and fever); pseudoaldosteronism (decreased urine volume, swelling of the face, hands, and feet, heaviness of the eyelids, stiffening of the hands, raised blood pressure, or headache); or myopathy (weakness, cramping of the limbs, paralysis).

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinson drugs, etc.), antitussive-expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.
  • If taken together with diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, potassium-containing preparations, licorice-containing preparations, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, ethacrynic acid) or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide), or flucloxacillin, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

This medicine is used for chronic polyarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, arthrosis, and ankylosing spondylitis. This medicine is used as an adjunct in the treatment of painful swelling or inflammation after injury and surgery and of infections accompanied by inflammation, pain, and fever.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for chronic polyarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, arthrosis, and ankylosing spondylitis. This medic

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201904806. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults take 1 tablet at a time, 2 to 4 times a day.Do not exceed 4 tablets (1,200 mg) a day.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction, and stroke, which can be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration, and perforation may occur.
  • Patients with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, or cerebrovascular disease should avoid taking high-dose dexibuprofen (1,200 mg a day), and patients with cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, smoking, etc.) who need to take high-dose dexibuprofen should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with bronchial asthma or those who have experienced it, and those who have experienced asthma, urticaria, or allergic reactions to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics must not take this medicine.Patients who have or show signs of gastrointestinal ulcer or who have experienced recurrence, patients with bleeding in impairment, heart failure, or high blood pressure must not take this medicine.Those being treated for pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery and pregnant women at 6 months of pregnancy or later must not take this medicine.Before taking this medicine, patients with blood abnormalities, liver impairment, or kidney impairment or those who have experienced them, patients with coagulation disorders or a bleeding tendency, patients with fluid retention or heart failure, high blood pressure, systemic lupus erythematosus or mixed connective tissue disease, patients with gastric cancer, alcoholism, ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, cerebrovascular disease, or hepatic porphyria, patients with cardiovascular disease risk factors such as high blood pressure, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, or smoking, and patients who have undergone major surgery causing blood loss should consult a doctor or pharmacist.Before taking this medicine, pregnant women in early or mid pregnancy, women at 20 weeks of pregnancy or later, women planning pregnancy, women who may be pregnant, elderly people, children aged 6 years and older, those who have experienced hypersensitivity reactions, and patients with hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5 or Sunset Yellow FCF or those who have experienced it should consult a doctor or pharmacist.In the case of breastfeeding women, either stop administration of this medicine or stop breastfeeding.Limit long-term administration to within 5 days.Dizziness or fatigue may occur.Take it with caution when driving or operating machinery.

Possible side effects

  • If indigestion, abdominal bloating, heartburn, upper abdominal pain, diarrhea, constipation, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, stomach discomfort, erythema multiforme showing red spots of various shapes, systemic lupus erythematosus, hair loss, angioedema, rash, urticaria, itching, purpura, rhinitis, bronchospasm, fatigue, drowsiness, headache, dizziness, anxiety, restlessness, confusion, depression, reduced fertility in women, an increased risk of acute pulmonary edema in patients with heart failure, peripheral edema, or periorbital edema with swelling around the eyes occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If, rarely, shock symptoms such as chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, and a drop in blood pressure, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome), acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, triggering of asthma attacks, eczema, anaphylactic reactions, photosensitivity reactions, aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function, an increased risk of acute pneumonia in patients with heart failure, jaundice, abnormal liver function, hepatitis, jaundice, anxiety, restlessness, depression, raised blood pressure, palpitations, acute renal failure, malaise, fever, nosebleed, or worsening of inflammation occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take aspirin, other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics or high-dose methotrexate.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients receiving corticosteroids, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, sulfonylureas, ACE inhibitors or angiotensin II receptor antagonists, diuretics, lithium, coumarin anticoagulants (warfarin, etc.), baclofen, immunosuppressants (cyclosporine, tacrolimus, sirolimus), thrombolytics, ticlopidine, antithrombotic agents, medicines that increase the blood potassium level (potassium-sparing diuretics, ACE inhibitors, angiotensin II receptor antagonists, immunosuppressants such as cyclosporine and tacrolimus, trimethoprim, heparin, etc.), inducers of CYP2C8 or CYP2C9 (rifampicin, phenobarbital), low-dose methotrexate (less than 15 mg per week), antiplatelet agents or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
