This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), fever and pain caused by a cold, low back pain, dysmenorrhea, postoperative pain, ankylosing spondylitis, headache, toothache, muscle pain, neuralgia, acute gout, psoriatic arthritis, soft tissue injury (sprain, contusion) and non-articular rheumatic disease (tendinitis, tenosynovitis, bursitis).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint diseas

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 199602438. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout and psoriatic arthritis, take 200 to 600 mg per dose 3 to 4 times a day. Up to a maximum of 3200 mg a day may be taken. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, take 30 to 40 mg per kg of body weight a day, divided into 3 to 4 doses. For mild to moderate pain and for a cold, take 200 to 400 mg per dose 3 to 4 times a day. Increase or decrease the amount appropriately according to age and symptoms. Children take the recommended amount per dose 3 to 4 times a day. For the recommended amount for each age group of children, refer to the approved product information.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • When non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics including this medicine are taken, serious cardiovascular thrombotic reactions, myocardial infarction and stroke that may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcer and perforation, may appear.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be taken by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, by patients who have or have had gastrointestinal ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding, by patients with severe blood abnormality, severe liver impairment, severe renal impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure, by patients who have or have had bronchial asthma, by patients who have or have had a hypersensitivity reaction such as asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic (including COX-2 inhibitors), by patients with pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), by pregnant women in the last 3 months of pregnancy, by patients receiving high-dose methotrexate as anticancer therapy, or by patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user has or has had blood abnormality, has a bleeding tendency, has or has had cirrhosis or liver impairment, has or has had renal impairment, has cardiac insufficiency, heart disease, high blood pressure, hypersensitivity, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, is elderly, is a child, or is a pregnant woman or a breast-feeding woman.
  • Do not take more than the recommended amount.
  • If an excessive amount has been taken, get prompt medical treatment even if there is no obvious symptom or sign.

Possible side effects

  • If any of the following appears, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: shock, anaphylactoid reaction, chest discomfort (heartburn), chills, difficulty breathing, fall in blood pressure; decreased hematocrit, decreased hemoglobin, aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, hematemesis, Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, thirst, stomatitis, abdominal distension, oral ulcer, constipation, black stools; mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), photosensitivity reaction (unknown frequency), drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency, angioneurotic edema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash; hepatitis, jaundice, hepatic dysfunction such as increases in GOT, GPT and alkaline phosphatase (ALP), liver impairment; hypersensitivity, anaphylactic reaction, asthma attack, urticaria, eczema, purpura (purple spots), rash, itching, asthma, bronchoconstriction, difficulty breathing, wheezing; visual disturbance such as scotoma (a blind area of the visual field), hearing loss, tinnitus, abnormal taste, vertigo, drowsiness, dizziness, depression, headache, cerebrovascular accident or nervousness; aseptic meningitis or meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness, etc.); fall in blood pressure, rise in blood pressure, palpitations, heart failure, myocardial infarction or angina; acute renal failure, oliguria (decreased urine), hematuria, proteinuria, increases in BUN and blood creatinine, hyperkalemia, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, reduced urine volume, generalized edema, shortness of breath, languor, periorbital edema, facial edema, malaise, fever, nosebleed, edema, peripheral edema, metabolic acidosis, loss of consciousness and convulsion.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics (NSAIDs).
  • People who are taking low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with ACE inhibitors, lithium, furosemide and thiazide diuretics, methotrexate, coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin), or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs).
  • Do not breast-feed while taking this medicine.

Those aged 15 years and over take 1 sachet (15 ml) at a time, those aged 11 years and over but under 15 years take 2/3 sachet (10 ml) at a time, those aged 8 years and over but under 11 years take 1/2 sachet (7.5 ml) at a time, those aged 5 years and over but under 8 years take 1/3 sachet (5 ml) at a time, those aged 3 years and over but under 5 years take 1/4 sachet (3.75 ml) at a time, and those aged 2 years and over but under 3 years take 1/5 sachet (3 ml) at a time, three times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

  • Patients with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their phenylalanine intake must not take this medicine.
  • This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolized to phenylalanine in the body.
  • The permitted daily amount, as recommended by the WHO, is 40 mg/kg per day or less as aspartame.
  • It should be used at the smallest possible amount.
  • For an adult weighing 60 kg, the maximum daily dose is 2.4 g.

Precautions for use

  • Patients hypersensitive to this medicine or with such a history, infants under 3 months of age, and children under 2 years of age must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, children under 2 years of age when it is absolutely necessary, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, elderly people, and people who are physically weak or who have a high fever should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Before taking this medicine, people with an allergic constitution, people who have experienced allergic symptoms caused by medicines such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, or itching, people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, or high blood pressure, and people with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that persists or recurs for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash, or a persistent headache should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Children should take it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness in which the skin becomes congested and red, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, or insomnia occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take other antitussive-expectorants, cold medicines or oral medicines containing antihistamines.
  • People who are taking MAO inhibitors used in the treatment of depression or Parkinson's disease, or who are within 2 weeks of stopping them, must not take this medicine.

Adults take 8 mL as 1 dose, those aged 11 years to under 15 years take 5 mL at a time, those aged 8 years to under 11 years take 4 mL at a time, those aged 3 years to under 8 years take 2 mL at a time, and those aged 2 years to under 3 years take 1.5 mL at a time, 3 times a day.   • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When giving it to children, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

  • If rash, redness, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, decreased urine volume, swelling of the face or of the hands and feet, heavy eyelids, stiffening of the hands, a rise in blood pressure, headache, or myopathy (weakness, cramps in the limbs, paralysis, etc.) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Do not take it together with other antitussives and expectorants, cold remedies, antihistamines, sedatives, or alcohol.

payloads.summary: This medicine is used as an adjunct in the treatment of chronic polyarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, arthropathy, ankylo
payloads.content:

Oral medicine (MFDS 201702324)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201702324. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used as an adjunct in the treatment of chronic polyarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, arthropathy, ankylosing spondylitis, painful swelling or inflammation after trauma and surgery, and infections accompanied by inflammation, pain, and fever.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used as an adjunct in the treatment of chronic polyarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, arthropathy, ankylo

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201702324. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults take 1 capsule (300 mg) at a time, 2 to 4 times a day. However, do not exceed 4 capsules (1,200 mg) a day.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious, potentially fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction, and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration, and perforation may occur.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with or a history of gastrointestinal ulcer, patients with bleeding in the gastrointestinal tract, the cerebral blood vessels, or other sites, severe blood disorders, severe liver disorder, severe kidney disorder, severe cardiac insufficiency, severe high blood pressure, or bronchial asthma or a history of it, those who have experienced asthma, urticaria, or an allergic reaction to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, patients being treated for pain before or after coronary artery (heart artery) bypass graft surgery (CABG), pregnant women at 6 months of pregnancy or later, nursing mothers, patients with inflammatory bowel disease such as Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis, and those who have experienced gastrointestinal bleeding or perforation from previous treatment with non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with or a history of blood disorders, patients with a bleeding tendency, patients with or a history of liver disorder or kidney disorder, patients with fluid retention (accumulation of body fluid) or heart failure, patients with high blood pressure, those who have experienced hypersensitivity, patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), elderly people, children aged 6 years and older, patients with stomach cancer or alcoholism, pregnant women in early or mid pregnancy and women who may be pregnant, patients with ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, cerebrovascular disease, or risk factors for cardiovascular disease (e.g., high blood pressure, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, smoking), patients with hepatic porphyria, patients who have had major surgery that caused blood loss, patients with a blood coagulation disorder or who are receiving anticoagulants, and those who have experienced hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 5 should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Considering the importance of the drug treatment, either stop breastfeeding or stop taking the drug.
  • Dizziness or fatigue may occur after taking this medicine, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.
  • When it is taken for a long period for an acute illness, in principle this should be limited to within 5 days.

Possible side effects

  • If the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: rarely shock (chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, lowered blood pressure, etc.); rarely blood disorders such as aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, agranulocytosis, pancytopenia, thrombocytopenia, decreased platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), and eosinophilia; indigestion, abdominal distension, heartburn, upper abdominal pain, diarrhea or constipation; occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, or stomach discomfort; rarely esophagitis, esophageal stricture, worsening of diverticula, nonspecific hemorrhagic colitis, ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, bloody stools, gastritis, or pancreatitis; very rarely thirst, stomatitis, erythema multiforme, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), or hair loss; occasionally angioedema; rarely Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency; occasionally rash, urticaria, itching, or purpura; rarely induction of an asthma attack, eczema, anaphylactic reactions, or photosensitivity reactions; rarely jaundice, elevated ALT, elevated AST, elevated ALP, abnormal liver function, hepatitis, or jaundice; occasionally rhinitis, bronchospasm, or acute pneumonia; rarely visual disturbances such as impaired vision and dark spots, hearing loss, tinnitus, or taste abnormality; fatigue, drowsiness, headache, or dizziness; occasionally anxiety, restlessness, confusion, or depression; rarely aseptic meningitis, severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, stiff neck, fever, or impaired consciousness; rarely mental abnormality, agitation, excitement, disorientation, or reversible toxic amblyopia; rarely lowered blood pressure, raised blood pressure, palpitations, oliguria, hematuria, proteinuria, elevated BUN and blood creatinine, hyperkalemia, decreased urine volume, generalized edema and the accompanying shortness of breath, or languor; rarely renal papillary necrosis, nephrotic syndrome, interstitial nephritis, peripheral edema, acute pulmonary edema, fluid retention, hypertension, heart failure, or reduced fertility in women; occasionally periorbital edema; very rarely malaise, fever, nosebleed, or worsening of inflammation.

Interactions

  • Do not take together with aspirin, other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, or high-dose methotrexate used in cancer chemotherapy (15 mg/week or more).
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are taking corticosteroids, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, sulfonylureas, ACE inhibitors, angiotensin II receptor antagonists, diuretics, lithium, coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin), baclofen, immunosuppressants (cyclosporine, tacrolimus, sirolimus), thrombolytics, ticlopidine, antithrombotic agents, medicines that increase blood potassium levels (trimethoprim, heparin, etc.), inducers of CYP2C8 or CYP2C9 (e.g., rifampicin, phenobarbital), low-dose methotrexate (less than 15 mg/week), antiplatelet agents, or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, if you take low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke, or if you have experienced hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 5.

This medicine is used to relieve various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, chills, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to relieve various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, chills

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201405342. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults aged 15 years and over take 1 packet (90 mL) at a time, those aged 11 years and over but under 15 years take 2/3 of a packet (about 60 mL) at a time, those aged 7 years and over but under 11 years take 1/2 of a packet (about 45 mL) at a time, those aged 3 years and over but under 7 years take 1/3 of a packet (about 30 mL) at a time, and those aged 2 years and over but under 3 years take 1/4 of a packet (about 22.5 mL) at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. If necessary it may be taken at bedtime, and in principle the interval between doses should be 4 hours.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of a hypersensitivity reaction appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients hypersensitive to this medicine or those who have experienced it, people who have had an asthma attack when taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics or cold medicines, and infants under 3 months of age and children under 2 years of age must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, the following should consult a doctor or pharmacist: infants and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza; children under 2 years of age when it is absolutely necessary; people with a constitution prone to urticaria, contact dermatitis, bronchial asthma, allergic rhinitis, migraine or food allergy; patients who have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine; people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, edema, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma or difficulty urinating; the elderly; people with a weak body or a high fever; people with persistent or recurrent stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or with ulcers or bleeding problems; pregnant women or women who may be pregnant; breastfeeding women; and people with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • When giving it to a child, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, difficulty urinating, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, rarely shock (urticaria, swelling, or chest tightness immediately after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, difficulty breathing, etc.), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome: accompanied by high fever, with severe symptoms such as rash and redness and burn-like blistering), asthma, liver function disorder (generalized lassitude, jaundice), interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever, etc.), pseudoaldosteronism (decreased urine volume, swelling of the face, hands and feet, heaviness of the eyelids, stiffening of the hands, raised blood pressure, headache, etc.), or myopathy (weakness, cramps in the limbs, paralysis) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.), antitussives and expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).
  • People who are within 2 weeks of stopping MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.) must not take this medicine.
  • If it is taken together with diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, potassium-containing preparations, licorice-containing preparations, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, etacrynic acid), or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide), consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile (appearing at a young age) rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), fever and pain due to a cold, back pain, dysmenorrhea, postoperative pain, ankylosing spondylitis, headache, toothache, muscle pain, neuralgia, acute gout, psoriatic arthritis, soft tissue injuries (sprains, contusions (bruises)), and non-articular rheumatic diseases (tendinitis, tenosynovitis, bursitis).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile (appearing at a young age) rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202300213. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout and psoriatic arthritis, adults take 200-600 mg of ibuprofen at a time, orally 3-4 times a day. Up to a maximum of 3200 mg a day may be given. For juvenile (occurring at a young age) rheumatoid arthritis, give 30-40 mg per kg of body weight a day orally in 3-4 divided doses. For mild and moderate pain and for colds, adults take 200-400 mg at a time, orally 3-4 times a day. Increase or decrease the dose as appropriate according to age and symptoms. For children, a single dose is 200-250 mg (10-13 ml) at 11-14 years of age and 150-200 mg (8-10 ml) at 7-10 years of age,
Children aged 3-6 years take 100-150 mg (5-8 ml) and children aged 1-2 years take 50-100 mg (3-5 ml), 3-4 times a day. For children weighing less than 30 kg, the daily amount must not exceed 500 mg (25 ml), and administration on an empty stomach should be avoided.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when they take this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic reactions, myocardial infarction, and stroke, which may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcers, and perforation may occur.
  • When non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics including this medicine are taken, serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions that may be fatal, such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcers, and perforation (a hole forming), may occur.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, gastrointestinal ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding or those who have experienced it, patients with severe blood abnormalities, severe liver disorder, severe renal disorder, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure, patients with bronchial asthma or those who have had it, those who have experienced asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics (including COX-2 inhibitors), patients with pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), women in the last 3 months of pregnancy, and patients receiving high-dose methotrexate as chemotherapy must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with blood abnormalities or those who have experienced them, patients with a tendency to bleed, patients with liver cirrhosis or liver disorder or those who have experienced it, patients with renal disorder or those who have experienced it, patients with cardiac insufficiency or heart disease, patients with high blood pressure, those who have experienced hypersensitivity, patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, the elderly and children, pregnant women, breastfeeding women, and people taking low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • Without the instruction of a doctor or pharmacist, do not take it for pain for more than 10 days (adults) or more than 5 days (children), and do not take it for fever for more than 3 days.
  • If pain or fever persists or worsens, or if new symptoms appear, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (chest distress (heartburn), chills, difficulty breathing, a drop in blood pressure, etc.), blood disorders such as decreased hematocrit, decreased hemoglobin, anemia, aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), or eosinophilia, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, Category

Who should ask first

How to take it

Adults and those 12 years and older take 2 tablets at a time, twice a day, and those 36 months and older but under 12 years take 1 tablet at a time, twice a day, dissolving it in the mouth or chewing it after meals.

  • Taking 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A a day may cause congenital malformations.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypercalcemia (a condition in which there is an excess of calcium in the blood), sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause), kidney disease or hypersensitivity to this medicine, nursing infants under 12 months of age, patients with kidney stones or severe renal failure, and patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption must not take this medicine.

  • Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids, or levodopa.
  • If you take it together with oral contraceptives containing estrogen, consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Because concomitant use with antialdosterone agents or triamterene may cause hyperkalemia, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Who should ask first

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and older and adults take 1 sachet (3 g) at a time, those aged 11 years to under 15 years take 2/3 sachet (2 g) at a time, and those aged 7 years to under 11 years take 1/2 sachet (1.5 g) at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • In patients taking acetaminophen, serious and potentially fatal skin reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) have been reported very rarely; if a skin rash or other signs of hypersensitivity appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen.
  • This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolized to phenylalanine in the body, so patients with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their intake of phenylalanine must not take it.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, people who have experienced asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, infants under 3 months of age, and patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, infants and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, children under 2 years of age, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, elderly people, people who are physically weak, people with an allergic constitution, people who have experienced allergic symptoms (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.), patients with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, edema, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), difficulty urinating, high fever, gastrointestinal problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain, or ulcers or bleeding problems, and patients with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, or emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts 1 week or more or recurs, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash, or persistent headache should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration exactly.
  • When giving it to a child, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If rash, redness, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty urinating, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, rarely shock symptoms (urticaria, swelling, and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweats, and difficulty breathing), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, liver function disorder, interstitial pneumonia (with cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever, etc.), pseudoaldosteronism (decreased urine volume, swelling of the face, hands and feet, heaviness of the eyelids, stiffening of the hands, rising blood pressure, headache, etc.), or myopathy (weakness, cramps in the limbs, paralysis, etc.) occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen, MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian drugs, etc.), antitussives and expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).
  • People who are taking MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian drugs, etc.) or are within 2 weeks of stopping them must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who are receiving diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, steroids, and the like should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, potassium-containing preparations, licorice-containing preparations, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, ethacrynic acid), or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide).
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of a hypersensitivity reaction appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.
  • If severe skin adverse reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis occur, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolized to phenylalanine in the body, so patients with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their phenylalanine intake must not take it.

Precautions for use

  • Patients hypersensitive to this medicine or with such a history, people who have had asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, infants (newborns) under 3 months of age, and patients with severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are a child aged 3 months and over but under 2 years, an infant or a child under 15 years of age who is infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, a person with an allergic constitution or a history of allergy to medicines, a person with liver, kidney, heart, or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), or difficulty urinating (passing urine), an elderly person, a person who is physically weak or who has a high fever, a person with persistent or recurring gastrointestinal problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain or with ulcers or bleeding problems, a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant, a breastfeeding woman, or a person with symptoms such as smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that persists or recurs for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash, or a persistent headache.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • When administering it to children, do so under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.
  • If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness (turning red from congestion), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema (swelling), difficulty urinating (passing urine), persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, shock symptoms (urticaria, swelling, and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, along with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome: accompanied by high fever, with severe symptoms such as rash and redness and blistering like burns), asthma, general fatigue, jaundice (the skin or the whites of the eyes take on a yellow color), interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by coughing, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, and fever), symptoms of ischemic colitis associated with the pseudoephedrine component (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding), or posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance, etc.) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.), antitussives and expectorants (cough and phlegm medicines), other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis [nasal inflammation], motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).
  • People who are within 2 weeks of stopping MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.) must not take this medicine.
  • People who are being given other medicines such as barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants and alcohol, diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, or steroids should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

How to take it

Adults take 1 capsule per dose, 1 time a day. Since this medicine is an enteric-coated capsule, it may be taken before meals with plenty of water.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or other salicylate preparations, patients with peptic ulcer, patients with aspirin-induced asthma (induction of asthma attacks by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, etc.) or those who have experienced it, patients with hemophilia, severe hepatic impairment, severe renal impairment, cardiac insufficiency, or a bleeding tendency, patients receiving concomitant methotrexate at a dose of 15 milligrams or more per week (15 mg/week), and pregnant women in the third trimester of pregnancy should not take this medicine.

  • Take care not to damage the enteric coating of this medicine.
  • If you are to undergo surgery (including dental surgery), you must tell the doctor in charge that you are taking an aspirin preparation and receive advice.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (for example, difficulty breathing, generalized flushing, angioedema, urticaria), asthma attacks, erythema, itching, nasal congestion, cardiac and respiratory disorders, occasionally rash, swelling, urticaria, rhinitis symptoms, conjunctivitis, rarely toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), exfoliative dermatitis, rarely aplastic anemia, anemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), ringing in the ears, hearing loss, dizziness, headache, agitation, rarely liver disorder, very rarely temporary liver damage with elevated liver transaminases, kidney disorder, acute renal failure, hyperventilation, metabolic acidosis, excessive drop in body temperature, collapse, or coldness of the limbs occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Loss of appetite, heartburn, stomach pain, nausea, and vomiting may occur.

  • Do not use it together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, salicylate preparations, or high-dose methotrexate.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with anticoagulants, thrombolytics or other platelet aggregation inhibitors, hemostatics, antidiabetic medicines (insulin preparations, tolbutamide, etc.), uricosuric agents (benzbromarone, probenecid), lithium preparations, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, digoxin, systemically acting adrenocortical hormone preparations (except hydrocortisone used as replacement therapy for Addison's disease), angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, valproic acid, or alkaline preparations (e.g. sodium bicarbonate, magnesium carbonate).
  • When taken together with alcohol, damage to the gastrointestinal mucosa may increase and bleeding time may be prolonged.

People aged 15 years and over and adults take 1 film per dose, 3 times a day, letting it dissolve in the mouth. The interval between doses must be 4 hours or more. This medicine (film) is a film that dissolves easily in water, so do not handle it with wet hands. This medicine (film) dissolves in the mouth immediately, but if it sticks to the throat, drink water and swallow it. Also, if there is little saliva and it is difficult to take, put water in the mouth and take it while it dissolves.

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilizers, antiparkinson drugs, etc.), other oral medicines for rhinitis, oral medicines containing antihistamines (cold remedies, antitussives and expectorants, motion sickness medicines, allergy medicines, etc.), or gastrointestinal analgesic and antispasmodic medicines.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and over take 24 mL at a time, those aged 11 years to under 15 years take 16 mL at a time, those aged 7 years to under 11 years take 12 mL at a time, those aged 3 years to under 7 years take 8 mL at a time, and those aged 2 years to under 3 years take 6 mL at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.   • Patients hypersensitive to this medicine, those who have experienced asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold medicines, infants (newborns) under 3 months of age, and breastfeeding women must not take this medicine.

  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • If rash and redness (congestion causing reddening), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema (swelling), difficulty urinating (passing urine), thirst (persistent or severe), light-headedness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, or, rarely, shock symptoms (urticaria, edema (swelling), chest tightness, etc. immediately after taking it, together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweats, and difficulty breathing), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) (severe symptoms accompanied by high fever, in which rash and redness and blisters like burns appear on the skin of the whole body or on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), asthma, liver function disorder (listlessness of the whole body, jaundice, etc.), or interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by coughing, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever, etc.) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

How it works

This medicine is used for disinfection of the patient's skin before surgery or before insertion of a syringe needle or a

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201801818. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the applicator from its packaging and hold it with the sponge facing downwards. Do not touch the sponge part of the applicator. Squeeze the applicator firmly only once so that the ampoule breaks and the solution comes out, and leave the broken ampoule inside the applicator. For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

Precautions for use

  • People with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine, isopropanol, or Yellow No. 5 and infants aged 2 months or younger should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use this medicine for disinfecting surgical instruments, or on nervous tissue (e.g., brain or spinal cord tissue), the eyes, ears, mouth, mucous membranes, genital mucous membranes, open wounds, or torn or damaged skin, or for general washing of the skin.
  • Before using this medicine, people with hypersensitivity to other medicines, people who have experienced allergic diseases such as asthma or who have a family history of them, people with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, and people with a drug-hypersensitive constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only on intact skin.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get in, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty breathing, redness, a sudden drop in blood pressure, urticaria, angioedema, etc.), occasionally rash, photosensitization, irritation, sensitization, erythema or inflammation, itching, dry and thinly peeling skin, local pain at the application site, or local skin reactions, or very rarely rash (e.g., erythematous, papular, or maculopapular), blisters, small blisters at the application site, a burning sensation of the skin, dermatitis, eczema, chemical burns in newborns, eye irritation, congestion, impaired vision, or eye damage occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

This medicine is used to relieve all the symptoms of a cold (runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills (feeling cold and shivering), fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to relieve all the symptoms of a cold (runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, cough,

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202401314. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Take the following single dose 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. Those aged 15 years and over take 1 sachet (20 mL) at a time, those aged 11 years and over but under 15 years take 2/3 of a sachet at a time, those aged 7 years and over but under 11 years take 1/2 of a sachet at a time, those aged 3 years and over but under 7 years take 1/3 of a sachet at a time, and those aged 2 years and over but under 3 years take 1/4 of a sachet at a time.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of hypersensitivity appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine, people who have experienced asthma when taking the ingredients of this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, and infants (newborns) under 3 months of age must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is an infant or young child under 2 years of age; if the user is an infant (nursing infant, newborn) or a child under 15 years of age who has or is suspected of having chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if you have an allergic constitution or have experienced allergic reactions (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), or difficulty urinating; if you are elderly, frail, or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain, or ulcer or bleeding problems; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant, or are breastfeeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or recurs for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever and rash or a persistent headache.
  • If the symptoms do not improve after taking 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When giving it to a child, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness (turning red from congestion), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema (swelling), difficulty urinating (passing urine), thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, rarely shock symptoms (urticaria, swelling, and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, along with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) (accompanied by high fever, with severe symptoms such as rash and redness and blistering like burns appearing on the skin all over the body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), asthma, liver function disorder (general fatigue, jaundice), or interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by coughing, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, and fever) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.), antitussive (cough-stopping) expectorants (phlegm remedies), other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis (nasal inflammation), motion sickness remedies, allergy remedies).
  • People within 2 weeks of stopping MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.) must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who are taking diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, or steroids should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, or alcohol.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

How to apply it

Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area several times in 1 day.

At a glance

Category

How it works

This medicine is used for the relief of the various symptoms of colds (sore throat, chills, fever, headache, joint pain,

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201900045. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Ordinarily, adults (aged 15 years and older) take 1 sachet (a single dose) at a time; those aged 11 years and older but under 15 years take 2/3 sachet (2/3 of the adult single dose) at a time; and those aged 7 years and older but under 11 years take 1/2 sachet (1/2 of the adult single dose) at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Serious skin reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), which can very rarely be fatal, have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of a hypersensitivity reaction appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.
  • This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolized to phenylalanine in the body, so patients with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their phenylalanine intake must not take it.

Precautions for use

  • Patients hypersensitive to this medicine, those who have experienced asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold medicines, infants (nursing infants) under 3 months of age, patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption, and patients with severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, infants and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, children under 2 years of age, people with an allergic constitution or who have experienced an allergic reaction (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.), people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, edema or gastroduodenal ulcer, the elderly, people with a weak body or a high fever, people with persistent or recurrent stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or with ulcers or bleeding problems, and pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When giving it to a child, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If the following occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia; rarely shock symptoms (urticaria, swelling (puffiness), and chest tightness right after taking it, together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing); Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) (severe symptoms accompanied by high fever, with rash and redness and blistering like burns appearing on the skin all over the body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes); asthma; liver function disorder (general lethargy, jaundice, etc.); interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever, etc.); pseudoaldosteronism (decreased urine volume, swelling of the face, hands, and feet, heaviness of the eyelids, stiffening of the hands, raised blood pressure or headache, etc.); or myopathy (weakness, cramping of the limbs, paralysis).

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.), antitussives and expectorants, other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness remedies, antiallergic remedies).
  • If you take it together with antidiabetic drugs, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants and alcohol, potassium-containing preparations, licorice-containing preparations, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, ethacrynic acid), or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide), consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

Adolescents aged 12 years and older and adults take 1 tablet at a time, 1 time a day.

This medicine is used to relieve various symptoms of a cold, such as runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to relieve various symptoms of a cold, such as runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202302835. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adolescents aged 15 years and older and adults take 1 packet at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. If necessary, it may be taken at bedtime. Keep the interval between doses at 4 hours.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious and potentially fatal skin reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of hypersensitivity appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen.
  • If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking this medicine and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or a history of it, those who have experienced asthma when taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, infants under 3 months of age and children under 2 years of age, and patients with severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, children under 2 years of age for whom it is absolutely necessary, infants and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, people with an allergic constitution, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, those in whom symptoms of ischemic colitis such as sudden abdominal pain or rectal bleeding related to the pseudoephedrine component appear, those who have experienced allergic symptoms caused by medicines such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching, elderly people, and people with a weak constitution or a high fever should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Before taking this medicine, people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric and duodenal ulcer, glaucoma or difficulty urinating, people with persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort and stomach pain or with ulcers or bleeding problems, and people with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, cough with excessive phlegm, cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, chronic cough, or cough accompanied by fever and rash or persistent headache should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If symptoms do not improve after taking 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • Drowsiness may occur while taking this medicine.
  • Avoid driving a car or operating machinery.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty urinating, (persistent or severe) thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, or insomnia occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If, rarely, shock (anaphylaxis) occurs, which may appear immediately after taking it as hives, swelling, and chest tightness together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing, or if skin-mucosa-eye syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, liver dysfunction such as general lethargy and jaundice, interstitial pneumonia, or symptoms of reversible posterior encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome such as sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, or visual disturbance occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take antitussives and expectorants, other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).
  • People who are taking MAO inhibitors, which are used to treat depression and Parkinson's disease, or who are within 2 weeks of stopping them, must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who are receiving diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, steroids, etc. should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Patients who are receiving barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, or alcohol should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

At a glance

Category

How it works

This drug is used for reducing fever when fever occurs due to acute upper respiratory tract infection.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201000953. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Children aged 6 months and over take 0.4 to 0.6 mL/kg (5 to 7 mg/kg) at a time as needed, at intervals of 4 to 6 hours, not exceeding a maximum of 4 times a day (28 mg/kg). For children weighing 30 kg or less, do not exceed a maximum of 25 mL (300 mg) a day. If the body weight is known it is more appropriate to give the dose based on body weight, so refer to the approved labelling for the recommended doses by age group.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious, potentially fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction, and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration, and perforation may occur.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, peptic ulcer, severe blood abnormalities, severe liver disorder, severe renal disorder, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure, patients with bronchial asthma or those who have had it, those who have experienced asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics (including COX-2 inhibitors), patients being treated for pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), and pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, those who have experienced peptic ulcer, patients with blood abnormalities or those who have experienced them, patients with a tendency to bleed (platelet dysfunction may occur), patients with liver disorder or those who have experienced it, patients with renal disorder or those who have experienced it, patients with cardiac insufficiency, high blood pressure or a history of hypersensitivity, patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, the elderly and children, patients with stomach cancer, and people taking low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • When it is taken over a long period for an acute illness, as a rule this should be limited to within 5 days.

Possible side effects

  • If, rarely, shock (chest distress, chills, difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure, etc.), blood disorders such as aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, granulocytopenia, thrombocytopenia, impaired platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) or eosinophilia, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) or Lyell's syndrome (toxic epidermal necrolysis), drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency, acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, induction of an asthma attack, urticaria, eczema or purpura occurs, or occasionally rash, itching, visual disturbance (blurred vision, dark spots, etc.), aseptic meningitis, severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or impaired consciousness, acute renal failure, oliguria, blood in the urine, protein in the urine, a rise in BUN or blood creatinine, or hyperkalemia occurs, stop taking the medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea or stomach discomfort, very rarely dry mouth, stomatitis, a feeling of abdominal fullness or constipation, rarely jaundice, a rise in GOT, GPT or ALP, hearing loss, tinnitus, taste disturbance, a fall in blood pressure, a rise in blood pressure, palpitations, decreased urine volume, generalized edema, shortness of breath, listlessness or acute pulmonary edema, occasionally periorbital edema, and very rarely malaise, fever or nosebleeds may occur.

Interactions

  • Do not use this medicine together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, aspirin or high-dose methotrexate.
  • If used together with glucocorticoids, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, sulfonylureas, a combination of a diuretic and an antihypertensive, ACE inhibitors, furosemide, lithium, low-dose methotrexate or coumarin anticoagulants (warfarin, etc.), consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Adults usually take 15 to 30 mL orally a day before breakfast for the first 2 to 3 days, and then continue with 10 to 15 mL a day. In severe cases, up to 45 mL may be given.   • Before taking this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, infants, young children, and children, elderly people, and patients with diabetes, fructose intolerance, fluid and electrolyte imbalance, acute gastritis, or chronic constipation should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If loose stools or diarrhea occur, reduce the dose or stop administration.
  • When a patient who has taken this medicine undergoes electrocautery during proctoscopy or colonoscopy, the presence of a high concentration of hydrogen gas in the intestine creates a risk of explosion from an electrical flame, so perform the examination after completely cleansing the bowel with a non-fermentable solution.

  • If belching, cramping abdominal discomfort, diarrhea, or occasionally borborygmus, a feeling of abdominal fullness, abdominal pain, loss of appetite, nausea, or vomiting occurs, or If there is a sudden change in bowel habits, or if there is no improvement in constipation after taking it for about 1 week, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist or doctor.

Interactions

  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine together with glycosidase inhibitors such as acarbose, broad-spectrum antibiotics, diuretics, corticoids, amphotericin B, cardiac glycosides, or antacids.

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the applicator from its packaging and hold it with the sponge facing downwards. Do not touch the sponge part of the applicator.   • If it does, the solution may become contaminated or cloudy from eye mucus, mold and the like.

  • If eye irritation rarely appears, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • When you use this medicine at the same time as another eye drop, use the other eye drop first and use this medicine about 10 minutes later.

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202104595. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and over take 1 sachet (20 mL), those aged 11 years and over but under 15 years take 2/3 of a sachet, those aged 7 years and over but under 11 years take 1/2 of a sachet, those aged 3 years and over but under 7 years take 1/3 of a sachet, and those aged 2 years and over but under 3 years take 1/4 of a sachet, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. Do not administer it to children under 2 years of age. As a rule, allow an interval of 4 hours between doses.

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of a hypersensitivity reaction appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine or have experienced such hypersensitivity, people who have had an asthma attack when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold medicines, infants (newborns) under 3 months of age, and people who are taking MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.) or are within 2 weeks of having stopped them must not take this medicine.

  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • Do not take it continuously over a long period.
  • When giving it to a child, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness (turning red from congestion), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema (swelling), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, shock symptoms (urticaria, swelling, and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, along with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome: accompanied by high fever, with severe symptoms such as rash and redness and blistering like burns), asthma, general fatigue, jaundice (the skin or the whites of the eyes take on a yellow color), or interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by coughing, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, and fever) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use the eye drops

When necessary, put 1 drop at a time into each eye, several times a day. When you put it into the eye, gently pull the lower eyelid down and put one drop into the lower conjunctival sac while looking upward.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user has severe eye pain, has glaucoma, or has experienced allergic symptoms caused by eye drops, such as redness of the eye, itching, swelling or rash.
  • Use this medicine only as eye drops, that is, only as a medicine to be put into the eye.
  • If the symptoms worsen or last for 3 days or more, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Wash the hands thoroughly before use.
  • When using a single-use product for the first time, discard the first 1 to 2 drops without instilling them, in order to remove any fragments of the container that may be produced when it is opened.
  • After opening, use a single-use product only once and discard the remaining solution and the container, and use a preservative-free multi-use product for up to 4 weeks only.
  • Do not let the tip of the container touch the eyelid or the eyelashes.
  • If it does, the solution may become contaminated or cloudy from eye mucus, mold and the like.
  • Also, do not use the medicine if it has become cloudy.
  • To prevent contamination, do not share it with others.
  • This medicine can be used even while contact lenses are being worn.
  • Follow the prescribed directions and amounts.

Possible side effects

  • If eye irritation rarely appears, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • When you use this medicine at the same time as another eye drop, use the other eye drop first and use this medicine about 10 minutes later.
