Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202400280. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults take 1 sachet (bottle) at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals, with an interval of 4 hours between doses.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, in patients taking acetaminophen, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported, and if a skin rash or another sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Those with hypersensitivity to this medicine or a history of it, those who have experienced asthma when taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, children under 2 years of age, and people who are taking MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.) or are within 2 weeks of stopping them must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, infants and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza (if there are changes in behavior accompanied by nausea or vomiting, this may be an early symptom of Reye's syndrome, a rare but serious illness, so consult a doctor), people with an allergic constitution, those who have experienced allergic symptoms caused by medicines (for example, fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.), people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, edema (swelling) or gastric and duodenal ulcer, elderly people, people with a weak constitution or a high fever, people with persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort and stomach pain or with ulcers or bleeding problems, and pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking about 5 to 6 doses, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness (congestion and reddening), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema (swelling), dizziness, high anion gap metabolic acidosis (HAGMA), or, rarely, shock (urticaria, swelling (puffiness), and chest tightness right after taking the medicine, together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing, etc.), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) (severe symptoms accompanied by high fever, with rash and redness (congestion and reddening) and burn-like blisters appearing on the skin over the whole body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), asthma, liver dysfunction (general languor, jaundice (the skin or the whites of the eyes turn yellow)), interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by a dry cough (a cough without phlegm), shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever, etc.), pseudoaldosteronism (decreased urine volume, swelling of the face, hands and feet, heavy eyelids, stiffening of the hands, raised blood pressure, headache, etc.), or myopathy (weakness, cramps in the limbs, paralysis, etc.) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with antitussive (cough-stopping) expectorants (phlegm remedies), other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis (nasal inflammation), motion sickness remedies, allergy remedies).
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, or flucloxacillin.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

Category

How it works

This medicine is used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, ph

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202403031. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

People aged 15 years and older take 1 sachet (20 mL), those aged 11 years or older and under 15 years take 2/3 of a sachet, those aged 7 years or older and under 11 years take 1/2 of a sachet, those aged 3 years or older and under 7 years take 1/3 of a sachet, and those aged 2 years or older and under 3 years take 1/4 of a sachet, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. If necessary, a dose may be taken at bedtime, and as a rule the interval between doses should be 4 hours. Do not give this medicine to children under 2 years of age.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of a hypersensitivity reaction appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.
  • If severe skin adverse reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis occur, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Precautions for use

  • Those with hypersensitivity to this medicine or a history of it, people who have experienced asthma when taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics, or cold medicines, children under 2 years of age, nursing mothers, people who are taking MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian drugs, etc.) or are within 2 weeks of stopping them, patients with severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure, and patients with severe acute or chronic kidney disease/renal failure must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, infants and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, people who have developed sudden abdominal pain in connection with pseudoephedrine, those with an allergic constitution, those who have experienced allergic symptoms to medicines (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.), people with liver, kidney, heart, or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision), or difficulty urinating, elderly people, people who are physically weak or have a high fever, people with persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain or with ulcer or bleeding problems, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, nursing mothers, and people who smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or longer, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash, or persistent headache should consult a doctor or pharmacist Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • When giving this medicine to children, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • If symptoms do not improve after taking 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Drowsiness may occur while taking this medicine.
  • Avoid driving a car or operating machinery.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty urinating, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, high anion gap metabolic acidosis, shock symptoms such as urticaria and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweats and difficulty breathing, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) (severe symptoms with high fever, rash and redness, and burn-like blisters), asthma, general listlessness, jaundice, or cough with shortness of breath, difficulty breathing and fever occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take it together with antitussives and expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, antihistamines, or preparations containing diphenhydramine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who are receiving diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants and alcohol, flucloxacillin, barbiturates, or tricyclic antidepressants should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use the eye drops

Put 1 to 2 drops into the affected eye as needed.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine must not use it.
  • Before using this medicine, people with severe eye pain and those who have experienced allergic symptoms from eye drops such as redness of the eye, itching, swelling, or rash should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use this medicine only for instillation, that is, as a medicine put into the eye.
  • If you swallow this medicine by mistake, get help from a doctor or another professional immediately.
  • If symptoms worsen or last for 72 hours or longer, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not reuse it after 1 use.
  • After instilling it in the eye, discard the remaining solution and the container.
  • To avoid contamination of this medicine and damage to the eye, do not let the tip of the container touch the eye or any outside surface.
  • Do not use it if the color of the medicine has changed or if it has become cloudy.
  • Do not use it as a wetting solution for soft contact lenses or while wearing soft contact lenses.
  • Remove contact lenses before using this medicine.
  • Put them back on 15 minutes after instilling it in the eye.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.

How to apply it

For sterilizing and disinfecting the hands and arms of the surgeon, put 5 mL of this medicine on the hands and arms, rub it in well for about 5 minutes to produce plenty of lather, and then rinse it off thoroughly with running water. Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and over and adults take 2 capsules at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. Those aged 8 years and over but under 15 years take 1 capsule at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious and potentially fatal skin reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of a hypersensitivity reaction appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.
  • If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Precautions for use

  • Patients hypersensitive to this medicine and those who have experienced it, those who have experienced asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold medicines, infants under 3 months of age, and people who are taking MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinson drugs, etc.) or are within 2 weeks of stopping them must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, the following should consult a doctor or pharmacist: infants and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza; infants and young children aged 3 months and over but under 2 years; pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women; the elderly; people with a weak body; people with an allergic constitution or who have experienced allergic symptoms (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.); and patients with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), difficulty urinating, high fever, stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, ulcers or bleeding problems, smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • When giving it to a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If rash, redness, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, difficulty urinating, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, shock symptoms (urticaria, edema and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms accompanied by high fever, with rash and redness and blistering like a burn appearing on the skin all over the body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, asthma, generalized listlessness, jaundice, interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by coughing, breathlessness, difficulty breathing and fever), or ischemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding) occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen, MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.), antitussives and expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).
  • If it is taken together with diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, or alcohol, consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

Spray and apply an appropriate amount several times in 1 day.

People aged 15 years and older and adults take 2 tablets as 1 dose, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of a hypersensitivity reaction appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it about 5 to 6 times, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • If rash, redness, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, or, rarely, shock symptoms after taking it (urticaria, swelling, and chest tightness right after taking the medicine, together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms accompanied by high fever, with rash and redness and burn-like blisters appearing on the skin over the whole body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), asthma, general languor, jaundice, interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by coughing, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, and fever), pseudoaldosteronism (decreased urine volume, swelling of the face, hands and feet, heavy eyelids, stiffening of the hands, raised blood pressure, or headache), or myopathy (weakness, cramps in the limbs, paralysis) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Who should ask first

How it works

This medicine is used for the relief of the various symptoms of colds (runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore thro

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201802575. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

People aged 15 years and older and adults take 2 tablets as 1 dose, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious and potentially fatal skin reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of a hypersensitivity reaction appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.
  • If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, those who have experienced asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, infants (nursing infants, newborns) under 3 months of age, and patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption must not take this medicine.Before taking this medicine, infants (nursing infants, newborns) infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza and children under 15 years of age, children under 2 years of age, those with an allergic constitution, those who have experienced allergic reactions (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.), people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, edema (swelling), gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), or difficulty urinating (passing urine), elderly people, physically weak people or people with a high fever, people with heartburn, gastric discomfort, stomach pain, ulcer, or bleeding problems, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, and patients who smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough persisting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever and rash or persistent headache should consult a doctor or pharmacist.Strictly observe the specified dosage and administration.Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it about 5 to 6 times, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema (swelling), difficulty urinating (passing urine), thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, rarely shock symptoms (urticaria, edema (swelling), or chest tightness immediately after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, difficulty breathing, etc.), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) (accompanied by high fever, with severe symptoms such as rash and redness (congested and reddened skin) and burn-like blistering appearing on the skin over the whole body, the mouth, or the mucous membranes of the eyes), asthma, liver function disorder (generalized lassitude, jaundice (the skin or the whites of the eyes turn yellow), etc.), interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever, etc.), weakness, cramps in the limbs, or paralysis occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.), antitussives (which stop coughing) and expectorants (phlegm remedies), other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis (nasal inflammation), motion sickness remedies, anti-allergy remedies).
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol, potassium-containing preparations, licorice-containing preparations, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, etacrynic acid), or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide).
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Vaginal medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the local treatment of candidal vaginitis, trichomonal vaginitis, vaginitis caused by non-spec

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 199700636. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to insert it

Dilute 30 mL of povidone-iodine 10% (available iodine 1%) in about 1 L of warm water and wash the inside and the outside of the vagina 1 to 2 times a day. For germicidal vaginal washing, local washing and deodorizing, wash 1 to 2 times a week.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be used by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, by patients with thyroid dysfunction (especially nodular goiter, endemic goiter, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, etc.), by patients with renal failure, by newborns and infants under 6 months of age, by patients with dermatitis herpetiformis, or by patients before or after radioactive iodine treatment.
  • Before using this medicine, patients in a serious condition (burn patients, etc.), patients who have had a thyroid disease, patients who have had renal failure, and pregnant or breast-feeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If it has been used right before delivery, wash the newborn's eyes and bathe the baby as soon as possible after the delivery so that the medicine does not remain on the skin.
  • Do not use it for the eyes or internally.
  • If the undiluted solution gets into the eyes, rinse them out immediately with clean water.
  • Do not mix it with other preparations for use.
  • When this medicine is used on a patient with extensive burns, provide sufficient fluids.
  • Because this medicine has a spermicidal action, do not use it if pregnancy is desired.

Possible side effects

  • Anaphylactoid symptoms (difficulty breathing, flushing, urticaria, etc.) and hypersensitivity in the form of iododerma may rarely appear, pain, itching, a feeling of irritation, rash, redness and dermatitis may occasionally appear, and a burning sensation, skin ulcer, contact dermatitis and skin discoloration may rarely appear.

Interactions

  • Do not use this medicine together with hydrogen peroxide.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when using it together with lithium, chlorhexidine, sulfadiazine and silver compounds, alkalis, preparations containing mercury, or enzyme-based wound treatments.
  • This medicine may damage latex or rubber products such as condoms and vaginal contraceptive diaphragms.

How to use the eye drops

Put 1 to 2 drops into the affected eye as needed.

  • Do not use it if the color of the medicine has changed or if it has become cloudy.
  • Do not use it as a wetting solution for soft contact lenses or while wearing soft contact lenses.
  • Remove contact lenses before using this medicine.
  • Put them back on 15 minutes after instilling it in the eye.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.

  • Because of its high viscosity, vision may become temporarily blurred when this medicine is instilled into the eye.

Interactions

  • When this medicine is used at the same time as other eye drops, leave an interval of at least 15 minutes before using this medicine.

How it works

Why this one

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

After the hair and the scalp are completely dry, apply 0.5 to 1 mL of this medicine to the affected area only, twice a day (morning and evening), for at least 4 months, and do not let the total daily amount exceed 2 mL.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be used by women, people under 18 years of age, patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with a cardiovascular disease (coronary artery disease, arrhythmia, congestive heart failure, valvular heart disease, treated or untreated high blood pressure, low blood pressure), patients who have no hereditary factor for hair loss, patients with sudden patchy hair loss, patients with a scalp abnormality such as erythema, inflammation, infection, irritation or pain of the scalp, psoriasis or sunburn, patients with hair loss of unknown cause, patients who are using another medicine for the scalp, patients who have shaved the scalp, or patients who tolerate the 2 % strength poorly.
  • Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is elderly, has edema, has thyroid dysfunction (hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism), has local exfoliation, dermatitis, psoriasis of the scalp or a severe burn, or has a history of heart disease.
  • Use this medicine externally only and do not use it on any area other than the scalp.
  • Do not use an occlusive dressing.
  • Because this medicine may cause burning and irritation of the eyes, be careful to keep it out of the eyes, and if it touches a sensitive area such as the eyes, broken skin or a mucous membrane, rinse it off immediately with clean water.
  • Use hair styling products after this medicine has dried, and when using it in the evening, use it 2 to 4 hours before bedtime so that it can dry.
  • Because circulation of air over the scalp may reduce the effect of this medicine, do not use a hair dryer to speed up its drying.

Possible side effects

  • If any of the following appears, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: itching, scaling, erythema, redness, dermatitis, dry skin, excessive hair growth at sites other than the area where this medicine was applied (facial hair growth in women), folliculitis, local irritation including a burning sensation and skin eruption, exfoliation, hair loss, skin abscess, acne, nail disorder, seborrhea, eczema, hair abnormality, bronchitis, upper respiratory tract infection, sinusitis, difficulty breathing, occasional diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, chest pain, change in blood pressure, change in pulse, palpitations, increased heart rate, pericardial effusion, pericarditis, embolism, tachycardia, worsening of pre-existing angina or induction of angina in a person with undiagnosed coronary artery disease, shortness of breath, fracture, back pain, tendinitis, pain, neuritis (including polyneuritis), weakness, dizziness, headache, feeling dazed, fainting, hepatitis, edema, kidney stones, inflammation and fluid retention, fever, urticaria, allergic rhinitis, systemic erythema and facial swelling, chills, eye irritation, bitter taste, otitis (especially otitis externa), change in taste, visual disturbance, erectile dysfunction, stabbing pain, or sudden unexplained weight gain.

Interactions

  • Do not use it together with other medicines for the scalp, medicines that promote absorption through the skin (for example topical corticosteroids, retinoids, petrolatum, dithranol), or vasodilators (for example guanethidine, etc.).

How to take it

People aged 15 years and older take 1 sachet (20 mL) as 1 dose, those aged 11 years or older and under 15 years take 2/3 of a sachet as 1 dose, those aged 7 years or older and under 11 years take 1/2 of a sachet as 1 dose, those aged 3 years or older and under 7 years take 1/3 of a sachet as 1 dose, and those aged 2 years or older and under 3 years take 1/4 of a sachet as 1 dose, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals, with an interval of 4 hours between doses.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of hypersensitivity appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.
  • This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolized to phenylalanine in the body, so patients with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their phenylalanine intake should not take it.

Precautions for use

  • People with hypersensitivity to this medicine, people who have experienced asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, infants under 3 months of age and children under 2 years of age, and people who are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian drugs, etc.) or who stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks should not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, infants and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, people with an allergic constitution, people who have experienced allergic symptoms from medicines (e.g., fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.), people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (e.g., eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), or difficulty urinating, elderly people, people who are physically weak or have a high fever, people whose gastrointestinal problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain persist or recur or who have ulcers or bleeding problems, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, and patients with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, or emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts 1 week or more or recurs, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash, or persistent headache should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration exactly.
  • When giving it to a child, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness (congestion and reddening), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, difficulty urinating, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, or, rarely, shock symptoms (urticaria and chest tightness right after taking the medicine, together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome: severe symptoms accompanied by high fever, with rash and redness and burn-like blisters), asthma, general languor, jaundice (the skin or the whites of the eyes turn yellow), coughing, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, or fever occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with antitussive expectorants, other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness remedies, allergy remedies).
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, or alcohol.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.

  • Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen, MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinson drugs, etc.), antitussives (which stop coughing) and expectorants (phlegm medicines), other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).

  • It must not be taken by mouth; use it vaginally only.
  • Douching is not recommended after using this medicine, so if douching is necessary, do it at least 6 hours after intercourse.

  • If abdominal pain, fever, chills, a foul odor in the vaginal discharge, a burning sensation, itching, rash or other irritation of the vagina or penis in yourself or your sexual partner, difficulty urinating or pain on urination, or pregnancy occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Who should ask first

Before using this medicine, brush your teeth and rinse your mouth with plenty of water. 2 to 3 times a day, after meals and after brushing, apply an appropriate amount of this medicine directly to the inflamed area in the mouth using the nozzle, leave it for about 1 minute, and then spit it out.   • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine must not use this medicine.

  • Do not take it orally.
  • Do not use it on or around the eyes or ears, and if it is applied there by mistake, rinse thoroughly with water.

  • If you apply too much of this medicine, wash it off with water.
  • It may cause discoloration of oral surfaces such as the tooth surfaces, dental prostheses, and the underside of the tongue.

  • This medicine does not combine well with soap or with the anionic substances that are common ingredients of toothpaste, so do not use this medicine at the same time as those ingredients; after brushing your teeth, rinse your mouth with plenty of water and use this medicine at least 5 minutes later.
  • After using this medicine, refrain from eating food or drinking beverages containing sugar.

Topical medicine (MFDS 201600079)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201600079. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for fungal skin infections caused by dermatophytes (athlete's foot, jock itch (tinea cruris), ringworm).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for fungal skin infections caused by dermatophytes (athlete's foot, jock itch (tinea cruris), ring

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201600079. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area (diseased site) 1 time a day.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, and infants and children should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use it on the eyes or the area around the eyes, on mucous membranes (inside the mouth, inside the nose, the vagina), on the scrotum or external genitalia, on eczema, on diseased areas with severe moistness (dampness), skin breakdown, cracking, or injury (wounds), on the nails, or on the scalp.
  • Before using this medicine, people with an allergic constitution, patients whose diseased area is on the face or is widespread or has become purulent (festering), and patients with hypersensitivity to propylene glycol or those who have experienced it should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration exactly.
  • Do not use it while the diseased area or the area around it is dirty.
  • Do not touch your eyes or mucous membranes with hands that have this medicine on them.
  • Be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get into the eyes, rinse immediately with cold or lukewarm water.
  • This medicine is for external use only.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, swelling, irritation, a feeling of heat, scaling, desquamation (peeling of the skin like dandruff or flakes), skin maceration, dry skin and a feeling of skin tightness, or cracking of the skin occur, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

At a glance

Category

How it works

This medicine is used for the sterilization and disinfection of torn wounds, burns and wounds, the sterilization and dis

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200713754. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area (diseased site) several times a day.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be used by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, by patients with thyroid dysfunction (especially nodular goiter, endemic goiter, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, etc.), renal failure, dermatitis herpetiformis, by patients before or after radioactive iodine treatment, or by newborns and infants under 6 months of age.
  • Before using this medicine, patients in a serious condition (burn patients, etc.), patients with a thyroid disease, patients who have had renal failure, and a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant and a breast-feeding woman should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not use it for the eyes or internally.
  • Be careful to keep it out of the eyes, and if it does get into the eyes, rinse them immediately with clean water.
  • Do not mix it with other preparations for use.
  • Because soaps weaken the germicidal action of this medicine, wash them off thoroughly before use.
  • Wash and disinfect the affected area thoroughly.
  • When it is used on a severe wound, use distilled water for injection or sterile purified water as the diluent, and do not use tap water or purified water.

Possible side effects

  • If symptoms of shock (difficulty breathing, flushing, urticaria, itching, swelling, heartburn and at the same time pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, shortness of breath, etc.) or iododerma rarely appear, if pain, a feeling of irritation, rash, redness or dermatitis occasionally appears, or if a burning sensation, skin ulcer, contact dermatitis or skin discoloration rarely appears, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not use this medicine together with hydrogen peroxide.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when using it together with lithium preparations, chlorhexidine, sulfadiazine and silver compounds, alkalis, preparations containing mercury, or enzyme-based wound healing preparations.

This medicine is used to reduce the tactile sensitivity of the male genitals.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to reduce the tactile sensitivity of the male genitals.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201904494. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Apply 0.25 to 0.66 g of the cream (23 to 62 mg as lidocaine) 5 to 15 minutes before sexual intercourse. The amount and the application time differ from person to person, so use the lowest effective amount and do not use more than 2 g (184 mg as lidocaine) within 24 hours.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be used by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or to other amide-type local anesthetics, by patients with a wound or inflammation at the application site, or when the partner is pregnant.
  • Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user has a liver or kidney disease or hypersensitivity to propylene glycol.
  • Use it externally only.
  • Do not use it in the eyes or the nose.
  • It is preferable not to apply it to the same area repeatedly.

Possible side effects

  • If a rash or irritation appears in the user or in the partner, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

payloads.title: Topical medicine (MFDS 201903112)
payloads.summary: This medicine is used for difficulty in expectorating sputum in bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis, pu
payloads.content:

Topical medicine (MFDS 201903112)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201903112. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for difficulty in expectorating sputum in bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis, pulmonary tuberculosis, emphysema, upper respiratory tract inflammation (pharyngitis and laryngitis), lung abscess, pneumonia, cystic fibrosis and postoperative pulmonary complications, and for the preparation and aftercare of bronchography, bronchoscopy, lung cancer cytology and tracheostomy.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for difficulty in expectorating sputum in bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis, pu

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201903112. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

For nebulization therapy using a face mask, mouthpiece, or tracheostomy, nebulize 1 to 10 mL every 2 to 6 hours. The recommended amount is 3 to 5 mL nebulized 3 to 4 times a day. Nebulization therapy using a mist tent or an inhalation device (Croupette) is a method needed in special cases and is used on an individual basis according to the patient's personal needs and the convenience of the administration method. This method of administration requires a large volume of solution, and sometimes up to about 300 mL may be required for a single treatment. The recommended amount should be a volume that can maintain a very dense, fog-like state inside the tent or inhalation device throughout the treatment period. Intermittent or continuous long-term administration is desirable. For direct instillation, administer 1 to 2 mL every hour. For the routine treatment of patients who have had a tracheostomy, administer 1 to 2 mL through the tracheostomy every 1 to 4 hours. When administering directly to a specific part of the bronchial tree of the lung by inserting a small plastic catheter into the trachea under local anesthesia and a direct incision, administer 2 to 5 mL every 1 to 4 hours using a syringe connected to the catheter. For diagnostic bronchography, administer 1 to 2 mL 2 to 3 times before performing the bronchography, by nebulization or by instillation into the bronchi.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine should not use it.
  • Before using this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, patients with bronchial asthma or accompanying respiratory insufficiency, elderly people, and children should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • It is not used as an injection or as eye drops.
  • After nebulization therapy the face mask may stick to the face, but it comes off easily when washed with water.

Possible side effects

  • A slight odor (a sulfurous smell), occasionally nausea, vomiting and loss of appetite, and rarely bloody sputum, chills, fever, runny nose, stomatitis, drowsiness, a feeling of pressure in the chest, and irritation of the trachea and bronchi may occur.

Interactions

  • When it is necessary to use this medicine together with an antibiotic, inhale them separately, or give the antibiotic by injection or orally.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the early treatment of recurrent herpes labialis.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202002583. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Adults use an appropriate amount, enough to cover the affected area fully up to its edges, 5 times a day for 5 days. Start treatment as soon as possible, as soon as the initial symptoms and signs appear. Limit the treatment period with this medicine to 5 days or less.

Precautions for use

  • Do not use this medicine in patients hypersensitive to it, in patients with bacterial (tuberculosis, syphilis, etc.), fungal (candidiasis, tinea, etc.), viral (herpes zoster, chickenpox, vaccinia, etc., excluding herpes simplex), or animal-borne (scabies, pubic lice, etc.) skin infections, in patients whose immune system is severely impaired such as bone marrow transplant patients or AIDS patients, in patients with eczematous otitis externa with a perforated eardrum, ulcers (excluding Behcet's disease), burns or frostbite of deep second degree or worse, perioral dermatitis, acne vulgaris, or rosacea, in breastfeeding women, in children under 18 years of age, in patients with or with a history of myocardial infarction, or on the eyes, nose, inside of the mouth, or genitals.
  • Before using this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and elderly people should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not breastfeed while using this medicine.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.

Possible side effects

  • If commonly a feeling of dryness or peeling of the skin, occasionally a temporary burning sensation or numbness, rarely erythema, pigmentation, or application site reactions including the signs and symptoms of inflammation, contact dermatitis, impetigo contagiosa, folliculitis, candidiasis, tinea, boils, skin irritation, stabbing pain, fever, a burning sensation, rash, redness, flushing, itching, dry skin, pustular dermatitis, allergic contact dermatitis, prickly heat, miliaria, worsening of wounds, bedsores, pustulosis, a rise in intraocular pressure or glaucoma when it is used on the skin of the eyelids, or blurred vision of unknown frequency occurs, stop using the medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Use 15 mL per dose, twice a day: rinse the mouth or gargle for about 1 minute and then spit it out; use it after brushing the teeth. Squeeze the applicator firmly only once so that the ampoule breaks and the solution comes out, and leave the broken ampoule inside the applicator. For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

  • People with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine, isopropanol, or Yellow No. 5 and infants aged 2 months or younger should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use this medicine for disinfecting surgical instruments, or on nervous tissue (e.g., brain or spinal cord tissue), the eyes, ears, mouth, mucous membranes, genital mucous membranes, open wounds, or torn or damaged skin, or for general washing of the skin.
  • Before using this medicine, people with hypersensitivity to other medicines, people who have experienced allergic diseases such as asthma or who have a family history of them, people with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, and people with a drug-hypersensitive constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only on intact skin.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get in, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty breathing, redness, a sudden drop in blood pressure, urticaria, angioedema, etc.), occasionally rash, photosensitization, irritation, sensitization, erythema or inflammation, itching, dry and thinly peeling skin, local pain at the application site, or local skin reactions, or very rarely rash (e.g., erythematous, papular, or maculopapular), blisters, small blisters at the application site, a burning sensation of the skin, dermatitis, eczema, chemical burns in newborns, eye irritation, congestion, impaired vision, or eye damage occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

People aged 15 years and older take 1 sachet (20 mL) as 1 dose, those aged 11 years or older and under 15 years take 2/3 of a sachet as 1 dose, those aged 7 years or older and under 11 years take 1/2 of a sachet as 1 dose, those aged 3 years or older and under 7 years take 1/3 of a sachet as 1 dose, and those aged 2 years or older and under 3 years take 1/4 of a sachet as 1 dose, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals, with an interval of 4 hours between doses.

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.

  • It may cause liver damage.

How to take it

For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout, and psoriatic arthritis, adults take 1/2 to 1.5 tablets (200 to 600 mg) at a time, 3 to 4 times a day, up to a maximum of 3200 mg per day. Do not take more than the recommended dose. Adjust the dose appropriately according to age and symptoms.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic reactions, myocardial infarction and stroke, which may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcer and perforation may appear.
  • Patients with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease must avoid taking high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day), and patients who have cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, smoking, etc.) and need to take high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine, patients with gastrointestinal ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding or a history of them, severe blood abnormalities, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency, severe high blood pressure, or bronchial asthma or a history of it, patients who have hypersensitivity such as asthma, hives, or allergic reactions to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics (including COX-2 inhibitors) or a history of it, patients with pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass surgery, women in the last 3 months of pregnancy, patients taking high-dose methotrexate as cancer chemotherapy, and patients with genetic problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption must not take this medicine.

Possible side effects

  • If an increased risk of myocardial infarction and stroke, or serious and potentially fatal gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If shock symptoms (heartburn, chills, difficulty breathing, drop in blood pressure), blood disorders such as decreased hematocrit, decreased hemoglobin, anemia, aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) and eosinophilia, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stool, gastritis, pancreatitis, vomiting of blood, Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, stomach (Lyell's syndrome), photosensitivity reactions, drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome), angioneurotic edema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash, exfoliative dermatitis, acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, hepatitis, jaundice, abnormal liver function such as elevated GOT, GPT and ALP, liver disorder, hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reactions, asthma attacks, urticaria, eczema, purpura, rash, itching, asthma, bronchoconstriction, difficulty breathing or wheezing, visual disturbances such as blind spots, hearing loss, ringing in the ears, taste disturbance, vertigo, drowsiness, dizziness, depression, headache, cerebrovascular accident or nervousness, aseptic meningitis or meningitis (symptoms such as severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, stiff neck, fever or impaired consciousness), rise in blood pressure, palpitations, heart failure, myocardial infarction or angina, acute renal failure, oliguria, hematuria, proteinuria, elevated BUN and blood creatinine, hyperkalemia, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, decreased urine volume, generalized edema and accompanying shortness of breath, listlessness, swelling around the eyes, facial swelling, malaise, fever, nosebleed, or peripheral edema occur, stop taking this medicine How to take it

Those aged 15 years and over take 1 sachet (20 ml) at a time, those aged 11 years to under 15 years take 2/3 of a sachet (13.3 ml) at a time, those aged 8 years to under 11 years take 1/2 of a sachet (10 ml) at a time, those aged 5 years to under 8 years take 1/3 of a sachet (6.7 ml) at a time, those aged 3 years to under 5 years take 1/4 of a sachet (5 ml) at a time, and those aged 2 years to under 3 years take 1/5 of a sachet (4 ml) at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or a history of it, infants under 3 months of age, and children under 2 years of age must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, children under 2 years of age in cases where it is truly necessary, women who are pregnant or may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, elderly people, and people who are physically weak or have a high fever should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Before taking this medicine, people with an allergic constitution, people who have had allergic symptoms caused by medicines such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, or itching, people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, or high blood pressure, and people with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough lasting 1 week or longer or recurring, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever and rash or a persistent headache should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If symptoms do not improve after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Children should take it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Follow the specified dosage and administration carefully.

  • If rash and redness in which the skin becomes congested and red, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, or insomnia occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • While taking this medicine, do not take other antitussive expectorants or oral medicines containing antihistamines.
  • People who are taking MAO inhibitors, which are used to treat depression, Parkinson's disease and the like, or who are within 2 weeks of having stopped them, must not take this medicine.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

How to apply it

For disinfecting the surgeon's hands and arms, measure out 5 mL of this medicine, rub it well into the hands and arms for about 2 minutes and 30 seconds to work up plenty of lather, and then rinse thoroughly under running water. For disinfecting the hands, measure out 5 mL of this medicine, rub it into the hands for about 1 minute, and rinse thoroughly under running water.   • Do not use it for the eyes or internally.
  • Be careful to keep it out of the eyes, and if it does get into the eyes, rinse them immediately with clean water.
  • Do not mix it with other preparations for use.
  • Because soaps weaken the germicidal action of this medicine, wash them off thoroughly before use.
  • Wash and disinfect the affected area thoroughly.
  • When it is used on a severe wound, use distilled water for injection or sterile purified water as the diluent, and do not use tap water or purified water.

  • If symptoms of shock (difficulty breathing, flushing, urticaria, itching, swelling, heartburn and at the same time pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, shortness of breath, etc.) or iododerma rarely appear, if pain, a feeling of irritation, rash, redness or dermatitis occasionally appears, or if a burning sensation, skin ulcer, contact dermatitis or skin discoloration rarely appears, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and older take 3 sachets at a time; those aged 11 years and older but under 15 years take 2 sachets at a time; those aged 7 years and older but under 11 years take 1½ sachets at a time; those aged 3 years and older but under 7 years take 1 sachet at a time; and those aged 2 years and older but under 3 years take 3/4 sachet at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals and, if necessary, at bedtime, leaving an interval of 4 hours between doses.

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious and potentially fatal skin reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of a hypersensitivity reaction appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the following apply: an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; a person with an allergic constitution; a person who has experienced allergic reactions (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.); a person with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), or difficulty urinating; an elderly person; a person in poor physical condition or a person with a high fever; a person whose gastrointestinal problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain persist or recur, or who has ulcers or bleeding problems; a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant; a breastfeeding woman; a person under treatment by a doctor or dentist (a person who is being given other medicines such as diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, or steroids); or a patient with a cough (smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that persists or recurs for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash, or a persistent headache).
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When administering it to children, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Drowsiness may occur while taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.
  • In patients given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, or alcohol, the ability to metabolize large amounts of acetaminophen is reduced, which may increase the plasma half-life of acetaminophen, so take care.

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, difficulty urinating, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, shock symptoms (urticaria, edema, and chest tightness together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, difficulty breathing, etc.), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, liver function disorder, or interstitial pneumonia occurs, or if symptoms do not improve after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.), antitussives and expectorants, other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

  • If abdominal pain, fever, chills, a foul odor in the vaginal discharge, a burning sensation, itching, rash or other irritation of the vagina or penis in yourself or your sexual partner, difficulty urinating or pain on urination, or pregnancy occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint diseas

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 198700315. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout, and psoriatic arthritis, adults take 200-600 mg at a time, 3-4 times a day. Up to a maximum of 3,200 mg a day may be administered. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, take 30-40 mg per kg of body weight at a time, 3 to 4 times a day. For mild to moderate pain and colds, adults take 200-400 mg at a time, 3 to 4 times a day. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms. Children 11 to 14 years of age take 200 to 250 mg (10 to 12.5 mL) at a time, children 7 to 10 years of age take 150 to 200 mg (7.5 to 10 mL) at a time, children 3 to 6 years of age take 100 to 150 mg (5 to 7.5 mL) at a time, and children 1 to 2 years of age take 50 to 100 mg (2.5 to 5 mL) at a time, 3 to 4 times a day.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic reactions, myocardial infarction and stroke, which may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcer and perforation may appear.
  • Patients with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease must avoid taking high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day), and patients who have cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, smoking, etc.) and need to take high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, severe blood abnormalities, severe hepatic impairment, severe renal impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency, severe high blood pressure, or bronchial asthma, patients who have experienced asthma, urticaria, or allergic reactions caused by aspirin or other anti-inflammatory analgesics, patients with pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass surgery, pregnant women in the last 3 months of pregnancy, breastfeeding women, patients receiving high-dose methotrexate as cancer chemotherapy, and patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.
  • Do not take more than the recommended dose.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with blood abnormalities or a bleeding tendency, patients with liver cirrhosis, hepatic impairment, renal impairment, cardiac insufficiency, heart disease, high blood pressure, systemic lupus erythematosus, mixed connective tissue disease, ulcerative colitis, or Crohn's disease, elderly people, children under 2 years of age, pregnant women, and patients with chickenpox should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • When taking it for a cold, take it for no more than 5 days as a rule, and without the direction of a doctor or pharmacist do not take it for pain for 10 days or more (adults) or 5 days or more (children), and do not take it for fever for 3 days or more.

Possible side effects

  • If shock (difficulty breathing, drop in blood pressure, etc.), blood disorders such as decreased hematocrit, decreased hemoglobin, anemia, aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function and eosinophilia, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stool, gastritis, pancreatitis, vomiting of blood, Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, dry mouth, stomatitis, abdominal bloating, oral ulcer, constipation, black stool, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms of unknown frequency, angioneurotic edema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash, exfoliative dermatitis, acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, hepatitis, jaundice, abnormal liver function, liver disorder, hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reactions, asthma attacks, urticaria, eczema, purple spots, visual disturbance, hearing loss, ringing in the ears, taste disturbance, vertigo, drowsiness, dizziness, depression, headache, cerebrovascular accident or nervousness, aseptic meningitis or meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, stiff neck, fever or impaired consciousness), acute renal failure, decreased urination, hematuria, proteinuria, elevated BUN and blood creatinine, hyperkalemia, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, decreased urine volume, generalized edema and accompanying shortness of breath, listlessness, swelling around the eyes, facial swelling, malaise, fever, nosebleed, swelling, or peripheral edema occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Patients receiving high-dose methotrexate as cancer chemotherapy should not take this medicine, and do not take this medicine together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics.
  • Before taking this medicine, people taking low-dose aspirin or ACE inhibitors and patients taking lithium, furosemide and thiazide diuretics, low-dose methotrexate, coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin), or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Category

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and over and adults take 1 to 2 capsules at a time, and those aged 8 years and over but under 15 years take 1 capsule at a time, 1 to 3 times a day, avoiding times on an empty stomach and allowing an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Patients with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, or cerebrovascular disease should avoid taking high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day), and patients with cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, smoking, etc.) should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine if high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) is needed.

Precautions for use

  • Patients hypersensitive to this medicine, people who have experienced asthma when taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics, or cold remedies, infants and young children under 3 months of age and under 2 years of age, and women from week 30 of pregnancy onward must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, infants (newborns) and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, people with an allergic constitution, people who have experienced allergic symptoms caused by medicines (e.g. fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.), people with liver disease, kidney disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, or high blood pressure, people who are physically weak or who have a high fever, elderly people, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, people with persistent or recurring gastrointestinal problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain or with ulcers or bleeding problems, and people who have lost a lot of fluid through vomiting and diarrhea or who are not taking in fluids should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When administering it to children, do so under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

  • If the following occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: rash and redness (reddening of the skin), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, stomach pain, gastrointestinal bleeding, stomach discomfort, dizziness, swelling (puffiness); rarely shock (urticaria, swelling (puffiness), and chest tightness together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, difficulty breathing, etc.); Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) (when severe symptoms accompanied by high fever, with rash and redness (reddening of the skin) and blistering like burns, appear on the skin all over the body or on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes); asthma; erythema multiforme; exfoliative dermatitis; photosensitivity reactions (frequency unknown); drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency; or acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with other antipyretic analgesics, cold remedies, or sedatives.
  • If you take it together with antidiabetic drugs, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, steroids, diuretics, or low-dose aspirin (for the prevention of myocardial infarction or stroke), consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

At a glance

How it works

This medicine is used for disinfection of the patient's skin before surgery or before insertion of a syringe needle or a

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201801818. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the applicator from its packaging and hold it with the sponge facing downwards. Do not touch the sponge part of the applicator. Squeeze the applicator firmly only once so that the ampoule breaks and the solution comes out, and leave the broken ampoule inside the applicator. For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

Precautions for use

  • People with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine, isopropanol, or Yellow No. 5 and infants aged 2 months or younger should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use this medicine for disinfecting surgical instruments, or on nervous tissue (e.g., brain or spinal cord tissue), the eyes, ears, mouth, mucous membranes, genital mucous membranes, open wounds, or torn or damaged skin, or for general washing of the skin.
  • Before using this medicine, people with hypersensitivity to other medicines, people who have experienced allergic diseases such as asthma or who have a family history of them, people with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, and people with a drug-hypersensitive constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only on intact skin.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get in, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty breathing, redness, a sudden drop in blood pressure, urticaria, angioedema, etc.), occasionally rash, photosensitization, irritation, sensitization, erythema or inflammation, itching, dry and thinly peeling skin, local pain at the application site, or local skin reactions, or very rarely rash (e.g., erythematous, papular, or maculopapular), blisters, small blisters at the application site, a burning sensation of the skin, dermatitis, eczema, chemical burns in newborns, eye irritation, congestion, impaired vision, or eye damage occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
