This medicine is used to relieve various symptoms of a cold, such as runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to relieve various symptoms of a cold, such as runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202301171. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

People aged 15 years and older and adults take 1 capsule as 1 dose, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported, and if a skin rash or another sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or a history of it, people who have had asthma when taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics, or cold remedies, and infants under 3 months of age must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, children under 2 years of age, infants and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, people with an allergic constitution, women who are pregnant or may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, people who have had allergic symptoms caused by medicines such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, or itching, elderly people, people who are physically weak or have a high fever, and patients with hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5 or Sunset Yellow FCF or a history of it should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Before taking this medicine, people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma, or difficulty urinating, people with persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain, or with ulcers or bleeding problems, and people with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough lasting 1 week or longer or recurring, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever and rash or a persistent headache should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If symptoms do not improve after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • Drowsiness may occur while taking it.
  • Avoid driving a car or operating machinery.
  • Follow the specified dosage and administration carefully.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, difficulty urinating, (persistent or severe) thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, or insomnia occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If, rarely, shock (anaphylaxis) occurs — in which urticaria, edema, and chest tightness appear right after taking it, together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing — or if Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, general lethargy, liver function disorders such as jaundice, or interstitial pneumonia occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take antitussives and expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives or oral medicines containing an antihistamine.
  • People who are taking an MAO inhibitor used for the treatment of depression, Parkinson's disease and the like, or who are within 2 weeks of stopping one, should not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who are being given a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid or the like should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Patients who are being given a barbiturate, a tricyclic antidepressant or alcohol should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

Those aged 15 years and over take 1 bottle (30 mL) at a time, those aged 11 years and over but under 15 years take 2/3 of a bottle (20 mL) at a time, those aged 7 years and over but under 11 years take 1/2 of a bottle (15 mL) at a time, and those aged 3 years and over but under 7 years take 1/3 of a bottle (10 mL) at a time.   • Do not take this medicine together with other antiemetics, cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, antihistamines, sedatives, or antitussives and expectorants.

How to apply it

After drying the hair and scalp completely, apply 0.5 to 1 mL of this medicine only to the affected area, 2 times a day (morning and evening), for at least 4 months, and do not let the total daily dose exceed 2 mL.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients under 18 years of age, patients with cardiovascular disease (coronary artery disease, arrhythmia, congestive heart failure, heart valve disease, treated or untreated high blood pressure, low blood pressure), hair loss without a genetic cause, sudden patchy hair loss, abnormalities of the scalp (erythema, inflammation, infection, irritation or pain, psoriasis, sunburn), hair loss of unknown cause, patients who have shaved the scalp, and patients with myocardial infarction or a history of it must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, elderly people should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Even if you forget to use this medicine, do not make up for the missed dose; simply apply the next dose as usual.
  • Use this medicine for external use only and do not use it on areas other than the scalp.
  • Do not use occlusive dressings.
  • This medicine may cause burning and irritation of the eyes, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes, and if it comes into contact with sensitive areas such as the eyes, broken skin or mucous membranes, rinse immediately with clean water.
  • Wash your hands thoroughly after using this medicine.
  • Use hair styling products only after this medicine has dried, and when using it in the evening, apply it 2 to 4 hours before bedtime so that it can dry.
  • Because circulation of air over the scalp may reduce the effect of this medicine, do not use a hair dryer to speed up drying.

Possible side effects

  • If itching, scaling, erythema, redness, dermatitis, dry skin, hypertrichosis in areas other than where this medicine was applied (facial hair growth in women), folliculitis, local irritation including burning sensation and skin eruption, peeling, hair loss, skin abscess, acne, nail disorder, seborrhea, eczema, hair abnormalities, occasionally diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, chest pain, changes in blood pressure, changes in pulse, palpitations, increased heart rate, pericardial effusion, pericarditis, embolism, tachycardia, worsening of pre-existing angina or induction of angina in patients with undiagnosed coronary artery disease, bronchitis, upper respiratory tract infection, sinusitis, difficulty breathing, shortness of breath, fracture, back pain, tendinitis, pain, neuritis (such as polyneuritis), weakness, dizziness, headache, feeling dazed, fainting, hepatitis, edema, kidney stones, inflammation and fluid retention, fever, urticaria, allergic rhinitis, generalized erythema and facial swelling, chills, eye irritation, bitter taste, otitis (especially otitis externa), taste changes, visual impairment, erectile dysfunction, stabbing pain, or sudden unexplained weight gain occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While using this medicine, do not use it together with other scalp medicines, topical corticoids, retinoids, petrolatum, dithranol, medicines known to promote absorption through the skin, or vasodilators such as guanethidine.

How to take it

Children aged 6 months and over take 0.4 to 0.6 mL per kg of body weight per dose, at intervals of 4 to 6 hours when needed, and must not exceed 4 doses a day (28 mg/kg). For children weighing 30 kg or less, do not exceed 25 mL a day. When the body weight is known it is more appropriate to use the amount based on body weight, so refer to the approved product information for details.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic reactions, myocardial infarction and stroke, which may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcer and perforation may appear.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be taken by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, peptic ulcer, severe blood abnormality, liver impairment, renal impairment, cardiac insufficiency, high blood pressure or bronchial asthma or by those who have had them, by people who have had asthma, urticaria or an allergy in response to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, by patients being treated for pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass surgery, or by a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant or a breast-feeding woman.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user has or has had peptic ulcer, blood abnormality, a bleeding tendency, liver impairment, renal impairment, cardiac insufficiency, high blood pressure or hypersensitivity, is a patient with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, is elderly or a child, has stomach cancer, or is taking low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke, especially a patient with an autoimmune disease (SLE, MCTD).

Possible side effects

  • If any of the following appears, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: rarely shock (chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, fall in blood pressure, etc.); blood disorders such as aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, granulocytopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) and eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, or very rarely dry mouth, stomatitis, abdominal distension and constipation; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) or toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency; acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis; jaundice and increases in GOT, GPT and AL-P; induction of an asthma attack; urticaria, eczema, purpura, occasionally rash and itching; rarely visual disturbance such as blurred or dim vision, hearing loss, tinnitus and abnormal taste; aseptic meningitis, severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness; fall in blood pressure, rise in blood pressure and palpitations; acute renal failure, oliguria and hematuria together with proteinuria and increases in BUN and blood creatinine; hyperkalemia, reduced urine volume, generalized edema and the accompanying shortness of breath and languor; acute pulmonary edema; occasionally periorbital edema; and very rarely malaise, fever and nosebleed.

Interactions

  • Do not use it together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when using it together with glucocorticoids, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, sulfonylureas, diuretics, antihypertensive medicines, ACE inhibitors, furosemide, aspirin, lithium, methotrexate, or coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin).

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.

  • When administering it to children, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

  • Patients with severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure must not take this medicine.

  • If symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbances, etc.) occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

This medicine is used for difficulty in expectorating sputum in bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis, pulmonary tuberculosis, emphysema, upper respiratory tract inflammation (pharyngitis and laryngitis), lung abscess, pneumonia, cystic fibrosis and postoperative pulmonary complications, and for the preparation and aftercare of bronchography, bronchoscopy, lung cancer cytology and tracheostomy.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for difficulty in expectorating sputum in bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis, pu

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201903112. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

For nebulization therapy using a face mask, mouthpiece, or tracheostomy, nebulize 1 to 10 mL every 2 to 6 hours. The recommended amount is 3 to 5 mL nebulized 3 to 4 times a day. Nebulization therapy using a mist tent or an inhalation device (Croupette) is a method needed in special cases and is used on an individual basis according to the patient's personal needs and the convenience of the administration method. This method of administration requires a large volume of solution, and sometimes up to about 300 mL may be required for a single treatment. The recommended amount should be a volume that can maintain a very dense, fog-like state inside the tent or inhalation device throughout the treatment period. Intermittent or continuous long-term administration is desirable. For direct instillation, administer 1 to 2 mL every hour. For the routine treatment of patients who have had a tracheostomy, administer 1 to 2 mL through the tracheostomy every 1 to 4 hours. When administering directly to a specific part of the bronchial tree of the lung by inserting a small plastic catheter into the trachea under local anesthesia and a direct incision, administer 2 to 5 mL every 1 to 4 hours using a syringe connected to the catheter. For diagnostic bronchography, administer 1 to 2 mL 2 to 3 times before performing the bronchography, by nebulization or by instillation into the bronchi.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine should not use it.
  • Before using this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, patients with bronchial asthma or accompanying respiratory insufficiency, elderly people, and children should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • It is not used as an injection or as eye drops.
  • After nebulization therapy the face mask may stick to the face, but it comes off easily when washed with water.

Possible side effects

  • A slight odor (a sulfurous smell), occasionally nausea, vomiting and loss of appetite, and rarely bloody sputum, chills, fever, runny nose, stomatitis, drowsiness, a feeling of pressure in the chest, and irritation of the trachea and bronchi may occur.

Interactions

  • When it is necessary to use this medicine together with an antibiotic, inhale them separately, or give the antibiotic by injection or orally.

  • Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Interactions

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with inflammatory bowel disease (ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease), patients with gastrointestinal obstruction, patients with abdominal pain of unknown cause, patients on a low-galactose diet (galactosemia), patients with gastrointestinal perforation or at risk of it, and patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.

  • If belching, cramping abdominal discomfort, diarrhea, or occasionally borborygmus, a feeling of abdominal fullness, abdominal pain, loss of appetite, nausea, or vomiting occurs, or If there is a sudden change in bowel habits, or if there is no improvement in constipation after taking it for about 1 week, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist or doctor.

Interactions

  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine together with glycosidase inhibitors such as acarbose, broad-spectrum antibiotics, diuretics, corticoids, amphotericin B, cardiac glycosides, or antacids.

Those aged 15 years and over take 1 sachet (20 mL), those aged 11 years to under 15 years take 2/3 of a sachet, those aged 7 years to under 11 years take 1/2 of a sachet, those aged 3 years to under 7 years take 1/3 of a sachet, and those aged 2 years to under 3 years take 1/4 of a sachet, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. Do not give it to those under 2 years of age.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when they take this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of a hypersensitivity reaction appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.
  • If severe skin adverse reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis occur, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Precautions for use

  • Patients hypersensitive to this medicine or with such a history, people who have had asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, infants (newborns) under 3 months of age, and patients with severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are a child aged 3 months and over but under 2 years, an infant or a child under 15 years of age who is infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, a person with an allergic constitution or a history of allergy to medicines, a person with liver, kidney, heart, or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), or difficulty urinating (passing urine), an elderly person, a person who is physically weak or who has a high fever, a person with persistent or recurring gastrointestinal problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain or with ulcers or bleeding problems, a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant, a breastfeeding woman, or a person with symptoms such as smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that persists or recurs for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash, or a persistent headache.

  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • When administering it to children, do so under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.
  • If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • If the following occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: rash and redness (reddening of the skin), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling (puffiness), difficulty urinating (passing urine), persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia; shock symptoms (urticaria, edema, and chest tightness right after taking it, together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing); Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome: severe symptoms accompanied by high fever, with rash and redness and blistering like burns); asthma; general lethargy; jaundice (the skin or the whites of the eyes turn yellow); interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever, etc.); symptoms of ischemic colitis related to the pseudoephedrine component (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding); or posterior reversible encephalopathy and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbances, etc.).

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.), antitussives and expectorants (cough and phlegm medicines), other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis [nasal inflammation], motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).

This medicine is used for seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis, chronic idiopathic urticaria, and pruritus, and for eczema and dermatitis when used together with a topical hydrocortisone preparation.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis, chronic idiopathic urticari

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 199803133. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults and children aged 6 years and over take 1 tablet (10 mg) once a day before bedtime, and patients who are sensitive to adverse reactions take 1/2 tablet (5 mg) in divided doses in the morning and in the evening. Increase or decrease the dose as appropriate according to age and symptoms. In patients with moderate to severe (severe symptoms) renal impairment the dosing interval must be adjusted according to the patient's renal function, and in child patients with renal impairment the dose must be adjusted individually taking into account the patient's renal clearance and body weight, so refer to the approved product information for details.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or to hydroxyzine or piperazine derivatives, patients with renal failure, children under 6 years of age, and patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, pregnant women, breastfeeding women, patients with renal impairment (kidney disorder) or hepatic impairment, elderly people, patients with epilepsy and patients at risk of seizures, and patients with predisposing factors for urinary retention (spinal cord lesions, benign prostatic hyperplasia, etc.) should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If drowsiness or headache; occasionally malaise, a sensation of numbness, asthenia, restlessness, or paresthesia; rarely mild and transient lassitude, fatigue, dizziness, a heavy feeling in the head, excitement, convulsions, dyskinesia, dystonia, fainting, tremor, aggression, confusion, depression, hallucinations, insomnia, tic disorder, amnesia, memory impairment, suicidal ideation, or nightmares; occasionally thirst, dryness of the lips, nausea, loss of appetite, gastric discomfort, indigestion, abdominal pain, stomach pain, abdominal discomfort, or diarrhea; rarely vomiting, gastrointestinal disorders, cheilitis, taste disturbance, or increased appetite; rarely tachycardia, arrhythmia, or a rise in blood pressure; occasionally palpitations or vasculitis; occasionally leukopenia, neutropenia, lymphocytosis, or eosinophilia; rarely monocytosis, an increase or decrease in platelets, or photosensitivity; rarely hypersensitivity and anaphylactic shock, urticaria, angioneurotic edema, fixed drug eruption, or acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis; rarely blurred vision, conjunctival congestion, disturbance of ocular accommodation, oculogyric crisis, vertigo, or hepatitis; occasionally elevated BUN, glycosuria, or blood-stained urine; rarely difficulty urinating, nocturnal enuresis, urinary retention, joint pain, muscle pain, pharyngitis, cough, nosebleed, bronchospasm, hearing abnormalities, or visual abnormalities; occasionally chest pain; or rarely menstrual irregularity, ringing in the ears, rhinitis, or weight gain occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.Itching, urticaria, and the like may occur after stopping this medicine.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with theophylline, ritonavir, or excessive alcohol while taking it.

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area (the diseased site) 1 to 4 times a day.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine must not use it, and it must not be used on the eyes or around the eyes, on mucous membranes, on eczema, on dermatitis caused by lacquer, on wounded areas, or on sensitive skin.
  • Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have experienced allergic reactions (rash and redness (congested and reddened), itching, dermatitis caused by lacquer, etc.), if you have an allergic constitution, if you have severe moist skin (dampness) or erosion, if you have circulatory disorders or diabetes, if you are pregnant, may be pregnant, or are breastfeeding, or if the user is a child aged 12 years or younger.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When using it in children, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Use this medicine for external use only.
  • Be careful not to let it get into the eyes, and if it does get into the eyes, rinse them immediately with water.
  • If hands with the solution on them touch mucous membranes such as the eyes, irritation will occur, so wash the solution off your hands thoroughly.
  • Do not cover or wrap the treated area, and do not expose it to external heat or hot water.
  • If water touches the area where this medicine has been used, you may feel strong irritation.
  • Patients with particularly delicate skin must not use this medicine repeatedly on the same area.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 to 6 days of use, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness (congestion and reddening), swelling (puffiness), itching, or pain occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

At a glance

How it works

This medicine is used for fever and pain due to colds, headache, neuralgia, muscle pain, menstrual pain, and pain from s

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202302828. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Children aged 12 years and under take the following recommended 1-time dose every 4 to 6 hours as needed. For the recommended 1-time dose by age group, refer to the approved labeling. Take the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible period, and do not take it more than 5 times a day (75 mg/kg). If the body weight is known, it is more appropriate to take a dose based on body weight (10 to 15 mg/kg).

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported, and if a skin rash or another sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with peptic ulcer, severe blood disorders, liver disorder, kidney disorder, or reduced cardiac function, and patients with aspirin-induced asthma or a history of it must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, children under 2 years of age, patients with a bleeding tendency, patients with or a history of liver disorder, kidney disorder, or blood disorders, those with a history of peptic ulcer, patients with bronchial asthma or abnormal cardiac function, those who have experienced hypersensitivity, elderly people, pregnant women, and nursing mothers should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If pain or fever persists or worsens, or if new symptoms appear, consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Without instructions from a doctor or pharmacist, adults must not take it for pain for 10 days or longer and children must not take it for 5 days or longer, and it must not be taken for fever for 3 days or longer.
  • Children and elderly people should take the minimum necessary amount and watch for adverse reactions.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms such as difficulty breathing, reddening of the whole body, angioedema, or urticaria, or an asthma attack, thrombocytopenia, granulocytopenia, hemolytic anemia, methemoglobinemia, decreased platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), or hypersensitivity symptoms such as cyanosis, facial swelling, sweating, or low blood pressure, or nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, gastrointestinal bleeding, peptic ulcer, perforation, rash, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), elevated AST, elevated ALT, or fixed drug eruption occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • People who have taken barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, or alcohol should not take this medicine.
  • Do not take it together with other anti-inflammatory analgesics.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients on long-term warfarin and patients taking lithium or thiazide diuretics should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202302506. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and over take 1 sachet (15 ml) at a time, those aged 11 years and over but under 15 years take 2/3 sachet (10 ml) at a time, those aged 8 years and over but under 11 years take 1/2 sachet (7.5 ml) at a time, those aged 5 years and over but under 8 years take 1/3 sachet (5 ml) at a time, those aged 3 years and over but under 5 years take 1/4 sachet (3.75 ml) at a time, and those aged 2 years and over but under 3 years take 1/5 sachet (3 ml) at a time, three times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Warning

  • Patients with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their phenylalanine intake must not take this medicine.
  • This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolized to phenylalanine in the body.
  • The permitted daily amount, as recommended by the WHO, is 40 mg/kg per day or less as aspartame.
  • It should be used at the smallest possible amount.
  • For an adult weighing 60 kg, the maximum daily dose is 2.4 g.

Precautions for use

  • Patients hypersensitive to this medicine or with such a history, infants under 3 months of age, and children under 2 years of age must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, children under 2 years of age when it is absolutely necessary, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, elderly people, and people who are physically weak or who have a high fever should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Before taking this medicine, people with an allergic constitution, people who have experienced allergic symptoms caused by medicines such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, or itching, people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, or high blood pressure, and people with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that persists or recurs for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash, or a persistent headache should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Children should take it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness in which the skin becomes congested and red, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, or insomnia occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take other antitussive-expectorants, cold medicines or oral medicines containing antihistamines.
  • People who are taking MAO inhibitors used in the treatment of depression or Parkinson's disease, or who are within 2 weeks of stopping them, must not take this medicine.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

This drug is used for reducing fever when fever occurs due to acute upper respiratory tract infection.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This drug is used for reducing fever when fever occurs due to acute upper respiratory tract infection.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201000953. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Children aged 6 months and over take 0.4 to 0.6 mL/kg (5 to 7 mg/kg) at a time as needed, at intervals of 4 to 6 hours, not exceeding a maximum of 4 times a day (28 mg/kg). For children weighing 30 kg or less, do not exceed a maximum of 25 mL (300 mg) a day. If the body weight is known it is more appropriate to give the dose based on body weight, so refer to the approved labelling for the recommended doses by age group.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious, potentially fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction, and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration, and perforation may occur.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, peptic ulcer, severe blood abnormalities, severe liver disorder, severe renal disorder, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure, patients with bronchial asthma or those who have had it, those who have experienced asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics (including COX-2 inhibitors), patients being treated for pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), and pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, those who have experienced peptic ulcer, patients with blood abnormalities or those who have experienced them, patients with a tendency to bleed (platelet dysfunction may occur), patients with liver disorder or those who have experienced it, patients with renal disorder or those who have experienced it, patients with cardiac insufficiency, high blood pressure or a history of hypersensitivity, patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, the elderly and children, patients with stomach cancer, and people taking low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • When it is taken over a long period for an acute illness, as a rule this should be limited to within 5 days.

Possible side effects

  • If, rarely, shock (chest distress, chills, difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure, etc.), blood disorders such as aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, granulocytopenia, thrombocytopenia, impaired platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) or eosinophilia, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) or Lyell's syndrome (toxic epidermal necrolysis), drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency, acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, induction of an asthma attack, urticaria, eczema or purpura occurs, or occasionally rash, itching, visual disturbance (blurred vision, dark spots, etc.), aseptic meningitis, severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or impaired consciousness, acute renal failure, oliguria, blood in the urine, protein in the urine, a rise in BUN or blood creatinine, or hyperkalemia occurs, stop taking the medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea or stomach discomfort, very rarely dry mouth, stomatitis, a feeling of abdominal fullness or constipation, rarely jaundice, a rise in GOT, GPT or ALP, hearing loss, tinnitus, taste disturbance, a fall in blood pressure, a rise in blood pressure, palpitations, decreased urine volume, generalized edema, shortness of breath, listlessness or acute pulmonary edema, occasionally periorbital edema, and very rarely malaise, fever or nosebleeds may occur.

Interactions

  • Do not use this medicine together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, aspirin or high-dose methotrexate.
  • If used together with glucocorticoids, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, sulfonylureas, a combination of a diuretic and an antihypertensive, ACE inhibitors, furosemide, lithium, low-dose methotrexate or coumarin anticoagulants (warfarin, etc.), consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

For first-degree burns, apply thickly 2 to 4 times a day until no more of the medicine is absorbed, then massage gently. For second-degree burns and other non-infected skin wounds, apply the medicine thickly to the wound and the area around it and reapply repeatedly so that an excess of the medicine is always present on the wound; when a dressing is needed, apply this medicine thickly (to a thickness of about 0.5 cm), cover with a moist sterile pad and apply the dressing. For erythema (red patches) secondary to radiation therapy, apply the medicine thickly to the area to be irradiated and the surrounding area 2 to 3 times a day at regular intervals and massage gently.

Precautions for use

  • Do not use this medicine in patients with or with a history of hypersensitivity to this medicine, or on dermatitis caused by drug or food allergy, on bleeding or infected skin wounds, on infected areas, or on skin graft sites before grafting is performed.
  • Before using this medicine, patients with or with a history of hypersensitivity to propylene glycol should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • This medicine does not contain a disinfectant, so keep the wound area clean.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • Do not use it for ophthalmic purposes, and if it gets into the eyes, rinse it out with water.
  • This medicine does not contain a sunscreen, so do not use it to prevent sunburn (burns from sunlight).

Possible side effects

  • A moderate, temporary stinging sensation may occur, and rarely contact allergy may occur.

This medicine is used to inhibit thrombus formation in myocardial infarction, cerebral infarction, and unstable angina, to inhibit thrombus formation after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG) or percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA), and to reduce cardiovascular risk in high-risk patients (patients with multiple risk factors such as a family history of ischemic heart disease, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, obesity, and diabetes).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to inhibit thrombus formation in myocardial infarction, cerebral infarction, and unstable angina,

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201603416. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults take 1 tablet as 1 dose, 1 time a day. Since this medicine is an enteric-coated tablet, it may be taken before meals with plenty of water.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or to other salicylate preparations, analgesics, anti-inflammatory agents or antirheumatic agents, patients with peptic ulcer or aspirin-induced asthma or a history of it, patients with hemophilia, severe liver disorder, severe kidney disorder, severe cardiac insufficiency or a tendency to bleed, patients receiving concomitant methotrexate at doses of 15 mg or more per week (15 mg/week), and pregnant women in the third trimester must not take this medicine.
  • Do not take this medicine during the first and second trimesters of pregnancy unless it is absolutely necessary.
  • Before using this medicine, patients with kidney disorder, cardiovascular circulatory dysfunction (renal vascular disease, congestive heart failure, fluid depletion, major surgery, sepsis or major bleeding events, etc.), liver disorder, impaired cardiac function or bronchial asthma, patients before surgery, young children aged 3 years or under, elderly people, patients with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency, patients with Reye's syndrome, patients aged 14 years or under with chickenpox or influenza infection, and patients with gout should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Because there is a risk of bleeding, tell your doctor that you are taking this medicine if you are going to have surgery (including dental surgery).
  • Take care not to damage the enteric coating of this medicine.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (e.g. difficulty breathing, generalized flushing, angioedema, hives), asthma attacks, hypersensitivity (erythema, itching, nasal congestion, cardiac and respiratory disorders, and sometimes rash, swelling, hives, rhinitis-like symptoms, conjunctivitis), rarely toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), skin-mucosa-eye syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), exfoliative dermatitis, rarely aplastic anemia, anemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), ringing in the ears, deafness, dizziness, headache, agitation, rarely liver disorder, or very rarely temporary liver damage, renal impairment, acute renal failure, hyperventilation, metabolic acidosis, an excessive drop in body temperature, collapse, or coldness of the limbs occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Loss of appetite, heartburn, stomach pain, nausea, and vomiting may occur.

Interactions

  • Other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics and salicylate preparations, and methotrexate at doses of 15 mg or more per week (15 mg/week), must not be used together with this medicine, because concomitant use may increase bleeding or reduce kidney function.
  • People taking anticoagulants, some non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics such as ibuprofen and naproxen, thrombolytics, other platelet aggregation inhibitors, hemostatics, antidiabetic agents (insulin preparations, tolbutamide, etc.), uricosuric agents (benzbromarone, probenecid), thiazide diuretics, lithium preparations, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, digoxin, systemically acting adrenocortical hormone preparations (excluding hydrocortisone used as replacement therapy for Addison's disease), angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors, or valproic acid preparations should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not mix this medicine with alkaline preparations (for example, sodium bicarbonate, magnesium carbonate) or with preparations that easily absorb moisture.
  • Concomitant use with alcohol increases damage to the gastrointestinal mucosa, and the synergistic effect of this medicine and alcohol may prolong bleeding time.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adolescents aged 15 years and older and adults take 1 packet at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. If necessary, it may be taken at bedtime. Keep the interval between doses at 4 hours.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious and potentially fatal skin reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of hypersensitivity appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen.
  • If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking this medicine and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or a history of it, those who have experienced asthma when taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, infants under 3 months of age and children under 2 years of age, and patients with severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, children under 2 years of age for whom it is absolutely necessary, infants and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, people with an allergic constitution, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, those in whom symptoms of ischemic colitis such as sudden abdominal pain or rectal bleeding related to the pseudoephedrine component appear, those who have experienced allergic symptoms caused by medicines such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching, elderly people, and people with a weak constitution or a high fever should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • If symptoms do not improve after taking 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • Drowsiness may occur while taking this medicine.
  • Avoid driving a car or operating machinery.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty urinating, (persistent or severe) thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, or insomnia occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If, rarely, shock (anaphylaxis) occurs, which may appear immediately after taking it as hives, swelling, and chest tightness together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing, or if skin-mucosa-eye syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, liver dysfunction such as general lethargy and jaundice, interstitial pneumonia, or symptoms of reversible posterior encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome such as sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, or visual disturbance occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take antitussives and expectorants, other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).
  • People who are taking MAO inhibitors, which are used to treat depression and Parkinson's disease, or who are within 2 weeks of stopping them, must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who are receiving diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, steroids, etc. should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Patients who are receiving barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, or alcohol should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

Category

How it works

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201310592. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults take 1 tablet as 1 dose, 1 time a day. Since this medicine is an enteric-coated tablet, it may be taken before meals with plenty of water.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or to other salicylate preparations, analgesics, anti-inflammatory agents or antirheumatic agents, patients with peptic ulcer or aspirin-induced asthma or a history of it, patients with hemophilia, severe liver disorder, severe kidney disorder, severe cardiac insufficiency or a tendency to bleed, patients receiving concomitant methotrexate at doses of 15 mg or more per week (15 mg/week), and pregnant women in the third trimester must not take this medicine.
  • Do not take this medicine during the first and second trimesters of pregnancy unless it is absolutely necessary.
  • Before using this medicine, patients with kidney disorder, cardiovascular circulatory dysfunction (renal vascular disease, congestive heart failure, fluid depletion, major surgery, sepsis or major bleeding events, etc.), liver disorder, impaired cardiac function or bronchial asthma, patients before surgery, young children aged 3 years or under, elderly people, patients with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency, patients with Reye's syndrome, patients aged 14 years or under with chickenpox or influenza infection, and patients with gout should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Because there is a risk of bleeding, tell your doctor that you are taking this medicine if you are going to have surgery (including dental surgery).
  • Take care not to damage the enteric coating of this medicine.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (e.g., difficulty breathing, generalized flushing, angioedema, urticaria), asthma attacks, hypersensitivity (erythema, itching, nasal congestion, cardiac and respiratory disorders, occasionally rash, edema, urticaria, rhinitis-like symptoms, conjunctivitis), rarely toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), exfoliative dermatitis, aplastic anemia, anemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), ringing in the ears, deafness, dizziness, headache, agitation, liver disorder, very rarely transient liver damage, kidney disorder, acute renal failure, hyperventilation, metabolic acidosis, excessive lowering of body temperature, collapse, or coldness of the limbs occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Loss of appetite, heartburn, stomach pain, nausea, and vomiting may occur.

Interactions

  • Other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics and salicylate preparations, and methotrexate at doses of 15 mg or more per week (15 mg/week), must not be used together with this medicine, because concomitant use may increase bleeding or reduce kidney function.
  • People taking anticoagulants, some non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics such as ibuprofen and naproxen, thrombolytics, other platelet aggregation inhibitors, hemostatics, antidiabetic agents (insulin preparations, tolbutamide, etc.), uricosuric agents (benzbromarone, probenecid), thiazide diuretics, lithium preparations, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, digoxin, systemically acting adrenocortical hormone preparations (excluding hydrocortisone used as replacement therapy for Addison's disease), angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors, or valproic acid preparations should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not mix this medicine with alkaline preparations (for example, sodium bicarbonate, magnesium carbonate) or with preparations that easily absorb moisture.
  • Concomitant use with alcohol increases damage to the gastrointestinal mucosa, and the synergistic effect of this medicine and alcohol may prolong bleeding time.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Children 12 years of age and under take the recommended single dose every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Do not take it more than 5 times a day (75 mg/kg). For the recommended dose by age group, refer to the approved product information.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of hypersensitivity appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, peptic ulcer, severe blood abnormalities, liver disorder, kidney disorder, or reduced cardiac function, and patients with or with a history of aspirin-induced asthma must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with or with a history of liver disorder or kidney disorder, people who have had peptic ulcer, patients with or with a history of blood abnormalities, patients with a bleeding tendency or abnormal cardiac function, people who have experienced hypersensitivity, patients with bronchial asthma, the elderly, children under 2 years of age, pregnant women, and breastfeeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Children and the elderly should take the minimum necessary amount and be alert for adverse reactions.
  • In particular, in children and the elderly with a high fever and in patients with wasting diseases, observe their condition carefully after they take it.
  • Without instructions from a doctor or pharmacist, adults must not take it for more than 10 days and children must not take it for more than 5 days for pain, and it must not be taken for more than 3 days for fever.
  • If pain or fever persists or worsens, or if new symptoms appear, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (difficulty breathing, reddening of the whole body, angioedema, urticaria), asthma attacks, thrombocytopenia, granulocytopenia, hemolytic anemia, methemoglobinemia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), cyanosis, hypersensitivity symptoms (facial swelling, difficulty breathing, sweating, low blood pressure), nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, rash, allergic reactions, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), high anion gap metabolic acidosis, elevated AST, elevated ALT, or fixed drug eruption occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take it together with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, or other anti-inflammatory analgesics.If taking it together with warfarin, lithium, thiazide diuretics, or flucloxacillin, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

How to apply it

Press the cap at the end of the applicator handle so that the antiseptic solution soaks into the sponge, and apply it to the area to be disinfected. During use, adjust the amount of solution with the sponge attached to the applicator. Do not use it on the head, the neck, or small areas. Do not rub it off. Do not let the solution pool, and if a lot of solution runs, absorb it using the sponge. If the solution runs outside the area of use, wipe it off with gauze. If the solution gets into the navel, wipe it off with a cotton swab. Prepare a towel as needed to keep the solution from running down, and remove it before covering with a surgical drape. When applying it to skin folds such as the fingers and toes, hold the application site open with sterile-gloved hands until the liquid dries. Otherwise the skin surfaces may stick together. Use it as a single-use product only and discard any remaining solution.

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine, patients with thyroid function abnormalities (nodular goiter, endemic goiter, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, etc.), patients with renal failure, newborns and infants under 6 months of age, patients with dermatitis herpetiformis, patients before and after radioactive iodine treatment, severely ill patients such as burn patients, and patients receiving lithium treatment must not use this medicine.

  • Do not apply it to burns or mucous membranes, and do not use it as a substitute for an ordinary skin cleanser.
  • Use it for external use only.
  • Do not mix it with other preparations.

  • If occasionally pain, itching, an irritating sensation, rash, redness or dermatitis, or rarely shock (anaphylaxis: severe symptoms such as sudden itching, swelling and heartburn together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and shortness of breath), a burning sensation, skin ulcer, contact dermatitis or skin discoloration occur, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Topical medicine (MFDS 202401179)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202401179. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used to relieve nasal congestion, runny nose, sneezing, and a heavy feeling in the head caused by a head cold, allergic rhinitis, or sinusitis.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to relieve nasal congestion, runny nose, sneezing, and a heavy feeling in the head caused by a hea

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202401179. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Those aged 7 years and older and adults spray 2 times into the nose per use.Spray with an interval of at least 3 hours between doses, and do not exceed 6 times a day.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or those who have experienced it, children under 7 years of age, and infants under 2 years of age must not use this medicine.Before using this medicine, those with an allergic constitution, those who have experienced allergic symptoms caused by medicines including nasal sprays for rhinitis, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, and patients with high blood pressure, heart disease, diabetes, thyroid disease, or glaucoma should consult a doctor or pharmacist.Before using this medicine, people who smoke or who have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough persisting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever and rash or persistent headache should consult a doctor or pharmacist.If symptoms do not improve after 3 days of use, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.Use this medicine only as a nasal spray for rhinitis, that is, a medicine sprayed inside the nose, and do not use it in the eyes or ears.To prevent contamination, do not share it with others.Do not use it excessively.It may cause nasal congestion.Children should use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.Do not use it continuously for more than 7 days.Strictly observe the specified dosage and administration.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, swelling, a feeling of irritation, itching or the like occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • This medicine contains benzalkonium chloride, so it may cause bronchospasm.

Interactions

  • People who are taking MAO inhibitors, which are used to treat depression and Parkinson's disease, or who are within 2 weeks of stopping them, must not use this medicine.
  • Do not drink alcohol while using it.

Oral medicine (MFDS 202500756)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202500756. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for the relief of pain from headache, toothache, pain after tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint pain, neuralgia, back pain, muscle pain, stiff shoulders, bruise pain, fracture pain, sprain pain (pain from a twist), menstrual pain (period pain), and pain from injury, and for the reduction of fever when there are chills and fever.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the relief of pain from headache, toothache, pain after tooth extraction, sore throat, earache

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202500756. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those 15 years and older take 3 sachets at a time, those 11 years and older but under 15 years take 2 sachets at a time, those 7 years and older but under 11 years take 3/2 sachet at a time, those 3 years and older but under 7 years take 1 sachet at a time, and those 2 years and older but under 3 years take 3/4 sachet at a time, 3 times a day, avoiding an empty stomach. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of hypersensitivity appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine and those who have experienced it, people who have had asthma when taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics, or cold remedies, infants under 3 months of age, and patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist in the following cases: infants and children under 15 years of age who have had or are suspected of having chickenpox or influenza; people with an allergic constitution; people who have had allergic reactions (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.); people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, or high blood pressure; people who are physically weak or have a high fever; elderly people; women who are pregnant or may be pregnant; breastfeeding women; people with stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain, or with ulcers or bleeding problems; and children under 2 years of age.
  • If symptoms do not improve after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the specified dosage and administration carefully.
  • When it is given to children, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Possible side effects

  • If the following occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: rash, redness, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, dizziness, edema, high anion gap metabolic acidosis; rarely shock symptoms (urticaria, edema, and chest tightness right after taking it, together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing); Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms accompanied by high fever, with rash and redness and blistering like burns appearing on the skin all over the body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes); asthma; general lethargy; or jaundice.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with other antipyretic analgesics, cold medicines or sedatives.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.
  • If you take it together with diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol or flucloxacillin, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Oral medicine (MFDS 199502575)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 199502575. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), fever and pain due to a cold, low back pain, dysmenorrhea, post-operative pain and ankylosing spondylitis, headache, toothache, muscle pain, neuralgia, acute gout, psoriatic arthritis, soft tissue injury (sprain, contusion), and non-articular rheumatic diseases (tendinitis, tenosynovitis, bursitis).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint diseas

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 199502575. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout, and psoriatic arthritis, adults take 1/2 to 1.5 tablets (200 to 600 mg) at a time, 3 to 4 times a day, up to a maximum of 3200 mg per day. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, take 30-40 mg per kg of body weight per day, divided into 3 to 4 doses; for mild to moderate pain or colds, adults take 1/2 to 1 tablet (200 to 400 mg) at a time, 3 to 4 times a day. Do not take more than the recommended dose. Adjust the dose appropriately according to age and symptoms.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic reactions, myocardial infarction and stroke, which may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcer and perforation may appear.
  • Patients with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease must avoid taking high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day), and patients who have cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, smoking, etc.) and need to take high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine, patients with gastrointestinal ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding or a history of them, severe blood abnormalities, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency, severe high blood pressure, or bronchial asthma or a history of it, patients who have hypersensitivity such as asthma, hives, or allergic reactions to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics (including COX-2 inhibitors) or a history of it, patients with pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass surgery, women in the last 3 months of pregnancy, patients taking high-dose methotrexate as cancer chemotherapy, and patients with genetic problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have blood abnormalities or a history of them, a bleeding tendency, liver cirrhosis, liver impairment or a history of it, kidney impairment or a history of it, cardiac insufficiency or heart disease, high blood pressure, systemic lupus erythematosus or mixed connective tissue disease, ulcerative colitis, or Crohn's disease; if the user is elderly or a child; if you are pregnant or breastfeeding; or if you are hypersensitive to Yellow No. 5.

Possible side effects

  • If an increased risk of myocardial infarction and stroke, or serious and potentially fatal gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If shock symptoms (heartburn, chills, difficulty breathing, drop in blood pressure), blood disorders such as decreased hematocrit, decreased hemoglobin, anemia, aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) and eosinophilia, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stool, gastritis, pancreatitis, vomiting of blood, Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, dry mouth, stomatitis, abdominal bloating, oral ulcer, constipation, black stool, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), photosensitivity reactions, drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome), angioneurotic edema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash, exfoliative dermatitis, acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, hepatitis, jaundice, abnormal liver function such as elevated GOT, GPT and ALP, liver disorder, hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reactions, asthma attacks, urticaria, eczema, purpura, rash, itching, asthma, bronchoconstriction, difficulty breathing or wheezing, visual disturbances such as blind spots, hearing loss, ringing in the ears, taste disturbance, vertigo, drowsiness, dizziness, depression, headache, cerebrovascular accident or nervousness, aseptic meningitis or meningitis (symptoms such as severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, stiff neck, fever or impaired consciousness), rise in blood pressure, palpitations, heart failure, myocardial infarction or angina, acute renal failure, oliguria, hematuria, proteinuria, elevated BUN and blood creatinine, hyperkalemia, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, decreased urine volume, generalized edema and accompanying shortness of breath, listlessness, swelling around the eyes, facial swelling, malaise, fever, nosebleed, or peripheral edema occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, low-dose aspirin, or high-dose methotrexate.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with ACE inhibitors, lithium, furosemide and thiazide diuretics, coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin), or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors.

This medicine is used for allergic dermatitis, cosmetic-induced skin reactions, heat rash, itching, contact dermatitis such as diaper rash, shaving irritation, and the prevention of rough skin.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for allergic dermatitis, cosmetic-induced skin reactions, heat rash, itching, contact dermatitis s

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202303158. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Several times a day, apply an appropriate amount to the diseased area, or spread it on gauze or similar material and apply it.

Precautions for use

  • Patients hypersensitive to this medicine or with such a history, wounds or mucous membrane areas, patients with bacterial, fungal, viral, or animal-borne skin infections, patients with festering, patients with eczematous otitis externa with a perforated eardrum, patients with ulcers other than Behcet's disease, patients with burns or frostbite of deep second degree or worse, and patients with perioral dermatitis, acne vulgaris, or rosacea must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, people who have experienced allergic symptoms such as rash, redness from congestion, itching, or reactions to lacquer caused by medicines or cosmetics, patients hypersensitive to propylene glycol or with such a history, people with an allergic constitution, people with an extensive diseased area, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, and infants and children should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Before using this medicine, patients with eczema and dermatitis accompanied by skin infection and patients who use topical corticoids over an extensive body surface or under occlusive dressing should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If no improvement in symptoms is seen after 5 to 6 days of use, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Once symptoms improve, stop using it as soon as possible.
  • This medicine is for external use only, so do not take it by mouth.
  • Do not use it for purposes other than treatment, such as after applying make-up or shaving.
  • Take care that it does not get into the eyes.
  • If it gets into the eyes, rinse them immediately with water.
  • If the symptoms are severe, seek treatment from an ophthalmologist.
  • Do not use occlusive dressing without a doctor's supervision.
  • When using occlusive dressing, clean the diseased area before application.
  • Children should use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.

Possible side effects

  • If bacterial or viral infections such as impetigo contagiosa or folliculitis occur, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If folliculitis, boils, skin irritation, stinging pain, fever, a persistent feeling of irritation, rash or redness with congestion, flushing, itching, dry skin, pustular dermatitis, allergic contact dermatitis, heat rash, worsening of wounds, bedsores, pustulosis, ringworm such as athlete's foot or tinea, acne, or festering occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • When it is used on the skin of the eyelids, it may cause increased intraocular pressure, glaucoma, or blurred vision, so be careful.

  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist in the following cases: patients with hypersensitivity to caramel or people who have experienced allergic reactions to it; infants and children under 15 years of age who have had or are suspected of having chickenpox or influenza; symptoms of ischemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, etc.); people with an allergic constitution; people who have had allergic reactions (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.); people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), or difficulty urinating; elderly people; people who are physically weak or have a high fever; people with stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain, or with ulcers or bleeding problems; women who are pregnant or may be pregnant; breastfeeding women; patients with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough lasting 1 week or longer or recurring, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever and rash or a persistent headache; and children under 2 years of age.
