At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This drug is used for reducing fever when fever occurs due to acute upper respiratory tract infection.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201802676. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Children 6 months of age and older take 0.4 to 0.6 mL/kg (5 to 7 mg/kg) at a time, as needed at intervals of 4 to 6 hours, not exceeding a maximum of 4 times a day (28 mg/kg). For children weighing 30 kg or less, do not exceed a maximum of 25 mL (300 mg) a day. If the body weight is known, dosing according to body weight is more appropriate, so refer to the approved product information for the recommended dose by age group.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious, potentially fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction, and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration, and perforation may occur.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, peptic ulcer, severe blood abnormalities, severe liver disorder, severe kidney disorder, severe heart failure, severe high blood pressure, or bronchial asthma, people who have experienced asthma, urticaria, or allergic reactions caused by aspirin or other anti-inflammatory analgesics, patients being treated for pain before or after coronary artery bypass surgery, and pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with or with a history of blood abnormalities, patients with a bleeding tendency, patients with or with a history of liver disorder, patients with or with a history of kidney disorder, patients with heart failure or high blood pressure, people who have experienced hypersensitivity, patients with systemic lupus erythematosus or mixed connective tissue disease, patients with ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, the elderly, children, patients with stomach cancer, and people who take low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If it is taken long term, as a rule limit this to 5 days or less.

Possible side effects

  • If rarely shock (difficulty breathing, fall in blood pressure, etc.), blood disorders such as aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) or eosinophilia, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), induction of an asthma attack, urticaria, eczema, purpura, occasionally rash or itching, or rarely visual disturbances such as loss of vision or dimming of vision, aseptic meningitis, acute renal failure, oliguria, hematuria, proteinuria, elevated BUN or blood creatinine, or hyperkalemia occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea or stomach discomfort, or very rarely dry mouth, stomatitis, abdominal distension or constipation, or rarely jaundice, elevated GOT, GPT or ALP, hearing loss, tinnitus, taste abnormality, fall in blood pressure, rise in blood pressure, palpitations, decreased urine volume, generalized edema and the accompanying shortness of breath or listlessness, acute pulmonary edema, occasionally periorbital edema, or very rarely malaise, fever or nosebleed occur, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not use this medicine together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, aspirin or high-dose methotrexate.
  • If used together with glucocorticoids, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, sulfonylureas, a combination of a diuretic and an antihypertensive, ACE inhibitors, furosemide, lithium, low-dose methotrexate or coumarin anticoagulants (warfarin, etc.), consult a doctor or pharmacist.

This medicine is used for the disinfection of medical equipment (examination tables, operating tables, medical lighting

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201700813. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Spray 6 ml per 1 ㎥ using the dedicated sprayer, which has a spray performance of 80 m per second and a capacity of 1000 ml per hour. Use this medicine in the following order. Press the spray nozzle button of the dedicated sprayer to detach the spray nozzle. Carefully attach the product container to the device in the correct direction. Connect the spray nozzle with the product container attached to the dedicated sprayer. Use the power cable to connect the device to an electrical outlet. Set the spray adjustment lever to 6 times the volume of the space to be sprayed. (For example, if the volume of the space to be sprayed is 50 ㎥, set it to 300 ㎥.) The spray time and spray volume according to the marking (㎥) on the spray adjustment lever are set to 1 ml per 1 ㎥. Press the power switch button to supply power to the device. Using the handle, aim the spray nozzle at the area to be sprayed. When you press the start button, a buzzer sounds for 15 seconds, and at this time the user leaves the space to be sprayed. When spraying ends, the device stops automatically. Re-enter the sprayed space after a certain time has passed following the end of spraying. To stop the device, press the power switch button to cut off the power. The waiting time before re-entering after spraying ends is 2 hours. If there are contaminants, remove the contamination thoroughly and then disinfect and sterilize with this product.

Warning

  • Do not use it on the human body.

Precautions for use

  • If it comes into contact with the skin, immediately take off any contaminated clothing and wash the area thoroughly with running water.
  • If it gets into the eyes, immediately rinse them with running water for at least 15 minutes and then consult a doctor.
  • If the vapor is inhaled, move immediately to a place with fresh air and then consult a doctor.
  • If it is swallowed by mistake, immediately have the person drink a large amount of water or milk, do not force vomiting, and consult a doctor.
  • Before use, familiarize yourself thoroughly with the dosage, administration and precautions for this product.
  • Avoid contact with the skin and eyes, and wear gloves, protective goggles and other suitable protective equipment or clothing to avoid contact with the product.
  • Use it with a dedicated sprayer approved by the manufacturer.
  • Before disinfecting, clean thoroughly to remove visible contamination.
  • When disposing of the disinfectant solution, flush it away with a large amount of water.
  • This product disinfects the surface of medical devices, so do not use it for devices that require internal disinfection.

Who should ask first

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and older take 1 sachet (20 ml) at a time; those aged 11 years and older but under 15 years take 2/3 sachet at a time; those aged 7 years and older but under 11 years take 1/2 sachet at a time; those aged 3 years and older but under 7 years take 1/3 sachet at a time; and those aged 2 years and older but under 3 years take 1/4 sachet at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious and potentially fatal skin reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of hypersensitivity appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen.
  • If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking this medicine and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Precautions for use

  • Patients hypersensitive to this medicine or those who have experienced it, those who have experienced asthma when taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics or cold medicines, infants under 3 months of age and children under 2 years of age, patients with severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure, and women from 30 weeks of pregnancy onwards must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, the following should consult a doctor or pharmacist: children under 2 years of age when it is absolutely necessary; infants and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza; people with an allergic constitution; pregnant women or women who may be pregnant; breastfeeding women; those in whom symptoms of ischemic colitis such as sudden abdominal pain or rectal bleeding appear in relation to the pseudoephedrine component; those who have experienced allergic symptoms to a medicine such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching; the elderly; and people with a weak body or a high fever.
  • Before taking this medicine, people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma or difficulty urinating, people with persistent or recurrent stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or with ulcers or bleeding problems, and people with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If the symptoms do not improve after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Children should take it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • Drowsiness may occur while taking it.
  • Avoid driving a car or operating machinery.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, or insomnia occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If shock (anaphylaxis), which rarely may appear immediately after taking the medicine with urticaria, swelling, and chest tightness along with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing, or mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, liver function disorders such as general fatigue and jaundice, interstitial pneumonia, or symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome such as sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, or visual disturbance occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take antitussives and expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives or oral medicines containing an antihistamine.
  • People who are taking an MAO inhibitor used for the treatment of depression, Parkinson's disease and the like, or who are within 2 weeks of stopping one, should not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who are being given a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid or the like should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Patients who are being given a barbiturate, a tricyclic antidepressant or alcohol should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

  • Do not use this medicine together with hydrogen peroxide.

Who should ask first

How to apply it

For nebulization therapy using a face mask, mouthpiece, or tracheostomy, nebulize 1 to 10 mL every 2 to 6 hours. The recommended amount is 3 to 5 mL nebulized 3 to 4 times a day. Nebulization therapy using a mist tent or an inhalation device (Croupette) is a method needed in special cases and is used on an individual basis according to the patient's personal needs and the convenience of the administration method. This method of administration requires a large volume of solution, and sometimes up to about 300 mL may be required for a single treatment. The recommended amount should be a volume that can maintain a very dense, fog-like state inside the tent or inhalation device throughout the treatment period. Intermittent or continuous long-term administration is desirable. For direct instillation, administer 1 to 2 mL every hour. For the routine treatment of patients who have had a tracheostomy, administer 1 to 2 mL through the tracheostomy every 1 to 4 hours. When administering directly to a specific part of the bronchial tree of the lung by inserting a small plastic catheter into the trachea under local anesthesia and a direct incision, administer 2 to 5 mL every 1 to 4 hours using a syringe connected to the catheter. For diagnostic bronchography, administer 1 to 2 mL 2 to 3 times before performing the bronchography, by nebulization or by instillation into the bronchi.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine should not use it.
  • Before using this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, patients with bronchial asthma or accompanying respiratory insufficiency, elderly people, and children should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • It is not used as an injection or as eye drops.
  • After nebulization therapy the face mask may stick to the face, but it comes off easily when washed with water.

Possible side effects

  • A mild odor (sulfur smell) may occur, sometimes bronchial obstruction, bronchospasm, nausea, vomiting, or loss of appetite, and rarely anaphylaxis, bloody sputum, chills, fever, runny nose, stomatitis, drowsiness, a feeling of chest pressure, or irritation of the trachea and bronchi may occur.

Interactions

  • When it is necessary to use this medicine together with an antibiotic, inhale them separately, or give the antibiotic by injection or orally.

Who should ask first

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the applicator from its packaging and hold it with the sponge facing downwards. Do not touch the sponge part of the applicator. Squeeze the applicator firmly only once so that the ampoule breaks and the solution comes out, and leave the broken ampoule inside the applicator. For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

  • Use it externally only on intact skin.

For chronic constipation, take this medicine before breakfast. Adults usually take 15 to 30 mL a day before breakfast for the first 2 to 3 days, and then continue with 10 to 15 mL a day.   • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, inflammatory bowel disease (ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease), gastrointestinal obstruction, abdominal pain of unknown cause, or a low-galactose diet (galactosemia), patients with gastrointestinal perforation or a risk of it, and patients with genetic problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption must not take this medicine.

How it works

This medicine is used for disinfection of the patient's skin before surgery or before insertion of a syringe needle or a

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201801818. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the applicator from its packaging and hold it with the sponge facing downwards. Do not touch the sponge part of the applicator. Squeeze the applicator firmly only once so that the ampoule breaks and the solution comes out, and leave the broken ampoule inside the applicator. For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

  • People with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine, isopropanol, or Yellow No. 5 and infants aged 2 months or younger should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use this medicine for disinfecting surgical instruments, or on nervous tissue (e.g., brain or spinal cord tissue), the eyes, ears, mouth, mucous membranes, genital mucous membranes, open wounds, or torn or damaged skin, or for general washing of the skin.
  • Before using this medicine, people with hypersensitivity to other medicines, people who have experienced allergic diseases such as asthma or who have a family history of them, people with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, and people with a drug-hypersensitive constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only on intact skin.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get in, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.

  • If shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty breathing, redness, a sudden drop in blood pressure, urticaria, angioedema, etc.), occasionally rash, photosensitization, irritation, sensitization, erythema or inflammation, itching, dry and thinly peeling skin, local pain at the application site, or local skin reactions, or very rarely rash (e.g., erythematous, papular, or maculopapular), blisters, small blisters at the application site, a burning sensation of the skin, dermatitis, eczema, chemical burns in newborns, eye irritation, congestion, impaired vision, or eye damage occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

This medicine is used for diarrhea, for the adsorption of gas produced by abnormal fermentation in the digestive tract, and as an adsorbent for emergency detoxification in poisoning by drugs and chemicals. (However, medicinal charcoal does not adsorb cyanide, and it is relatively ineffective at adsorbing alcohol, aliphatic hydrocarbons, lithium salts, corrosive sodium chloride, heavy metals such as iron, lead, and lead cyanide, boric acid, other inorganic acids, and petroleum distillates.)

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for diarrhea, for the adsorption of gas produced by abnormal fermentation in the digestive tract,

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202302822. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Take 2 to 20 g of medicinal charcoal a day, divided into several doses. In acute poisoning, medicinal charcoal is administered within 30 minutes after ingestion of the poisonous substance. (When the amount of the ingested poisonous substance is known, the recommended dose of medicinal charcoal is usually 5-10 times the amount of the ingested poisonous substance.)
Increase or decrease the dose appropriately according to age and symptoms, following the instructions of a doctor.

Warning

  • Because it degrades the imaging of esophageal erosion, do not use it when a corrosive substance has been ingested.
  • Do not use it in patients with diabetes without a doctor's diagnosis and prescription.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine should be administered after gastric aspiration or gastric lavage has been completed with the involvement of a doctor.
  • Within 2 hours of administering medicinal charcoal, the charcoal adsorbs other medicines and so reduces their effect.
  • This medicine may turn the stools black.

Possible side effects

  • Be careful, as indigestion may occur and as the adsorption of vitamins, minerals and the like may cause nutritional disturbance.

Interactions

  • Ice cream and sherbet lower the adsorptive power of medicinal charcoal, so do not take them together with it.
  • When it is used as an antidote for oral poisoning, do not take it together with ipecac syrup.
  • The ipecac syrup may be adsorbed by the medicinal charcoal and so prevent vomiting.
  • If ipecac syrup and medicinal charcoal are used at the same time, it is recommended that the medicinal charcoal be given after vomiting has been induced and has finished.

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201907024. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and over and adults take 2 capsules at a time 3 times a day, and those aged 8 years to under 15 years take 1 capsule at a time 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of a hypersensitivity reaction appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.
  • If severe skin adverse reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis occur, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Precautions for use

  • Patients hypersensitive to this medicine or those who have experienced it, those who have experienced asthma when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics or cold medicines, infants under 3 months of age, and patients with severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, the following should consult a doctor or pharmacist: infants and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza; those in whom symptoms of ischemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, etc.) appear in relation to the pseudoephedrine component; people with an allergic constitution or who have experienced an allergic reaction to a medicine (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.); people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.) or difficulty urinating; the elderly; people with a weak body or a high fever; people with persistent or recurrent stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or with ulcers or bleeding problems; pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women; and children under 2 years of age.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with a cough (smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache) should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, difficulty urinating, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, rarely shock symptoms (urticaria, swelling, and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, along with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) (accompanied by high fever, with severe symptoms such as rash and redness and blistering like burns that may appear on the skin all over the body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), asthma, liver function disorder (general fatigue and jaundice (the skin or the whites of the eyes take on a yellow color) may appear), interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by coughing, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, and fever), or posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance, etc. may appear) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Category

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202500570. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Press the cap at the end of the applicator handle so that the antiseptic solution soaks into the sponge, and apply it to the area to be disinfected. During use, adjust the amount of solution with the sponge attached to the applicator. Do not use it on the head, the neck, or small areas. Do not rub it off. Do not let the solution pool, and if a lot of solution runs, absorb it using the sponge. If the solution runs outside the area of use, wipe it off with gauze. If the solution gets into the navel, wipe it off with a cotton swab. Prepare a towel as needed to keep the solution from running down, and remove it before covering with a surgical drape. When applying it to skin folds such as the fingers and toes, hold the application site open with sterile-gloved hands until the liquid dries. Otherwise the skin surfaces may stick together. Use it as a single-use product only and discard any remaining solution.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine, patients with thyroid function abnormalities (nodular goiter, endemic goiter, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, etc.), patients with renal failure, newborns and infants under 6 months of age, patients with dermatitis herpetiformis, patients before and after radioactive iodine treatment, severely ill patients such as burn patients, and patients receiving lithium treatment must not use this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who have had thyroid disease and patients with it, patients with renal failure, women who are pregnant or may be pregnant, and breastfeeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not apply it to burns or mucous membranes, and do not use it as a substitute for an ordinary skin cleanser.
  • Use it for external use only.
  • Do not mix it with other preparations.

Possible side effects

  • If occasionally pain, itching, an irritating sensation, rash, redness or dermatitis, or rarely shock (anaphylaxis: severe symptoms such as sudden itching, swelling and heartburn together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and shortness of breath), a burning sensation, skin ulcer, contact dermatitis or skin discoloration occur, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not use it together with lithium, chlorhexidine, sulfadiazine-silver compounds, alkalis, preparations containing mercury, enzyme-based wound treatments, or hydrogen peroxide.

How it works

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202302990. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and over and adults take 2 capsules at a time, and those over 7 years but under 15 years take 1 capsule at a time, three times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious and potentially fatal skin reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of hypersensitivity appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen.
  • If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking this medicine and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine or have experienced such hypersensitivity, people who have experienced asthma when taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics or cold medicines, infants under 3 months of age and children under 2 years of age, and patients with severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, children under 2 years of age when it is absolutely necessary, infants and children under 15 years of age who have or are suspected of having a chickenpox or influenza infection, people with an allergic constitution, women who are pregnant or may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, people in whom symptoms of ischemic colitis such as sudden abdominal pain or rectal bleeding appear in connection with the pseudoephedrine component, people who have experienced allergic symptoms caused by a medicine such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching, the elderly, and people with a weak body or a high fever should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Before taking this medicine, people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma or difficulty urinating, people with persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or with ulcer or bleeding problems, and people with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts more than 1 week or recurs, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever and rash or a persistent headache should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If symptoms do not improve after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Children should take it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Do not take it continuously over a long period.
  • Drowsiness may come on while you are taking it.
  • Avoid driving a car or operating machinery.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty urinating, (persistent or severe) thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, or insomnia occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If, rarely, shock (anaphylaxis) occurs, which may appear immediately after taking it as hives, swelling, and chest tightness together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing, or if skin-mucosa-eye syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, liver dysfunction such as general lethargy and jaundice, interstitial pneumonia, or symptoms of reversible posterior encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome such as sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, or visual disturbance occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take antitussives and expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives or oral medicines containing an antihistamine.
  • People who are taking an MAO inhibitor used for the treatment of depression, Parkinson's disease and the like, or who are within 2 weeks of stopping one, should not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who are being given a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid or the like should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Patients who are being given a barbiturate, a tricyclic antidepressant or alcohol should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

  • Patients hypersensitive to this medicine, people who have experienced asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, and infants under 3 months of age must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, infants and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, elderly people, people who are physically weak, people with an allergic constitution, people who have experienced allergic symptoms (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.), patients with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, edema, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), difficulty urinating, high fever, gastrointestinal problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain, ulcers, or bleeding problems, patients with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that persists or recurs for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash, or a persistent headache, and children under 2 years of age should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • When administering it to children, do so under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Who should ask first

How to take it

Children aged 12 years and older and adults take 1 to 2 sachets at a time, 3 to 4 times a day (every 4-6 hours) as needed, placing it directly on the tongue without water.Do not take more than a maximum of 4 grams (8 sachets) a day.Take this medicine at the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible period.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis have been reported; if a skin rash or another sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • People with hypersensitivity to this medicine, peptic ulcer, severe blood abnormalities, severe liver disorder, severe kidney disorder, or severe cardiac dysfunction, and people with aspirin-induced asthma or a history of it must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with liver disorder or a history of it, patients with kidney disorder or a history of it, people who have had peptic ulcer, patients with blood abnormalities or a history of them, a bleeding tendency, cardiac dysfunction, or a history of hypersensitivity, patients with bronchial asthma, elderly people (the aged), pregnant or breastfeeding women, people who are under treatment by a doctor or dentist, and patients with low glutathione reserves should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Without the direction of a doctor or pharmacist, do not take it for pain for more than 10 days (adults) or more than 5 days (children), and do not take it for fever for more than 3 days.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (difficulty breathing, reddening of the whole body, swelling of the blood vessels, urticaria), an asthma attack, thrombocytopenia, granulocytopenia, hemolytic (red blood cell destroying) anemia, methemoglobinemia, impaired platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), cyanosis, facial swelling, sweating, low blood pressure, gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, gastrointestinal bleeding, peptic ulcer or perforation (a hole forming), rash, allergic reactions, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), a rise in AST, a rise in ALT or fixed drug eruption occurs, stop taking the medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Children and the elderly should take the smallest necessary amount, and if symptoms such as an excessive drop in body temperature, collapse, cooling of the limbs or high fever occur, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, or alcohol.
  • People who are being given other medicines such as warfarin or flucloxacillin should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Avoid taking it together with other anti-inflammatory analgesics.

Oral medicine (MFDS 202303142)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202303142. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for the relief of various cold symptoms such as runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills in which one feels cold and shivers, fever, headache, joint pain, and muscle pain.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the relief of various cold symptoms such as runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throa

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202303142. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and over take 3 sachets (15 mL) at a time, those aged 11 years and over but under 15 years take 2 sachets (10 mL) at a time, those aged 7 years and over but under 11 years take 1.5 sachets (7.5 mL) at a time, those aged 3 years and over but under 7 years take 1 sachet (5 mL) at a time, and those aged 2 years and over but under 3 years take 0.75 of a sachet (3.75 mL) at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. If necessary, it may be taken at bedtime. Allow an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported, and if a skin rash or another sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with or with a history of hypersensitivity to this medicine, people who have experienced asthma after taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics, or cold medicines, and infants under 3 months of age and children under 2 years of age must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the following apply: a person with an allergic constitution; a person who has experienced allergic symptoms from medicines such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, or itching; an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant; a breastfeeding woman; a child under 2 years of age for whom it is absolutely necessary; an elderly person; a person in poor physical condition or a person with a high fever; a person with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma, or difficulty urinating; a person whose gastrointestinal problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain persist or recur, or who has ulcers or bleeding problems; a person with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that persists or recurs for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever and rash or a persistent headache; or a patient with or with a history of hypersensitivity to caramel.
  • If symptoms do not improve after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Children should take it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • Drowsiness may occur while taking it.
  • Avoid driving a car or operating machinery.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, (persistent or severe) thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, or insomnia occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.If, rarely, shock (anaphylaxis), in which urticaria, swelling, or chest tightness appears immediately after taking it together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, or difficulty breathing, or mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, or liver function disorder such as generalized lassitude or jaundice, or interstitial pneumonia occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take antitussives and expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives or oral medicines containing an antihistamine.
  • People who are taking an MAO inhibitor used for the treatment of depression, Parkinson's disease and the like, or who are within 2 weeks of stopping one, should not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who are being given a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid or the like should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Patients who are being given a barbiturate, a tricyclic antidepressant or alcohol should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

Attach it to the affected area 1 to 2 times a day.

This medicine is used for chronic constipation, constipation in infants, young children, and children, and constipation after childbirth.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for chronic constipation, constipation in infants, young children, and children, and constipation

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201211097. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

For chronic constipation, take this medicine before breakfast. Adults usually take 15 to 30 mL a day before breakfast for the first 2 to 3 days, and then continue with 10 to 15 mL a day. In severe cases, up to 45 mL may be given. Children aged 7 to 14 years take 15 mL a day for the first 2 to 3 days, and then continue with 10 mL a day. Young children aged 1 to 6 years take 5 to 10 mL a day. Infants under 12 months of age take 5 mL a day.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, inflammatory bowel disease (ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease), gastrointestinal obstruction, abdominal pain of unknown cause, or a low-galactose diet (galactosemia), patients with gastrointestinal perforation or a risk of it, and patients with genetic problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and nursing mothers, infants, young children and children, elderly people, and patients with diabetes, fructose intolerance, fluid and electrolyte imbalance, acute gastritis, or chronic constipation should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it for about 1 week, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If you think there has been a sudden change in your bowel habits, consult a doctor.

Possible side effects

  • If loose stools or diarrhea, rash, itching, urticaria, or erythema occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Belching, cramping abdominal discomfort, and occasionally rumbling in the abdomen, abdominal bloating, abdominal pain, loss of appetite, nausea, and vomiting may occur.

Interactions

  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with glycosidase inhibitors such as acarbose, broad-spectrum antibacterial antibiotics, diuretics, corticoids, amphotericin B, cardiac glycosides, or antacids.

Category

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202400824. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use the eye drops

Instill 2 to 3 drops into the eye 5 to 6 times a day.

Precautions for use

  • If symptoms such as redness of the eyes, itching or swelling occur, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If, in a person who wears hard contact lenses, discharge such as eye mucus increases and, rarely, the lenses become cloudy, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the sterilization and disinfection of the surgeon's hands and arms and for the sterilization a

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 199904088. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

For sterilizing and disinfecting the hands and arms of the surgeon, put 5 mL of this medicine on the hands and arms, rub it in well for about 5 minutes to produce plenty of lather, and then rinse it off thoroughly with running water. For sterilizing and disinfecting the surgical site, apply this medicine directly or use an appropriate amount, rub it in well to produce plenty of lather, and then wipe it off with sterile gauze.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be used by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, by patients with thyroid dysfunction (especially nodular goiter, endemic goiter, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, etc.), renal failure, dermatitis herpetiformis, by patients before or after radioactive iodine treatment, or by newborns and infants under 6 months of age.
  • Before using this medicine, patients in a serious condition (burn patients, etc.), patients with a thyroid disease, patients who have had renal failure, and a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant and a breast-feeding woman should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not use it for the eyes or internally.
  • Be careful to keep it out of the eyes, and if it does get into the eyes, rinse them immediately with clean water.
  • Do not mix it with other preparations for use.
  • Because soaps weaken the germicidal action of this medicine, wash them off thoroughly before use.
  • Wash and disinfect the affected area thoroughly.
  • When it is used on a severe wound, use distilled water for injection or sterile purified water as the diluent, and do not use tap water or purified water.

Possible side effects

  • If symptoms of shock (difficulty breathing, flushing, urticaria, itching, swelling, heartburn and at the same time pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, shortness of breath, etc.) or iododerma rarely appear, if pain, a feeling of irritation, rash, redness or dermatitis occasionally appears, or if a burning sensation, skin ulcer, contact dermatitis or skin discoloration rarely appears, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not use this medicine together with hydrogen peroxide.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when using it together with lithium preparations, chlorhexidine, sulfadiazine and silver compounds, alkalis, preparations containing mercury, or enzyme-based wound healing preparations.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and over and adults take 1 sachet (one dose) at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. If necessary, take it at bedtime, and leave an interval of 4 hours between doses.

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.

  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported, and if a skin rash or another sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine, people who have experienced asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold medicines, infants under 3 months of age, and people who are taking MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.) or are within 2 weeks of having stopped them must not take this medicine.

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.), antitussives (medicines that stop coughing) and expectorants (phlegm medicines), other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines), or other products containing acetaminophen.

  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients who are taking cardiac glycosides should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If you take it together with antialdosterone agents or triamterene, consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Avoid teas containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, while taking it and before and after taking it.

Those aged 15 years and over take 1 sachet (20 ml) at a time, those aged 11 years to under 15 years take 2/3 of a sachet at a time, those aged 7 years to under 11 years take 1/2 of a sachet at a time, those aged 3 years to under 7 years take 1/3 of a sachet at a time, and those aged 2 years to under 3 years take 1/4 of a sachet at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious and potentially fatal skin reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of hypersensitivity appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen.
  • If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking this medicine and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine or have experienced such hypersensitivity, people who have experienced asthma when taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics or cold medicines, infants under 3 months of age and children under 2 years of age, and patients with severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, children under 2 years of age when it is absolutely necessary, infants and children under 15 years of age who have or are suspected of having a chickenpox or influenza infection, people with an allergic constitution, women who are pregnant or may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, people in whom symptoms of ischemic colitis such as sudden abdominal pain or rectal bleeding appear in connection with the pseudoephedrine component, people who have experienced allergic symptoms caused by a medicine such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching, the elderly, and people with a weak body or a high fever should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Before taking this medicine, people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma or difficulty urinating, people with persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or with ulcer or bleeding problems, and people with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts more than 1 week or recurs, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever and rash or a persistent headache should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If symptoms do not improve after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Children should take it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Do not take it continuously over a long period.
  • Drowsiness may come on while you are taking it.
  • Avoid driving a car or operating machinery.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty urinating, (persistent or severe) thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, or insomnia occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If, rarely, shock (anaphylaxis) occurs, which may appear immediately after taking it as hives, swelling, and chest tightness together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing, or if skin-mucosa-eye syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, liver dysfunction such as general lethargy and jaundice, interstitial pneumonia, or symptoms of reversible posterior encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome such as sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, or visual disturbance occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take antitussives and expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives or oral medicines containing an antihistamine.
  • People who are taking an MAO inhibitor used for the treatment of depression, Parkinson's disease and the like, or who are within 2 weeks of stopping one, should not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who are being given a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid or the like should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Children aged 6 months and older take a dose of 0.4–0.6 mL/kg (5 – 7 mg/kg) at a time at intervals of 4 to 6 hours as needed, not exceeding a maximum of 4 times a day (28 mg/kg).For children weighing 30 kg or less, do not exceed a maximum of 25 mL (300 mg) a day.For the recommended dose by age group, refer to the approved product information.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and potentially fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction, and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration, and perforation may occur.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine, patients with peptic ulcer, severe blood abnormalities, liver disorder, kidney disorder, cardiac insufficiency, high blood pressure or bronchial asthma or who have experienced these, patients who have asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics or have experienced these, and patients being treated for pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG) must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with hypersensitivity, peptic ulcer, blood abnormalities, liver disorder or kidney disorder or who have experienced these, patients with a tendency to bleed, patients with cardiac insufficiency, high blood pressure, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, the elderly and children, patients with stomach cancer, people taking low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke, women who are pregnant or may be pregnant, and breastfeeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, a drop in blood pressure, etc.), aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, granulocytopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), eosinophilia, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome) or toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency, acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, induction of asthma attacks, urticaria, eczema, purpura, occasionally rash, itching, visual disturbances such as loss of vision (not being able to see) or dark spots in the field of vision, aseptic meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or impaired consciousness, etc.), acute renal failure, oliguria (reduced urine), blood in the urine, protein in the urine, elevated BUN and blood creatinine, or hyperkalemia rarely occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, or periorbital edema; rarely jaundice, elevated GOT, GPT, or AL-P, hearing loss, tinnitus, abnormal taste, a drop in blood pressure, a rise in blood pressure, palpitations, decreased urine volume, generalized edema and the accompanying shortness of breath, or listlessness; and very rarely thirst, stomatitis, abdominal bloating, constipation, malaise, fever, or nosebleeds may occur.

Interactions

  • Do not use this medicine together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, aspirin, or high-dose methotrexate.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when using it together with glucocorticoids, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, sulfonylureas, the combined use of diuretics and antihypertensives, ACE inhibitors, furosemide, lithium, low-dose methotrexate, or coumarin anticoagulants (warfarin, etc.).

This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile (appearing at a young age) rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), fever and pain due to a cold, back pain, dysmenorrhea, postoperative pain, ankylosing spondylitis, headache, toothache, muscle pain, neuralgia, acute gout, psoriatic arthritis, soft tissue injuries (sprains, contusions (bruises)), and non-articular rheumatic diseases (tendinitis, tenosynovitis, bursitis).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile (appearing at a young age) rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202300213. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout and psoriatic arthritis, adults take 200-600 mg of ibuprofen at a time, orally 3-4 times a day. Up to a maximum of 3200 mg a day may be given. For juvenile (occurring at a young age) rheumatoid arthritis, give 30-40 mg per kg of body weight a day orally in 3-4 divided doses. For mild and moderate pain and for colds, adults take 200-400 mg at a time, orally 3-4 times a day. Increase or decrease the dose as appropriate according to age and symptoms. For children, a single dose is 200-250 mg (10-13 ml) at 11-14 years of age and 150-200 mg (8-10 ml) at 7-10 years of age,
Children aged 3-6 years take 100-150 mg (5-8 ml) and children aged 1-2 years take 50-100 mg (3-5 ml), 3-4 times a day. For children weighing less than 30 kg, the daily amount must not exceed 500 mg (25 ml), and administration on an empty stomach should be avoided.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when they take this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic reactions, myocardial infarction, and stroke, which may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcers, and perforation may occur.
  • When non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics including this medicine are taken, serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions that may be fatal, such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcers, and perforation (a hole forming), may occur.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, gastrointestinal ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding or those who have experienced it, patients with severe blood abnormalities, severe liver disorder, severe renal disorder, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure, patients with bronchial asthma or those who have had it, those who have experienced asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics (including COX-2 inhibitors), patients with pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), women in the last 3 months of pregnancy, and patients receiving high-dose methotrexate as chemotherapy must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with blood abnormalities or those who have experienced them, patients with a tendency to bleed, patients with liver cirrhosis or liver disorder or those who have experienced it, patients with renal disorder or those who have experienced it, patients with cardiac insufficiency or heart disease, patients with high blood pressure, those who have experienced hypersensitivity, patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, the elderly and children, pregnant women, breastfeeding women, and people taking low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • Without the instruction of a doctor or pharmacist, do not take it for pain for more than 10 days (adults) or more than 5 days (children), and do not take it for fever for more than 3 days.
  • If pain or fever persists or worsens, or if new symptoms appear, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (chest distress (heartburn), chills, difficulty breathing, a drop in blood pressure, etc.), blood disorders such as decreased hematocrit, decreased hemoglobin, anemia, aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), or eosinophilia, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, hematemesis (vomiting of blood), Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, dry mouth, stomatitis, abdominal bloating, oral ulcers, constipation, black stools, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), photosensitivity reactions (frequency unknown), drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency, angioneurotic edema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash, exfoliative dermatitis, acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, hepatitis, jaundice, abnormal liver function such as elevated GOT, GPT, or alkaline phosphatase (ALP), liver disorder, hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reactions, asthma attacks, urticaria, eczema, purpura, rash, itching, asthma, bronchoconstriction, difficulty breathing or wheezing, visual impairment such as scotoma (an area of the visual field where sight is lost), hearing loss, tinnitus (ringing in the ears), taste disturbance, vertigo, drowsiness, dizziness, depression, headache, cerebrovascular accident or irritability, aseptic meningitis or meningitis (symptoms such as severe headache, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever, or impaired consciousness), a drop in blood pressure, a rise in blood pressure, palpitations, heart failure, myocardial infarction or angina, acute renal failure, oliguria, hematuria, elevated urinary protein, BUN, or blood creatinine, hyperkalemia, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, decreased urine volume, generalized edema and the accompanying shortness of breath and lassitude, periorbital edema (swelling around the eyes), facial edema (swelling of the face), malaise, fever, epistaxis (nosebleed), edema (swelling), or peripheral edema occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with ACE inhibitors, lithium, furosemide and thiazide diuretics, methotrexate, coumarin anticoagulants, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics.

This medicine is used for difficulty in expectorating sputum in bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis, pulmonary tuberculosis, emphysema, upper respiratory tract inflammation (pharyngitis and laryngitis), lung abscess, pneumonia, cystic fibrosis and postoperative pulmonary complications, and for the preparation and aftercare of bronchography, bronchoscopy, lung cancer cytology and tracheostomy.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for difficulty in expectorating sputum in bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis, pu

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201903112. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

For nebulization therapy using a face mask, mouthpiece, or tracheostomy, nebulize 1 to 10 mL every 2 to 6 hours. The recommended amount is 3 to 5 mL nebulized 3 to 4 times a day. Nebulization therapy using a mist tent or an inhalation device (Croupette) is a method needed in special cases and is used on an individual basis according to the patient's personal needs and the convenience of the administration method. This method of administration requires a large volume of solution, and sometimes up to about 300 mL may be required for a single treatment. The recommended amount should be a volume that can maintain a very dense, fog-like state inside the tent or inhalation device throughout the treatment period. Intermittent or continuous long-term administration is desirable. For direct instillation, administer 1 to 2 mL every hour. For the routine treatment of patients who have had a tracheostomy, administer 1 to 2 mL through the tracheostomy every 1 to 4 hours. When administering directly to a specific part of the bronchial tree of the lung by inserting a small plastic catheter into the trachea under local anesthesia and a direct incision, administer 2 to 5 mL every 1 to 4 hours using a syringe connected to the catheter. For diagnostic bronchography, administer 1 to 2 mL 2 to 3 times before performing the bronchography, by nebulization or by instillation into the bronchi.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine should not use it.
  • Before using this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, patients with bronchial asthma or accompanying respiratory insufficiency, elderly people, and children should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • It is not used as an injection or as eye drops.
  • After nebulization therapy the face mask may stick to the face, but it comes off easily when washed with water.

Possible side effects

  • A slight odor (a sulfurous smell), occasionally nausea, vomiting and loss of appetite, and rarely bloody sputum, chills, fever, runny nose, stomatitis, drowsiness, a feeling of pressure in the chest, and irritation of the trachea and bronchi may occur.

Interactions

  • When it is necessary to use this medicine together with an antibiotic, inhale them separately, or give the antibiotic by injection or orally.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use the eye drops

When necessary, put 1 drop at a time into each eye, several times a day. When you put it into the eye, gently pull the lower eyelid down and put one drop into the lower conjunctival sac while looking upward.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user has severe eye pain, has glaucoma, or has experienced allergic symptoms caused by eye drops, such as redness of the eye, itching, swelling or rash.
  • Use this medicine only as eye drops, that is, only as a medicine to be put into the eye.
  • If the symptoms worsen or last for 3 days or more, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Wash the hands thoroughly before use.
  • When using a single-use product for the first time, discard the first 1 to 2 drops without instilling them, in order to remove any fragments of the container that may be produced when it is opened.
  • After opening, use a single-use product only once and discard the remaining solution and the container, and use a preservative-free multi-use product for up to 4 weeks only.
  • Do not let the tip of the container touch the eyelid or the eyelashes.
  • If it does, the solution may become contaminated or cloudy from eye mucus, mold and the like.
  • Also, do not use the medicine if it has become cloudy.
  • To prevent contamination, do not share it with others.
  • This medicine can be used even while contact lenses are being worn.
  • Follow the prescribed directions and amounts.

Possible side effects

  • If eye irritation rarely appears, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • When you use this medicine at the same time as another eye drop, use the other eye drop first and use this medicine about 10 minutes later.

Those aged 15 years and older take 1 packet, those aged 11 years to under 15 years take 2/3 packet, those aged 7 years to under 11 years take 1/2 packet, and those aged 3 years to under 7 years take 1/3 packet, 30 minutes before boarding.   • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

  • If rash, redness, itching, headache, facial flushing, sensitivity to light, difficulty urinating (passing urine), thirst, or constipation occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Do not take this medicine together with other antiemetics, cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, antihistamines, sedatives, antitussives (which stop coughing) and expectorants (phlegm medicines), or gastrointestinal analgesic and antispasmodic (cramp-relieving) agents.

How to take it

Adults take 1 capsule per dose, 1 time a day. Since this medicine is an enteric-coated capsule, it may be taken before meals with plenty of water.

Adults and children aged 8 years and over take 20 to 40 mL (1 to 2 sachets) a day, based on a package unit of 1 sachet (20 mL). Children from 6 months to 7 years of age, based on a package unit of 1 sachet (8 mL), take 8 mL (1 sachet) a day at 6 months to 1 year of age, 8 to 16 mL (1 to 2 sachets) a day at 1 to 4 years of age, and 16 to 32 mL (2 to 4 sachets) a day at 4 to 7 years of age. When 1 sachet (8 mL) a day is taken, take it in the morning, and when more than 1 sachet (8 mL) a day is taken, divide it between morning and evening. Dissolve 8 mL (1 sachet) of this medicine in water to make 50 mL and take it.

  • Even if you forget to use this medicine, do not make up for the missed dose; simply apply the next dose as usual.
  • Use this medicine for external use only and do not use it on areas other than the scalp.
  • Do not use occlusive dressings.
  • This medicine may cause burning and irritation of the eyes, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes, and if it comes into contact with sensitive areas such as the eyes, broken skin or mucous membranes, rinse immediately with clean water.
  • Wash your hands thoroughly after using this medicine.
  • Use hair styling products only after this medicine has dried, and when using it in the evening, apply it 2 to 4 hours before bedtime so that it can dry.

Interactions

  • While using this medicine, do not use it together with other scalp medicines, topical corticoids, retinoids, petrolatum, dithranol, medicines known to promote absorption through the skin, or vasodilators such as guanethidine.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and over and adults take 2 capsules at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. Those aged 8 years and over but under 15 years take 1 capsule at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
