  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.
  • If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Precautions for use

  • Patients hypersensitive to this medicine or with such a history, people who have experienced asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, infants (newborns) under 3 months of age, and patients with severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, infants (newborns) and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, people with an allergic constitution, people who have experienced allergic symptoms caused by medicines (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.), people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), or difficulty urinating (passing urine), elderly people, people who are physically weak or who have a high fever, people with persistent or recurring gastrointestinal problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain, or with ulcers or bleeding problems, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, patients with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that persists or recurs for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash, or a persistent headache, and children under 2 years of age should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When administering it to children, do so under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema (swelling), difficulty urinating, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, rarely shock (urticaria, edema (swelling) and chest tightness together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing, etc.), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) (when severe symptoms accompanied by high fever, with rash and redness (congested and reddened skin) and blistering like a burn, appear on the skin all over the body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), asthma, liver function disorder (generalized listlessness, jaundice (the skin or the whites of the eyes turning yellow), etc.), interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by coughing, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever, etc.), symptoms of ischemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, etc.), or posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizure, visual disturbance, etc.) occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.), antitussives (which stop coughing) and expectorants (phlegm medicines), other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis (nasal inflammation), motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).

  • Before taking this medicine, people who are being given diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, steroids, etc. should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Patients who are given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, or alcohol should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

How it works

This medicine is used for disinfection of the patient's skin before surgery or before insertion of a syringe needle or a

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201801818. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the applicator from its packaging and hold it with the sponge facing downwards. Do not touch the sponge part of the applicator. Squeeze the applicator firmly only once so that the ampoule breaks and the solution comes out, and leave the broken ampoule inside the applicator. For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

Precautions for use

  • People with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine, isopropanol, or Yellow No. 5 and infants aged 2 months or younger should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use this medicine for disinfecting surgical instruments, or on nervous tissue (e.g., brain or spinal cord tissue), the eyes, ears, mouth, mucous membranes, genital mucous membranes, open wounds, or torn or damaged skin, or for general washing of the skin.
  • Before using this medicine, people with hypersensitivity to other medicines, people who have experienced allergic diseases such as asthma or who have a family history of them, people with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, and people with a drug-hypersensitive constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only on intact skin.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get in, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty breathing, redness, a sudden drop in blood pressure, urticaria, angioedema, etc.), occasionally rash, photosensitization, irritation, sensitization, erythema or inflammation, itching, dry and thinly peeling skin, local pain at the application site, or local skin reactions, or very rarely rash (e.g., erythematous, papular, or maculopapular), blisters, small blisters at the application site, a burning sensation of the skin, dermatitis, eczema, chemical burns in newborns, eye irritation, congestion, impaired vision, or eye damage occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

Adults take 1 tablet at a time, 2 to 4 times a day. Do not exceed 4 tablets a day.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious, potentially fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction, and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcer, and perforation may occur.Patients with uncontrolled hypertension, congestive heart failure, established ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, or cerebrovascular disease should avoid taking high-dose dexibuprofen (1,200 mg a day), and patients with cardiovascular risk factors such as hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, or smoking should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine if high-dose dexibuprofen is required.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with bronchial asthma or a history of it, and people who have experienced asthma, urticaria, or allergic reactions to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics must not take this medicine.
  • Patients who have or show signs of gastrointestinal ulcers or who have had them recur, patients with bleeding in the gastrointestinal tract, cerebral blood vessels, or other sites, patients with inflammatory bowel disease such as Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis, and people who have had gastrointestinal bleeding or perforation caused by previous non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics must not take this medicine.
  • Patients with severe blood abnormalities, liver disorder, kidney disorder, heart failure, or high blood pressure, people being treated for pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass surgery, and pregnant women 6 months or more into pregnancy must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with blood abnormalities, liver disorder, or kidney disorder or a history of them, patients with coagulation disorders or a bleeding tendency, patients with fluid retention or heart failure, high blood pressure, systemic lupus erythematosus, or mixed connective tissue disease, patients with stomach cancer, alcoholism, ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, cerebrovascular disease, or hepatic porphyria, patients with cardiovascular disease risk factors such as high blood pressure, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, or smoking, and patients who have undergone major surgery causing blood loss should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Before taking this medicine, pregnant women in early or mid-pregnancy, women after 20 weeks of pregnancy, women planning a pregnancy, women who may become pregnant, elderly people, children 6 years and older, people who have experienced hypersensitivity reactions, and patients who have gastrointestinal ulcers caused by long-term use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics in the past and who, needing long-term use of this medicine, are also being treated for peptic ulcer with misoprostol or similar agents should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Limit long-term use to 5 days or less.
  • Dizziness or fatigue may occur.
  • Take it with care when driving or operating machinery.

  • If indigestion, abdominal bloating, heartburn, upper abdominal pain, diarrhea, constipation, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, stomach discomfort, erythema multiforme with red spots of various shapes, systemic lupus erythematosus, hair loss, angioedema, rash, urticaria, itching, purpura, rhinitis (inflammation of the nose), bronchospasm, fatigue, drowsiness, headache, dizziness, anxiety, restlessness, confusion, depression, reduced fertility in women, an increased risk of acute pulmonary edema in patients with heart failure, peripheral edema, or periorbital edema, which is swelling around the eyes, occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If rarely shock symptoms such as chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, or a drop in blood pressure, or mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome), acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, induction of asthma attacks, eczema, anaphylactic reactions, photosensitivity reactions, aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), an increased risk of acute pneumonia in patients with heart failure, jaundice, abnormal liver function, hepatitis, jaundice, anxiety, restlessness, depression, a rise in blood pressure, palpitations, acute renal failure, malaise, fever, nosebleeds, or worsening of inflammation occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take aspirin, other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics or high-dose methotrexate together with it.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients who are being given corticosteroids, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, sulfonylureas, ACE inhibitors or angiotensin II receptor antagonists, diuretics, lithium, coumarin anticoagulants (warfarin, etc.), baclofen, immunosuppressants (cyclosporine, tacrolimus, sirolimus), thrombolytics, ticlopidine, antithrombotic agents, medicines that increase blood potassium levels (potassium-sparing diuretics, ACE inhibitors, angiotensin II receptor antagonists, immunosuppressants such as cyclosporine and tacrolimus, trimethoprim, heparin, etc.), CYP2C8 and CYP2C9 inducers (rifampicin, phenobarbital), low-dose (less than 15mg/week) methotrexate, antiplatelet agents or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202203959. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and older take 2 capsules at a time, 3 times a day, and those aged 8 years and older but under 15 years take 1 capsule at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of a hypersensitivity reaction appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.
  • If severe skin adverse reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis occur, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine or have experienced such hypersensitivity, people who have experienced asthma when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics or cold medicines, infants under 3 months of age, and patients with severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, infants and children under 15 years of age who have or are suspected of having a chickenpox or influenza infection, people in whom symptoms of ischemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, etc.) appear in connection with the pseudoephedrine component, people with an allergic constitution, people who have experienced an allergic reaction to a medicine (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.), people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.) or difficulty urinating, the elderly, people with a weak body or a high fever, people with persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or with ulcer or bleeding problems, women who are pregnant or may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, and children under 2 years of age should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with a cough (smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts more than 1 week or recurs, a chronic cough, a cough accompanied by fever and rash or a persistent headache) should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If symptoms do not improve after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When using it in a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, difficulty urinating, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, rarely shock symptoms (urticaria, edema and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing, etc.), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) (severe symptoms accompanied by high fever, with rash and redness and blistering like a burn, which may appear on the skin all over the body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), asthma, liver function disorder (generalized listlessness and jaundice (the skin or the whites of the eyes turning yellow) may appear), interstitial pneumonia (coughing, breathlessness, difficulty breathing and fever appear), or posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizure and visual disturbance may appear) occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.), antitussives and expectorants, other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness remedies, antiallergic remedies).
  • People who are within 2 weeks of stopping an MAO inhibitor (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.) must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who are receiving other medicines such as antidiabetic drugs, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, or steroids should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Patients who have taken barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, or alcohol should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

Children aged 12 years and under take the recommended single dose for their age group and body weight every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Precautions for use

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with other anti-inflammatory analgesics, other products containing acetaminophen, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, or alcohol.

  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported; if a skin rash or another sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • People with or with a history of hypersensitivity to this medicine, people who have had asthma after taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold medicines, infants (newborns) under 3 months of age, and people who are taking MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.) or who are within 2 weeks of stopping them must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the following apply: an infant or young child aged 3 months and over but under 2 years; an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; a person with an allergic constitution; a person who has experienced allergy to medicines (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.); a person with liver, kidney, heart, or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), or difficulty urinating (passing urine); an elderly person; a person in poor physical condition or a person with a high fever; a person whose gastrointestinal problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain persist or recur, or who has ulcers or bleeding problems; a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant; a breastfeeding woman; or symptoms such as smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that persists or recurs for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash, or a persistent headache.
  • If symptoms do not improve after taking it 5 to 6 times, consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • When administering it to children, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema (swelling), difficulty urinating, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, shock symptoms (urticaria, edema and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome: severe symptoms accompanied by high fever, with rash and redness and blistering like a burn), asthma, generalized listlessness, jaundice (the skin or the whites of the eyes turning yellow), or interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by coughing, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever, etc.) occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.), antitussive-expectorants (cough and phlegm remedies), other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis [nasal inflammation], motion sickness remedies, anti-allergy remedies).
  • Patients who have taken barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, or alcohol should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Those aged 15 years and over take 24 mL at a time, those aged 11 years to under 15 years take 16 mL at a time, those aged 7 years to under 11 years take 12 mL at a time, those aged 3 years to under 7 years take 8 mL at a time, and those aged 2 years to under 3 years take 6 mL at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.   • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

  • Patients hypersensitive to this medicine, those who have experienced asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold medicines, infants (newborns) under 3 months of age, and breastfeeding women must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, the following should consult a doctor or pharmacist: infants (newborns) and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza; children under 2 years of age; people with an allergic constitution or who have experienced allergic symptoms (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.); people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.) or difficulty urinating; the elderly; people with a weak body or a high fever; people with persistent or recurrent stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or with ulcers or bleeding problems; pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women; and patients with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When giving it to a child, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • If rash and redness (congestion causing reddening), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema (swelling), difficulty urinating (passing urine), thirst (persistent or severe), light-headedness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, or, rarely, shock symptoms (urticaria, edema (swelling), chest tightness, etc. immediately after taking it, together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweats, and difficulty breathing), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) (severe symptoms accompanied by high fever, in which rash and redness and blisters like burns appear on the skin of the whole body or on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), asthma, liver function disorder (listlessness of the whole body, jaundice, etc.), or interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by coughing, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever, etc.) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

This medicine is used for difficulty in expectorating sputum in bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis, pulmonary tuberculosis, emphysema, upper respiratory tract inflammation (pharyngitis and laryngitis), lung abscess, pneumonia, cystic fibrosis and postoperative pulmonary complications, and for the preparation and aftercare of bronchography, bronchoscopy, lung cancer cytology and tracheostomy.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for difficulty in expectorating sputum in bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis, pu

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201903112. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

For nebulization therapy using a face mask, mouthpiece, or tracheostomy, nebulize 1 to 10 mL every 2 to 6 hours. The recommended amount is 3 to 5 mL nebulized 3 to 4 times a day. Nebulization therapy using a mist tent or an inhalation device (Croupette) is a method needed in special cases and is used on an individual basis according to the patient's personal needs and the convenience of the administration method. This method of administration requires a large volume of solution, and sometimes up to about 300 mL may be required for a single treatment. The recommended amount should be a volume that can maintain a very dense, fog-like state inside the tent or inhalation device throughout the treatment period. Intermittent or continuous long-term administration is desirable. For direct instillation, administer 1 to 2 mL every hour. For the routine treatment of patients who have had a tracheostomy, administer 1 to 2 mL through the tracheostomy every 1 to 4 hours. When administering directly to a specific part of the bronchial tree of the lung by inserting a small plastic catheter into the trachea under local anesthesia and a direct incision, administer 2 to 5 mL every 1 to 4 hours using a syringe connected to the catheter. For diagnostic bronchography, administer 1 to 2 mL 2 to 3 times before performing the bronchography, by nebulization or by instillation into the bronchi.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine should not use it.
  • Before using this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, patients with bronchial asthma or accompanying respiratory insufficiency, elderly people, and children should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • It is not used as an injection or as eye drops.
  • After nebulization therapy the face mask may stick to the face, but it comes off easily when washed with water.

Possible side effects

  • A slight odor (a sulfurous smell), occasionally nausea, vomiting and loss of appetite, and rarely bloody sputum, chills, fever, runny nose, stomatitis, drowsiness, a feeling of pressure in the chest, and irritation of the trachea and bronchi may occur.

Interactions

  • When it is necessary to use this medicine together with an antibiotic, inhale them separately, or give the antibiotic by injection or orally.

This medicine is used for diarrhea, for the adsorption of gas produced by abnormal fermentation in the digestive tract, and as an adsorbent for emergency detoxification in poisoning by drugs and chemicals. (However, medicinal charcoal does not adsorb cyanide, and it is relatively ineffective at adsorbing alcohol, aliphatic hydrocarbons, lithium salts, corrosive sodium chloride, heavy metals such as iron, lead, and lead cyanide, boric acid, other inorganic acids, and petroleum distillates.)

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for diarrhea, for the adsorption of gas produced by abnormal fermentation in the digestive tract,

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202302822. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Take 2 to 20 g of medicinal charcoal a day, divided into several doses. In acute poisoning, medicinal charcoal is administered within 30 minutes after ingestion of the poisonous substance. (When the amount of the ingested poisonous substance is known, the recommended dose of medicinal charcoal is usually 5-10 times the amount of the ingested poisonous substance.)
Increase or decrease the dose appropriately according to age and symptoms, following the instructions of a doctor.

Warning

  • Because it degrades the imaging of esophageal erosion, do not use it when a corrosive substance has been ingested.
  • Do not use it in patients with diabetes without a doctor's diagnosis and prescription.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine should be administered after gastric aspiration or gastric lavage has been completed with the involvement of a doctor.
  • Within 2 hours of administering medicinal charcoal, the charcoal adsorbs other medicines and so reduces their effect.
  • This medicine may turn the stools black.

Possible side effects

  • Be careful, as indigestion may occur and as the adsorption of vitamins, minerals and the like may cause nutritional disturbance.

Interactions

  • Ice cream and sherbet lower the adsorptive power of medicinal charcoal, so do not take them together with it.
  • When it is used as an antidote for oral poisoning, do not take it together with ipecac syrup.
  • The ipecac syrup may be adsorbed by the medicinal charcoal and so prevent vomiting.
  • If ipecac syrup and medicinal charcoal are used at the same time, it is recommended that the medicinal charcoal be given after vomiting has been induced and has finished.

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to insert it

Dilute 30 mL of povidone-iodine 10% (available iodine 1%) in about 1 L of warm water and wash the inside and the outside of the vagina 1 to 2 times a day. For germicidal vaginal washing, local washing and deodorizing, wash 1 to 2 times a week.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be used by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, by patients with thyroid dysfunction (especially nodular goiter, endemic goiter, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, etc.), by patients with renal failure, by newborns and infants under 6 months of age, by patients with dermatitis herpetiformis, or by patients before or after radioactive iodine treatment.

  • If it has been used right before delivery, wash the newborn's eyes and bathe the baby as soon as possible after the delivery so that the medicine does not remain on the skin.
  • Do not use it for the eyes or internally.
  • If the undiluted solution gets into the eyes, rinse them out immediately with clean water.
  • Do not mix it with other preparations for use.
  • When this medicine is used on a patient with extensive burns, provide sufficient fluids.
  • Because this medicine has a spermicidal action, do not use it if pregnancy is desired.

  • Anaphylactoid symptoms (difficulty breathing, flushing, urticaria, etc.) and hypersensitivity in the form of iododerma may rarely appear, pain, itching, a feeling of irritation, rash, redness and dermatitis may occasionally appear, and a burning sensation, skin ulcer, contact dermatitis and skin discoloration may rarely appear.

  • Do not use this medicine together with hydrogen peroxide.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when using it together with lithium, chlorhexidine, sulfadiazine and silver compounds, alkalis, preparations containing mercury, or enzyme-based wound treatments.

How to take it

Children aged 6 months and older take a dose of 0.4–0.6 mL/kg (5 – 7 mg/kg) at a time at intervals of 4 to 6 hours as needed, not exceeding a maximum of 4 times a day (28 mg/kg).For children weighing 30 kg or less, do not exceed a maximum of 25 mL (300 mg) a day.For the recommended dose by age group, refer to the approved product information.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and potentially fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction, and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration, and perforation may occur.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine, patients with peptic ulcer, severe blood abnormalities, liver disorder, kidney disorder, cardiac insufficiency, high blood pressure or bronchial asthma or who have experienced these, patients who have asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics or have experienced these, and patients being treated for pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG) must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with hypersensitivity, peptic ulcer, blood abnormalities, liver disorder or kidney disorder or who have experienced these, patients with a tendency to bleed, patients with cardiac insufficiency, high blood pressure, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, the elderly and children, patients with stomach cancer, people taking low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke, women who are pregnant or may be pregnant, and breastfeeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, a drop in blood pressure, etc.), aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, granulocytopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), eosinophilia, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome) or toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency, acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, induction of asthma attacks, urticaria, eczema, purpura, occasionally rash, itching, visual disturbances such as loss of vision (not being able to see) or dark spots in the field of vision, aseptic meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or impaired consciousness, etc.), acute renal failure, oliguria (reduced urine), blood in the urine, protein in the urine, elevated BUN and blood creatinine, or hyperkalemia rarely occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, or periorbital edema; rarely jaundice, elevated GOT, GPT, or AL-P, hearing loss, tinnitus, abnormal taste, a drop in blood pressure, a rise in blood pressure, palpitations, decreased urine volume, generalized edema and the accompanying shortness of breath, or listlessness; and very rarely thirst, stomatitis, abdominal bloating, constipation, malaise, fever, or nosebleeds may occur.

Interactions

  • Do not use this medicine together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, aspirin, or high-dose methotrexate.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when using it together with glucocorticoids, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, sulfonylureas, the combined use of diuretics and antihypertensives, ACE inhibitors, furosemide, lithium, low-dose methotrexate, or coumarin anticoagulants (warfarin, etc.).

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the applicator from its packaging and hold it with the sponge facing downwards. Do not touch the sponge part of the applicator. Squeeze the applicator firmly only once so that the ampoule breaks and the solution comes out, and leave the broken ampoule inside the applicator. For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

Precautions for use

  • People with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine, isopropanol, or Yellow No. 5 and infants aged 2 months or younger should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use this medicine for disinfecting surgical instruments, or on nervous tissue (e.g., brain or spinal cord tissue), the eyes, ears, mouth, mucous membranes, genital mucous membranes, open wounds, or torn or damaged skin, or for general washing of the skin.
  • Before using this medicine, people with hypersensitivity to other medicines, people who have experienced allergic diseases such as asthma or who have a family history of them, people with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, and people with a drug-hypersensitive constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only on intact skin.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get in, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty breathing, redness, a sudden drop in blood pressure, urticaria, angioedema, etc.), occasionally rash, photosensitization, irritation, sensitization, erythema or inflammation, itching, dry and thinly peeling skin, local pain at the application site, or local skin reactions, or very rarely rash (e.g., erythematous, papular, or maculopapular), blisters, small blisters at the application site, a burning sensation of the skin, dermatitis, eczema, chemical burns in newborns, eye irritation, congestion, impaired vision, or eye damage occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Why this one

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Children 6 months of age and older take 0.4 to 0.6 mL/kg (5 to 7 mg/kg) at a time, as needed at intervals of 4 to 6 hours, not exceeding a maximum of 4 times a day (28 mg/kg). For children weighing 30 kg or less, do not exceed a maximum of 25 mL (300 mg) a day. If the body weight is known, dosing according to body weight is more appropriate, so refer to the approved product information for the recommended dose by age group.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious, potentially fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction, and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration, and perforation may occur.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, peptic ulcer, severe blood abnormalities, severe liver disorder, severe kidney disorder, severe heart failure, severe high blood pressure, or bronchial asthma, people who have experienced asthma, urticaria, or allergic reactions caused by aspirin or other anti-inflammatory analgesics, patients being treated for pain before or after coronary artery bypass surgery, and pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with or with a history of blood abnormalities, patients with a bleeding tendency, patients with or with a history of liver disorder, patients with or with a history of kidney disorder, patients with heart failure or high blood pressure, people who have experienced hypersensitivity, patients with systemic lupus erythematosus or mixed connective tissue disease, patients with ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, the elderly, children, patients with stomach cancer, and people who take low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If it is taken long term, as a rule limit this to 5 days or less.

Possible side effects

  • If rarely shock (difficulty breathing, fall in blood pressure, etc.), blood disorders such as aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) or eosinophilia, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), induction of an asthma attack, urticaria, eczema, purpura, occasionally rash or itching, or rarely visual disturbances such as loss of vision or dimming of vision, aseptic meningitis, acute renal failure, oliguria, hematuria, proteinuria, elevated BUN or blood creatinine, or hyperkalemia occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not use this medicine together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, aspirin or high-dose methotrexate.
  • If used together with glucocorticoids, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, sulfonylureas, a combination of a diuretic and an antihypertensive, ACE inhibitors, furosemide, lithium, low-dose methotrexate or coumarin anticoagulants (warfarin, etc.), consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Why this one

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and over and adults take 1 to 2 capsules at a time, 1 to 3 times a day, avoiding an empty stomach. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Patients with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, or cerebrovascular disease should avoid taking high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day), and patients with cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, smoking, etc.) should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine if high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) is required.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with hypersensitivity to soybeans or peanuts, people who have experienced allergic reactions to soybean oil, people who have had an asthma attack when taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics, or cold remedies, infants under 3 months of age, and women after 30 weeks of pregnancy must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist in the following cases: patients with hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4 or Yellow No. 5; people who have had allergies caused by medicines (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.); infants and young children 3 months of age and older but under 2 years of age; infants and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza; people with liver, kidney, or thyroid disease, diabetes, or high blood pressure; elderly people; people who are physically weak or have a high fever; people with persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain, or with ulcers or bleeding problems; women who are pregnant or may be pregnant; breastfeeding women; people who lose a lot of fluid through vomiting and diarrhea or who do not take in fluids, or who take diuretics; people who take low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke; patients with disorders of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinemia, diabetic hyperlipidemia, and pancreatitis, or patients who must be given lipid emulsions with caution; and patients for whom a particular risk from fat overload is expected.
  • If symptoms do not improve after taking it 5 to 6 times, consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the specified dosage and administration carefully.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.

  • If rash and redness (turning red from congestion), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, stomach pain, gastrointestinal bleeding, stomach discomfort, dizziness, edema (swelling), rarely anaphylactic shock (hypersensitivity shock: urticaria, swelling, and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, along with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome: accompanied by high fever, with severe symptoms such as rash and redness (turning red from congestion) and blistering like burns), asthma, very rarely erythema multiforme, exfoliative dermatitis, photosensitivity reactions of unknown frequency, drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome), or acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with other antipyretic analgesics, cold medicines, or sedatives.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the sterilization and disinfection of lacerations, burns, wounds, bedsores, ulcers, abscesses,

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202303116. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Apply an appropriate amount to the diseased area several times a day.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, newborns and infants under 6 months of age, patients before or after radioactive iodine treatment, patients with thyroid dysfunction such as nodular goiter, endemic goiter, or Hashimoto's thyroiditis, patients with renal failure, and patients with dermatitis herpetiformis must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, seriously ill patients such as burn patients, people who have had thyroid disease, and people who have had renal failure should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not use it in the eyes or take it internally.
  • Take care not to let the undiluted solution get into the eyes.
  • If it gets into the eyes, rinse immediately with clean water.
  • Wash and disinfect the affected area thoroughly.
  • When using it on severe wounds, use distilled water for injection or sterile purified water as the diluent.
  • Do not use tap water or purified water.
  • If this medicine gets on clothing or the like, washing it immediately makes it come out easily with water.
  • In the case of synthetic fibers, it can be removed with ammonia water or sodium thiosulfate.
  • Wash off soaps thoroughly before using this medicine.
  • When it is used just before delivery, wash the newborn's eyes and bathe the baby as soon as possible after delivery so that the medicine does not remain on the baby.
  • Provide plenty of fluids to patients with extensive burns.
  • In the case of ulcers caused by burns, use it only on ulcers resulting from secondary damage after a burn.
  • Do not use it on newly occurring burns.
  • Leave an interval of 1 to 2 weeks between the use of this medicine and flash irradiation.
  • If an infection such as peritonitis or osteomyelitis occurs, wash with physiological saline before using this medicine.
  • If the iodine of this medicine is absorbed through healthy or damaged skin, it interferes with thyroid function tests.

Possible side effects

  • Occasionally, pain, itching, a sensation of irritation, rash, redness, and dermatitis may occur.If these symptoms are severe, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.If, rarely, hypersensitivity such as difficulty breathing, flushing, or urticaria, a burning sensation, skin ulcer, contact dermatitis, skin discoloration, metabolic acidosis, or abnormal kidney function occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.Rarely, anaphylactic symptoms or shock may occur.If sudden itching, swelling, or heartburn appears together with severe symptoms such as pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, or shortness of breath, stop using this medicine immediately and seek medical attention from a doctor.When used in the vagina, blood inorganic iodine levels and blood total iodine levels may rise.

Interactions

  • Do not use this medicine together with lithium therapy or hydrogen peroxide solution.
  • If you use it together with chlorhexidine, sulfadiazine-silver compounds, alkali- and mercury-containing preparations, or enzyme-based wound treatments, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Those aged 15 years and older take 1 sachet at a time; those aged 11 years and older but under 15 years take 2/3 sachet at a time; those aged 7 years and older but under 11 years take 1/2 sachet at a time; those aged 3 years and older but under 7 years take 1/3 sachet at a time; and those aged 2 years and older but under 3 years take 1/4 sachet at a time, up to 3 times a day, avoiding an empty stomach.Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of a hypersensitivity reaction appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.
  • Patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption must not take this medicine.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, those who have experienced asthma when taking the components of this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, and infants under 3 months of age must not take this medicine.Before taking this medicine, infants infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza and children under 15 years of age, children under 2 years of age, those with an allergic constitution, those who have experienced allergic reactions (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.), people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, or high blood pressure, physically weak people or people with a high fever, elderly people, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, and people with persistent or recurring gastrointestinal problems such as heartburn, gastric discomfort, or stomach pain or with ulcer or bleeding problems should consult a doctor or pharmacist.If symptoms do not improve after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.Strictly observe the specified dosage and administration.When administering to children, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, light-headedness, edema, or, rarely, shock symptoms (urticaria, swelling, chest tightness, etc. immediately after taking it, together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweats, and difficulty breathing), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) (severe symptoms accompanied by high fever, in which rash and redness and blisters like burns appear on the skin of the whole body or on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), asthma, or liver function disorder (listlessness of the whole body, jaundice) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with other antipyretic analgesics, cold remedies, or sedatives.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, or alcohol.

How to apply it

After the hair and the scalp are completely dry, apply 0.5 to 1 mL of this medicine to the affected area only, twice a day (morning and evening), for at least 4 months, and do not let the total daily amount exceed 2 mL.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be used by women, people under 18 years of age, patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with a cardiovascular disease (coronary artery disease, arrhythmia, congestive heart failure, valvular heart disease, treated or untreated high blood pressure, low blood pressure), patients who have no hereditary factor for hair loss, patients with sudden patchy hair loss, patients with a scalp abnormality such as erythema, inflammation, infection, irritation or pain of the scalp, psoriasis or sunburn, patients with hair loss of unknown cause, patients who are using another medicine for the scalp, patients who have shaved the scalp, or patients who tolerate the 2 % strength poorly.
  • Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is elderly, has edema, has thyroid dysfunction (hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism), has local exfoliation, dermatitis, psoriasis of the scalp or a severe burn, or has a history of heart disease.
  • Use this medicine externally only and do not use it on any area other than the scalp.
  • Do not use an occlusive dressing.
  • Because this medicine may cause burning and irritation of the eyes, be careful to keep it out of the eyes, and if it touches a sensitive area such as the eyes, broken skin or a mucous membrane, rinse it off immediately with clean water.
  • Use hair styling products after this medicine has dried, and when using it in the evening, use it 2 to 4 hours before bedtime so that it can dry.
  • Because circulation of air over the scalp may reduce the effect of this medicine, do not use a hair dryer to speed up its drying.

Possible side effects

  • If any of the following appears, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: itching, scaling, erythema, redness, dermatitis, dry skin, excessive hair growth at sites other than the area where this medicine was applied (facial hair growth in women), folliculitis, local irritation including a burning sensation and skin eruption, exfoliation, hair loss, skin abscess, acne, nail disorder, seborrhea, eczema, hair abnormality, bronchitis, upper respiratory tract infection, sinusitis, difficulty breathing, occasional diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, chest pain, change in blood pressure, change in pulse, palpitations, increased heart rate, pericardial effusion, pericarditis, embolism, tachycardia, worsening of pre-existing angina or induction of angina in a person with undiagnosed coronary artery disease, shortness of breath, fracture, back pain, tendinitis, pain, neuritis (including polyneuritis), weakness, dizziness, headache, feeling dazed, fainting, hepatitis, edema, kidney stones, inflammation and fluid retention, fever, urticaria, allergic rhinitis, systemic erythema and facial swelling, chills, eye irritation, bitter taste, otitis (especially otitis externa), change in taste, visual disturbance, erectile dysfunction, stabbing pain, or sudden unexplained weight gain.

Interactions

  • Do not use it together with other medicines for the scalp, medicines that promote absorption through the skin (for example topical corticosteroids, retinoids, petrolatum, dithranol), or vasodilators (for example guanethidine, etc.).

  • If there is no improvement in symptoms, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • If shock, anaphylaxis, difficulty breathing, generalized flushing (reddening of the whole body), facial edema (swelling of the face), pharyngeal edema (swelling), urticaria, decreases in white blood cells, red blood cells, platelets, or eosinophils, anemia, delayed hemostasis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome, epidermal necrolysis, rash, urticaria (erythema), abnormal liver function, elevation of AST (GOT) and ALT (GPT), elevation of total bilirubin and LDH, jaundice, hepatitis, muscle pain, rhabdomyolysis, joint pain, muscle cramps, bradycardia (slow pulse), tachycardia (fast pulse), chest pain, raised blood pressure, facial flushing, tinnitus (ringing in the ears), impaired consciousness, convulsions, general malaise, headache, drowsiness, insomnia, hallucinations, agitation, excitement, decreased libido, abnormal sensation, a feeling of heaviness in the head, confusion, depression, dizziness, constipation, diarrhea, thirst, nausea and vomiting, abdominal distension, loss of appetite, stomatitis (inflammation of the mouth), interstitial nephritis (inflammation of the kidney), acute renal failure, fever, abnormal kidney function test values (elevated BUN and creatinine, etc.), menstrual irregularity, interstitial pneumonia accompanied by high fever, cough, difficulty breathing and chest X-ray abnormalities, bronchospasm, gynecomastia, or taste abnormality occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Before taking this medicine, patients taking non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, athlete's foot treatments and antifungal agents (such as itraconazole and posaconazole oral suspension), or tyrosine kinase inhibitors (dasatinib, erlotinib, gefitinib, pazopanib, etc.) should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and older take 12 mL (2 packets) at a time, those aged 11 years to under 15 years take 8 mL (11/3 packets) at a time, those aged 7 years to under 11 years take 6 mL (1 packet) at a time, and those aged 3 years to under 7 years take 4 mL (2/3 packet) at a time. To prevent motion sickness, take 1 dose 30 minutes before boarding. If an additional dose is needed, take 1 dose at an interval of 4 hours or more, and limit the number of doses to 3 times a day.

Precautions for use

  • Breastfeeding women and infants and young children under 3 years of age must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients who have had allergic symptoms caused by medicines, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, and patients suffering from glaucoma, urinary difficulty, or respiratory diseases such as emphysema or chronic bronchitis should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When giving this medicine to children, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking this medicine, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.
  • If you use only part of 1 sachet and keep the rest, seal the opening well and use it within 2 days.

Possible side effects

  • If rash, congestion and reddening, itching, palpitations, or thirst occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take other antiemetics, cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, antihistamines, sedatives, antitussives and expectorants, or alcoholic drinks.

Spray and apply an appropriate amount several times in 1 day.

  • Do not use it in the eyes, nose, mouth or genitals.
  • Do not use this medicine to prevent transmission to other people or to prevent recurrent herpes simplex (blister) infection.
  • Do not use this medicine as a base for diluting it or for mixing other medicines.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • Use it only for cold sores on the lips or around the mouth.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after using it for about 5 days, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • If commonly a feeling of dryness or peeling of the skin, occasionally a temporary burning sensation or numbness, rarely erythema, pigmentation, inflammation, bacterial (impetigo contagiosa, folliculitis, etc.) or fungal (candidiasis, tinea, etc.) skin infections, general skin symptoms (folliculitis, boils, skin irritation, stinging pain, fever, a burning sensation, rash, redness, flushing, itching, dry skin, pustular dermatitis, allergic contact dermatitis, heat rash, miliaria, worsening of wounds, bedsores, pustulosis), or, when it is used on the eyelid skin, increased intraocular pressure or glaucoma, or blurred vision of unknown frequency occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

After drying the hair and scalp completely, apply 0.5 to 1 mL of this medicine only to the affected area, 2 times a day (morning and evening), for at least 4 months, and do not let the total daily dose exceed 2 mL.

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients under 18 years of age, patients with cardiovascular disease (coronary artery disease, arrhythmia, congestive heart failure, heart valve disease, treated or untreated high blood pressure, low blood pressure), hair loss without a genetic cause, sudden patchy hair loss, abnormalities of the scalp (erythema, inflammation, infection, irritation or pain, psoriasis, sunburn), hair loss of unknown cause, patients who have shaved the scalp, and patients with myocardial infarction or a history of it must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, elderly people should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Even if you forget to use this medicine, do not make up for the missed dose; simply apply the next dose as usual.
  • Use this medicine for external use only and do not use it on areas other than the scalp.
  • Do not use occlusive dressings.
  • This medicine may cause burning and irritation of the eyes, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes, and if it comes into contact with sensitive areas such as the eyes, broken skin or mucous membranes, rinse immediately with clean water.
  • Wash your hands thoroughly after using this medicine.
  • Use hair styling products only after this medicine has dried, and when using it in the evening, apply it 2 to 4 hours before bedtime so that it can dry.
  • Because circulation of air over the scalp may reduce the effect of this medicine, do not use a hair dryer to speed up drying.

  • If itching, scaling, erythema, redness, dermatitis, dry skin, hypertrichosis in areas other than where this medicine was applied (facial hair growth in women), folliculitis, local irritation including burning sensation and skin eruption, peeling, hair loss, skin abscess, acne, nail disorder, seborrhea, eczema, hair abnormalities, occasionally diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, chest pain, changes in blood pressure, changes in pulse, palpitations, increased heart rate, pericardial effusion, pericarditis, embolism, tachycardia, worsening of pre-existing angina or induction of angina in patients with undiagnosed coronary artery disease, bronchitis, upper respiratory tract infection, sinusitis, difficulty breathing, shortness of breath, fracture, back pain, tendinitis, pain, neuritis (such as polyneuritis), weakness, dizziness, headache, feeling dazed, fainting, hepatitis, edema, kidney stones, inflammation and fluid retention, fever, urticaria, allergic rhinitis, generalized erythema and facial swelling, chills, eye irritation, bitter taste, otitis (especially otitis externa), taste changes, visual impairment, erectile dysfunction, stabbing pain, or sudden unexplained weight gain occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

How it works

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the applicator from its packaging and hold it with the sponge facing downwards. Do not touch the sponge part of the applicator. Squeeze the applicator firmly only once so that the ampoule breaks and the solution comes out, and leave the broken ampoule inside the applicator. For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

Precautions for use

  • People with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine, isopropanol, or Yellow No. 5 and infants aged 2 months or younger should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use this medicine for disinfecting surgical instruments, or on nervous tissue (e.g., brain or spinal cord tissue), the eyes, ears, mouth, mucous membranes, genital mucous membranes, open wounds, or torn or damaged skin, or for general washing of the skin.
  • Before using this medicine, people with hypersensitivity to other medicines, people who have experienced allergic diseases such as asthma or who have a family history of them, people with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, and people with a drug-hypersensitive constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only on intact skin.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get in, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty breathing, redness, a sudden drop in blood pressure, urticaria, angioedema, etc.), occasionally rash, photosensitization, irritation, sensitization, erythema or inflammation, itching, dry and thinly peeling skin, local pain at the application site, or local skin reactions, or very rarely rash (e.g., erythematous, papular, or maculopapular), blisters, small blisters at the application site, a burning sensation of the skin, dermatitis, eczema, chemical burns in newborns, eye irritation, congestion, impaired vision, or eye damage occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for difficulty in expectorating sputum in bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis, pu

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 198600267. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

This medicine may be diluted to a lower concentration with sodium chloride solution for injection, sodium chloride solution for inhalation, sterile distilled water for injection or sterile distilled water for inhalation. For nebulization therapy using a face mask, a mouthpiece or a tracheostomy, nebulize 1 to 10 mL every 2 to 6 hours. The recommended amount is 3 to 5 mL nebulized 3 to 4 times a day. Nebulization therapy using a nebulization tent or an inhaler (Croupette) is a method needed in special cases, and it is used individually according to the personal needs of the patient and the convenience of the method of administration. This method of administration requires a large volume of solution, and sometimes as much as about 300 mL may be required for a single treatment. The recommended amount should be an amount that can maintain a very dense mist-like state inside the tent or the inhaler during the treatment period. Intermittent or continuous administration over a long period is preferable. For direct instillation, give 1 to 2 mL every hour. For the regular treatment of a patient who has had a tracheostomy, give 1 to 2 mL through the tracheostomy every 1 to 4 hours. When a small plastic catheter is inserted into the trachea under local anesthesia through a direct incision to give it directly to a specific part of the bronchial tree, give 2 to 5 mL every 1 to 4 hours using a syringe connected to the catheter. When it is given using a percutaneous intrabronchial catheter, give 1 to 2 mL of this medicine every 1 to 4 hours with a syringe connected to the catheter. For diagnostic bronchography, give 1 to 2 mL 2 to 3 times by nebulization or by intrabronchial instillation before the bronchography is performed.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user has bronchial asthma or accompanying respiratory insufficiency, is a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant or a breast-feeding woman, is a child, or is elderly.
  • Do not use it as an injection or as eye drops.
  • After nebulization therapy the face mask may stick to the face, but it comes off easily when washed with water.

Possible side effects

  • If bronchial obstruction, bronchospasm, rash or difficulty breathing occasionally appears, or if anaphylaxis rarely appears, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • A slight odor (smell of sulfur) may appear, nausea, vomiting and loss of appetite may occasionally appear, and bloody sputum, chills, fever, runny nose, stomatitis, drowsiness, a feeling of pressure in the chest and irritation of the trachea and bronchi may rarely appear.

Interactions

  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when it is used together with an antibiotic, tetracycline, erythromycin, bromhexine or the like.

How it works

This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint diseas

How to take it

For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout, and psoriatic arthritis, adults take 200-600 mg per dose, 3 to 4 times a day. Up to a maximum of 3,200 mg a day may be taken. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, take 30 to 40 mg per kg of body weight per dose, in 3 to 4 divided doses a day. For mild to moderate pain and for colds, adults take 200 to 400 mg per dose, 3 to 4 times a day. The dose may be increased or decreased as appropriate according to age and symptoms. For children, those aged 11 to 14 years take 200 to 250 mg (10 to 12.5 mL) per dose, those aged 7 to 10 years take 150 to 200 mg (7.5 to 10 mL) per dose, those aged 3 to 6 years take 100 to 150 mg (5 to 7.5 mL) per dose, and those aged 1 to 2 years take 50 to 100 mg (2.5 to 5 mL) per dose, 3 to 4 times a day, and it is advisable to avoid taking it on an empty stomach. For children, those aged 11 to 14 years may take up to 1,000 mg (50 mL) a day, those aged 7 to 10 years up to 800 mg (40 mL), those aged 3 to 6 years up to 600 mg (30 mL), and those aged 1 to 2 years up to 400 mg (20 mL).

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic reactions, myocardial infarction and stroke, which may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcer and perforation may appear.
  • Patients with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease must avoid taking high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day), and patients who have cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, smoking, etc.) and need to take high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, severe blood abnormalities, severe hepatic impairment, severe renal impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency, severe high blood pressure, or bronchial asthma, patients who have experienced asthma, urticaria, or allergic reactions caused by aspirin or other anti-inflammatory analgesics, patients with pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass surgery, pregnant women in the last 3 months of pregnancy, breastfeeding women, patients receiving high-dose methotrexate as cancer chemotherapy, and patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.
  • Do not take more than the recommended dose.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with blood abnormalities or a bleeding tendency, patients with liver cirrhosis, hepatic impairment, renal impairment, cardiac insufficiency, heart disease, high blood pressure, systemic lupus erythematosus, mixed connective tissue disease, ulcerative colitis, or Crohn's disease, elderly people, children under 2 years of age, pregnant women, and patients with chickenpox should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • When taking it for a cold, take it for no more than 5 days as a rule, and without the direction of a doctor or pharmacist do not take it for pain for 10 days or more (adults) or 5 days or more (children), and do not take it for fever for 3 days or more.

  • If shock (difficulty breathing, drop in blood pressure, etc.), decreased hematocrit, decreased hemoglobin, anemia, aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, decreased platelet function, or blood disorders such as eosinophilia, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation (a hole forming), ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, vomiting of blood, Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, dry mouth, stomatitis, abdominal bloating, oral ulcer, constipation, black stools, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis, drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms of unknown frequency, angioneurotic edema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash, exfoliative dermatitis, acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, hepatitis, jaundice, liver function abnormalities, hepatic impairment, hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reaction, asthma attack, urticaria, eczema, purple spots, visual disturbance, deafness, ringing in the ears, taste disturbance, dizziness, drowsiness, lightheadedness, depression, headache, cerebrovascular accident or nervousness, aseptic meningitis or meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness), acute renal failure, decreased urination, hematuria, proteinuria, elevated BUN or blood creatinine, hyperkalemia, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, decreased urine volume, generalized edema and accompanying shortness of breath, listlessness, Kounis syndrome of unknown frequency, swelling around the eyes, facial swelling, malaise, fever, nosebleed, swelling, or peripheral edema occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

payloads.content:
