This medicine is used for the early treatment of recurrent herpes labialis (cold sores).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the early treatment of recurrent herpes labialis (cold sores).

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202000951. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Adults use an appropriate amount, enough to cover the affected area (the diseased part) fully to its edge, 5 times a day for 5 days. Start the treatment as soon as possible, right when the first symptoms and signs appear.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be used by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, by breast-feeding women, by children under 18 years of age, by patients with a skin infection (tuberculosis, syphilis, candidiasis, tinea, herpes zoster, chickenpox, vaccinia, scabies, pubic lice), by patients whose immune system is seriously impaired (bone marrow transplant patients, AIDS patients), by patients with eczematous otitis externa with perforation of the eardrum, ulcer (except Behcet's disease), a burn or frostbite of deep second degree or worse, perioral dermatitis, acne vulgaris or rosacea, or by patients who have or have had myocardial infarction.
  • Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant, is elderly, or has or has had hypersensitivity to propylene glycol.
  • Do not use it in the eyes, the nose, the mouth or the genitals.
  • Use it only on herpes labialis (cold sores) on the lips or around the mouth.
  • Follow the prescribed directions and amounts.
  • Do not use this medicine as a base for diluting it or for mixing other medicines.

Possible side effects

  • If a feeling of dryness or peeling of the skin, which are common, a temporary burning sensation (a hot feeling) or numbness, which occur occasionally, or, rarely, erythema (red spots), pigmentation or the symptoms and signs of inflammation occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Because of systemic absorption, reversible suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, Cushing's syndrome, hyperglycemia, diabetes and visual disturbance may occur.

payloads.title: Oral medicine (MFDS 202501826)
payloads.summary: This medicine is used for constipation.
payloads.content:

Oral medicine (MFDS 202501826)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202501826. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for constipation.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for constipation.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202501826. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults and children aged 8 years and older take 1 to 2 sachets (20–40 mL) a day, based on a packaging unit of 1 sachet (20 mL).Depending on symptoms, children in particular may take 1 sachet (20 mL) every two days.Dissolve 1 sachet (20 mL) in water to make 50 mL and take it.It is recommended to take it in the morning.For children from 6 months to 7 years of age, based on a packaging unit of 1 sachet (8 mL), those aged 6 months to 1 year take 1 sachet (8 mL) a day, those aged 1 to 4 years take 1 to 2 sachets (8–16 mL) a day, and those aged 4 to 7 years take 2 to 4 sachets (16–32 mL) a day.Dissolve 1 sachet (8 mL) of this medicine in water to make 50 mL and take it.If taking 1 sachet (8 mL) a day, take it in the morning; if taking more than 1 sachet (8 mL) a day, divide the dose between morning and evening.

Warning

  • Patients with inflammatory bowel disease (ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease, etc.), toxic megacolon, intestinal perforation or a risk of intestinal perforation, intestinal obstruction or suspected intestinal obstruction, intestinal stricture, or abdominal pain of unknown cause, and patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, people with acute constipation not caused by a change in lifestyle, people with acute constipation accompanied by pain, fever, or abdominal distension, patients with irritable bowel syndrome, and children with neurological oral motor disorders should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not administer this medicine to children for 3 months or longer.
  • Before administering this medicine, clearly confirm whether there is any organic disorder.

Possible side effects

  • In adults, if abdominal pain and abdominal distension, diarrhea or nausea occurs, uncommonly vomiting, urgent bowel movements or fecal incontinence occurs, electrolyte disturbances (hyponatremia, hypokalemia) and dehydration or erythema occurs at an unknown frequency, particularly in the elderly, or very rarely hypersensitivity reactions (itching, rash, facial edema, angioedema, urticaria, anaphylaxis, shock) occur, stop taking the medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • In children, if abdominal pain, diarrhea and pain around the anus caused by diarrhea occurs, uncommonly vomiting, abdominal distension or nausea occurs, or hypersensitivity reactions (hypersensitivity, angioedema, urticaria, rash, itching) occur at an unknown frequency, stop taking the medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Hypersensitivity reactions to macrogol (polyethylene glycol) (hypersensitivity, angioedema, urticaria, rash, itching, erythema) may occur.

This medicine is used to supply vitamins E, B1, B2, B6 and C in cases of physical fatigue, pregnancy and lactation, reduced physical strength during or after an illness, and old age.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to supply vitamins E, B1, B2, B6 and C in cases of physical fatigue, pregnancy and lactation, redu

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202000586. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Children aged 12 months and over but under 8 years take 1 sachet at a time, once a day; those aged 8 years and over and adults take 1 sachet at a time, twice a day.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, infants under 12 months of age, and patients with severe heart failure must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, women who are pregnant or may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, premature infants, young children, and patients with hyperoxaluria (a condition in which excessive oxalate is excreted in the urine), cardiac and circulatory dysfunction, kidney impairment, hypoproteinemia, gout, kidney stones, or a predisposition to thrombosis should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the specified dosage and administration carefully.
  • When it is given to children, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • It may interfere with the detection of glucose in various urine tests, and it may turn the urine yellow and thereby affect clinical test values.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it for about 1 month, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If stomach discomfort, diarrhea, constipation, rash, redness, nausea, vomiting, loose stools, red spots, asystole (cardiac arrest), depressed central nervous system function, gastrointestinal disorders, indigestion, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure, or pulmonary edema occurs, or if menstruation comes earlier than expected, the flow gradually becomes heavier, and bleeding continues for a long time, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa.
  • If taken together with oral contraceptives containing estrogen, consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If taken together with antialdosterone agents or triamterene, consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Avoid teas containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, while taking it and before and after taking it.

Eye drops (MFDS 200710762)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200710762. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for the temporary relief of a burning sensation, a feeling of irritation and discomfort caused by dry eye syndrome or by exposure to wind and sun, and for the prevention of eye irritation.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Eye drops

How it works

This medicine is used for the temporary relief of a burning sensation, a feeling of irritation and discomfort caused by

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200710762. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use the eye drops

When necessary, instill 1 to 2 drops into the eye that has symptoms, and discard the remaining solution and the container after instillation. When it is used at the same time as another eye drop, leave an interval of at least 15 minutes between instillations in order to avoid a dilution effect.

Precautions for use

  • Use it externally only.
  • Do not reuse it after a single use, and be sure to discard the remaining solution and the container.
  • To avoid contamination, do not let the tip of the container touch anything outside.
  • Do not use it if the color of the solution has changed or if it has become cloudy.
  • Because temporary blurring of vision may occur, be careful when driving or operating dangerous machinery until the vision becomes clear.

Possible side effects

  • If you experience pain, a change in the field of vision, or persistent redness of the eye or a feeling of irritation, or if the symptoms get worse or last for 72 hours or more, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

This medicine is used for the sterilization and disinfection of torn wounds, burns and wounds, the sterilization and disinfection of ulcers and abscesses, the disinfection of infected skin surfaces, the sterilization and disinfection of surgical sites, and the disinfection of injection and catheter sites.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the sterilization and disinfection of torn wounds, burns and wounds, the sterilization and dis

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200713754. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area (diseased site) several times a day.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be used by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, by patients with thyroid dysfunction (especially nodular goiter, endemic goiter, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, etc.), renal failure, dermatitis herpetiformis, by patients before or after radioactive iodine treatment, or by newborns and infants under 6 months of age.
  • Before using this medicine, patients in a serious condition (burn patients, etc.), patients with a thyroid disease, patients who have had renal failure, and a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant and a breast-feeding woman should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not use it for the eyes or internally.
  • Be careful to keep it out of the eyes, and if it does get into the eyes, rinse them immediately with clean water.
  • Do not mix it with other preparations for use.
  • Because soaps weaken the germicidal action of this medicine, wash them off thoroughly before use.
  • Wash and disinfect the affected area thoroughly.
  • When it is used on a severe wound, use distilled water for injection or sterile purified water as the diluent, and do not use tap water or purified water.

Possible side effects

  • If symptoms of shock (difficulty breathing, flushing, urticaria, itching, swelling, heartburn and at the same time pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, shortness of breath, etc.) or iododerma rarely appear, if pain, a feeling of irritation, rash, redness or dermatitis occasionally appears, or if a burning sensation, skin ulcer, contact dermatitis or skin discoloration rarely appears, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not use this medicine together with hydrogen peroxide.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when using it together with lithium preparations, chlorhexidine, sulfadiazine and silver compounds, alkalis, preparations containing mercury, or enzyme-based wound healing preparations.

At a glance

Category

How it works

This medicine is used for the treatment of inflammation and the relief of pain in the throat, the oral cavity, and the g

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201206423. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Adults and those aged 12 years and over spray 2 to 4 sprays at a time, and those aged 6 years to under 12 years spray 2 sprays at a time, 2 to 6 times a day.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with peptic ulcer, severe blood abnormalities, severe liver disorder, severe kidney disorder, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure, patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine or have experienced such hypersensitivity, patients who have asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics (including COX-2 inhibitors) or have experienced these, patients being treated for pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG), pregnant women and breastfeeding women must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, people who have had a peptic ulcer, patients with blood abnormalities or who have experienced them, patients with liver disorder or who have experienced it, patients with kidney disorder or who have experienced it, patients with bronchial asthma, the elderly, and patients with cardiovascular disease or with risk factors for cardiovascular disease should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If the following occur, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: occasionally mild numbness of the mouth, a pricking sensation, a burning sensation, rash, and urticaria; rarely skin photosensitivity, laryngospasm, bronchoconstriction, eye floaters, clouded vision, stomatitis, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhea, constipation, gastrointestinal disorders, thirst, heaviness of the head, drowsiness, dizziness, and lethargy; rarely sleep disturbances and abnormal sensation; and occasionally edema and general malaise.

Interactions

  • While using this medicine, do not take (use) it together with other anti-inflammatory analgesics, ACE inhibitors, aspirin, furosemide, lithium, methotrexate, or warfarin.

This medicine is used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, chills (feeling cold and shivering), fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, ch

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202003410. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and over and adults take 2 capsules at a time, three times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when they take this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of a hypersensitivity reaction appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.
  • If severe skin adverse reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis occur, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, those who have experienced asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, infants under 3 months of age, people who are taking MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.) or who stopped taking them within the past 2 weeks, and patients with severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure must not take this medicine.Before taking this medicine, infants infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza and children under 15 years of age, infants and young children aged 3 months and older but under 2 years, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, elderly people, physically weak people, those with an allergic constitution, those who have experienced allergic symptoms (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.), patients with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), difficulty urinating, high fever, gastrointestinal problems such as heartburn, gastric discomfort, or stomach pain, ulcer or bleeding problems, patients who smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough persisting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever and rash or persistent headache, and patients with hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5 or those who have experienced it should consult a doctor or pharmacist.Strictly observe the specified dosage and administration.Do not take it continuously over a long period.Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If rash, redness, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema (swelling), difficulty urinating, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, shock symptoms (urticaria, swelling and tightness in the chest immediately after taking it, together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweats and difficulty breathing), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms accompanied by high fever, in which rash and redness and blisters like burns appear on the skin all over the body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), asthma, listlessness of the whole body, jaundice, interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by coughing, breathlessness, difficulty breathing and fever), sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance, or ischemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding) occurs, stop taking the medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen, MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.), antitussives and expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).
  • If it is taken together with diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, or alcohol, consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

How to take it

Adults (aged 15 years and older) take 2 tablets at a time and children (aged 8 years to under 15 years) take 1 tablet at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.   • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.

  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

  • If rash, redness, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty urinating, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, high anion gap metabolic acidosis, rarely shock symptoms (hives, swelling, and chest tightness immediately after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing), skin-mucosa-eye syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (accompanied by high fever, with severe symptoms such as rash and redness and burn-like blisters appearing on the skin all over the body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), asthma, general lethargy, jaundice, or interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, and fever) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian drugs, etc.), antitussives and expectorants (cough and phlegm medicines), other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Before application, wash the affected area (the diseased area) clean, dry it completely, and then spray an appropriate amount once a day.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be used by patients who have or have had hypersensitivity to this medicine, by a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant or a breast-feeding woman, or by young children and children, and it must not be used on the eyes or around the eyes, on mucous membranes (the mouth, the nose, the vagina, etc.), on the scrotum or the external genitals, on an affected area (a diseased part) with severe eczema, moistness, erosion or wounds, on the nails or on the scalp.

  • Do not use it while the affected area (the diseased part) or its surroundings are contaminated.
  • Be careful to keep it out of the eyes, and if it does get into the eyes, rinse them immediately with water or lukewarm water.
  • Use it externally only and do not use it internally.
  • Shake it well before use.
  • Spray it from a distance of 5 cm from the affected area (the diseased part), and check the nozzle carefully so that it is not sprayed toward or inhaled into the face, especially the eyes.

  • Do not let the eyes or mucous membranes be touched by hands on which this medicine has been left.
  • If the symptoms do not get better after about 2 weeks of use, or if the symptoms worsen because of the use of this medicine, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • If skin rash, redness (reddening from congestion), lacquer-type dermatitis, itching, swelling (puffiness), a feeling of irritation, a feeling of heat, peeling of the skin (flaking), erosion (maceration), dryness or cracking of the skin (splitting) occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Who should ask first

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and over take 3 sachets (15 mL) at a time, those aged 11 years and over but under 15 years take 2 sachets (10 mL) at a time, those aged 7 years and over but under 11 years take 1.5 sachets (7.5 mL) at a time, those aged 3 years and over but under 7 years take 1 sachet (5 mL) at a time, and those aged 2 years and over but under 3 years take 0.75 of a sachet (3.75 mL) at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. If necessary, it may be taken at bedtime. Allow an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported, and if a skin rash or another sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with or with a history of hypersensitivity to this medicine, people who have experienced asthma after taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics, or cold medicines, and infants under 3 months of age and children under 2 years of age must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the following apply: a person with an allergic constitution; a person who has experienced allergic symptoms from medicines such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, or itching; an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant; a breastfeeding woman; a child under 2 years of age for whom it is absolutely necessary; an elderly person; a person in poor physical condition or a person with a high fever; a person with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma, or difficulty urinating; a person whose gastrointestinal problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain persist or recur, or who has ulcers or bleeding problems; a person with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that persists or recurs for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever and rash or a persistent headache; or a patient with or with a history of hypersensitivity to caramel.
  • If symptoms do not improve after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Children should take it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • Drowsiness may occur while taking it.
  • Avoid driving a car or operating machinery.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, (persistent or severe) thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, or insomnia occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.If, rarely, shock (anaphylaxis), in which urticaria, swelling, or chest tightness appears immediately after taking it together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, or difficulty breathing, or mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, or liver function disorder such as generalized lassitude or jaundice, or interstitial pneumonia occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take antitussives and expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives or oral medicines containing an antihistamine.
  • People who are taking an MAO inhibitor used for the treatment of depression, Parkinson's disease and the like, or who are within 2 weeks of stopping one, should not take this medicine.

At a glance

Category

How it works

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202300213. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout and psoriatic arthritis, adults take 200-600 mg of ibuprofen at a time, orally 3-4 times a day. Up to a maximum of 3200 mg a day may be given. For juvenile (occurring at a young age) rheumatoid arthritis, give 30-40 mg per kg of body weight a day orally in 3-4 divided doses. For mild and moderate pain and for colds, adults take 200-400 mg at a time, orally 3-4 times a day. Increase or decrease the dose as appropriate according to age and symptoms. For children, a single dose is 200-250 mg (10-13 ml) at 11-14 years of age and 150-200 mg (8-10 ml) at 7-10 years of age,
Children aged 3-6 years take 100-150 mg (5-8 ml) and children aged 1-2 years take 50-100 mg (3-5 ml), 3-4 times a day. For children weighing less than 30 kg, the daily amount must not exceed 500 mg (25 ml), and administration on an empty stomach should be avoided.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when they take this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic reactions, myocardial infarction, and stroke, which may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcers, and perforation may occur.
  • When non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics including this medicine are taken, serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions that may be fatal, such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcers, and perforation (a hole forming), may occur.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, gastrointestinal ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding or those who have experienced it, patients with severe blood abnormalities, severe liver disorder, severe renal disorder, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure, patients with bronchial asthma or those who have had it, those who have experienced asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics (including COX-2 inhibitors), patients with pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), women in the last 3 months of pregnancy, and patients receiving high-dose methotrexate as chemotherapy must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with blood abnormalities or those who have experienced them, patients with a tendency to bleed, patients with liver cirrhosis or liver disorder or those who have experienced it, patients with renal disorder or those who have experienced it, patients with cardiac insufficiency or heart disease, patients with high blood pressure, those who have experienced hypersensitivity, patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, the elderly and children, pregnant women, breastfeeding women, and people taking low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • Without the instruction of a doctor or pharmacist, do not take it for pain for more than 10 days (adults) or more than 5 days (children), and do not take it for fever for more than 3 days.
  • If pain or fever persists or worsens, or if new symptoms appear, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (chest distress (heartburn), chills, difficulty breathing, a drop in blood pressure, etc.), blood disorders such as decreased hematocrit, decreased hemoglobin, anemia, aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), or eosinophilia, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, hematemesis (vomiting of blood), Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, dry mouth, stomatitis, abdominal bloating, oral ulcers, constipation, black stools, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), photosensitivity reactions (frequency unknown), drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency, angioneurotic edema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash, exfoliative dermatitis, acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, hepatitis, jaundice, abnormal liver function such as elevated GOT, GPT, or alkaline phosphatase (ALP), liver disorder, hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reactions, asthma attacks, urticaria, eczema, purpura, rash, itching, asthma, bronchoconstriction, difficulty breathing or wheezing, visual impairment such as scotoma (an area of the visual field where sight is lost), hearing loss, tinnitus (ringing in the ears), taste disturbance, vertigo, drowsiness, dizziness, depression, headache, cerebrovascular accident or irritability, aseptic meningitis or meningitis (symptoms such as severe headache, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever, or impaired consciousness), a drop in blood pressure, a rise in blood pressure, palpitations, heart failure, myocardial infarction or angina, acute renal failure, oliguria, hematuria, elevated urinary protein, BUN, or blood creatinine, hyperkalemia, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, decreased urine volume, generalized edema and the accompanying shortness of breath and lassitude, periorbital edema (swelling around the eyes), facial edema (swelling of the face), malaise, fever, epistaxis (nosebleed), edema (swelling), or peripheral edema occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with ACE inhibitors, lithium, furosemide and thiazide diuretics, methotrexate, coumarin anticoagulants, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics.

When necessary, put 1 drop at a time into each eye, several times a day. When you put it into the eye, gently pull the lower eyelid down and put one drop into the lower conjunctival sac while looking upward.

  • This medicine can be used even while contact lenses are being worn.
  • Follow the prescribed directions and amounts.

Possible side effects

  • If eye irritation rarely appears, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • When you use this medicine at the same time as another eye drop, use the other eye drop first and use this medicine about 10 minutes later.

This medicine is used for difficulty in expectorating sputum in bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis, pulmonary tuberculosis, emphysema, upper respiratory tract inflammation (pharyngitis and laryngitis), lung abscess, pneumonia, cystic fibrosis and postoperative pulmonary complications, and for the preparation and aftercare of bronchography, bronchoscopy, lung cancer cytology and tracheostomy.

At a glance

Category

How it works

This medicine is used for difficulty in expectorating sputum in bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis, pu

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 198700683. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

For nebulization therapy using a face mask, mouthpiece, or tracheostomy, nebulize 1 to 10 mL every 2 to 6 hours. The recommended amount is 3 to 5 mL nebulized 3 to 4 times a day. Nebulization therapy using a mist tent or an inhalation device (Croupette) is a method needed in special cases and is used on an individual basis according to the patient's personal needs and the convenience of the administration method. This method of administration requires a large volume of solution, and sometimes up to about 300 mL may be required for a single treatment. The recommended amount should be a volume that can maintain a very dense, fog-like state inside the tent or inhalation device throughout the treatment period. Intermittent or continuous long-term administration is desirable. For direct instillation, administer 1 to 2 mL every hour. For the routine treatment of patients who have had a tracheostomy, administer 1 to 2 mL through the tracheostomy every 1 to 4 hours. When administering directly to a specific part of the bronchial tree of the lung by inserting a small plastic catheter into the trachea under local anesthesia and a direct incision, administer 2 to 5 mL every 1 to 4 hours using a syringe connected to the catheter. For diagnostic bronchography, administer 1 to 2 mL 2 to 3 times before performing the bronchography, by nebulization or by instillation into the bronchi.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine should not use it.
  • Before using this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, patients with bronchial asthma or accompanying respiratory insufficiency, elderly people, and children should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • It is not used as an injection or as eye drops.
  • After nebulization therapy the face mask may stick to the face, but it comes off easily when washed with water.

Possible side effects

  • A mild odor (sulfur smell) may occur, sometimes bronchial obstruction, bronchospasm, nausea, vomiting, or loss of appetite, and rarely anaphylaxis, bloody sputum, chills, fever, runny nose, stomatitis, drowsiness, a feeling of chest pressure, or irritation of the trachea and bronchi may occur.

Interactions

  • When it is necessary to use this medicine together with an antibiotic, inhale them separately, or give the antibiotic by injection or orally.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilizers, antiparkinson drugs, etc.), other oral medicines for rhinitis, oral medicines containing antihistamines (cold remedies, antitussives and expectorants, motion sickness medicines, allergy medicines, etc.), or gastrointestinal analgesic and antispasmodic medicines.

Those aged 15 years and over take 1 sachet (20 mL) at a time, those aged 11 years and over but under 15 years take ⅔ of a sachet at a time, those aged 7 years and over but under 11 years take ½ of a sachet at a time, those aged 3 years and over but under 7 years take ⅓ of a sachet at a time, and those aged 2 years and over but under 3 years take ¼ of a sachet at a time, three times a day, 30 minutes after meals, leaving an interval of 4 hours.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.

  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When administering it to children, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • If rash, redness, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, rarely shock symptoms (urticaria, swelling, or chest tightness immediately after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, liver function disorder (generalized lassitude, jaundice), or interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, and fever) occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.If symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance, etc.) occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Do not take this medicine together with antitussive-expectorants, other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness remedies, anti-allergy remedies).

At a glance

Category

How it works

This medicine is used for disinfection of the patient's skin before surgery or before insertion of a syringe needle or a

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201801818. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the applicator from its packaging and hold it with the sponge facing downwards. Do not touch the sponge part of the applicator. Squeeze the applicator firmly only once so that the ampoule breaks and the solution comes out, and leave the broken ampoule inside the applicator. For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

Precautions for use

  • People with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine, isopropanol, or Yellow No. 5 and infants aged 2 months or younger should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use this medicine for disinfecting surgical instruments, or on nervous tissue (e.g., brain or spinal cord tissue), the eyes, ears, mouth, mucous membranes, genital mucous membranes, open wounds, or torn or damaged skin, or for general washing of the skin.
  • Before using this medicine, people with hypersensitivity to other medicines, people who have experienced allergic diseases such as asthma or who have a family history of them, people with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, and people with a drug-hypersensitive constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only on intact skin.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get in, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty breathing, redness, a sudden drop in blood pressure, urticaria, angioedema, etc.), occasionally rash, photosensitization, irritation, sensitization, erythema or inflammation, itching, dry and thinly peeling skin, local pain at the application site, or local skin reactions, or very rarely rash (e.g., erythematous, papular, or maculopapular), blisters, small blisters at the application site, a burning sensation of the skin, dermatitis, eczema, chemical burns in newborns, eye irritation, congestion, impaired vision, or eye damage occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Those aged 15 years and over take 1 packet (75 mL) at a time, those aged 11 years and over but under 15 years take 2/3 of a packet (50 mL) at a time, those aged 7 years and over but under 11 years take 1/2 of a packet (37.5 mL) at a time, those aged 3 years and over but under 7 years take 1/3 of a packet (25 mL) at a time, and those aged 2 years and over but under 3 years take 1/4 of a packet (18.7 mL) at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Precautions for use

  • Patients hypersensitive to this medicine or with such a history, people who have experienced asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, infants under 3 months of age, and people who are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.) or are within 2 weeks of stopping one must not take this medicine.

  • If symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome or reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance, etc.) occur, stop taking the medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.), antitussive expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).
  • People who are within 2 weeks of having stopped taking MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.) must not take this medicine.
  • Patients who have been given diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, steroids and the like, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.

  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When administering it to children, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • If rash, redness, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, rarely shock symptoms (urticaria, swelling, or chest tightness immediately after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, liver function disorder (generalized lassitude, jaundice), or interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, and fever) occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.If symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance, etc.) occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Do not take this medicine together with antitussive-expectorants, other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness remedies, anti-allergy remedies).
  • People who are taking MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.) or who stopped taking them within the past 2 weeks must not take this medicine.

This medicine is used for difficulty in expectorating sputum in bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis, pulmonary tuberculosis, emphysema, upper respiratory tract inflammation (pharyngitis and laryngitis), lung abscess, pneumonia, cystic fibrosis and postoperative pulmonary complications, and for the preparation and aftercare of bronchography, bronchoscopy, lung cancer cytology and tracheostomy.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for difficulty in expectorating sputum in bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis, pu

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 198600267. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

This medicine may be diluted to a lower concentration with sodium chloride solution for injection, sodium chloride solution for inhalation, sterile distilled water for injection or sterile distilled water for inhalation. For nebulization therapy using a face mask, a mouthpiece or a tracheostomy, nebulize 1 to 10 mL every 2 to 6 hours. The recommended amount is 3 to 5 mL nebulized 3 to 4 times a day. Nebulization therapy using a nebulization tent or an inhaler (Croupette) is a method needed in special cases, and it is used individually according to the personal needs of the patient and the convenience of the method of administration. This method of administration requires a large volume of solution, and sometimes as much as about 300 mL may be required for a single treatment. The recommended amount should be an amount that can maintain a very dense mist-like state inside the tent or the inhaler during the treatment period. Intermittent or continuous administration over a long period is preferable. For direct instillation, give 1 to 2 mL every hour. For the regular treatment of a patient who has had a tracheostomy, give 1 to 2 mL through the tracheostomy every 1 to 4 hours. When a small plastic catheter is inserted into the trachea under local anesthesia through a direct incision to give it directly to a specific part of the bronchial tree, give 2 to 5 mL every 1 to 4 hours using a syringe connected to the catheter. When it is given using a percutaneous intrabronchial catheter, give 1 to 2 mL of this medicine every 1 to 4 hours with a syringe connected to the catheter. For diagnostic bronchography, give 1 to 2 mL 2 to 3 times by nebulization or by intrabronchial instillation before the bronchography is performed.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user has bronchial asthma or accompanying respiratory insufficiency, is a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant or a breast-feeding woman, is a child, or is elderly.
  • Do not use it as an injection or as eye drops.
  • After nebulization therapy the face mask may stick to the face, but it comes off easily when washed with water.

Possible side effects

  • If bronchial obstruction, bronchospasm, rash or difficulty breathing occasionally appears, or if anaphylaxis rarely appears, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • A slight odor (smell of sulfur) may appear, nausea, vomiting and loss of appetite may occasionally appear, and bloody sputum, chills, fever, runny nose, stomatitis, drowsiness, a feeling of pressure in the chest and irritation of the trachea and bronchi may rarely appear.

Interactions

  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when it is used together with an antibiotic, tetracycline, erythromycin, bromhexine or the like.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for disinfection of the patient's skin before surgery or before insertion of a syringe needle or a

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201801818. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the applicator from its packaging and hold it with the sponge facing downwards. Do not touch the sponge part of the applicator. Squeeze the applicator firmly only once so that the ampoule breaks and the solution comes out, and leave the broken ampoule inside the applicator. For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

Precautions for use

  • People with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine, isopropanol, or Yellow No. 5 and infants aged 2 months or younger should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use this medicine for disinfecting surgical instruments, or on nervous tissue (e.g., brain or spinal cord tissue), the eyes, ears, mouth, mucous membranes, genital mucous membranes, open wounds, or torn or damaged skin, or for general washing of the skin.
  • Before using this medicine, people with hypersensitivity to other medicines, people who have experienced allergic diseases such as asthma or who have a family history of them, people with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, and people with a drug-hypersensitive constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only on intact skin.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get in, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty breathing, redness, a sudden drop in blood pressure, urticaria, angioedema, etc.), occasionally rash, photosensitization, irritation, sensitization, erythema or inflammation, itching, dry and thinly peeling skin, local pain at the application site, or local skin reactions, or very rarely rash (e.g., erythematous, papular, or maculopapular), blisters, small blisters at the application site, a burning sensation of the skin, dermatitis, eczema, chemical burns in newborns, eye irritation, congestion, impaired vision, or eye damage occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and potentially fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction, and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration, and perforation may occur.
  • Taking this medicine may cause serious and potentially fatal gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration, and perforation.

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, peptic ulcer, severe blood disorders, severe liver disorder, severe kidney disorder, severe heart failure, severe high blood pressure, or bronchial asthma or a history of it, patients with or a history of asthma, urticaria, or allergy caused by aspirin or other anti-inflammatory analgesics, patients being treated for pain before or after coronary artery bypass surgery, and pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and nursing mothers must not take this medicine.

Adults take 100 mg as iron once a day; children aged 12 years and older to under 19 years take 50 mg as iron at a time, twice a day; children aged 1 year and older to under 12 years take 50 mg as iron at a time, 1 to 2 times a day; and children aged 1 year and under take 15–50 mg as iron once a day, before, during, or after a meal.

  • An overdose in children aged 6 years or younger may cause fatal iron poisoning, so keep this medicine out of the reach of children.

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, and patients with hemochromatosis (a disease in which iron is deposited in the liver and pancreas due to abnormal iron metabolism), hemosiderosis, non-iron-deficiency anemia, impaired iron utilization, iron overload, anemia due to bone marrow insufficiency, chronic hemolytic anemia, iron deficiency anemia due to infection or tumor, chronic pancreatitis, or liver cirrhosis must not take this medicine.Before taking this medicine, infants under 12 months of age, patients with gastrointestinal diseases such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis, or regional colitis, patients with cardiac and circulatory system dysfunction, paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria, kidney impairment, or hypoproteinemia, and patients receiving repeated blood transfusions should consult a doctor or pharmacist.Strictly observe the specified dosage and administration.When administering to children, do so under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

  • If urticaria, itching, skin hypersensitivity reactions on exposure to sunlight, abdominal or stomach pain, stomach cramps, vomiting, diarrhea, fever, coma, occasionally elevated AST and ALT, rarely elevated ALP, nausea, loss of appetite, constipation, black stools, tooth discoloration, stomach discomfort, or toxicity occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Do not take it together with phosphates, calcium salts, parenteral iron preparations, or parenteral iron(III) hydroxide polymaltose complex preparations.If taking it together with iron-containing preparations (iron supplements, liver contrast agents for MRI, etc.), antialdosterone agents, triamterene, diphosphonate salts, thyroxine, cefdinir preparations, quinolones, penicillamine, cholestyramine, preparations such as pancreatic extract and vitamin E, or 200 mg or more of ascorbic acid (vitamin C), consult a doctor or pharmacist.Avoid teas containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, and milk and dairy products while taking it and before and after taking it.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202104595. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and over take 1 sachet (20 mL), those aged 11 years and over but under 15 years take 2/3 of a sachet, those aged 7 years and over but under 11 years take 1/2 of a sachet, those aged 3 years and over but under 7 years take 1/3 of a sachet, and those aged 2 years and over but under 3 years take 1/4 of a sachet, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. Do not administer it to children under 2 years of age. As a rule, allow an interval of 4 hours between doses.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of a hypersensitivity reaction appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine or have experienced such hypersensitivity, people who have had an asthma attack when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold medicines, infants (newborns) under 3 months of age, and people who are taking MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.) or are within 2 weeks of having stopped them must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, infants and young children aged 3 months and over but under 2 years, infants and children under 15 years of age who have or are suspected of having a chickenpox or influenza infection, people with an allergic constitution, people who have experienced an allergy to a medicine (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.), people with liver, kidney, heart or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer and the like, the elderly, people with a weak body or a high fever, people with persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or with ulcer or bleeding problems, women who are pregnant or may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, and people with symptoms such as smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts more than 1 week or recurs, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever and rash or a persistent headache should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If symptoms do not improve after taking it 5 to 6 times, consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • Do not take it continuously over a long period.
  • When giving it to a child, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness (turning red from congestion), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema (swelling), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, shock symptoms (urticaria, swelling, and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, along with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome: accompanied by high fever, with severe symptoms such as rash and redness and blistering like burns), asthma, general fatigue, jaundice (the skin or the whites of the eyes take on a yellow color), or interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by coughing, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, and fever) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian drugs, etc.), antitussives and expectorants (cough and phlegm medicines), other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis [nasal inflammation], motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).

Those 15 years and older take 1 sachet (20 mL) at a time, those 11 years and older but under 15 years take 2/3 sachet at a time, those 7 years and older but under 11 years take 1/2 sachet at a time, those 3 years and older but under 7 years take 1/3 sachet at a time, and those 2 years and older but under 3 years take 1/4 sachet at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Precautions for use

  • Children under 2 years of age, patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, people who have had asthma after taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics, or cold medicines, infants under 3 months of age, and people who are taking MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.) or who are within 2 weeks of stopping them must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; a person with a constitution prone to urticaria, contact dermatitis, bronchial asthma, allergic rhinitis, migraine, or food allergy; a person with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma, or difficulty urinating; an elderly person; a person in poor physical condition; a person with a high fever; a person whose gastrointestinal problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain persist or recur, or who has ulcers or bleeding problems; a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant; a breastfeeding woman; or a person with a cough (smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that persists or recurs for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash, or a persistent headache).
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • When administering it to children, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking this medicine, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty urinating, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, shock symptoms (rarely, urticaria, swelling, and chest tightness immediately after taking it, together with pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms accompanied by high fever, with rash, redness, and burn-like blisters), asthma, general listlessness, jaundice, or interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, and fever) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen, MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian drugs, etc.), antitussives and expectorants, other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).
  • Patients who have taken diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, or alcohol should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201700813. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Spray 6 ml per 1 ㎥ using the dedicated sprayer, which has a spray performance of 80 m per second and a capacity of 1000 ml per hour. Use this medicine in the following order. Press the spray nozzle button of the dedicated sprayer to detach the spray nozzle. Carefully attach the product container to the device in the correct direction. Connect the spray nozzle with the product container attached to the dedicated sprayer. Use the power cable to connect the device to an electrical outlet. Set the spray adjustment lever to 6 times the volume of the space to be sprayed. (For example, if the volume of the space to be sprayed is 50 ㎥, set it to 300 ㎥.) The spray time and spray volume according to the marking (㎥) on the spray adjustment lever are set to 1 ml per 1 ㎥. Press the power switch button to supply power to the device. Using the handle, aim the spray nozzle at the area to be sprayed. When you press the start button, a buzzer sounds for 15 seconds, and at this time the user leaves the space to be sprayed. When spraying ends, the device stops automatically. Re-enter the sprayed space after a certain time has passed following the end of spraying. To stop the device, press the power switch button to cut off the power. The waiting time before re-entering after spraying ends is 2 hours. If there are contaminants, remove the contamination thoroughly and then disinfect and sterilize with this product.

Warning

  • Do not use it on the human body.

Precautions for use

  • If it comes into contact with the skin, immediately take off any contaminated clothing and wash the area thoroughly with running water.
  • If it gets into the eyes, immediately rinse them with running water for at least 15 minutes and then consult a doctor.
  • If the vapor is inhaled, move immediately to a place with fresh air and then consult a doctor.
  • If it is swallowed by mistake, immediately have the person drink a large amount of water or milk, do not force vomiting, and consult a doctor.
  • Before use, familiarize yourself thoroughly with the dosage, administration and precautions for this product.
  • Avoid contact with the skin and eyes, and wear gloves, protective goggles and other suitable protective equipment or clothing to avoid contact with the product.
  • Use it with a dedicated sprayer approved by the manufacturer.
  • Before disinfecting, clean thoroughly to remove visible contamination.
  • When disposing of the disinfectant solution, flush it away with a large amount of water.
  • This product disinfects the surface of medical devices, so do not use it for devices that require internal disinfection.

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201801818. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the applicator from its packaging and hold it with the sponge facing downwards. Do not touch the sponge part of the applicator. Squeeze the applicator firmly only once so that the ampoule breaks and the solution comes out, and leave the broken ampoule inside the applicator. For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

Precautions for use

  • People with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine, isopropanol, or Yellow No. 5 and infants aged 2 months or younger should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use this medicine for disinfecting surgical instruments, or on nervous tissue (e.g., brain or spinal cord tissue), the eyes, ears, mouth, mucous membranes, genital mucous membranes, open wounds, or torn or damaged skin, or for general washing of the skin.
  • Before using this medicine, people with hypersensitivity to other medicines, people who have experienced allergic diseases such as asthma or who have a family history of them, people with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, and people with a drug-hypersensitive constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only on intact skin.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get in, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty breathing, redness, a sudden drop in blood pressure, urticaria, angioedema, etc.), occasionally rash, photosensitization, irritation, sensitization, erythema or inflammation, itching, dry and thinly peeling skin, local pain at the application site, or local skin reactions, or very rarely rash (e.g., erythematous, papular, or maculopapular), blisters, small blisters at the application site, a burning sensation of the skin, dermatitis, eczema, chemical burns in newborns, eye irritation, congestion, impaired vision, or eye damage occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

How it works

Why this one

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the applicator from its packaging and hold it with the sponge facing downwards. Do not touch the sponge part of the applicator. Squeeze the applicator firmly only once so that the ampoule breaks and the solution comes out, and leave the broken ampoule inside the applicator. For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

Precautions for use

  • People with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine, isopropanol, or Yellow No. 5 and infants aged 2 months or younger should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use this medicine for disinfecting surgical instruments, or on nervous tissue (e.g., brain or spinal cord tissue), the eyes, ears, mouth, mucous membranes, genital mucous membranes, open wounds, or torn or damaged skin, or for general washing of the skin.
  • Before using this medicine, people with hypersensitivity to other medicines, people who have experienced allergic diseases such as asthma or who have a family history of them, people with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, and people with a drug-hypersensitive constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only on intact skin.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get in, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.

Possible side effects

  • Do not mix it with other preparations.

  • Wash and disinfect the affected area thoroughly.

Adults usually insert 1 tablet per dose deep into the vagina at bedtime, 1 time a day for 6 consecutive days. When used as short-term therapy, adults insert 2 tablets per dose deep into the vagina at bedtime, 1 time a day for 3 consecutive days.

  • Do not use it orally.

  • Do not use the applicator during pregnancy.
  • Do not use it during menstruation.
  • If vulvitis or candidal balanitis is also present, it is advisable to use a clotrimazole cream preparation in addition.
  • If symptoms such as itching or inflammation occur, the sexual partner should also receive topical treatment.
  • To prevent reinfection, change personal items such as towels and underwear every day, and boil and wash the ones that have been used.
  • While using this medicine, do not use tampons, vaginal douches, cleansers, or other products inserted into the vagina.
  • In addition, do not have vaginal intercourse.
  • Do not let this medicine come into contact with the eyes.
  • Only children aged 12 years and older and adults should use it.
  • This medicine may weaken latex or rubber products such as condoms and contraceptive diaphragms.
