Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the applicator from its packaging and hold it with the sponge facing downwards. Do not touch the sponge part of the applicator. Squeeze the applicator firmly only once so that the ampoule breaks and the solution comes out, and leave the broken ampoule inside the applicator. For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

Precautions for use

  • People with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine, isopropanol, or Yellow No. 5 and infants aged 2 months or younger should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use this medicine for disinfecting surgical instruments, or on nervous tissue (e.g., brain or spinal cord tissue), the eyes, ears, mouth, mucous membranes, genital mucous membranes, open wounds, or torn or damaged skin, or for general washing of the skin.
  • Before using this medicine, people with hypersensitivity to other medicines, people who have experienced allergic diseases such as asthma or who have a family history of them, people with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, and people with a drug-hypersensitive constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only on intact skin.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get in, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty breathing, redness, a sudden drop in blood pressure, urticaria, angioedema, etc.), occasionally rash, photosensitization, irritation, sensitization, erythema or inflammation, itching, dry and thinly peeling skin, local pain at the application site, or local skin reactions, or very rarely rash (e.g., erythematous, papular, or maculopapular), blisters, small blisters at the application site, a burning sensation of the skin, dermatitis, eczema, chemical burns in newborns, eye irritation, congestion, impaired vision, or eye damage occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

This medicine is used for the sterilization and disinfection of lacerations, burns, wounds, bedsores, ulcers, abscesses,

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, newborns and infants under 6 months of age, patients before or after radioactive iodine treatment, patients with thyroid dysfunction such as nodular goiter, endemic goiter, or Hashimoto's thyroiditis, patients with renal failure, and patients with dermatitis herpetiformis must not use this medicine.

  • Wash and disinfect the affected area thoroughly.
  • When using it on severe wounds, use distilled water for injection or sterile purified water as the diluent.
  • Do not use tap water or purified water.
  • If this medicine gets on clothing or the like, washing it immediately makes it come out easily with water.
  • In the case of synthetic fibers, it can be removed with ammonia water or sodium thiosulfate.

  • In the case of ulcers caused by burns, use it only on ulcers resulting from secondary damage after a burn.
  • Do not use it on newly occurring burns.
  • Leave an interval of 1 to 2 weeks between the use of this medicine and flash irradiation.
  • If an infection such as peritonitis or osteomyelitis occurs, wash with physiological saline before using this medicine.
  • If the iodine of this medicine is absorbed through healthy or damaged skin, it interferes with thyroid function tests.

  • Occasionally, pain, itching, a sensation of irritation, rash, redness, and dermatitis may occur.If these symptoms are severe, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.If, rarely, hypersensitivity such as difficulty breathing, flushing, or urticaria, a burning sensation, skin ulcer, contact dermatitis, skin discoloration, metabolic acidosis, or abnormal kidney function occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.Rarely, anaphylactic symptoms or shock may occur.If sudden itching, swelling, or heartburn appears together with severe symptoms such as pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, or shortness of breath, stop using this medicine immediately and seek medical attention from a doctor.When used in the vagina, blood inorganic iodine levels and blood total iodine levels may rise.

Interactions

  • Do not use this medicine together with lithium therapy or hydrogen peroxide solution.
  • If you use it together with chlorhexidine, sulfadiazine-silver compounds, alkali- and mercury-containing preparations, or enzyme-based wound treatments, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

How it works

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201801818. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the applicator from its packaging and hold it with the sponge facing downwards. Do not touch the sponge part of the applicator. Squeeze the applicator firmly only once so that the ampoule breaks and the solution comes out, and leave the broken ampoule inside the applicator. For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

Precautions for use

  • People with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine, isopropanol, or Yellow No. 5 and infants aged 2 months or younger should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use this medicine for disinfecting surgical instruments, or on nervous tissue (e.g., brain or spinal cord tissue), the eyes, ears, mouth, mucous membranes, genital mucous membranes, open wounds, or torn or damaged skin, or for general washing of the skin.
  • Before using this medicine, people with hypersensitivity to other medicines, people who have experienced allergic diseases such as asthma or who have a family history of them, people with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, and people with a drug-hypersensitive constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only on intact skin.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get in, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty breathing, redness, a sudden drop in blood pressure, urticaria, angioedema, etc.), occasionally rash, photosensitization, irritation, sensitization, erythema or inflammation, itching, dry and thinly peeling skin, local pain at the application site, or local skin reactions, or very rarely rash (e.g., erythematous, papular, or maculopapular), blisters, small blisters at the application site, a burning sensation of the skin, dermatitis, eczema, chemical burns in newborns, eye irritation, congestion, impaired vision, or eye damage occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

How it works

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

After the hair and the scalp are completely dry, apply 0.5 to 1 mL of this medicine to the affected area only, twice a day (morning and evening), for at least 4 months, and do not let the total daily amount exceed 2 mL.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be used by women, people under 18 years of age, patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with a cardiovascular disease (coronary artery disease, arrhythmia, congestive heart failure, valvular heart disease, treated or untreated high blood pressure, low blood pressure), patients who have no hereditary factor for hair loss, patients with sudden patchy hair loss, patients with a scalp abnormality such as erythema, inflammation, infection, irritation or pain of the scalp, psoriasis or sunburn, patients with hair loss of unknown cause, patients who are using another medicine for the scalp, patients who have shaved the scalp, or patients who tolerate the 2 % strength poorly.
  • Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is elderly, has edema, has thyroid dysfunction (hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism), has local exfoliation, dermatitis, psoriasis of the scalp or a severe burn, or has a history of heart disease.
  • Use this medicine externally only and do not use it on any area other than the scalp.
  • Do not use an occlusive dressing.
  • Because this medicine may cause burning and irritation of the eyes, be careful to keep it out of the eyes, and if it touches a sensitive area such as the eyes, broken skin or a mucous membrane, rinse it off immediately with clean water.
  • Use hair styling products after this medicine has dried, and when using it in the evening, use it 2 to 4 hours before bedtime so that it can dry.
  • Because circulation of air over the scalp may reduce the effect of this medicine, do not use a hair dryer to speed up its drying.

Possible side effects

  • If any of the following appears, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: itching, scaling, erythema, redness, dermatitis, dry skin, excessive hair growth at sites other than the area where this medicine was applied (facial hair growth in women), folliculitis, local irritation including a burning sensation and skin eruption, exfoliation, hair loss, skin abscess, acne, nail disorder, seborrhea, eczema, hair abnormality, bronchitis, upper respiratory tract infection, sinusitis, difficulty breathing, occasional diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, chest pain, change in blood pressure, change in pulse, palpitations, increased heart rate, pericardial effusion, pericarditis, embolism, tachycardia, worsening of pre-existing angina or induction of angina in a person with undiagnosed coronary artery disease, shortness of breath, fracture, back pain, tendinitis, pain, neuritis (including polyneuritis), weakness, dizziness, headache, feeling dazed, fainting, hepatitis, edema, kidney stones, inflammation and fluid retention, fever, urticaria, allergic rhinitis, systemic erythema and facial swelling, chills, eye irritation, bitter taste, otitis (especially otitis externa), change in taste, visual disturbance, erectile dysfunction, stabbing pain, or sudden unexplained weight gain.

Interactions

  • Do not use it together with other medicines for the scalp, medicines that promote absorption through the skin (for example topical corticosteroids, retinoids, petrolatum, dithranol), or vasodilators (for example guanethidine, etc.).

How it works

This medicine is used for the disinfection of medical equipment (examination tables, operating tables, medical lighting

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201700813. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Spray 6 ml per 1 ㎥ using the dedicated sprayer, which has a spray performance of 80 m per second and a capacity of 1000 ml per hour. Use this medicine in the following order. Press the spray nozzle button of the dedicated sprayer to detach the spray nozzle. Carefully attach the product container to the device in the correct direction. Connect the spray nozzle with the product container attached to the dedicated sprayer. Use the power cable to connect the device to an electrical outlet. Set the spray adjustment lever to 6 times the volume of the space to be sprayed. (For example, if the volume of the space to be sprayed is 50 ㎥, set it to 300 ㎥.) The spray time and spray volume according to the marking (㎥) on the spray adjustment lever are set to 1 ml per 1 ㎥. Press the power switch button to supply power to the device. Using the handle, aim the spray nozzle at the area to be sprayed. When you press the start button, a buzzer sounds for 15 seconds, and at this time the user leaves the space to be sprayed. When spraying ends, the device stops automatically. Re-enter the sprayed space after a certain time has passed following the end of spraying. To stop the device, press the power switch button to cut off the power. The waiting time before re-entering after spraying ends is 2 hours. If there are contaminants, remove the contamination thoroughly and then disinfect and sterilize with this product.

Warning

  • Do not use it on the human body.

Precautions for use

  • If it comes into contact with the skin, immediately take off any contaminated clothing and wash the area thoroughly with running water.
  • If it gets into the eyes, immediately rinse them with running water for at least 15 minutes and then consult a doctor.
  • If the vapor is inhaled, move immediately to a place with fresh air and then consult a doctor.
  • If it is swallowed by mistake, immediately have the person drink a large amount of water or milk, do not force vomiting, and consult a doctor.
  • Before use, familiarize yourself thoroughly with the dosage, administration and precautions for this product.
  • Avoid contact with the skin and eyes, and wear gloves, protective goggles and other suitable protective equipment or clothing to avoid contact with the product.
  • Use it with a dedicated sprayer approved by the manufacturer.
  • Before disinfecting, clean thoroughly to remove visible contamination.
  • When disposing of the disinfectant solution, flush it away with a large amount of water.
  • This product disinfects the surface of medical devices, so do not use it for devices that require internal disinfection.

Apply this medicine to the infected area (trunk, face, scalp, hair), leave it on for 3 to 5 minutes like an ordinary shampoo, and then rinse it off. Who should ask first

Before application, wash the affected area (the diseased area) clean, dry it completely, and then spray an appropriate amount once a day.

  • This medicine must not be used by patients who have or have had hypersensitivity to this medicine, by a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant or a breast-feeding woman, or by young children and children, and it must not be used on the eyes or around the eyes, on mucous membranes (the mouth, the nose, the vagina, etc.), on the scrotum or the external genitals, on an affected area (a diseased part) with severe eczema, moistness, erosion or wounds, on the nails or on the scalp.
  • Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user has an allergic constitution, if the affected area (the diseased part) is on the face or is extensive or has suppuration, or if it is unclear whether the condition is "eczema" or "athlete's foot, tinea cruris (ringworm of the groin) or tinea corporis".
  • Follow the prescribed directions and amounts.
  • Do not use it while the affected area (the diseased part) or its surroundings are contaminated.
  • Be careful to keep it out of the eyes, and if it does get into the eyes, rinse them immediately with water or lukewarm water.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use the eye drops

When necessary, instill 1 to 2 drops into the eye that has symptoms, and discard the remaining solution and the container after instillation. When it is used at the same time as another eye drop, leave an interval of at least 15 minutes between instillations in order to avoid a dilution effect.

  • Use it externally only.
  • Do not reuse it after a single use, and be sure to discard the remaining solution and the container.

  • If you experience pain, a change in the field of vision, or persistent redness of the eye or a feeling of irritation, or if the symptoms get worse or last for 72 hours or more, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

This medicine is used for difficulty in expectorating sputum in bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis, pulmonary tuberculosis, emphysema, upper respiratory tract inflammation (pharyngitis and laryngitis), lung abscess, pneumonia, cystic fibrosis and postoperative pulmonary complications, and for the preparation and aftercare of bronchography, bronchoscopy, lung cancer cytology and tracheostomy.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for difficulty in expectorating sputum in bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis, pu

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201903112. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

For nebulization therapy using a face mask, mouthpiece, or tracheostomy, nebulize 1 to 10 mL every 2 to 6 hours. The recommended amount is 3 to 5 mL nebulized 3 to 4 times a day. Nebulization therapy using a mist tent or an inhalation device (Croupette) is a method needed in special cases and is used on an individual basis according to the patient's personal needs and the convenience of the administration method. This method of administration requires a large volume of solution, and sometimes up to about 300 mL may be required for a single treatment. The recommended amount should be a volume that can maintain a very dense, fog-like state inside the tent or inhalation device throughout the treatment period. Intermittent or continuous long-term administration is desirable. For direct instillation, administer 1 to 2 mL every hour. For the routine treatment of patients who have had a tracheostomy, administer 1 to 2 mL through the tracheostomy every 1 to 4 hours. When administering directly to a specific part of the bronchial tree of the lung by inserting a small plastic catheter into the trachea under local anesthesia and a direct incision, administer 2 to 5 mL every 1 to 4 hours using a syringe connected to the catheter. For diagnostic bronchography, administer 1 to 2 mL 2 to 3 times before performing the bronchography, by nebulization or by instillation into the bronchi.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine should not use it.
  • Before using this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, patients with bronchial asthma or accompanying respiratory insufficiency, elderly people, and children should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • It is not used as an injection or as eye drops.
  • After nebulization therapy the face mask may stick to the face, but it comes off easily when washed with water.

Possible side effects

  • A slight odor (a sulfurous smell), occasionally nausea, vomiting and loss of appetite, and rarely bloody sputum, chills, fever, runny nose, stomatitis, drowsiness, a feeling of pressure in the chest, and irritation of the trachea and bronchi may occur.

Interactions

  • When it is necessary to use this medicine together with an antibiotic, inhale them separately, or give the antibiotic by injection or orally.

Adults use an amount sufficient to cover the affected area up to its edges, 5 times a day for 5 days. Start treatment as soon as possible as soon as the first symptoms and signs appear.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with skin infections caused by bacteria (tuberculosis, syphilis, etc.), fungi (candidiasis, ringworm, etc.), viruses other than herpes simplex (shingles, chickenpox, vaccinia, etc.) or animal parasites (scabies, pubic lice, etc.), patients with seriously impaired immune systems such as bone marrow transplant patients or AIDS patients, patients with eczematous otitis externa with perforation of the eardrum, patients with ulcers (excluding Behcet's disease), patients with deep burns or frostbite of grade 2 or higher, patients with perioral dermatitis, acne vulgaris or rosacea, breastfeeding women, children under 18 years of age, and patients with myocardial infarction or a history of it must not use this medicine.
  • Pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and elderly people should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not use it in the eyes, nose, mouth or genitals.
  • Do not use this medicine to prevent transmission to other people or to prevent recurrent herpes simplex (blister) infection.
  • Do not use this medicine as a base for diluting it or for mixing other medicines.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • Use it only for cold sores on the lips or around the mouth.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after using it for about 5 days, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If commonly a feeling of dryness or peeling of the skin, occasionally a temporary burning sensation or numbness, rarely erythema, pigmentation, inflammation, bacterial (impetigo contagiosa, folliculitis, etc.) or fungal (candidiasis, tinea, etc.) skin infections, general skin symptoms (folliculitis, boils, skin irritation, stinging pain, fever, a burning sensation, rash, redness, flushing, itching, dry skin, pustular dermatitis, allergic contact dermatitis, heat rash, miliaria, worsening of wounds, bedsores, pustulosis), or, when it is used on the eyelid skin, increased intraocular pressure or glaucoma, or blurred vision of unknown frequency occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Who should ask first

How to apply it

For sterilizing and disinfecting the hands and arms of the surgeon, put 5 mL of this medicine on the hands and arms, rub it in well for about 5 minutes to produce plenty of lather, and then rinse it off thoroughly with running water.   • Do not use this medicine together with hydrogen peroxide.

Category

How it works

This medicine is used for the disinfection of medical equipment (examination tables, operating tables, medical lighting

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201700813. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Spray 6 ml per 1 ㎥ using the dedicated sprayer, which has a spray performance of 80 m per second and a capacity of 1000 ml per hour. Use this medicine in the following order. Press the spray nozzle button of the dedicated sprayer to detach the spray nozzle. Carefully attach the product container to the device in the correct direction. Connect the spray nozzle with the product container attached to the dedicated sprayer. Use the power cable to connect the device to an electrical outlet. Set the spray adjustment lever to 6 times the volume of the space to be sprayed. (For example, if the volume of the space to be sprayed is 50 ㎥, set it to 300 ㎥.) The spray time and spray volume according to the marking (㎥) on the spray adjustment lever are set to 1 ml per 1 ㎥. Press the power switch button to supply power to the device. Using the handle, aim the spray nozzle at the area to be sprayed. When you press the start button, a buzzer sounds for 15 seconds, and at this time the user leaves the space to be sprayed. When spraying ends, the device stops automatically. Re-enter the sprayed space after a certain time has passed following the end of spraying. To stop the device, press the power switch button to cut off the power. The waiting time before re-entering after spraying ends is 2 hours. If there are contaminants, remove the contamination thoroughly and then disinfect and sterilize with this product.

Warning

  • Do not use it on the human body.

Precautions for use

  • If it comes into contact with the skin, immediately take off any contaminated clothing and wash the area thoroughly with running water.
  • If it gets into the eyes, immediately rinse them with running water for at least 15 minutes and then consult a doctor.
  • If the vapor is inhaled, move immediately to a place with fresh air and then consult a doctor.
  • If it is swallowed by mistake, immediately have the person drink a large amount of water or milk, do not force vomiting, and consult a doctor.
  • Before use, familiarize yourself thoroughly with the dosage, administration and precautions for this product.
  • Avoid contact with the skin and eyes, and wear gloves, protective goggles and other suitable protective equipment or clothing to avoid contact with the product.
  • Use it with a dedicated sprayer approved by the manufacturer.
  • Before disinfecting, clean thoroughly to remove visible contamination.
  • When disposing of the disinfectant solution, flush it away with a large amount of water.
  • This product disinfects the surface of medical devices, so do not use it for devices that require internal disinfection.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for disinfection of the patient's skin before surgery or before insertion of a syringe needle or a

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201801818. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the applicator from its packaging and hold it with the sponge facing downwards. Do not touch the sponge part of the applicator. Squeeze the applicator firmly only once so that the ampoule breaks and the solution comes out, and leave the broken ampoule inside the applicator. For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

Precautions for use

  • People with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine, isopropanol, or Yellow No. 5 and infants aged 2 months or younger should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use this medicine for disinfecting surgical instruments, or on nervous tissue (e.g., brain or spinal cord tissue), the eyes, ears, mouth, mucous membranes, genital mucous membranes, open wounds, or torn or damaged skin, or for general washing of the skin.
  • Before using this medicine, people with hypersensitivity to other medicines, people who have experienced allergic diseases such as asthma or who have a family history of them, people with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, and people with a drug-hypersensitive constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only on intact skin.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get in, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty breathing, redness, a sudden drop in blood pressure, urticaria, angioedema, etc.), occasionally rash, photosensitization, irritation, sensitization, erythema or inflammation, itching, dry and thinly peeling skin, local pain at the application site, or local skin reactions, or very rarely rash (e.g., erythematous, papular, or maculopapular), blisters, small blisters at the application site, a burning sensation of the skin, dermatitis, eczema, chemical burns in newborns, eye irritation, congestion, impaired vision, or eye damage occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine or have experienced such hypersensitivity, children under 12 years of age, people who have had surgery exposing the dura mater or transsphenoidal hypophysectomy, patients with closed-angle glaucoma, patients with rhinitis sicca (dry nasal inflammation) or atrophic rhinitis (nasal inflammation), and patients with pheochromocytoma or an enlarged prostate must not use this medicine.

  • Use this medicine only as a nasal spray for rhinitis, and do not use it in the eyes or ears.

  • If rash and redness, swelling, an irritating sensation, itching, or signs/symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome or reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, nausea, vomiting, visual disturbance, etc.) occur, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • People who are taking (using) MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.) or who are within 2 weeks of having stopped taking (using) them must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, patients who are being given tricyclic or tetracyclic antidepressants should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while using it.

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201707150. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area (the diseased site) 1 to 2 times a day (in the morning, or in the morning and evening).

Precautions for use

  • Do not use this medicine in patients hypersensitive to it, in patients with skin infections (tuberculosis, syphilis, herpes zoster, herpes simplex, chickenpox, vaccinia), eczematous otitis externa (inflammation of the ear canal) with a perforated eardrum, ulcers (excluding Behcet's disease), burns or frostbite of deep (not visible on the surface) second degree or worse, perioral dermatitis, acne vulgaris, rosacea, syphilis, tuberculosis, or a skin vaccine reaction, or on injured skin or over a wide area (10 % or more of the body surface area).

  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When administering it to children, do so under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Use it for external use only and do not use it internally.
  • If it is used on the genitals together with latex contraceptive devices (condoms and vaginal suppositories), it may damage the latex contraceptive devices and so may reduce their safety and effectiveness.

  • Bacterial skin infections (impetigo contagiosa (pus-crust disease), folliculitis) may occur, and increased intraocular pressure and glaucoma may occur when it is used on the skin of the eyelids.
  • If occasionally a burning sensation, skin irritation, rash, redness (turning red from congestion), allergic contact dermatitis, a stinging sensation, or swelling occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

How it works

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202007978. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Adults use an amount sufficient to cover the affected area up to its edges, 5 times a day for 5 days. Start treatment as soon as possible as soon as the first symptoms and signs appear.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with skin infections caused by bacteria (tuberculosis, syphilis, etc.), fungi (candidiasis, ringworm, etc.), viruses other than herpes simplex (shingles, chickenpox, vaccinia, etc.) or animal parasites (scabies, pubic lice, etc.), patients with seriously impaired immune systems such as bone marrow transplant patients or AIDS patients, patients with eczematous otitis externa with perforation of the eardrum, patients with ulcers (excluding Behcet's disease), patients with deep burns or frostbite of grade 2 or higher, patients with perioral dermatitis, acne vulgaris or rosacea, breastfeeding women, children under 18 years of age, and patients with myocardial infarction or a history of it must not use this medicine.
  • Pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and elderly people should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not use it in the eyes, nose, mouth or genitals.
  • Do not use this medicine to prevent transmission to other people or to prevent recurrent herpes simplex (blister) infection.
  • Do not use this medicine as a base for diluting it or for mixing other medicines.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • Use it only for cold sores on the lips or around the mouth.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after using it for about 5 days, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If commonly a feeling of dryness or peeling of the skin, occasionally a temporary burning sensation or numbness, rarely erythema, pigmentation, inflammation, bacterial (impetigo contagiosa, folliculitis, etc.) or fungal (candidiasis, tinea, etc.) skin infections, general skin symptoms (folliculitis, boils, skin irritation, stinging pain, fever, a burning sensation, rash, redness, flushing, itching, dry skin, pustular dermatitis, allergic contact dermatitis, heat rash, miliaria, worsening of wounds, bedsores, pustulosis), or, when it is used on the eyelid skin, increased intraocular pressure or glaucoma, or blurred vision of unknown frequency occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not use it together with probenecid.

Who should ask first

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the applicator from its packaging and hold it with the sponge facing downwards. Do not touch the sponge part of the applicator. Squeeze the applicator firmly only once so that the ampoule breaks and the solution comes out, and leave the broken ampoule inside the applicator. For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

Precautions for use

  • People with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine, isopropanol, or Yellow No. 5 and infants aged 2 months or younger should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use this medicine for disinfecting surgical instruments, or on nervous tissue (e.g., brain or spinal cord tissue), the eyes, ears, mouth, mucous membranes, genital mucous membranes, open wounds, or torn or damaged skin, or for general washing of the skin.
  • Before using this medicine, people with hypersensitivity to other medicines, people who have experienced allergic diseases such as asthma or who have a family history of them, people with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, and people with a drug-hypersensitive constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only on intact skin.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get in, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty breathing, redness, a sudden drop in blood pressure, urticaria, angioedema, etc.), occasionally rash, photosensitization, irritation, sensitization, erythema or inflammation, itching, dry and thinly peeling skin, local pain at the application site, or local skin reactions, or very rarely rash (e.g., erythematous, papular, or maculopapular), blisters, small blisters at the application site, a burning sensation of the skin, dermatitis, eczema, chemical burns in newborns, eye irritation, congestion, impaired vision, or eye damage occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area (diseased site) several times a day.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be used by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, by patients with thyroid dysfunction (especially nodular goiter, endemic goiter, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, etc.), renal failure, dermatitis herpetiformis, by newborns and infants under 6 months of age, or by patients before or after radioactive iodine treatment.

  • If anaphylactoid symptoms (difficulty breathing, flushing, urticaria, etc.) or iododerma rarely appears, if pain, itching, a feeling of irritation, rash, redness or dermatitis occasionally appears, or if a burning sensation, skin ulcer, contact dermatitis or skin discoloration rarely appears, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Category

How it works

This medicine is used for the early treatment of recurrent herpes labialis.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201908393. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Adults use an appropriate amount, enough to cover the affected area fully to its edge, 5 times a day for 5 days. Limit the treatment period with this medicine to 5 days or less. Start the treatment as soon as possible, right when the first symptoms and signs appear.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be used by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, by patients with a skin infection (tuberculosis, syphilis, candidiasis, tinea, herpes zoster, chickenpox, vaccinia, scabies, pubic lice), impairment of the immune system (bone marrow transplant, AIDS), eczematous otitis externa with perforation of the eardrum, ulcer (except Behcet's disease), a burn or frostbite of deep second degree or worse, perioral dermatitis, acne vulgaris or rosacea, by patients who have or have had myocardial infarction, by breast-feeding women, or by children under 18 years of age.
  • Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user has had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to propylene glycol, is a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant, or is elderly.
  • Use it only on herpes labialis on the lips or around the mouth, and do not use it in the eyes, the nose, the mouth or the genitals.
  • Do not use it on a person who has no sign or symptom.
  • Follow the prescribed directions and amounts.
  • Do not use it for the purpose of preventing infection of another person or preventing recurrent herpes simplex infection.
  • Do not use this medicine as a base for diluting it or for mixing other medicines.

Possible side effects

  • If a feeling of dryness or peeling of the skin, which are common, a temporary burning sensation or numbness, which occur occasionally, or, rarely, application site reactions including erythema, pigmentation and the symptoms and signs of inflammation, contact dermatitis, contagious impetigo, folliculitis, candidiasis, tinea, folliculitis, boils, skin irritation, a stabbing pain, fever, a burning sensation, rash, redness, flushing, itching, dry skin, pustular dermatitis, allergic contact dermatitis, heat rash, sweat rash, worsening of the wound, bedsores, pustulosis, a rise in intraocular pressure or glaucoma when it is used on the skin of the eyelid, or blurred vision of unknown frequency occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when using it together with probenecid.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use the eye drops

When necessary, instill 1 to 2 drops into the eye that has symptoms, and discard the remaining solution and the container after instillation. When it is used at the same time as another eye drop, leave an interval of at least 15 minutes between instillations in order to avoid a dilution effect.

Precautions for use

  • Use it externally only.
  • Do not reuse it after a single use, and be sure to discard the remaining solution and the container.
  • To avoid contamination, do not let the tip of the container touch anything outside.
  • Do not use it if the color of the solution has changed or if it has become cloudy.
  • Because temporary blurring of vision may occur, be careful when driving or operating dangerous machinery until the vision becomes clear.

Possible side effects

  • If you experience pain, a change in the field of vision, or persistent redness of the eye or a feeling of irritation, or if the symptoms get worse or last for 72 hours or more, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

This medicine is used to relieve inflammation caused by dentures, oral candidiasis such as thrush, gingivitis, pharyngit

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201708285. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use it in the mouth

Use 15 mL per dose, twice a day: rinse the mouth or gargle for about 1 minute and then spit it out; use it after brushing the teeth. Immediately after use, avoid rinsing with water or another mouthwash, brushing the teeth, or having food. In the case of stomatitis caused by dentures, soak and clean the dentures for 15 minutes twice a day. The amount may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.

Warning

  • Do not use it for a long period, because it may cause an imbalance of the normal bacterial flora in the mouth.

Precautions for use

  • People who have experienced hypersensitivity to this medicine must not use this medicine.
  • Patients who have an allergic disease such as asthma or who have such a history or a family history, pregnant women, breast-feeding women and children should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it only for gargling and do not use it internally.

Possible side effects

  • Temporary parotitis, an increase in staining on the teeth or the surface of the mouth (the inside of the mouth), an increase in the formation of supragingival calculus, a change in the sense of taste and the like may occur.
  • If, rarely, symptoms of shock (for example, nausea, discomfort, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty in breathing, seizure) or, occasionally, rash or urticaria occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

How to use the eye drops

When necessary, instill 1 to 2 drops into the eye that has symptoms, and discard the remaining solution and the container after instillation. When it is used at the same time as another eye drop, leave an interval of at least 15 minutes between instillations in order to avoid a dilution effect.

Precautions for use

  • Use it externally only.
  • Do not reuse it after a single use, and be sure to discard the remaining solution and the container.
  • To avoid contamination, do not let the tip of the container touch anything outside.
  • Do not use it if the color of the solution has changed or if it has become cloudy.
  • Because temporary blurring of vision may occur, be careful when driving or operating dangerous machinery until the vision becomes clear.

Possible side effects

  • If you experience pain, a change in the field of vision, or persistent redness of the eye or a feeling of irritation, or if the symptoms get worse or last for 72 hours or more, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

At a glance

Category

How it works

This medicine is used for the early treatment of recurrent herpes labialis (cold sores).

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202002774. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Adults use an appropriate amount, enough to cover the affected area (the diseased part) fully to its edge, 5 times a day for 5 days. Start the treatment as soon as possible, right when the first symptoms and signs appear.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be used by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, by breast-feeding women, by children under 18 years of age, by patients with a skin infection (tuberculosis, syphilis, candidiasis, tinea, herpes zoster, chickenpox, vaccinia, scabies, pubic lice), by patients whose immune system is seriously impaired (bone marrow transplant patients, AIDS patients), by patients with eczematous otitis externa with perforation of the eardrum, ulcer (except Behcet's disease), a burn or frostbite of deep second degree or worse, perioral dermatitis, acne vulgaris or rosacea, or by patients who have or have had myocardial infarction.
  • Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant, is elderly, or has or has had hypersensitivity to propylene glycol.
  • Do not use it in the eyes, the nose, the mouth or the genitals.
  • Use it only on herpes labialis (cold sores) on the lips or around the mouth.
  • Follow the prescribed directions and amounts.
  • Do not use this medicine as a base for diluting it or for mixing other medicines.

Possible side effects

  • If a feeling of dryness or peeling of the skin, which are common, a temporary burning sensation (a hot feeling) or numbness, which occur occasionally, or, rarely, erythema (red spots), pigmentation or the symptoms and signs of inflammation occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Because of systemic absorption, reversible suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, Cushing's syndrome, hyperglycemia, diabetes and visual disturbance may occur.

This medicine is used for difficulty in expectorating sputum in bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis, pulmonary tuberculosis, emphysema, upper respiratory tract inflammation (pharyngitis and laryngitis), lung abscess, pneumonia, cystic fibrosis and postoperative pulmonary complications, and for the preparation and aftercare of bronchography, bronchoscopy, lung cancer cytology and tracheostomy.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for difficulty in expectorating sputum in bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis, pu

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201903112. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

For nebulization therapy using a face mask, mouthpiece, or tracheostomy, nebulize 1 to 10 mL every 2 to 6 hours. The recommended amount is 3 to 5 mL nebulized 3 to 4 times a day. Nebulization therapy using a mist tent or an inhalation device (Croupette) is a method needed in special cases and is used on an individual basis according to the patient's personal needs and the convenience of the administration method. This method of administration requires a large volume of solution, and sometimes up to about 300 mL may be required for a single treatment. The recommended amount should be a volume that can maintain a very dense, fog-like state inside the tent or inhalation device throughout the treatment period. Intermittent or continuous long-term administration is desirable. For direct instillation, administer 1 to 2 mL every hour. For the routine treatment of patients who have had a tracheostomy, administer 1 to 2 mL through the tracheostomy every 1 to 4 hours. When administering directly to a specific part of the bronchial tree of the lung by inserting a small plastic catheter into the trachea under local anesthesia and a direct incision, administer 2 to 5 mL every 1 to 4 hours using a syringe connected to the catheter. For diagnostic bronchography, administer 1 to 2 mL 2 to 3 times before performing the bronchography, by nebulization or by instillation into the bronchi.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine should not use it.
  • Before using this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, patients with bronchial asthma or accompanying respiratory insufficiency, elderly people, and children should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • It is not used as an injection or as eye drops.
  • After nebulization therapy the face mask may stick to the face, but it comes off easily when washed with water.

Possible side effects

  • A slight odor (a sulfurous smell), occasionally nausea, vomiting and loss of appetite, and rarely bloody sputum, chills, fever, runny nose, stomatitis, drowsiness, a feeling of pressure in the chest, and irritation of the trachea and bronchi may occur.

Interactions

  • When it is necessary to use this medicine together with an antibiotic, inhale them separately, or give the antibiotic by injection or orally.

This medicine is used for the sterilization and disinfection of torn wounds, burns, wounds and bedsores, the sterilization and disinfection of ulcers and abscesses, the disinfection of infected skin surfaces, the sterilization and disinfection of surgical sites, and the disinfection of injection and catheter sites.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the sterilization and disinfection of torn wounds, burns, wounds and bedsores, the sterilizati

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200203626. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area (diseased site) several times a day.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be used by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, by patients with thyroid dysfunction (especially nodular goiter, endemic goiter, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, etc.), renal failure, dermatitis herpetiformis, by newborns and infants under 6 months of age, or by patients before or after radioactive iodine treatment.
  • Before using this medicine, patients in a serious condition (burn patients, etc.), patients with a thyroid disease, patients who have had renal failure, and a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant and a breast-feeding woman should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not use it for the eyes or internally.
  • Be careful to keep it out of the eyes, and if it does get into the eyes, rinse them immediately with clean water.
  • Do not mix it with other preparations for use.
  • Wash and disinfect the affected area thoroughly.
  • When it is used on a severe wound, use distilled water for injection or sterile purified water as the diluent, and do not use tap water or purified water.
  • Because soaps weaken the germicidal action of this medicine, wash them off thoroughly before use.

Possible side effects

  • If anaphylactoid symptoms (difficulty breathing, flushing, urticaria, etc.) or iododerma rarely appears, if pain, itching, a feeling of irritation, rash, redness or dermatitis occasionally appears, or if a burning sensation, skin ulcer, contact dermatitis or skin discoloration rarely appears, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not use hydrogen peroxide together with this medicine.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when using it together with lithium preparations, chlorhexidine, sulfadiazine silver compounds, alkalis, preparations containing mercury, or enzyme-based wound healing preparations.

Topical medicine (MFDS 202500570)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202500570. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for the disinfection of surgical sites.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the disinfection of surgical sites.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202500570. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Press the cap at the end of the applicator handle so that the antiseptic solution soaks into the sponge, and apply it to the area to be disinfected. During use, adjust the amount of solution with the sponge attached to the applicator. Do not use it on the head, the neck, or small areas. Do not rub it off. Do not let the solution pool, and if a lot of solution runs, absorb it using the sponge. If the solution runs outside the area of use, wipe it off with gauze. If the solution gets into the navel, wipe it off with a cotton swab. Prepare a towel as needed to keep the solution from running down, and remove it before covering with a surgical drape. When applying it to skin folds such as the fingers and toes, hold the application site open with sterile-gloved hands until the liquid dries. Otherwise the skin surfaces may stick together. Use it as a single-use product only and discard any remaining solution.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine, patients with thyroid function abnormalities (nodular goiter, endemic goiter, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, etc.), patients with renal failure, newborns and infants under 6 months of age, patients with dermatitis herpetiformis, patients before and after radioactive iodine treatment, severely ill patients such as burn patients, and patients receiving lithium treatment must not use this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who have had thyroid disease and patients with it, patients with renal failure, women who are pregnant or may be pregnant, and breastfeeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not apply it to burns or mucous membranes, and do not use it as a substitute for an ordinary skin cleanser.
  • Use it for external use only.
  • Do not mix it with other preparations.

Possible side effects

  • If occasionally pain, itching, an irritating sensation, rash, redness or dermatitis, or rarely shock (anaphylaxis: severe symptoms such as sudden itching, swelling and heartburn together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and shortness of breath), a burning sensation, skin ulcer, contact dermatitis or skin discoloration occur, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not use it together with lithium, chlorhexidine, sulfadiazine-silver compounds, alkalis, preparations containing mercury, enzyme-based wound treatments, or hydrogen peroxide.

This medicine is used for the temporary relief of dryness of the eye or of the burning sensation, irritation, and discomfort caused by exposure to wind or sun.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Eye drops

How it works

This medicine is used for the temporary relief of dryness of the eye or of the burning sensation, irritation, and discom

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202303025. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use the eye drops

Put 1 to 2 drops into the affected eye as needed.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine must not use it.
  • Before using this medicine, people with severe eye pain and those who have experienced allergic symptoms from eye drops such as redness of the eye, itching, swelling, or rash should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use this medicine only for instillation, that is, as a medicine put into the eye.
  • If you swallow this medicine by mistake, get help from a doctor or another professional immediately.
  • If symptoms worsen or last for 72 hours or longer, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not reuse it after 1 use.
  • After instilling it in the eye, discard the remaining solution and the container.
  • To avoid contamination of this medicine and damage to the eye, do not let the tip of the container touch the eye or any outside surface.
  • Do not use it if the color of the medicine has changed or if it has become cloudy.
  • Do not use it as a wetting solution for soft contact lenses or while wearing soft contact lenses.
  • Remove contact lenses before using this medicine.
  • Put them back on 15 minutes after instilling it in the eye.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.

Possible side effects

  • If symptoms such as itching, swelling, pain, changes in vision, persistent redness, or irritation occur, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If a person wearing hard contact lenses has increased discharge such as eye mucus and, rarely, clouding of the lenses, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Because of its high viscosity, vision may become temporarily blurred when this medicine is instilled into the eye.

Interactions

  • When this medicine is used at the same time as other eye drops, leave an interval of at least 15 minutes before using this medicine.

Category

How it works

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202301937. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use the eye drops

Instill 2 to 3 drops at a time, 2 to 4 times a day. After instillation, discard the remaining solution and the container.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, patients with significant corneal damage should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When giving this medicine to children, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Use this medicine for instillation into the eye only.
  • When using it for the first time, discard the first 1 to 2 drops without instilling them (to remove any container fragments produced when opening it).
  • Be careful, because if the tip of the container touches the eyelid or eyelashes the solution may become contaminated or cloudy from eye mucus or mold, and do not use it if it has become cloudy.
  • To prevent contamination, avoid sharing it with others as far as possible.

Possible side effects

  • If a hypersensitivity reaction occurs, or if no improvement in symptoms is seen after about 2 weeks of use, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for fungal skin infections (tinea, cutaneous candidiasis, tinea versicolor) accompanied by clinica

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200300836. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area (the diseased site) 1 to 2 times a day (in the morning, or in the morning and evening).

Precautions for use

  • Do not use this medicine in patients hypersensitive to it, in patients with skin infections (tuberculosis, syphilis, herpes zoster, herpes simplex, chickenpox, vaccinia), eczematous otitis externa (inflammation of the ear canal) with a perforated eardrum, ulcers (excluding Behcet's disease), burns or frostbite of deep (not visible on the surface) second degree or worse, perioral dermatitis, acne vulgaris, rosacea, syphilis, tuberculosis, or a skin vaccine reaction, or on injured skin or over a wide area (10 % or more of the body surface area).
  • Before using this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, infants and children, and patients hypersensitive to propylene glycol or with such a history should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When administering it to children, do so under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Use it for external use only and do not use it internally.
  • If it is used on the genitals together with latex contraceptive devices (condoms and vaginal suppositories), it may damage the latex contraceptive devices and so may reduce their safety and effectiveness.

Possible side effects

  • Bacterial skin infections (impetigo contagiosa (pus-crust disease), folliculitis) may occur, and increased intraocular pressure and glaucoma may occur when it is used on the skin of the eyelids.
  • If occasionally a burning sensation, skin irritation, rash, redness (turning red from congestion), allergic contact dermatitis, a stinging sensation, or swelling occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
